# Changelog

Newest first. Every change to code lands here in the same commit. A new dependency says why.
- feat(switchboard): when a chat's process ends because the chat moved to the server (the lent process carries `moved`), the session starts again on the server with `resume` and a turn that was cut is sent again from its start; a finished turn is not repeated, and a failure ends the thread saying why (`carryOn` in lib/lent-placement.js; the drivers hand `moved` to `onExit`). The lender's last whole turn is the chat's transcript here through link's resume loader. Test: core/sessions/lent-spawn.test.js.
- feat(work): `work.chat.title { chat }` -> `{ title }` (internal, modules only): a chat's name, up to 120 characters, for any chat id, so the home names a lent chat on its computer's list however the chat was started. Test: core/work/chat-title.test.js.
- feat(publish): Publish from the preview card (R032-07). `publish.quick { name, preview }` takes a files preview's id instead of a folder: the person who pressed the card, never a model, and the server resolves the folder through an internal `previews.folder` (Publish only, relaying the person; a server preview or a one-file preview is refused in words). The answer carries the held task and plan, and `public` plus the note until the public door is on; `publish.decide` answers the deployment with its `url`. Test: test/journey-publish-react.test.js.
- refactor(design): the A5 baseline is empty (#130). The app and the Deck read the owners' lists instead of keeping copies: the tools each yes covers and the reusable ones come from lib/one-yes-ops.js (lib/one-yes.js re-exports them), the AI providers from lib/ai-ids.js, and the tools that take a space from the tool reference, generated into apps/app/src/real/space-tools.generated.js and web/js/one-yes-ops.generated.js by scripts/gen-surface-lists.mjs (test/surface-lists.test.js fails when they are stale). The app now asks for a yes on every tool of the pair and vault moments the box lists, not a shorter list of its own.
- fix(kernel): the sealer's dev switch is read through devSwitch at boot (`dev: devSwitch(process.env.VYRE_SEAL_DEV)`), so a packaged build ignores VYRE_SEAL_DEV whatever the environment says and a development build (install-box --from with VYRE_DEV_SIGN=0) accepts a stand-in owner key only when the switch is set; a guard in kernel/devbuild.test.js keeps raw comparisons out. The sealing line cap is 1005 (was 960) with a reason per added function in kernel/seal/budget.test.js. core/vault/vault.js and core/modules/index.js are back under their file-size numbers.
- fix(app): a project started from a template no longer reads "No teammates yet" on its Team tab while its timeline says "research joined the team as researcher". The roles a template names are team records, the Team tab read only teammates (a different thing); it now also lists who is on the project's team and the role each fills (new read `work.project.members`, reach anyone, person surfaces only; apps/app/screens/teammates). Whether those roles should become teammates is a design question raised with the lead.
- test: four reds on the integration tip that were mine, settled. The watchers reach test knows watchers.hook.run (modules); the presence-bypass test follows R031-09 (a model, the assistant included, proposes a change to an agent and changes nothing itself); the turn-this-into-a-flow skill writes its tools as `tools_call flows_patch` and the others; the provider-adapters list takes the skill library's two Claude names (the plugin folder it lays down) until that writer moves behind the Claude driver.
- fix(switchboard): a new chat of the owner is placed on their computer at creation (end-to-end test `core/runner/lent-chat-e2e.test.js`: a real daemon, the lender's runner in the sandbox, a fake Claude; the chat is placed, runs there, answers in the chat and says `thread.placing` starting then up). Two bugs it found: the placement asked for a Space id the switchboard's kernel handle does not have (the runner host now says which Space it serves), and the CLI runner did not take the lent spawn. The same test calls a Vyre tool from inside the lent session (the fake Claude runs in place and the lender's sandbox reads the repo) and checks the call came down the lender's door for the chat's own thread. It needs the sandbox, so it runs where link's runner tests run.
- fix(infra): the pinned test browser came back. A merge in the runner work deleted test/headless-chrome.js, scripts/install-test-chrome.mjs and the install step of node.yml and merge-queue.yml, so core/previews/site.test.js and test/journey-publish-react.test.js failed at load on every shard. All three are restored.
- fix(redact): the browser extension's redactor (lib/siteops/redact.js) and the phone app's redactor (screens/connections/model.ts) now hide every credential shape the table (lib/credential-shapes.js) knows. Before, each held its own short list: a Stripe signing secret, a GitLab token, a SendGrid key, a Shopify, Linear, Notion, Supabase or Telegram key and about thirty more passed through both. The app reads a generated copy of the table (apps/app/src/store-core/credential-shapes.js, `node scripts/sync-copies.mjs`). Two bugs in the table itself: a credential that ends in `=` (base64 padding) was read as `NAME=` with nothing after it, and Shopify's `shpss_` secret was not classed as a key. `test/credential-pins.test.js` now builds a sample from every shape's own pattern instead of five by hand (guard audit #126).
- test: key-screens (guard audit #126) reads each route's code with the TypeScript parser. A route is drawn from blocks only if it renders `BlockScreen` (a JSX element or a call) itself or through a component it imports and uses; a comment, a string or an unused import no longer counts. The check also runs the other way: a route listed as hand-written that now draws blocks fails, which found `sites/[id]` still listed as hand-written. It moved to the block list.
- fix(box): a published server's wall removes a hook door left from before (a tag that once belonged to a catalog app with a hook port), and the compose lint for a published server now fails when `read_only` or the one tmpfs is missing; `sp_app_load` finds a published server when no app catalog exists. Each has a red-first test in test/space-helper-pub-up.test.js (link's review).
- test(guards): S6 and S8 have guards (issues #133, #134). `test/stranger-session.test.js` walks every signing route and public path in the catalog, a site's server and a preview as a stranger who brings a made-up Vyre cookie, another host's real session and the Vyre headers: the app is never sent the owner's session and no owner data comes back. `test/relay-never-reads.test.js` runs the relay's front in its own process behind real TLS and scans its memory (from /proc), logs, counters and folder for a marker that is in the request and the answer; a control finds a word the relay may read. The S6 walk found a real hole, now fixed: a stranger on an app's `public` path was sent the install's admin session (core/appmods/proxy.js).
- test(wink): the software-key test asks for a vault reveal, not a vault.put. Since one-yes step B a Vault save is the person's own act (no yes, contracts/one-yes.md: `vault.put` is refused as a card op on purpose); a reveal is a vault moment, and a software key's proof for it is still refused without the dev switch (checked: 13 of 13 in wink-paired-2-b). Not a hole: `vault.put` never took a yes after step B, and no secret is shown by it.
- fix(projects): starting a project from a template no longer says its first tasks are in Now when they could not be made. When an assistant the template names is not in the space yet, the stage could not make its task, said so only in the server log, and the app still toasted "Its first tasks are in Now" over a project with no tasks. `work.start-project` now answers `tasks_made` as a count and `tasks_skipped` with the task and why ("research is not in this space yet"), and the app says it (kernel/flows/stages.js, core/work/templates.js, apps/app/screens/templates).
- test(grants): the lender's cap test (CAP-3) agrees with the 10 Oct ruling: a lend that states no limit inherits the floor, so lending an accepted computer again with none stated is the same lend and keeps the limit; a stated different limit is still refused.
- test(app): the Run on this computer switch is proved against the real spaces tools (core/spaces/spaces.test.js): the plan reads spaces.devices.list for the device the app is on, lending shows in the list, and stopping asks nothing. The runner half (runner.settings.set enabled) is the runner contract's.
- feat(projects): the timeline of a project that started from a template begins with "Started from the Estate plan template", then each stage and task in order (core/work/timeline.js). The real-daemon template test now reads the timeline back and checks every line is plain words and in order (J2, the stage and timeline steps).
- test(design): a guard for A5, one owner per fact (#130). test/a5-no-copies.test.js finds literal lists of three or more names in the surfaces (apps/app, local, web) that copy an owner's registry (every tool name a module.json declares, the kernel's role ids, the AI providers) and fails on a new copy; the five that exist are in test/a5-baseline.json with the reason each stays, and the baseline may only shrink.
- feat(app): Glass on a phone away from the server (team/contracts/glass-relay.md, link's relay path). The screen page is bundled into the app (`apps/app/src/glass/frame-page.generated.ts`, `node scripts/gen-glass-page.mjs`: frame.js, the vendored noVNC and input.js as one module script), its WebSocket is replaced by link's shim, and the app carries the stream's bytes on the relay channel through `createWsBridge` and a socket that waits for the channel (`screens/glass/lazy-socket.js`). Where the phone reaches the box directly nothing changes. Checked: the bundled page runs in a browser, says ready, and opens its shim socket when told to connect. Not yet proven on a phone. Docs: using/mobile.
- test(flows): the lines form of a scheduled Flow with lanes and a sub-flow (what @Engineer writes) reads back as the same Flow, and the plain-words walk keeps a picture of a project's Overview and Team tabs.
- ci: android-app can be started by hand with `mock: 0` to build a real debug APK (no sample world) that talks to a box; its artifact is `android-app-real-debug-<sha>`. The default build is unchanged. It is the APK the Glass relay proof pairs with a box world.
- test(app): a proof that the phone's Glass page draws a frame in a real Android WebView, on a hosted emulator (`.github/workflows/android-glass-relay.yml`, `apps/app/scripts/glass-relay-android.sh`). A fake screen server (the Glass tests' fake Xvnc behind a WebSocket) runs on the runner; the mock build's proof route `vyre://glass-relay-proof` opens the bundled page in relay mode with its sockets pointed at the server (`GlassFrame` takes an optional `openSocket`); the job fails unless the screenshot is mostly the server's grey. It proves the page, the socket shim, the bridge and noVNC in the real WebView; the relay channel under it is proven in core/computers/glass-relay.test.js.
- feat(app): Glass on a phone away from the server (team/contracts/glass-relay.md, link's relay path). The screen page is bundled into the app (`apps/app/src/glass/frame-page.generated.ts`, `node scripts/gen-glass-page.mjs`: frame.js, the vendored noVNC and input.js as one module script), its WebSocket is replaced by link's shim, and the app carries the stream's bytes on the relay channel through `createWsBridge` and a socket that waits for the channel (`screens/glass/lazy-socket.js`). Where the phone reaches the box directly nothing changes. Checked: the bundled page runs in a browser, says ready, and opens its shim socket when told to connect. Not yet proven on a phone, so the doc still says the relay path is not proven (using/mobile).
- feat(app): the approval card on a Flow's page says what the Flow does before you approve it ("Reads: matter. Sends or publishes: email.send. Hands work to: the manager role."), the same words as under its code, instead of only the code. A send that rides an earlier yes says so there (apps/app/screens/flows/RealFlow.tsx).
- fix(app): "What it would do" under a Flow's code read "Sends or publishes: [object Object]". The kernel gives each effect as an object (the step, the action, who gets the task); the screen joined them as if they were names. It now says the action, the connector or who by name (a role as "the manager role"), and a send that rides an earlier yes says so (apps/app/screens/flows/engineer-model.ts; red first against the real compile output in engineer.test.js).
- fix(agents,work): start-up work that needs the Space's record store is tried again while a team Space's store is still starting, instead of giving up until the next restart. The agent records now follow the roster once the store joins (core/agents/mirror.js), and the Personal project / General migration and the access-restore item are retried (core/work/retry-away.js). Found in the J1 box log: "the agent records did not follow the roster", "Personal project / General migration did not finish", each said once and never retried.
- feat(design): the list block grows, additively (R031-58): a row may carry faces (people and assistants), provider marks, up to three accessories (a chip, or quiet text with `as: "text"`) and a dim flag. The language checks them (lib/views/blocks.js, LIST_ROW_EXTRAS), the list draws them (apps/app/ui/blocks/list-rules.js rowExtras, BlockViews ListBlock). The Chats list is a list block with them: same faces, provider badges, Needs you, Failed, unread, age and dim row. Settings and Sites are unchanged.
- fix(work): `work.chat.create` called again with the id the caller chose answers the chat instead of refusing "a chat id is new" (journey J1: the journey's store wait retried a create whose first attempt had already made the chat). Test: core/work/chat-engineer.test.js (red without the change).
- fix(work): a person's first @Engineer chat starts (journey J1). The app starts it with `work.chat.create` naming the built-in `engineer` agent, which no run had yet made an actor of the Space, so the kernel refused with "an assistant in a chat belongs to the Space" and the pinned chat never existed. `work.chat.create` now registers the agent through the daemon (`agentActor`, the kernel's own registration under the owner's chain) and starts the chat. Test: core/work/chat-engineer.test.js (red without the change).
- test/fix: tools-text-names (guard audit #126) can no longer pass on an empty text: a brief it slices by a marker fails when the marker is reworded or too little text is left to check. It was red on the tip from the description cuts, and is green now: the session brief (`ask.many`), the flow skill, the flows cheat sheet (kernel/flows/cheatsheet.js, same line count) and the hand-written parts of docs/agents/connections.md and flows.md name tools outside the core through `tools_call`; the flows page is back within its token budget.
- test: reach-anyone reasons are tried against the code (#116). test/reach-anyone-behaviour.test.js (in GUARDS): a reason that says "no model caller" must be true on a real daemon (a bare mcp and a bare harness are stopped before the tool's own input check; all 84 claims hold today, and a false one goes red), and a name with a mutating verb in any segment (`x.set-token` too) needs a reason that names a guard.
- feat(runner): Vyre's tools reach every chat on a Mac, including chats whose placement row is older than the rule (lent-spawn v1.3, chat's ask). `lentSpawn({ session, thread })` routes the tool socket by `thread` (the id the switchboard opens it under); `session` stays the book, checkpoint and transcript key and no row is rewritten. `thread.placing` is the one placement event (the switchboard's); the daemon no longer emits `thread.starting`.
- test: the sessions contract by behaviour (`test/chat-sessions-flow.test.js`, guard audit #126). A real daemon runs a real turn on a fake Claude and the events it emitted go through the app's own reducer; the test asserts the answer is one whole item and the session waits for the next words. It reads no source text. The other three guards in #126 (tools-text-names, key-screens, credential-pins) belong to projects-flows, design and trust.
- test(guards): S6 and S8 have guards (issues #133, #134). `test/stranger-session.test.js` walks every signing route and public path in the catalog, a site's server and a preview as a stranger who brings a made-up Vyre cookie, another host's real session and the Vyre headers: the app is never sent the owner's session and no owner data comes back. `test/relay-never-reads.test.js` runs the relay's front in its own process behind real TLS and scans its memory (from /proc), logs, counters and folder for a marker that is in the request and the answer; a control finds a word the relay may read. The S6 walk found a real hole, now fixed: a stranger on an app's `public` path was sent the install's admin session (core/appmods/proxy.js).
- test/fix(app): the sessions contract (`test/chat-sessions-contract.test.js`) has no known excuses any more: the AHEAD, FUTURE and LEGACY sets are gone. An event chat hears is emitted by the box (the plan, built as an event object, is now seen by the scan), or the listener goes: the app no longer listens for `ask.cancelled` (a withdrawn ask is `ask.answered` with decision `cancelled`), `thread.model` or `thread.starting`.
- fix(gate): who approved, rejected, revised or settled a held item was whatever `by` the caller sent (FOUNDATION S3: identity is set by the kernel, never read from input), so any caller allowed to approve could sign it as someone else in the item's row and events. The caller is stamped now; a `by` sent is not read. New guard test/identity-from-input.test.js (in GUARDS): every identity-looking input field on a tool a person or model can reach is reviewed with its reason (target, designation, narrowing, shim, caller), a new one fails until reviewed, and a rule that matches nothing fails. Closes #132. Also: the Flow rows of Used by come from flows.connections, as the person looking; lib/credential-shapes.js type-checks and preflight T3 fails on any app type error.
- test(guards): the outward-flags guard can fail (#115). It found modules one folder deep only, took a short verb list, trusted a named test that could be skipped, and rested on a reviewer's file that may be absent. It now finds every module.json at any depth, knows more outward verbs, requires the named test to run (not skipped), and no longer depends on the reviewer's list. No product code changed.
- test(guards): the person-label guards can fail (#124). New `test/model-label-matrix.test.js` reads the golden decisions and fails when an unproven model label (an agent name on mcp or cli, a tailnet or Space agent label) runs any tool, reach:person and owner-effect ones included, that its own surface does not run in the same world, whatever shape the deciding code has; it proves itself against a doctored matrix. In `person-label-hygiene` the SHIM(legacy labels) marker no longer blesses any line: today's four files are counted in `SHIMMED` and only shrink, and a test checks the detector still sees the label shapes. No product code changed.
- feat(runner): a screen hears a chat's process start on a computer and fall back: `thread.starting { thread, session, computer, state: starting | up | fallback, reason? }`, and each chat that borrows a computer is one line for the Space's timeline: `lease.borrowed { thread, session, person, device, limit, epoch, at }` (link module events; contract lent-spawn v1.3).
- fix(relay): onboarding can pair the first device on a Mac that keeps its keys in vyre-core. `relay.pair.first` asked for a yes, and before the first device exists no yes can: it asks none now (it is no longer one of the pairing moments). What guards it: only the onboarding listener's own caller (never a label a socket client can name), never once any person or owner exists, and a person's surface or an agent is refused. test/relay-d.test.js was red on this; core/relay/pair-first.test.js pins the guards.
- fix(app): Now on a box whose setup is unfinished shows the "Finish setting up Vyre" banner alone. The banner already lists "your assistant, your Claude and your devices", so the full-width "Create your assistant" card under it said the same thing twice (apps/app/screens/now/NowScreen.tsx).
- fix(app): Now, Recent no longer lists the Flows system's own bookkeeping ("Vyre def-flow.created", "Vyre flow-approval.created", "Vyre flow-run.created"). Event names with a hyphen were let through as if they were words; the same rule that hides "member.set" now covers them (apps/app/ui/tasks/model.js plainLine; red first in model.test.js).
- refactor(app): the Sites list is a list block (R031-58). Each site is a row (name, what is live and where, a site icon); a site waiting on you is a chip and the rest say their state in plain words, like Settings. A list block draws a tight row's accessory as a chip when its tone needs the person (accent, warn or err); every other tight row stays plain text, so Settings does not change (apps/app/ui/blocks/list-rules.js). The Sites route moves from hand-written to blocks in test/key-screens.test.js.
- test(flows): test/flows-daemon.test.js sets the runner's own memory of a schedule as well as the store's. The timer's early look at a new Flow (the wake-up fix) starts that memory at "now", so the test's two-minutes-ago schedule was not due.
- fix(flows): while a Space's record store is still starting, the Flows host no longer logs one "the record store is still starting" line for every event (the journey box's log had hundreds); events are skipped until the store joins, and an `unavailable` answer is never logged as a failure (core/daemon/flows-host.js).
- fix(app): in the Flows list the health line comes before the trigger, so on a phone, where the line is cut, what is cut is the trigger and not "Red: google is down" (apps/app/screens/flows/real-model.js).
- feat(documents): one yes covers both signing emails. The signing Flow's signed-copy step carries `with: "send"` (contract flow-runs.md item 7), so the person says yes once to the request and the signed copy goes out days later with no second card; `documents.send` names `documents.send-signed` in `covers`. `signed_field` (documents.signing.flow) sets a yes/no field to yes just before the move, which the Estate Kit's matter needs (rule `signed_before_drafting`). J2 walks the Estate Kit's own matter through Engagement to Drafting and no longer skips.
- test(stream): Ask about this on a real daemon (`core/stream/ask-about-live.test.js`): words picked in the conversation are quoted into the person's next message, the assistant hears the quote and the question, and the chat shows what was sent. Checked by picture in the sample world: selecting words shows the button, pressing it puts a chip above the composer with Remove.
- fix(app): Ask about this on selected text names the author of the message the words are in ("juno"), not "this chat" (each message row carries `data-from`).
- fix(flows): a Flow whose lane failed said "2 need you" in its health line while the Needs-you list had one row. A lane or sub-flow whose parent already reports the failure is one thing to look at (kernel/flows/health.js; red first in kernel/flows/joins.test.js).
- feat(app): a Flow's own page says how it is doing: a banner above the canvas when it is red (a connection it uses is down, a saved test fails, most of the week failed) or amber (paused, something waits for you), and one quiet line (last run, how many went well this week, the next time) otherwise. The words are the kernel's health line (apps/app/screens/flows/RealFlow.tsx, real-model.js).
- feat(runner): the Harness hooks run on a Mac too (lent-spawn v1.3). The box's Harness plugin is sent to the lender as a mark; the runner loads its own copy of the plugin and gives the session `VYRE_SOCKET` and `VYRE_THREAD`, so SessionStart, PreToolUse (the security floor), learn and the rest ask the home through the door as a `harness` caller. Without a door or a plugin folder the session runs without hooks, as before.
- feat(runner): a chat taking a lent computer is also a line on the Space's log (`lease.borrowed`, owner-visible, beside `lease.issued`/`lease.refused`), so the timeline can read it and a screen that was not listening still sees it.
- test(runner): chaos scenario `lidMidTurn`: the lid shuts in the middle of a chat's turn on a Mac; the SDK hears a move (not a crash), the server resumes once from the last whole turn, the cut turn is not in what it resumes from, and the lender writes nothing more.
- test(relay): Glass over the relay is proven end to end (contracts/glass-relay.md v1): the page's WebSocket shim, the app's bridge, a RelaySocket on a real Noise channel, the box's relay bridge, the real Glass and a fake Xvnc. The RFB handshake and a 1.9 MB frame cross; a spent ticket and any other stream are refused. Fix found by it: `RelaySocket` handed a Node Buffer's whole pool as a message, now its own copy.
- feat(runner): lending a computer needs no yes per lease (lead's ruling): the member's lend IS the permit. A computer's lease request is checked against the Offers, not a signature: it must come from the very computer the lend names (another computer of the member naming it gets nothing, and a probe never holds a key), it ends with an unlend, a revoke or a removal, a lease already held is not renewed after that, and what the computer says about itself (limit, runner version, protocol) can only tighten what the lender allowed (the floor still applies). Every request, granted or refused, is on the Space's log (`lease.issued` and `lease.refused`: who, which computer, what limit). The lease card on the lender's own queue (`approvals.lease-ask` and `lease-status`) and the signed-hello switch are gone. Docs: using/local-runner.
- fix(box): on an installed box root could not find the daemon's folder (`sp_lend_base` looked for a mount at `/home/vyre/.vyre`, but the installer mounts the whole home at `/home/vyre`). Every verb that reads the daemon's folder as root (`pub-build`, `pub-up`, `publish-fill`, the lent-workspace encryption) said "the daemon's home folder could not be found". It now also finds `.vyre` inside the home mount. The test rig had only the old shape, which hid it. Proof: `scripts/proof/pub-helper-proof.sh`, a site's server built, run, rotated, updated and retired on a real installer box.
- fix(spaces): a team Space's record store that is still starting says where it is and how long it has been, instead of a bare "still starting". While Records come up for the first time (download, database, Records themselves, workspace) every refused read, the health answer and the waiting list say, for example, "the record store is still starting: starting Records (the first start takes a few minutes) (2 minutes so far)" (stores/twenty/space-store.js `startingWords`, provision.js `onPhase`). Found by the J1 first-day journey; the speed of the first start itself is unchanged.
- fix(flows): a Kit proposal holding a key was stored whole, so the key sat in the proposal record, its change log and the approval card. `flows.kit.propose` now refuses a Kit with anything key-shaped in it, saying where and never repeating it (as a Flow already is). Found by the new guard test/references-not-values.test.js (R031-72): shipped kits, the app catalog, module manifests and skills are scanned for values, and on a real daemon a key sent through a Flow, a skill and a Kit proposal is refused and is in no file of the home. Both new guards (that and test/reach-person-split.test.js) are in preflight's GUARDS.
- feat(vault): "Used by" on every credential (R031-70). `vault.used-by { item }` lists everything that uses it in one answer: the modules and watchers it was granted to, the Connections that hold it, the agents it was lent to, the sites Publish granted it (kernel grants), the apps made with it, the Flows that name it (`flows.connections`, asked as the person) and the records it is linked to, each with `renews` (what a new value does to it) and `restarts`. Names, kinds and times only. When a key changes in the Vault, Publish now starts every Production server that holds it for runtime again (once per burst; event `deployment.restarted`), as appmods already does for an app. Tests: test/vault-used-by.test.js (real daemon), core/publish/publish.test.js.
- feat(runner): Vyre's tools reach a chat on a Mac (lent-spawn v1.2). The lender runs Vyre's own MCP server beside Claude, with a door in the sandbox (a unix socket, `VYRE_SOCKET`) that asks the Space's home for each tool call (`lent.http`, `POST /v1/tools/<name>` and `GET /v1/tools` only), and the home answers it on the chat's own session socket (`threadsock.lentRequest`): the same caller binding, kernel credential and refusals as on the box, so records, the Vault by reference, approvals, documents and tools_find have the same answers there. The SDK's in-process MCP servers are kept in the config the lender gets; the box's own are not sent. Tested on Linux through the real sandbox and a real daemon; the macOS socket rule runs in the runner-chaos workflow.
- feat(runner): the first chat on a Mac runs there the first time (contract lent-spawn v1.1). A new chat is placed when it is created (`runnerHost().placeNew`: a ready computer of the person's gets the row, none ready is the box and writes nothing, and a spawn that never started takes the row back). A computer set to lend itself to a Space beats for that Space from the moment the daemon starts or the lend is turned on, whether or not it ever ran a session there (`runnerHost().lentTo`), and waits on the home with a long call (`lent.wait`) so a chat is started in a second or two, not at the next heartbeat. - feat(publish): WebSockets from strangers reach a published server. The public gate carried an app host's requests but refused every upgrade that was not Headscale's. It now carries a `GET` with `Upgrade: websocket` on a running app's host to the apps' front as bytes both ways, with the real address and the spoofable headers dropped, under its own per-address budgets (60 a minute, 16 open, counted apart from Headscale's so a busy page cannot starve the control channel). The front lets a stranger's socket through only to an open server (one Publish made and the owner took live), with the visitor's own cookies and `Authorization` and never Vyre's; every other app still answers a socket only to the owner's ticket. A socket idles out after 10 minutes without a frame. - feat(publish): a site's server now runs on a server made by the Linux installer. Four root-side verbs in the Space helper (`box/vyre`: `pub-build`, `pub-up`, `pub-stop`, `pub-down`, each one line with a deployment id and nothing else). The daemon writes the build context, the settings and the granted secrets into a folder it owns; root takes it by rename, looks at it as root (plain files, no links, size caps), judges every setting by its own patterns and the daemon's rules (`core/appmods/host-pub.js` in the recorded image), builds with the pinned rootless BuildKit as an unprivileged container, tags the image itself, and records it. Starting is root's own compose file from root's record (linted, read-only root, one `/tmp`, one data volume, secrets by name from root's env file), walled with no door in (only answers to what the daemon asked), proved, and healthy before it counts as up; the walls are put back after an update. The daemon side: `lib/publish/server-folder.js`, the helper driver and the builder ask by deployment id. Tested on the helper rig (build, refusals, up, secrets, walls, stop/down, reattach), the daemon's side, and a real daemon with the helper driver; the proof on a real installer box is separate. Build-time secrets are not carried on this path.

- fix(flows): a short wait no longer sits out the Flows timer's last sleep. The host timer slept up to a minute and was not woken when a run started a wait due sooner, so a 3 second wait could finish 60 seconds late (and a retry backoff or a new schedule the same). The host checked the earlier question's approval in memory, which a restart loses, so the signed copy days later was refused; it now reads the answered question itself (done, approved, the riders it listed), which is kept (core/daemon/flows-host.js; test/flows-with-daemon.test.js stops and starts the server between the two sends).
- fix(publish): a deployment in a Space made with spaces.create can hold a secret. The grant Publish makes for a deployment's secret said the deployment's own Space in its address and its actor, so the kernel refused it ("publish may not make that grant") and every runtime or build secret in a created Space was stuck. The address and the actor now say the kernel's own Space, where the Vault and its credentials live (as Wink's grants do), so the Vault answers Publish on that grant and only on it. Test: test/publish-created-space-secret.test.js (real daemon, claimed name, created Space; failed first).

- feat(publish): an app with a server, from a Dockerfile (first slice; team/contracts/builder.md v2). A folder with a Dockerfile at its top is published as a running app: `build.image: "dockerfile"` (and `build.port`, else the Dockerfile's `EXPOSE`). Preview builds an image in a rootless BuildKit container (never a host process, only SETUID and SETGID kept for its user namespace, 2 GB, 15 minutes, the folder read as the static path reads it, `# syntax=` and bases outside official images and the `builder.from` registries refused); the plan the person says yes to names the server and that it has no way out; the yes runs it as an app module of its own through appmods (`appmods.publish.install` / `stop` / `remove`, Publish only, inside the held decision) on `<name>.<the server's name>.vyre.run`, with a read-only root, a `/data` volume, 512 MB, no capabilities, no webhook door and no way out. Its runtime secrets are the kernel grants Publish already makes: Publish writes them as files, appmods reads them into the container's environment. Visitors reach it on every route with their own cookies and nothing of Vyre's; its cookies keep to its own host. A version that does not start leaves the running one running; rollback starts the previous image; retire removes the app and keeps its data. Docker-direct servers only: a server that runs apps through the host helper says so and builds nothing. `lib/publish` gains a `runner` hook and `serves()`; the static edge compose leaves servers out. - feat(runner): a chat's agent process can run on a person's lent computer (lent spawn, contract lent-spawn v1). The home gives the Agent SDK a ChildProcess (`runnerHost().lentSpawn(space, ...)`, for `sandboxSpawn`) whose stdin, stdout and stderr ride one long-poll wire call, `lent.pipe`, to the lender's sandboxed `claude`: exactly once and in order (a chunk is kept and sent again until the other side says it has it), fenced by the epoch, never dropping output for a slow reader, and never sending the box's environment or paths to the lender. A Contact with no address, one that is not there, and a link to any other type are each said plainly and nothing is sent. With a Contact the Flow keeps no field on the record (the stage runs it once per entry); `submission_field` still asks for one. Now the class of the last answer (`auth`, `blocked`, `no_browser`) is kept with the light, `connectors.site.attention` lists the website Connections that wait for a person, and the approvals queue shows one quiet `signin` card each: "Sign in to <site> again" (on a box its first button opens the assistant's computer screen, `/u/glass/<agent>`), "<site> is checking the browser" with "I cleared it" for an account the governor stopped, and "No browser is signed in to <site>". - feat(flows): a later send can ride an earlier step's yes. A call step may say `with: "<earlier send step>"`: the question for the earlier step names both sends in plain words, one yes covers both, and the second goes out days later with no second question and nothing held at the Gate (a signing Flow costs one yes and sends two emails). Saving refuses a `with` that is not an earlier send on the same path (not across branches, not out of a loop or lane), a tool the earlier send's manifest `covers` does not name, or a step that is not a send; a no to the earlier step means the rider never goes. No kernel line: the question's task form lists the riders, the Flows host checks it, and each rider gets a receipt of its own (kernel/flows/rides.js, core/daemon/flows-host.js; `covers` now reaches the Flow catalog through registry.flowTools). - fix(tasks): Mark done and Yes/No on a Now card work on a real box. - fix(runner): a lent computer can get its lease in production (review rows 1 and 2). The home asks the computer to sign its lease request with the key listed for it, and that key lives in the app: the runner now puts the request on the computer's own approvals queue as a card (`approvals.lease-ask` and `lease-status`, the runner's alone; the card names the home and its one-use challenge, ends with it, and its proof goes only to the runner), the app signs exactly what the card shows, and the home checks the key. The lent home of a Space now exists as soon as anyone asks (after a restart the book of sessions lent before it is readable at once).

- feat(documents): a document nobody has signed is a quiet row in Needs you.
