The card carries no link and no signer code; it closes when the app stops listing the request. A box with no Documents app shows nothing and no warning. Contract: approvals v1.2. Tested on the mappers, the contract fixtures, Documents' tools, a real daemon's queue and `waiting.count`, and against the real DocuSeal image (`docuseal-live.test.js`).
- feat(documents): the link to a signed copy no longer expires by default. A client can open their signed contract from the email years later. The setting `documents.signed_link_days` (Settings, Documents; 0 is off, which is the default) gives new links an end after that many days, and a call that names `days` (1 to 3650) wins over it. The finished file is still behind a key only the server holds, never the signer's own address, and `documents.signed-link.revoke` ends every link made so far (the next link works). A link with no end is the same token with an end of `0` under the same HMAC, so an end cannot be added or removed by editing it. The signing Flow no longer fixes 30 days, and its email says "works for N days" only when there is an end. Tested with the clock moved 31 days and ten years on the real front.
- feat(app): Settings > Outside agents has New token, 30 more days: it keeps the agent for longer (`outside.token { id, days }`), giving again what it was given until the new end. Docs: using/outside-agents.
- fix(publish): one stranger could lock out every visitor of the public door. The tunnel end connects to the gate from loopback and dropped the visitor's address, so the gate and every listener behind it (webhooks, share links, the Vault MCP, the agents MCP, app hosts) counted all visitors as 127.0.0.1: one stranger spending a budget, or being blocked, shut the others out. The tunnel end now writes the address the relay saw in a PROXY protocol v2 header (`lib/publish/proxy.js`) before the TLS bytes; the public gate reads it from loopback peers only (a loopback connection with no header is as before, any other peer's bytes are never read as a header) and limits, blocks and forwards the visitor. A stream with no usable address is refused rather than sent as loopback. A connection that has not yet named a visitor is counted under its loopback address, so a silent peer still spends its own share. Tested against the real relay, tunnel end and gate with two source addresses (`test/contracts/ingress.test.js`), the gate alone over plain and TLS sockets, split headers, bad headers and an untrusted peer (`core/wink/control/gate.test.js`), and the header bytes (`lib/publish/tunnel.test.js`).
- feat(wink): the outside agents' MCP learns the public address with the other two. When the gate comes up on `<name>.vyre.run` it tells share links, the Vault MCP and now `outside.mcp.base`, so tokens made afterwards name the public `/agents-mcp` address (`core/wink/ingress-bases.js`).
- feat(vault): a Vault pass is one kind of outside agent (ext-agents contract v1.1). `vault.mcp.pass.list` and `vault.mcp.pass.revoke` admit the outside-agents module (so one list and one end cover passes and registered agents), and two module-only tools, `vault.mcp.agent.tools {agent}` and `vault.mcp.agent.call {agent, tool, arguments, source}`, serve the pass's own tools to an agent whose id is a pass (empty tools for an agent with none, nothing for an ended or expired pass). The pass door's rate and lock-out numbers now come from lib/token-door.js, the one copy. Also: a mailbox connection lists its address (the From address, else a username that is one) instead of the Vault item's name; a credential has one address spelling (`credentialUrn`, kernel/contracts) used by the lease gate, Publish's grants and the Vault; the mint handle refuses a literal `*` in a minted address [kernel +0]; who gave a deployment's secret is a field of the grant's source.
- fix(app): approving a Flow version says "Approve", not "Approve with Face ID" ("with your passkey" on the web). Approving a Flow is not one of the moments that ask for a device's proof, so the button named a check the box does not make. The plain-words walk now approves a draft Flow on each width and fails if the button names a biometric or the Flow cannot run afterwards (104 of 104 clean).
- fix(security): three more from the independent read. (1) The secret scan before a first push to GitHub fails closed (a folder git cannot check in time is "too large to check", never clean) and reads the history too, so a secret committed once and deleted later is found; the approval card names the folder. (2) `vault.links` is for people only and `vault.uses.for` for first-party modules only (a model or an added module could list which credentials exist and who used them). (3) The move of Wink's old grant rows makes no second grant after a stop in the middle. Tests: core/github/scan.test.js, core/wink/grants.test.js.
- feat(app): a person can start a project from a template in the app. The template page has **Start a project** (a name and a button) when a version is live; it makes the project through `work.start-project` and opens it. Before, only an assistant, @Engineer or a Flow could. The plain-words walk does it on both widths (apps/app/screens/templates, scripts/app-walk-plain.mjs; pictures in team/0.3.1/shots/templates).
- fix(app): a project started from a template shows its stage in the Projects list (a row of steps and the stage's name, and "1 Intake" in the heading) instead of a dash. The list read only a stage field; a template project keeps its stages in its pinned snapshot and its place in `template_stage` (apps/app/ui/tasks/template-stage.js, with its test).
- feat(appmods): a signer sees the firm's page, not the engine's. The engine's own logo and "powered by" links are hidden on signing pages by the stylesheet they already carry; the firm's name and colours (Brand) and the small open-source licence credit in the footer stay. Checked in a real browser at phone and laptop size (core/appmods/outside-signer.live.test.js).
- fix(publish): hardening after an independent security read. (1) Naming a folder as a deployment's source is the person's act; a model session is refused (before, "under Vyre's home" let it point a public site at the Vyre state and other members' files). (2) A write that is not about secrets never makes or ends a secret grant, so a stale copy of the record (a build that read it minutes ago) cannot bring back a secret the person took away; only granting, taking away and the start-up move do. (3) The plan lists what would go public (count, bytes, the first 30 names), so the one yes shows what leaves. (4) The folder builder opens each file without following a link and without waiting on a pipe, caps the left-out list at 100, and stops a build whose file holds a key-shaped string (GitHub, AWS, Slack, private key) with the file's name. (5) `publish.edge` reads a runtime secret for its own deployment (it was refused after the move to deployment grants). Tests: lib/publish/grants-kernel.test.js, lib/publish/index.test.js, lib/publish/folder-build.test.js.
- fix(runner): the second review. Daemon shutdown and a refused lease hand-over no longer tell the home the session was stopped (the home takes it after the lapse, as before); a failed start no longer forgets a row it had just moved to this computer (a resuming session goes back to the server) or one another start is using; a second computer's failed start no longer removes the credentials of a session running on the first (the book decides before anything is bound); the "sleep" freeze waits for the wake, and only on runners whose home is beating; a late heartbeat answer is believed; a hand-over whose flush or server answer hangs fails after twenty seconds instead of freezing the session for ever; thawing a reason nobody froze sends no signal; one Offer blip is not a reason to take a session; a take-over's late continuation clears only its own debt; a pid record that could not say when its process started is not obeyed (and macOS start times are read in UTC).
- fix(runner): the findings of an independent review of the lending code. A session that ends (the person stopped it, it finished, or it died) tells its home: the home forgets it, or takes a dead one at once with reason `crash`, instead of resuming it twenty seconds later as `offline`. One hand-over per session at a time, and a good heartbeat no longer wakes a session being handed over. A settings read that fails moves nothing (the last good value stands; with no settings module nothing is ever "switched off"). A session id belongs to the first person who used it for good, a session may not be named like a chat, and another of the person's computers cannot take a session that is running on one (it goes through the server). A lender's heartbeat is sent per Space with a timeout and a call that hangs counts as a miss and is given up; a Mac that wakes keeps its sessions frozen until its home has heard it. An Offer that no longer stands makes the server take the session. What the server owes a taken session survives a restart of the home and is carried on once. Starts of one session cannot race; a start that fails tells the home; freezing falls back to the group when the system lists nothing; stopping a frozen session ends its whole tree; a pid file of a reused pid is not obeyed on macOS; a release the home refuses fences the lender; an upload cannot claim more chunks than a file can have. A move to the server asked of a lending computer's own `runner.move { thread }` is done there. The Gate treats a repeated ask as one only inside a chat.
- fix(runner): an idle computer does nothing on the heartbeat (no settings read, no power query every few seconds), and a lender with more than a hundred sessions names them in several heartbeats so none is missed and taken by the server.
- fix(appmods): a signer who clicks Decline was refused, and Vyre never heard of a decline. (1) Signing pages carried `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; with that policy a browser posts the app's own forms with `Origin: null` and the app answered 422 "You're not allowed to access this page". It is now `same-origin`: the signing link in the address still never goes to another site. (2) The webhook the app is set up with asked for completed signatures only, so `documents.declined` (and `documents.expired`) could never arrive; it now asks for form.declined and submission.expired too (a fresh install; an existing install gets them when its setup runs again). Proved in a real browser through the public door: the signer declines with a reason, the app records it, Vyre emits documents.declined (core/appmods/outside-signer.live.test.js).
- fix(appmods): a signer is no longer shown a Download button that cannot work. The signing page offers one before and after signing; its file is not behind the signer's link (the signed copy comes by its own expiring link, e-mailed), so the button led to a refusal. The stylesheet every signer page already carries hides it (checked in the real browser, core/appmods/outside-signer.live.test.js).
- feat(app): Settings > Outside agents can give an agent one project's memory or files by typing the project's name. The changes sheet of a turn can be drawn open, for the sample-world pictures (`shots-attach`, `shots-outside`, `scripts/state-shots.mjs`). Docs: using/outside-agents.
- fix(appmods): an outside signer's signature was thrown away. A browser submits the signing form with `POST /s/<slug>` (`_method=put`), but the Documents app's public routes allowed only GET, HEAD, PUT and PATCH there, so the box answered 404 while the page told the signer "Document has been signed!" and the app recorded nothing. Found by driving a real browser through the public door (relay, TLS on the box, the apps' front, the real signing app): it types a signature, completes, and the app now shows the submission completed, with the open-source credit on the page and no refused request (core/appmods/outside-signer.live.test.js, VYRE_APPMODS_LIVE=1 with CHROME_BIN).
- fix(app): a project template is no longer a table of records (its JSON body showed on the tag page and could on any Records list): `project-template` is a hidden type like the Flow bookkeeping types (apps/app/ui/views/logic.js isHiddenType). The Flow page names a run by when it started, not by its id. The plain-words walk now covers 50 screens at a wide and a phone width, with one action on the Flow and project pages (100 of 100 clean).
- fix(documents): the signing Flow never saw the signature. It waited on `documents.signed` and matched the submission with `event.data.submission`, but a module's event reaches a wait as the log carries it, with its facts under `event.data.payload` (the Flow tests had sent a bare payload), so every matter would have waited out its 30 days. Proved with the real signing engine and a real mail account, end to end (R032-05): the matter enters the stage, one yes sends the request and the signer's e-mail, the signer signs, the matter moves to Signed, a second yes e-mails the signed copy and its link opens the PDF (core/appmods/docuseal-live.test.js, VYRE_APPMODS_LIVE=1).
- fix(runner): a reader killed at its deadline, and a session that must be ended, take their whole process tree with them. The sandbox starts a program through a second process of its own; ending only the first (the one Vyre started), at the instant it was started, left the second running and holding the pipes. That made `core/runner/hardening.test.js` hang about one run in six, which stopped the merge queue for any change under core/runner, and could leave a sandbox running after a runner ended a session. A reader that has finished is ended after two seconds.
- feat(approvals): every waiting card from `approvals.items` carries `presence { required, covered, since }` for the device that asked: whether answering takes a proof (a yes, a draft that sends, access to a secret), and whether that device already has a live presence session, so the phone's swipe answers at once on a covered device and opens the card on any other. The `waiting` lists carry it through.
- feat(relay): a page in a native WebView reaches the box's screen stream through the app's relay channel (`relay/client/wsbridge.js`, R031-88 on a phone). `webviewShim()` replaces the page's WebSocket with one that talks to the app; `createWsBridge` opens the stream on the channel (`connection.socket`), keeps only the path and ticket of the page's URL, allows only Glass's screen stream, holds at most two sockets and refuses a message too big for one relay frame.
- test(runner): a chaos suite for a lent computer (`scripts/runner-chaos.mjs`, workflow `runner-chaos`, hosted Linux and macOS): kill -9, sleep, short and long network outages, lease expiry, clock skew both ways and the Mac's sleep notice, against a real runner, sandbox, encrypted workspace and home. It asserts no turn is lost or repeated, the server resumes from the last whole turn, a woken computer writes nothing and a workspace is closed before "locked" is said. It found and fixed four things below.
- fix(runner): a session is frozen, thawed and measured by its whole process tree, not its group: the sandbox gives the agent a session of its own, so signalling the group of the process Vyre started missed it (Pause all, the offline freeze and the usage numbers were wrong on Linux). A fence that arrives twice ends the session once.
- fix(runner): a watchdog that sees its runner gone ends that Space's sessions before it closes their workspace. On macOS the sandboxed agent used to outlive a killed runner.
- fix(remote): a lender's heartbeat has a rate window of its own, so a burst of file writes (300 calls a minute is the limit) cannot make a live computer look dead and lose its sessions to the server.
- fix(app): @Engineer's "Waiting for you" no longer lists every Flow by its id: a Flow waits for approval only while no version of it is approved, and it is called by its label (assistant-model.ts shared the Flows screens' two questions in real-model.js). scripts/app-walk-plain.mjs is a new check that opens about 40 screens on a seeded box and fails on a blank page, a page error, or ids and references where words belong (37 of 37 clean after this).
- fix(app): the template studio and a project's stages say who does a task as a person would ("The attorney may move it early", "The researcher, checked by the attorney") instead of `role:attorney` (apps/app/screens/templates/model.ts whoWords). scripts/app-walk-timeline-shots.mjs takes the project timeline with a Flow's run on it (team/0.3.1/shots/timeline).
- fix(mail): a held e-mail from an IMAP/SMTP account could never be sent. When the Gate released it, mail asked the Vault for the account and read the answer one level too shallow (the Vault wraps it as { connection }), found no adapter and refused: "sends through its own module, not mail.release". The mail tests had stood in for the Vault with the unwrapped row. Proved from the connect in the Vault's catalog to a message on a mail server, on one yes from comms.send (test/gif-story.test.js).
- feat(app): the Flow canvas draws a parallel the way it is read. Its lanes sit side by side from the same row, each in its own columns, and the step after it is drawn as the join: a dashed edge from the end of every lane, and the words "When all are done". Parallel, branch and sub-flow have their own icons (columns, list, flows). The phone's list keeps the kernel's order and the same words. A gallery picture (flow-parallel) and a test against the kernel's own graph() keep it.
- fix(github): `github.repo.create` is the person's own act and no module's. The Publish module was named as a caller in the first cut, but the tool is person-only and the registry refused module callers anyway, so the claim that Publish could ask for it was wrong; the dead path (a module's folder check) is gone and the tool's callers are the person's surfaces. The person asks for the repo, with their one yes, and gives the folder.
- feat(publish): a folder of ready files can be published (R032-06, R032-07). A new `builder` module answers Publish's `builder.build` for a deployment whose source kind is `folder` and has no build command: it reads the folder as it is on disk (no link is followed, `.git`, `node_modules` and secret-looking files are left out and named, 2,000 files and 50 MB at most), makes a stable `sha256:` digest and returns a static runtime; a repo, a Drive folder or a build command is refused in words that name the missing container builder. A person may name any folder; a model only one under Vyre's home. `publish.go` approves a previewed version and puts it live on one decision (the plan the person decides on is the public one, both steps are stored together), and `publish.quick {name, folder}` builds, previews and holds that one yes. Tests: lib/publish/folder-build.test.js, core/builder/builder.test.js, lib/publish/index.test.js, core/publish/publish.test.js (the real builder). Docs: docs/using/publish.md.
- fix(comms): texts could not be sent. The send asked the Vault to make the Twilio call, but the Vault only does that for an API credential it is configured for (a plain API key is refused: "twilio is not an api-credential"), and a write it makes would have been held at the Gate a second time. Comms now takes the person's own Vault item for its Twilio need (comms-twilio: its auth token, or an API key's secret with its id in `sid`), connected from the Vault's Connections like any other provider (Twilio is now in the catalog; before, connecting it said the provider was not in the catalog), for the one send, as the mail module takes a mailbox password, and calls Twilio through the guarded client (lib/http.js, public https only, no retry of a POST). With no item the message says to connect Twilio for Comms (the tests had stood in for the Vault).
- fix(comms): texts could not be sent. The send asked the Vault to make the Twilio call, but the Vault only does that for an API credential it is configured for (a plain API key is refused: "twilio is not an api-credential"), and a write it makes would have been held at the Gate a second time. Comms now takes the person's own Vault item named twilio (its auth token, or an API key's secret with its id in `sid`) for the one send, as the mail module takes a mailbox password, and calls Twilio through the guarded client (lib/http.js, public https only, no retry of a POST). No item is a plain "add an API key named twilio" message (the tests had stood in for the Vault).
- fix(app): the Flow page opened on a real box no longer goes blank, and the Flows screens speak plainly. The page crashed on any Flow with a compile warning (every Flow without declared powers: it drew the kernel's { path, message } as text); the list and the page marked every Flow "Waiting for you" (they compared the Flow's status with "approved", a word the box never sends; now a Flow waits only while no version of it is approved); both showed the Flow's id as its title (now its label); a lane's runs no longer fill the run history; the canvas names a lane by its own word and a person as "a person" (or their name when the catalog has it), not as an id. Pictures in team/0.3.1/shots/flows/{before,after}; scripts/app-walk-flows-shots.mjs takes them; apps/app/screens/flows/real-model.js holds the questions the screens ask, with real-model.test.js.
- fix(app): the project timeline's day headings read through lib/time like every other screen (apps/app/screens/projects/days.js; the pane formatted dates by hand, which apps/app/src/time/show.test.js refuses, so CI was red). Headings read "Thursday, 1 October" as elsewhere; apps/app/screens/projects/days.test.js holds the zone and the year.
- feat(site-ops): a learned website operation can read a web page, not only JSON. `chrome_op learn` takes `page` (the text of the first row, one piece per field); Vyre finds the repeated structure (lib/siteops/htmlread.js, with its own forgiving HTML reader and selector subset in htmlparse.js, no new dependency), keeps it as the operation's recipe, proves it reads the example back, and every run on any rung (your Chrome, the box's, a plain fetch) reads the rows the same way. A page that says "no results" is an empty answer; a page whose structure changed is a drift to repair.
- feat(documents): a tip for your own address for signing pages, shown the first time you use Documents' signing as a power user: ask your assistant for `sign.yourfirm.com` and add the two DNS records it names.
- fix(documents): a generated document is now filed as a Document record on the real Documents type (R032-03). It was written with the client and project as bare strings and a status the Kit's type does not have, so on a Space with the Documents Kit the filing failed after the file was already in the Drive (the tests ran against a stand-in type). The row is now built from the Space's own type (core/documents/record.js): links hold { urn } (a project given by name is looked up), a choice takes only its options, unknown fields are dropped. Proved in a real vyred with the Kit's own type, and the document shows on the client's and the project's timeline (core/documents/timeline.test.js).
- test(relay): the edge's Caddy is rehearsed as written (relay/deploy/rehearse-caddy.sh): against a test certificate authority it gets a certificate for edge.vyre.run by HTTP-01 while the relay owns 443, serves the boxes' WebSocket control link on 8443 through to the relay, and leaves port 80 to the relay's redirect.
- feat(vault): a credential linked to a record or a project (R031-71). `vault.link` and `vault.unlink` (people only) tie a vault item to a record's address, `vault.links` lists them both ways and `vault.uses.for` answers the recent uses of the items linked to one record as plain lines (which item, when, by whom). `work.timeline` shows them as "portal-login was used to sign in by the agent kit" to anyone who can read the record; the login is on no record, link or timeline. A link is the record's own `credentials` link field (holding `vyre://<space>/credential/<name>`, the one `credentialUrn` address), not a table of the Vault's; Projects carry the field, other types add it where it is wanted. A link grants nothing; a deleted item drops out of every answer. Kernel: a link with no target type may be a list and may hold a Vault login by its address (one line in the records gateway). The work module asks `vault.uses.for` as the person looking (`work` may relay it). Two events: `vault.linked`, `vault.unlinked`. Tests: core/vault/links.test.js and, on a real daemon, test/vault-links-timeline.test.js. Docs: docs/using/vault.md.
- feat(documents): a signer who declines is no longer silent. The signing app's decline becomes the event `documents.declined` (submission, signer, document, the reason they gave), and the Documents Kit (version 2, applied to an installed Kit on upgrade) ships a Flow that files the Document as Declined on the signer's Contact, so the refusal is on their timeline at once instead of after the wait for the signature runs out.
- feat(ingress): your own domain for an app's public pages, `sign.yourfirm.com` for signing (R032-02 "or your own domain"; contract v2). `appmods.domain.add { host, app? }`, `.remove`, `.list` (owner or admin; two DNS records, the second is the proof of control and what the certificate needs). The directory lists the host for the name that owns the `_acme-challenge` CNAME (`POST|DELETE /v1/names/hosts`, `hosts` on `names/mine`, resolved for the relay like a name), the public gate orders and serves the host's own certificate by SNI, the tunnel end serves only hosts the apps module lists, the apps' front maps the host to its app, and signing links use the domain once it is live. The relay is unchanged. Docs: docs/using/documents.md; ADR 0053.
- fix(app): no command lines on screens (the copy sweep, FOUNDATION 4.3). Connections asks "Give access" with a button (vault.grant, one yes) where it printed `vyre vault grant`, and points the Google OAuth client at the Vault's Import instead of `vyre vault put`. Settings, This computer turns the webhook listener on and off, opens a route (a sheet: name, signed by, header, the Vault item) and closes one with buttons, where it printed `vyre hooks ...`. Pairing, Autofill and Glass say where to go in Vyre instead of a terminal. The design checker's command-line rule keeps them out.
- fix(flows): a run held at the Space's switch (or by a Flow's run limit) can be stopped before it starts (`flows.cancel`), so what it would have done never happens when the switch is released; stopping a parent stops its held lanes.
- fix(flows): a failed lane is one row in Needs attention (the parent's, which names the lane and why, and whose Retry sends the failed lanes round again), and a Flow's health line counts a run with lanes once, not once per lane.
- feat(documents,comms): Documents and Comms teach themselves (tips): send a template for signature with one yes, make a matter sign itself from a stage, and text a client from your own number.
- feat(relay): the public door opens and shuts at once. `relay.tunnel_url` is a live setting: set the edge's address and the box dials it, clear it and the box hangs up, with no restart (core/relay/tunnel.test.js).
- feat(app): the Vault's shared-vault buttons work (R031-76, contracts/vault.md v1). New shared vault, Invite (a role and a code to send), Manage (make admin, member or read only, take out of the vault), Change the keys, and Accept a share (a vault invite or a pass, told apart by how it starts) call vault.vaults.create and rotate, vault.members.invite, role, remove and accept, and vault.pass.accept, each with the person's one yes through the app's own call. Taking someone out names what to replace. Only an admin sees the buttons.
- refactor(app): Settings home is one list block (R031-58). Its groups, icons, descriptions and the devices count are data a screen draws through BlockScreen; each row opens its page; the Mac's "make this Mac a server" card sits in the block's `after:Devices` slot. Same pixels as before (before and after pictures in team/0.3.1/shots/design/settings-blocks). test/key-screens.test.js counts settings/index.tsx as drawn from blocks.
- fix(app): Settings gives every place its own icon (a download arrow stood for Spending limits, Backups and Updates; a link for Connections and Outside agents; a shield for four). logic.test.js keeps them unique and in the family.
- fix(app): an owner or doer the kernel knows only by its id (per_l47gpa4r2zy6cn6jmyzi5r...) reads as "You" for the signed-in person and "Someone" for another, in the Projects table and every actor cell, never as the id. The records store names unnamed actors; the actor cell says "You" for its own person.
- fix(app): Spaces and members adds a space from a button that says Add a space, not a lone plus.
- fix(app): the Chat page shows the chats a person has even when something is missing on this device (a Mac with no phone to approve). The gap is a banner above the list now; it fills the page only when there are no chats. chats-model `chatsView` decides.
- feat(blocks): the `list` block draws every field its spec declares. A row's `icon` is a tile before the title (a module names a system symbol, "gear" or "creditcard", and the app draws its own family's icon through ui/blocks/symbols.js; symbols.test.js fails when the module list grows a name the table lacks), rows with a `group` are one card per group, and `density: "tight"` is the settings density (dense rows, a chevron where a row opens, the accessory as a plain state). A new gallery picture, `grouped`, is Settings home as one list block.
- feat(github): a connected account makes a new repo for a folder and sends it as the first commit (R032-06, the GitHub part). `github.owners` lists the account and its organisations; `github.repo.create` makes the repo under either, private unless public is asked, after scanning the folder for secrets (nothing is made on GitHub for a folder that would be refused; `.env`, keys and the like stay out of the first commit). It is an outward act (the person's one yes). The push is the same isolated one as `github.session.push` (the token only reaches git through askpass). Tests: core/github/repo-create.test.js (GitHub's API and the remote are stand-ins). Docs: docs/using/connectors.md.
- feat(ingress): your own domain for an app's public pages, `sign.yourfirm.com` for signing (R032-02 "or your own domain"; contract v2). `appmods.domain.add { host, app? }`, `.remove`, `.list` (owner or admin; two DNS records, the second is the proof of control and what the certificate needs). The directory lists the host for the name that owns the `_acme-challenge` CNAME (`POST|DELETE /v1/names/hosts`, `hosts` on `names/mine`, resolved for the relay like a name), the public gate orders and serves the host's own certificate by SNI, the tunnel end serves only hosts the apps module lists, the apps' front maps the host to its app, and signing links use the domain once it is live. The relay is unchanged. Docs: docs/using/documents.md; ADR 0053.
- fix(flows): a once-a-minute schedule with business hours no longer takes half a minute to find its next time. A cron time outside the hours jumps straight to when the window opens (kernel/flows/schedule.js) instead of being walked a minute at a time through the night (37 s measured, 30 ms now).
- feat(flows): the cheat sheet says what lanes, sub-flows and the schedule keys mean, and the policy keys every step takes are said once instead of on every line (1,675 to 1,653 tokens with the new section), so an agent reads less each time it writes a Flow.
- test(relay): the box's end of the public door in a real vyred (core/relay/tunnel.test.js): with an edge address set and a claimed name the daemon dials the edge by itself, relay.status says it is connected, and the edge hands it a visitor for a host the directory says it serves; with no address it dials nothing.
- fix(documents,comms,mail): one yes reaches a Gmail or MCP mail account too. The sends documents.send, documents.send-signed and comms.send file go mail.send -> google.mail.send (a Gmail account) or mcp.call (an MCP account) -> the Gate, and the card named only the first two hops, so for a firm on Gmail the Gate held the e-mail again. The cards now name those hops in `covers` (documents.send and documents.send-signed list four, comms.send three, a card for mail.send itself two).
- fix(relay): the edge relay served nobody. It read the directory's answer to a host lookup as `{ route }` but the directory wraps every answer as `{ data: { route } }`, so every public host looked unknown and every visitor was closed (the in-process tests used a stand-in lookup of their own shape, which is why nothing caught it). The container rehearsal now runs against the Worker's own code (relay/node/directory.js with the box's name published through the tunnel by its signed call, and the support switch over HTTP), restarts the edge and checks the box reconnects by itself (relay/deploy/edge.live.test.js).
- fix(site-ops): a learned read that drifted on the assistant's own Chrome on the box is now repaired there, as it already was on your Mac: `chrome.op.run` relearns it from what the page sends when its trigger runs (the full answers are captured over CDP), keeps the repair as a new version only after a replay answers, and tries once in ten minutes per operation; otherwise it says "teach it again". Writes are never replayed to prove a repair.
- feat(chat): files in a message, end to end (R031-53). New module `attachments` (`attachments.put`, `attachments.list`): a file the person picks, pastes or drops is kept once, sealed, in the chat's own folder as `<id>-<name>`, and a message names it with `stream.send { attachments: [{ id, name, mime, bytes }] }`. The stream reads the files and the record the person named under the sender's own chain and tells each assistant only what it needs: an image rides inline with the words (every provider's adapter already turns `images` into its own form), any other file is written 0600 to `<session folder>/.vyre/attachments/<id>-<name>` and named in one sentence. A bad list refuses the whole send first; the chat shows the person's words and the file names. The composer has Attach a file and Attach a photo, a chip row, browser paste and drop; limits are five files, 5 MB an image, 8 MB a file, 20 MB a message. The context cards (R031-00t) now also reach the assistants through the chat, and move to lib/record-cards.js. Contract: team/contracts/attachments.md v1.1.
- fix(flows): outside content read in a lane or a sub-flow taints the run that started it (kernel/flows/joins.js). Before, a lane that read from outside could hand its data to a step after the join that sent mail without the Ask a tainted run needs. kernel/flows/joins.test.js holds both cases.
- fix(appmods,views): the Documents screen's Send for signature now sends. It made the signing request with no e-mail from the signing app and then told no one, so the signer never got a link. The form now calls `documents.send` (the request and the e-mail with its link, one act). A person's confirmed preview in any view is the Gate's yes for the send the tool files, as a Flow's answer is: the views and capsule modules pass the fresh, hash-bound confirmation to the registry under a symbol key, which records a receipt (`approvals.receipt`) and marks the call like a redeemed card, so nothing waits at the Gate after the person confirmed the words (test/gif-story.test.js). A first-party module's views may now call tools it lists in needs.tools (appmods lists `documents.send`).
- fix(app): a to-do that belongs to no stage and no record on Now says "It is waiting for you." instead of "Due with ." (apps/app/ui/tasks/model.js); scripts/app-walk-now-shots.mjs takes the Now pictures (the vault health card, the work waiting on the owner) at 1440 and 390, light and dark, on a test box.
- feat(app): the live screen on the phone. Glass's screen page runs in a WebView (the same page and messages as the browser's iframe, plus a marked host message and `ReactNativeWebView` in src/glass/frame.js, as the terminal's page does), so the live card in a chat and the Glass screen show a computer's screen, take over, sign in privately and hand back on iPhone and Android where the phone reaches the server directly. Away from the server (relay only) it says so; the stream over the relay is not built yet. The surface id works without localStorage. Not yet proven on a device.
- feat(chat): Undo per file in the turn's changes (R031-53). `threads.undo-edit { thread, path }` (a person's surface only) puts one file the session edited or wrote back as it was before the latest turn that touched it, and removes a file the turn created; it works for any provider whose tool events say a file was edited, because it keeps the file before the call and its fingerprint after. It refuses when the file no longer holds the turn's result (nothing of the person's is overwritten), outside the session's folder, for a file too large to keep or after a restart, and the session is told on its next turn. The changes sheet has an Undo on each file. New core/switchboard/edits.js, event `thread.edit-undone`.
- feat(publish): Publish uses the Vault's grants (R032-11). A deployment's secret is released to Publish on the deployment's own kernel grant (`vault.run` on the credential, made by Publish for the deployment's service actor), not on a grant to the Publish module: `vault.release` takes `deployment` for module:publish, and a call that names no deployment, or one with no live grant, gets "not granted to this deployment". One Deepgram key serves two deployments and the chat's transcripts, each on its own grant; ending one leaves the others; deleting the credential ends every deployment's use of it. The kernel's vault-made filter also counts `publish:secret:` grants so the Vault can see and take them back (no new kernel lines). Test: test/publish-vault-grants.test.js. Docs: docs/using/vault.md.
- fix(operations): the descriptions of `comms.send`, `computer.use`, `computer.targets`, `documents.template.add`, `documents.generate`, `documents.signed-link` and `vault.agent.fill` fit the 25-word cap (the detail is in docs/using/documents.md and computer.md), and `documents.generate` declares `projectArg` so an agent can file only under a project it is granted.
- fix(flows,gate): a Flow's yes is the Gate's yes. A Flow call step to an outward tool asked twice: the person approved the Flow's own question, then the send the tool filed was held at the Gate for a second yes (proved on a real daemon). The Flows host now hands the task it just spent to the registry (`callFlow`), which records a receipt with the approvals queue (`approvals.receipt`, registry only) and marks the call as a redeemed card does, so the send the tool files, down the hops it names in `covers`, goes out once and nothing waits at the Gate. A second send in the same act, a send behind a hop the tool does not name, and a forged mark are held as before (test/gif-story.test.js).
- feat(app): the Vault reads as words (R031-76): a name is shown as a person writes it ("Airline account" for Airline-account), a site as its host, a field as words ("One-time code", not totp), and each kind of item has its own icon in the list (a site, a key, a card, a terminal).
- fix(app): the run-on-my-computer screens call the runner by the contract's tool names (`runner.why-not`, `runner.pause-all`, `runner.resume-all`; they asked for camel-case names that do not exist, so Pause all and the why line did nothing). A test builds the chip, the moved line, Settings and the list from the producer's fixtures, so a drift in either side fails.
- feat(runner): sessions on a person's computer move to the server by themselves, with the reason the chat prints (R031-95 2.4). The Mac app's sleep notice (`link.sleep`, `link.wake`, new tools of the link module) hands every session over before the lid shuts (`lid-closed` or `asleep`); switching running here off in Settings (`switched-off`), going on battery with "only while plugged in" (`unplugged`) and a processor or memory limit passed for a minute (`cpu-cap`, `mem-cap`, the heaviest session first) do the same. A computer that cannot reach the Space's server freezes its sessions after two missed beats instead of running ahead; a lease that ends hands them over first (`lease-expired`). A move is frozen, flushed to the last whole turn, told to the server and only then ended; a server that holds the move back leaves the session running. The Gate now treats the same ask while it still waits as the same item, so a turn re-run after a move shows one draft.
- fix(approvals): a held outward call had an empty title in the waiting list (its digest looked like a secret); it reads "An assistant (kit) wants to run mail.send".
- refactor(app): one Vault screen. "Open the Vault" on a stuck task opened the older phone-first Vault list (/vault), a second screen beside /u/vault with its own state; it now opens the Vault, and the older routes (app/vault, src/vault/views, src/state/vault) are gone. One mechanism per job.
- feat(chat): context cards (R031-00t). When the person's own words name a record exactly (its whole title, unique among the records their chain may read), the model hears a short card of it (at most 800 characters, six key fields, values cut, a sealed field only as its placeholder) beside the words, once per record per 20 turns in a thread, so it need not fetch what was just named. Strict by design: two records of one name, a part of a name, pasted text or code, a service or assistant chain, or the new setting `threads.cards` off give no card. The transcript keeps only the person's words. New `core/switchboard/record-cards.js` and `lib/record-types.js` (the one list of the kernel's own bookkeeping types, now shared with records.types).
- feat(app): the chip, line and Settings read contracts/runner.md as written (design). A session pinned to the server or to this Mac offers no move and says it is kept there; the sessions-here list shows the box's own second line and accessory (`runner.here` `line`, `cpu`), so Settings and the Lumen list read the same; runner-model.test.js runs every placement, call and event the contract fixtures hold through the chip, the moved line and the list.
- feat(runner): where a session runs is one record at the Space's server, the placement book (R031-95 2.4, 2.5). A lent session has an epoch that rises at every change of place and every write names it, so a computer that was paused and wakes after the server took its session writes nothing. The computer's heartbeat (`lent.beat`, every 5 seconds) carries its sessions and answers what the server wants done; `lent.release` hands a session over after the last checkpoint. A computer silent for 20 seconds loses its sessions to the server (`offline`); a move the computer's own condition asked for waits out a two-minute cooldown. The book survives a restart of the server. New tools `runner.placement`, `runner.why-not`, `runner.here`, `runner.settings`, `runner.settings.set`, `runner.pause-all`, `runner.resume-all`; `runner.move { thread, to }` moves a chat's session; event `thread.moved`; the limits are the module's settings. Contract: team/contracts/runner.md.
- test(design): the design checker (R031-58). apps/app/scripts/check-design-rules.mjs counts colour literals, hand-set fonts, StyleSheets and imports of the second set of primitives (src/ui) in the app's screens; design-rules.baseline.json holds what is there today (38 lines in 24 files); test/design-rules.test.js is a guard, so a screen may go down and never up, and a new screen starts clean. Run `node apps/app/scripts/check-design-rules.mjs --update` after fixing one to lower it.
- test(design): the design checker (R031-58). apps/app/scripts/check-design-rules.mjs counts colour literals, hand-set fonts, StyleSheets and imports of the second set of primitives (src/ui) in the app's screens; design-rules.baseline.json holds what is there today (44 lines in 26 files); test/design-rules.test.js is a guard, so a screen may go down and never up, and a new screen starts clean. Run `node apps/app/scripts/check-design-rules.mjs --update` after fixing one to lower it. A fifth rule keeps command lines (`vyre vault pair`) out of strings a person reads: do it with a button, never ask for a terminal.
- feat(app): the Flow canvas draws parallel lanes, branches and sub-flows (design-language, for projects-flows' graph). A parallel step's lanes read "At the same time", and the three kinds get their own icons instead of the fallback. A kind the canvas does not know still draws, with the default icon and no words.
- feat(outside): Vyre as the home base of outside agents (R032-13). New module `outside` and MCP address `/agents-mcp`: a person registers an agent (Dots, Muse, Hermes, ChatGPT, their own Claude Code elsewhere), gets a token once, and gives it reach (`outside.grant`: records by type, a project's memory, a project's files); it is a kernel actor of its own (`ext_<id>`, no person behind it, external) so the kernel decides every read, sealed fields come back as the word "[sealed]", a record or type it was not given is "not found for you", and every use is an `outside.used` event with names and addresses only. `records_create` and `records_update` never run directly: they file a Gate item ("Muse wants to add a client: Dana Reyes"), the person may edit it, and one yes makes exactly that change as the agent. `outside.revoke` ends the token, takes the grants back and declines what was waiting; bad tokens lock an address out (lib/token-door.js). Kernel: a chain facts case `outside` and the module port `needs.kernel.outside` (8 lines). `ext` is a caller kind that no registry tool admits. Docs: docs/using/outside-agents.md. Contract: team/contracts/ext-agents.md.
- feat(wink): the public gate carries a second MCP door, exactly `POST /agents-mcp` (JSON up to 64 KB, the Authorization header kept for that listener alone), for the outside agents' module (team/contracts/ext-agents.md). It reaches the loopback listener `outside.mcp.status` names, has its own per-source budget (the Vault MCP's is separate), and is the gate's plain 404 while that module is not there. Shapes are in the table of team/contracts/ingress.md; test/contracts/ingress.test.js carries them through the relay.
- feat(documents): Documents speaks on the log (every change has an event). `documents.generated` (path, format, template and version, the Document record), `documents.sent` (the submission and the template, never the signer's code) and `documents.copy-sent` (days) are declared under watches.emits, so the timeline, Needs you and Flows can follow a document from the template to the signed copy.
- feat(documents,appmods): sending for signature costs one yes, not four (one-yes for signing). `documents.send` makes the signing request (`appmods.signing.request`, module-only: the app is asked with its own key and told to send nothing) and emails the signer their link through Comms; `documents.send-signed` makes the 30-day link to the finished copy and emails it. Each names the sends it files in `covers` (comms.send, mail.send), so an agent's one approved card carries the whole act and no second card appears. The signing Flow now asks twice in all (the request with its link, the signed copy) instead of four times, and `documents.signing.flow` no longer takes `base` or `connection`. Tested: appmods.signing.request against a stand-in app, the covered ride through the real manifests, the Flow's two yeses (core/documents, core/appmods).
- feat(relay,names,wink): the public door for signers outside your network (R032-02). A box with `relay.tunnel_url` set publishes its name through the tunnel: the names directory points `<name>.vyre.run` and `*.<name>` at the operator's relay (never an address the box names) only for what the box declared, the relay reads one server name from a visitor's hello and asks the directory which box serves it (`GET /v1/tunnel/resolve`, shared secret), and the bytes go to the box over its own outbound link. TLS ends on the box with its own certificate, so the relay holds no certificate and reads nothing; the box end serves only its own names and only its own public gate, and an unlisted path is the same 404 as ever. `POST /v1/names/admin/suspend` stops a name (a new visitor is refused within a minute, an open stream closes at the next re-check). The relay container serves the front (`VYRE_TUNNEL_DIRECTORY`, `VYRE_RELAY_SECRET`), and the address of the edge is a setting (Settings, Devices: `relay.tunnel_url`) that the person or the assistant can change. The edge's deploy kit is relay/deploy (compose, Caddyfile, an outside check, a runbook, and a live rehearsal of the container). The contract is team/contracts/ingress.md; tested over real sockets (relay/node/ingress.e2e.test.js, test/contracts/ingress.test.js).
- feat(documents): PDF works with no setup on a server with Records, and the signed copy expires. (1) Gotenberg (MIT) is one more container of the space's unit (lib/spaces/home-unit.js): digest-pinned (8.37.0), the internal network only (no published port, no way out), read-only, all capabilities dropped, its chromium routes cut; vyred is told where it is (VYRE_DOCUMENTS_PDF), `documents.pdf` in config overrides. Without Records a PDF says "PDF needs the Records server" and the Word file is still made. Checked: the hardened container converts a filled .docx. (2) The signer's slug opens the signing page but no longer lists or downloads the finished file (`/s/<slug>/documents` and `/download` are off the public list); `documents.signed-link` (outward) makes a link on the app's host, `/signed/<token>`, under a key only the box holds, good for 30 days at most and gone after (the page says so and does not repeat the slug), opened with no ticket and no admin session; calling it again re-issues. The signing Flow makes one after the signature and emails it, both held for the person's yes. Tests: core/appmods/signing.test.js, the live DocuSeal run.
- feat(vault): the person's own devices write to shared vaults (contract team/contracts/vault.md v1). `vault.vaults.create`, `.rotate`, `.sync` and every `vault.members.*` tool admit `device:<id>`; invite, role change, removal and key rotation each take the person's one yes in the vault moment (`vault.vaults.rotate` joins that list, with plain card sentences for all four); a model session is refused every one. Three events: `vault.shared-created`, `vault.shared-joined`, `vault.member-role`. Fixtures and a contract test (test/contracts/vault.test.js) and a daemon test of a signed-in device (test/vault-device-writes.test.js). Also: three red presence cases in core/vault/presence.test.js are named (vault.agent.fill, tagged, untag, the two health tools for Now).
- feat(runner): a lease request is a hello the computer signs (R031-95 2.2). Where the home asks for it (default on in the daemon; `VYRE_SIGNED_LEASES_OFF=1` turns it off in a development build only; a release build ignores it), `leases.issue` carries `{ device, device_key, eid, cap, runner_version, protocol }`. The wire's challenge covers exactly those fields under the sealing process's `lease.issue`; the lender's presence key signs it and the sealing process checks it with the one verifier every yes goes through: a key of this person, listed for the computer the hello names (`wrong_device` otherwise), single use, the fields bound (a proof for another limit or protocol is `wrong_payload`). A request with no hello is told to sign and never gets a key; the answer "no" (no Offer, removed) needs no proof, so the lender's reinstate check still reads it. The home keeps what was signed (`leases.helloOf`), and the lender's runner sends its limit in it. New core/runner/protocol.js holds the runner's version and protocol.
- feat(runner): the lender's network limit is a floor (R031-95 2.3). The tightest limit ever signed on a member's acceptance of a computer, active or ended, stands until the member lends again with `loosen` under a proof that binds it: stopping a lend and lending again with no limit, or a looser one, is refused in plain words, and a lend that allows more than before always takes a fresh proof (the live-session resume path no longer covers it). `capOf` reads the floor, so the home limits a lent session by it even when no acceptance stands. The runner's `lent.start` carries its own `cap`, and the home applies the tightest of the Space's choice, the floor and the runner's cap (a runner can only ask for less). `spaces.devices.lend` takes `network_cap` and `loosen`. Tests CAP-4 to CAP-7 in core/runner/rv2-lender-cap.test.js.
- fix(chat): the guard reds on chat's own tools are closed. `ask.answer`, `ask.cancel` and the person-side `previews.*` tools are classified for an assistant (`previews.share` asks first), `previews.share` and `previews.reply` say why they are not outward, the two raw requests in previews are listed as local and browser, ask and previews use the one person-surface list (no bare `mobile`), `ask.many` and the `previews` tools that ran over the 25-word cap are short and the detail is in the new docs/using/previews.md, and ask and previews are in the agent brief's families (one sentence that teaches `previews.open` and `ask.many`).
- fix(chat): owed fixes from previews. `ask.many`, `previews.open`, `previews.operator`, `previews.step` and `previews.signin` are classified for a plain model session (own: a card in its own chat, nothing outward). Preview spreadsheets use SheetJS 0.20.3, from SheetJS's own release tarball, committed in `core/previews/vendor-src/` and installed by build.mjs only if it matches its pinned sha256 (npm stops at 0.18.5, which has known flaws). The preview card's type errors are gone.
- feat(app): the Vault pass against a real Vault (R031-76). One Add button (login, API key, secret, SSH key, bring in from another app) replaces three buttons; a quiet row says when something needs a look instead of a card with Fix; the kind tabs start on All; Passes and Shared become one Sharing page; Devices reads Browsers; no command line or tool name appears on screen. A name typed as "Juniper Drive" is saved as Juniper-Drive instead of being refused (the placeholder itself broke the box's name rule). Buttons whose feature is not built say "Coming in this release" through the one `comingSoon` helper in @vyre/ui. scripts/app-walk-vault-shots.mjs draws the Vault from a real vyred at 1280 and 390, light and dark.
- fix(ui): a Button or IconButton as a Menu trigger opens the menu on the web. Radix hands the trigger its pointer handlers, aria props and ref; Button and IconButton dropped them, so every menu on a Button (Add, Manage, Create or join a space, the memory and sidebar menus) did nothing in a browser or in the app's web view. Both now pass the rest on to their pressable; menu.test.js keeps it. Segmented with `fill` and four or more choices takes less side padding so it fits 390.
- feat(flows): try it on last week (R032-10). `flows.simulate` with a Flow id (or `against`) and `since` replays the real triggers of the window through the version and sets the result beside the Flow's real runs: how many were the same, which steps differ, what is new and what it would not run, in one line (kernel/flows/replay.js). `flows.propose` adds how many of the last week's real runs would have gone the same way; a run with lanes counts its lanes' steps; `flows.run` paints a lane's steps on the run's picture and lists the lanes.
- feat(flows): schedules know business hours, holidays and what to do after downtime (R032-09). A time trigger takes `hours` (true, or days, from, to), `holidays` (dates, month-days, or "space" for the new setting `flows.holidays`) and `catch_up` (once, all, skip). A cron time outside the window is skipped, an interval waits for the window to open, and tick(), nextWake(), the health line, the canvas and practice runs all read the one `nextFire` in kernel/flows/schedule.js (the practice run also reads the schedule in its zone now; it read UTC). An interval can name its zone when it has hours. kernel/flows/schedule.test.js.
- feat(flows): parallel lanes and sub-flows (R032-08). A `parallel` step holds two to eight `branch` lanes that run at the same time; the step after it starts when every lane is done, a lane that fails fails the step naming the lane, and a retry sends only the failed lane round again. A `subflow` step runs another active Flow by name, checked as a manual start is (`flows.run`), and reads back what that Flow's new `returns` says. Both are runs that start runs: the parent waits on `{ kind: "children" }` (kernel/flows/joins.js), so a lane can wait for a person and nothing in the ledger changed. Practice runs walk every lane. Schema, compile, canvas, lines, text, cheat sheet and describe know the new kinds; kernel/flows/joins.test.js.
- feat(backup): a backup carries the Drive of every Space on the box (R031-83). `space-drives/<space id>` holds each Space's files, still sealed under that Space's key, and a restore puts them back where the Space's Drive opens, so a fresh box shows the same documents after the Space bundle restores. test/space-bundle-restore.test.js backs up and restores a project file, a plain file and a team's file.
- fix(flows): a stage move says so once (R032). The test world wrote a second record.stage-entered next to the gateway's own, so a Flow started on a stage ran twice there; the shim is gone and kernel/flows/stage-entered-once.test.js holds the line.
- feat(flows): a run is about the record that started it (contract flow-runs, team/contracts/flow-runs.md). `flow-run` gains `record` (a link) and `title`; `flows.runs` rows carry `record` and `label`; a record's and a project's timeline lists its runs in plain words ("Welcome the client: done"). A home made earlier gets the two fields at its next start. kernel/flows/run-record.js; test/contracts/flow-runs.test.js.
- refactor(flows): the runner's small pure helpers move to kernel/flows/runner-util.js so runner.js stays under 2,000 lines.
- feat(grants): Wink's member, shared-computer and storage grants are kernel grants (one grant model, step c). Wink makes them through the kernel's `mint` handle (`needs.kernel.mints` in its manifest: `member.act` under `member/`, `node.host` under `node/`, `storage.hold` under `storage/`) and keeps no grant table: `wink.access` and `wink.remove` read and end the kernel's grants, a storage device's `grant_id` follows its grant, and the first call after the update carries the old tables' active rows over once (old device grants still become registry rows). A revoked grant is no longer listed (the log keeps it). The mints contract (team/contracts/mints.md) and the vault contract (team/contracts/vault.md) are written with fixtures and tests.
- test: one-mechanism C holds (R031-00c). It lists every table with `grant` in its name and why it is not a second model (legacy tables kept for their migrations, the vault's core home of release grants, one-time presence tokens, the tag grants of chat), and fails on a new one. All four "one mechanism" tests pass.
- fix(vault): a login lent to an agent stays in the agent vault. `grantedNames()` still read the older `vault_agent_grants` table, which the carry-over empties, so after the one grant model a lent login could be filed with the personal items; it now reads the kernel grants (`Access.items()`).
- feat(backup): every Space the box holds is bundled, each under its own owner's recovery code (R031-83). One bundle per Space in `space-bundles/` (a backup carries the folder): a hosted Space adds a consistent copy of its own store and its drive pool key. `vyre restore --recovery-code` (or a prompt per Space) brings back every Space whose owner gave a code and names the others. New Settings, Backups screen: "Space Harbor isn't backed up: its owner hasn't turned on backups.", with Turn on (only the owner can). `spaces.bundle.enrol` takes the Space; status lists every Space. Hosted Spaces restore through kernel/spaces (restore.json at open). A member's own device opens their chat's ring after a restore (test). Kernel base unchanged (0 net); the Drive's chunks themselves are the pool's own backup.
- feat(vault): Vault health on Now as one calm row (R031-80s). `vault.health.summary` counts what the daily Watchtower run found and the person has not fixed (to rotate, to fix; counts only, nothing decrypted); `vault.health.dismiss` hides it for a week. The one Needs-you queue gets a quiet `vault-health` owner (one row, Rotate / Fix / Dismiss), and Now shows the same as a card. Never a row per item; the Vault names each item.
- feat(backup): the Space comes back on a fresh box (R031-83, #108). A Space bundle (lib/space-bundle.js) carries the Space id, the grants and members as plain data and every sealed value sealed under a bundle key that only the owner's recovery code opens; no key of the old box is in it. The code is given once (spaces.bundle.enrol); after that the bundle is written unattended into the home, hourly, and `vyre backup` carries it (space-bundle.vyb). `vyre restore --recovery-code` puts the identity back, re-seals the values under the new box's own keys with the same references (kernel/seal space.dump and space.restore), and the kernel's first start adopts the grants under its new seal and logs space.restored with the old head. Kernel base +20 lines (grants state and adopt, the restore hook, the narrow bundle handle).
- test(eval): the Vyre-native eval (R031-17): five jobs given in plain words with no instruction to use a Vyre tool and a shell as the foreign way (keep a client fact, say what happened with a client, a Monday reminder, send mail, save a procedure). The agent gets only the real environment brief (core/sessions/environment.js built over the fixture's tools); the checkers score whether it reached for a record, the timeline, a Flow, a held send and a skill. Scripted agents prove the checkers; `run.js --suite native` runs any model's adapter live in the next paid round. work/memory-031 is superseded by the tip's environment, rollover and identity-home work.
- feat(learn): a procedure the person keeps repeating becomes a skill draft in the skills library (R031-44). When learn proposes a skill (clean in 3 sessions) it is also drafted for the install's owner, at the project level when it names a project, else the owner's own, so it takes the one approval path (one card, versioned, every AI session at its level). New module-only tool skills.draft.learned; library.draftFor. A draft only: approving stays the person's.
- feat(chat): Chat about this, link a chat to a record, one timeline (R031-39, 41, 46). chat-record gains `about` (a link to any record) and `shared`. New tools work.timeline (everything linked to a record or project, only what the caller may read; a chat shows only to its people until shared, then by title), work.chat.link, work.link.suggest. App: Chat about this on record and project pages, a Timeline tab on the project page, and "Link this chat to Northwind?" in a chat.
- test(eval): five @Engineer tasks are registered before any live run (R031-16): a probate template, an agent change, a Flow, a skill draft and a screen fix, each with a deterministic checker, in scripts/eval/assistant-fit/engineer.js. The checkers hold the Engineer to its contract: it reads first, checks a Flow before asking for it, only proposes, and never says a change is live while it waits for the card. Scripted Engineers prove the checkers (good one 100 of 100; each failure loses its task). `run.js --suite engineer` runs them live in the next paid round.
- feat(appmods): public signing pages (R032-02). The Documents app's host now answers a signer who has the link and no ticket, and only on the routes the manifest lists under `app.signing` (the signing page, its form posts, the signature upload, its assets and the page images; exact method and path, no dot segment, no encoded dot or slash; `/sign/<document>/<signer>` goes to the page). Such a request reaches the app as a stranger: never the install's admin session, only the signer's own cookies, whose answers go back to the signer and not into the admin jar; the body is capped at 20 MB. The page is dressed from the space's brand (`signingBrand`: the colour for buttons and links, a band with the logo and name, served as /__vyre/brand.css) and carries the app's credit in the footer, with no script added; the page is sent with no-referrer, noindex and no-store because the link is in the address. Everything not listed is a plain 404 as before. The list was taken from the app's routes and checked against a real browser on the pinned DocuSeal 3.3.1 (the live test also checks that the owner's pages and the API stay closed). Tests: core/appmods/signing.test.js, core/appmods/docuseal-live.test.js.
- feat(comms): Comms delivers (R032-04). `comms.send` sends an email through the person's mail account or a text through their own Twilio account (`comms.sms` in config.json; the key in the Vault), held at the Gate for their yes to the final words, one yes for a text to several numbers. A text is released by `comms.release` (the Gate only) through Twilio, one message per number, a number that fails is reported and the rest still go. A sent text is logged on the client whose number it went to, as an email is (core/daemon/sent-mail-log.js). `comms.send` is a Flow step (outward).
- feat(documents): signing from a stage (R032-05). `documents.signing.flow` returns a Flow definition: a record entering a stage asks Documents for a signature (no email from the signing engine), claims the record so it is sent once, emails the signer their link through Comms (held), waits for `documents.signed` and moves the record on. Tested end to end in the Flows world. Docs: docs/using/documents.md.
- feat(documents): Documents generates documents (R032-01) and files them (R032-03). A Word template is a file in the Space's Drive (Templates/<name>.docx; the Drive keeps every version); `documents.generate` fills its {placeholders} from values and from the fields of records named by reference ({client.name}), deterministically (the same input gives the same bytes), and a missing value, a blank one or a loop with no list stops the document and names every one of them: nothing is guessed. The result is filed in the Drive under Documents/<project>/ and, when the Space has a `document` record type, as a Document record linked to the client and the project with the template and its version. A PDF comes from Gotenberg when `documents.pdf` is set in config.json, and says so plainly when it is not. Tools: documents.template.add/list/get, documents.generate (a Flow step). New dependencies: docxtemplater and pizzip (MIT), because Word splits a placeholder across runs of text and nothing else here reads .docx; test/allowed-dependencies.json says so. Tests: core/documents.
- feat(app): a chat's Files panel (chat tools, Files): the files the chat made or received by name, a mark on the shared ones, Share to project / Unshare, and a preview for text and images. New tool work.file.list; work.file.share now refuses a person who is not in the chat. Screenshot walk: scripts/app-walk-chat-files-shots.mjs.
- feat(link): `chrome.op.call` is split. `chrome.op.call` runs a learned READ for the box and refuses any other kind, naming `chrome.op.send`. `chrome.op.send` runs an operation that submits (a change, send, spend or delete): `outward: true` with `asks: true`, only after the link verified the box's signed assertion for exactly that site, operation and inputs (assert.js, 60 s, once), which counts as the one yes, so there is no second prompt. The box sends each by its kind (core/connectors/site.js); a send without its approval, or a read with one, is refused on the box and again on the Mac. Tests: test/site-mac-rung.test.js.
- feat(computer): Vyre Computer (R031-90, R031-93), the 0.3.1 core. `computer.use` is one tool over the engines that exist (the cloud computer's Chrome and desktop, this Mac's Chrome and apps, a paired Mac through the link): computers by name ("my Mac", "the office computer"; nothing named is the cloud computer; two matches or none is a question with the real names, never a guess), and interface first, screen last (a Connection or learned operation that covers the site is offered once before the screen is touched; `screen: true` skips it). `computer.targets` lists the computers. A box asks a Mac through the link with `computer.call`, only from the computer module, only for a class the person allowed on that Mac (`link.computer.allow` look, act, files; off by default; `link.computer.revoke`, `link.computer.list`); the Mac runs it through its own engines as the link and an engine still holds a send. Files: find and bring a file from Downloads, Desktop or Documents only (lib/computer-files.js), 8 MB at most, in parts, saved in the agent's inbox on the box. The tool is `computer.use` because a tool is module.verb. The display name is Vyre Computer everywhere a person reads it; the package and extension names (`vyre-chrome`) stay until 0.3.2. Docs: docs/using/computer.md. Tests: core/computer, lib/computer-files.test.js, test/computer-mac-rung.test.js.
- feat(vault): `vault.agent.fill` (ADR 0028, decision 3) signs an agent in on its own computer with a login lent to it; the agent never reads the login. Lent means a kernel grant (`vault.agent.grant`) or a `#` tag the person typed in this conversation. computers.fill.begin shields the computer, the fill opens the lent origin in a fresh browser context, reads the page's origin on its own connection (a different origin refuses and names it, never a field), finds the username, password and code fields and sets each with Input.insertText (never Runtime.evaluate), submits, clears leftover password fields and hands the signed-in tab to the agent's hands (hands-chrome works in it next). The authenticator code comes from the Vault; a code it cannot make (SMS, push) stops and asks the person. Every use is audited with names and origins only. A `#` tag (a "use" intent) now ends with its conversation (thread.deleted), after 8 hours idle (using it restarts the clock), or when the person takes it back: `vault.tagged` lists where a login is lent and `vault.untag` takes it back. The canary test (core/vault/agent-fill.test.js, a real Chrome and a login-page replica) shows the replica got the exact login once and that no result, event, audit row or log line holds any value.
- refactor(cdp): the Chrome DevTools client moves from modules/hands-chrome/cdp.js to lib/cdp.js so the vault's fill and the hands share the one client; hands-chrome re-exports it. A closed socket forgets the tab it was attached to, and the hands can be told to prefer a tab (CdpPool.prefer).
- feat(rename): "Vyre for Chrome" reads "Vyre Computer" wherever a person reads it (the extension's name and title, Settings text, docs, the standalone README). Package, command and tool names are unchanged.
- feat(chat): a share taken back while the chat is locked stops opening to the project at once, and the key rotation it owes is done by the first participant to open the chat (kernel/storage/sealed-drive.js, kept in the project's sealed share index). Documented in using/private-chats.
- feat(chat): Share to project works over an encrypted chat (R031-41). A file-share record by someone in the chat wraps the file's key into the project's ring (the project's sealed share index is read back at start); taking the last share back rotates the key. New tools work.file.share and work.file.unshare. The two chat-sealed todos are real tests. Kernel base 9340 of 9440.
- fix(flows-host): a task event the host published is not published again (the log took it back and looped, so stop() never returned); test/flows-publish-once.test.js.
- feat(grants): deployment secrets are kernel grants (one grant model, step b). The Publish module mints `vault.run` on the credential to the deployment's own service actor (source `publish:secret:<deployment>:<name>:<class>:<use>`), inside `needs.kernel.mints` in its manifest; the kernel refuses any other action, address or source. The deployment record carries no `secrets` field: the publisher's store (lib/publish/grants.js) adds it on read and, on write, makes or ends the grants the record names; a record written before moves at the first start after the update (and, failing that, on its first write); running it twice is the same as once. The kernel gains a generic `mint` handle for first-party modules (make, end, list).

The daemon asks the pin through the new modules-only tool `work.chat.pinned`, read from `work.chat.pin`'s own table; a failed lookup fails closed. Files that failed on main are fixed, split or cut with a reason: the sessions and switchboard cases follow the chat gate (a session or plain MCP call carries its person's chain; a call with nothing proven meets the gate first), the tailnet owner and second-person lease case went with Tailscale, the assistant brief regexes name tools_call; federation-answer keeps 2 of 9 cases and federation-send 5 of 8 (the rest drove labelled box calls into a Mac chat the gate hides, to be redesigned over Wink); box/vyre update tests give the script their own VYRE_UPDATE_ROOT (a root-owned /var/lib/vyre-update on a test box refused them); load-flaky files are robust to timing (spoken.test.js best of three under 300 ms, signin.test.js waits up to 20 s and accepts a flow already ended at its 150 ms limit, start-inputs.test.js drops its fixed 90 s, `vyre up` honours VYRE_UP_WAIT_MS for a local start); backup.test.js is five files and vault/module.test.js two, so no file nears the 300 s limit under load.

- fix(presence): a device that lost its session token signs in again with its own confirmed key (#112). Asking for a challenge renews the device's grant without ending the session it holds; answering it with the device's own key replaces that session, the old token is dead at once, and a presence.session-replaced event is logged. Another key, or a removed device, stays refused, and the refusal now says in plain words how to get back (sign in again with its own key; if the owner removed it, pair it again from the owner's device).

## Unreleased
- fix(site): assemble-site.sh survives a release download that breaks mid-stream: up to five rounds, each keeping complete files and removing any that do not match SHA256SUMS.
