## 0.3.1 (unreleased)
- chore(tools): every tool description an agent can see is 25 words or fewer (R031-00m). The 250 long ones were cut from about 12,400 words to under 6,300 (all descriptions together 16,100 to 9,300); what a caller needs to call a tool right moved into the input properties' own descriptions. tools_find ranks the same on the sealed and dev asks (first place 68% and 68%, first three 90% and 89%), and the description lint baseline is empty.
- feat(errors): errors teach (R031-00r). Every refusal in the code now says what to do next: it names the tool that lists or fixes the thing (`work.chat.list shows the chats you may see`), says who decides, or gives an instruction; 484 refusals in 121 files were reworded, and a lint (`test/errors-teach.test.js`) fails on a new one without a next step and on a tool name in a message that is no tool. An agent that fails a call through the MCP server also gets a ready call for each tool the message names (`Next: tools_call { tool: "work_chat_list", arguments: {} }`).
- fix(chat): an image sent to a Codex or Grok session that did not say it takes images is no longer sent as an image block it would refuse; the model gets the words and one line saying a picture came that it cannot see.
- feat(tools): tools_find learns from asks (R031-00k). Every tool has a bank of ordinary asks (`lib/tools-asks-bank.js`, about 15,000 in all, written by authors who saw the tool but not the benchmark); a new ask is scored against each tool by how much it resembles the tool's asks and by how likely its words are under them, and that is fused with the keyword ranking (`lib/tools-rank.js`). On 202 asks nobody tuned for (two labelers each, authors who never saw a tool name), the right tool is first in 67 of 100 (it was 46) and among the first three in 90 (it was 70). When the views disagree and the first two are close, the answer says so (`unsure`) and tells the model to ask the person which they mean. A local embedding model was tried as a view and added nothing. Every tool must carry three example asks, and the held-out score can only go up (`test/tools-find-quality.test.js`).
- fix(tools): the guards are green. Every tool that anyone may call says which guard stops a misuse, the new person-only tools say why, descriptions over 25 words (brand, design, sessions, skills, work) are short and their detail sits in the input property descriptions, and the four role-list checks are back.
- feat(vault): the Vault pass against real box answers (R031-76). `scripts/capture-vault-fixtures.mjs` records what a real vyred answers for the Vault's reads (a temp home, fake values, no value in the file), and the gallery draws the real Vault screen from them (`setBoxOverride`, gallery only), so it is shot with real shapes. The pass: section navigation is one scrolling tab row (it wrapped to two rows on a phone); kinds and search share one row; a name is read as a person reads it ("Airline account" for the vault's "Airline-account"; the name is still what every action sends); a site is shown as its host; the "Reveal in Vyre on your phone" line is said once, not per field. Shared-vault buttons say "Coming in this release" until the app's device may call the vault write tools. Before and after pictures in team/0.3.1/shots/design-language/vault.
- fix(link)!: the person on the box can answer and type into a paired Mac's session again (#114). The Mac's link runs the box's answer or words as `link:box` only after checking the box (the pinned key's signed assertion for an answer, the pinned channel for words); those calls now carry the facts of a person at this Mac's own terminal (`registry.deps.linkBoxFacts`, set by the daemon, handed out by core/modules only to the link module's `link:box` calls), so the Mac's chat gate judges them as the Mac's owner instead of answering not_found. Agents, MCP, guests and modules on the box still never reach the Mac. The ten cases cut from main-green (federation-answer 7, federation-send 3) are back.
- feat(app): agents and sessions together (R031-51). A hand-off row in a chat ("Asked kit") opens the teammate's own conversation once it has one; the @ picker shows what each live session is doing and on which project ("Working on billing"); the agents list says which projects an agent works on by name. Pure helpers tested in real-composer.test.js and settings/real.test.js.
- feat(previews): a React preview runs on libraries the box ships (react, react-dom, recharts, lucide-react, d3, lodash, papaparse, mathjs, three, chart.js, date-fns, xlsx and Tailwind's in-browser build), pinned and each checked against a recorded sha256 before it is served. Nothing comes from a CDN, so an offline box runs the same page; an import outside the set gets a plain message. Thumbnails no longer look for a Playwright download: a box with no Chrome shows the card's mark.
- A preview card now says how long it lives from the preview's own state: "Ends with this chat" for the agent's own server, "Keeps running" once Vyre looks after it. The assistant's line says the same.
- feat(previews): the preview card has the page's own picture, and Open opens in Vyre (lead review). When a preview comes up (and after each restart) the box's own Chrome (config previews.chrome, VYRE_CHROME, one on the path, or a Playwright download; Vyre ships none) takes one screenshot of its loopback address and the last good one is kept in a folder only the daemon's user reads; `previews.thumb` hands it, as base64, to a person who may open the preview, and the card shows it (a mark until the first). Open is a pane beside the chat on a computer and a full-screen sheet on a phone (an iframe on the web and in the Mac app, the system web view on a phone), with Reload, Open in browser and Close; "Open in browser" is also a menu item. For the frame: `previews.url { embed: true }` mints a ticket whose cookie is `SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned`, the front drops a preview page's own `X-Frame-Options` and `frame-ancestors` (the preview is the owner's own, shown in Vyre's own app), and the app's policy gains `frame-src` for this box's own preview addresses (`cspFor`). Tests: core/previews/thumb.test.js, core/appmods/proxy.test.js, core/daemon/app.test.js, scripts/previews-accept.mjs (the page loads in a frame of another origin); shots in team/0.3.1/shots/previews-chat/.
- feat(previews): the operator card shows the computer's own screen and asks for what it needs (lead review). The card's picture is a still of the computer (`previews.frame`, asking `sight.frame`: a person's call only, a Mac's pixels stay on the Mac) that follows each step and refreshes every few seconds while it works; tap for a larger one; on the web, Watch live (Glass) replaces it and Take over is Glass's own. The status line breathes while it works (the design language's Pulse). A stuck step may say what it needs typed (`previews.step { ask }`): the card shows a box for it, the person's reply (`previews.reply`, never a model) reaches the run through `previews.run-get { wait_ms }`; a stuck step with no question offers Take over. The sign-in card offers the Vault first: the logins bound to the site (vault.items.names) as "Fill from the Vault: <name>", which lends that login to the computer for an hour for that one site (vault.agent.grant, one yes) and marks the card done so the run retries the fill; "Sign in yourself" is second. Tests: core/previews/previews.test.js, screen-model.test.js; shots in team/0.3.1/shots/screens/.
- fix(appmods): the sign-in a person has on an app's or a preview's own origin survives a restart of vyred or an update (8 hours as before). The browser's session is kept in the module's own table by the hash of its cookie, never the cookie; it ends at its time and is dropped with its name (a preview stopped or its access narrowed). Test: core/appmods/proxy.test.js.
- feat(previews): the artifact-compatible container (R031-89). A preview of a file or folder (`previews.open { path, capabilities? }`) is served on its own origin AS WRITTEN: HTML, a folder with a single-page-app fallback, Markdown, SVG or Mermaid (drawn through the new modules-only `artifacts.render-page`); the root is a wall (no `..`, no dotfile, no link out). A page that declares capabilities (in the call or `.vyre/preview.json`, the same config shapes as Claude's) gets Claude's runtime shape: `window.claude.use(name)` answers `db`, `user`, `sample`, `downloads` and the built-in `permissions`, or `null` for what it did not declare or the viewer refused; each declared one asks the viewer in plain words at its first use, and a no is kept. `db` is Claude's document store (slash paths, collections, set, update, delete, where, orderBy, limit, acquire, onSnapshot, the `view < interact < admin < owner` rules with `{self}` privacy) kept in the Space's Records as one internal type `preview_doc` under the module's own service chain (last-writer-wins by re-reading on a version conflict; live subscribers over server-sent events); `sample` is a model call through the threads path; the front tells the page who is looking in a signed `x-vyre-viewer` header (tickets and sessions now carry the person and their role; a local process cannot forge it). The first cut is db, user, sample, permissions and downloads; room, assets, files and mcp are 0.3.2 (team/BACKLOG.md). Tests: core/previews/previews.test.js, bridge.test.js, and `scripts/previews-accept.mjs`, which runs a Claude-style dashboard (core/previews/testing/artifact-dashboard.html) UNCHANGED in a real browser against a real daemon: consent, live tasks, a reload that keeps them, a download. Shots in team/0.3.1/shots/artifact/.
- feat(previews): the operator card and the sign-in card (R031-88, R031-91). `previews.operator { computer }` puts a computer's live screen card in the chat; `previews.step { run, line, state }` says what it is doing now (the newest receipt, in words; the card keeps the last seven steps); `previews.signin { computer, site, why }` asks the person to sign in as a card and waits for them; `previews.signin-done` (a person's surface only) says they have. The cards are `operator` and `signin` blocks in the chat stream, patched by their own ids. The screen itself is Glass's: on the web the card embeds Glass's own viewer and hook (`LiveScreen`), Watch shows it, Take over, a private sign-in (the agent sees nothing of the page and never gets the password) and Hand back are Glass's own acts, so Glass's rules hold unchanged; the phone and desktop apps say to watch in the web app until Glass reaches them. Whatever images a harness sends in its own tool results still show inline as they come and are never replaced. Tests: core/previews/previews.test.js, apps/app/src/chat/screen-model.test.js, core/stream tests; shots in team/0.3.1/shots/screens/.
- feat(ask): one card for every question (R031-92). The new `ask` module: an agent (or Vyre Computer's tools) calls `ask.many { questions }` and the person sees ONE card in the chat, each question with its choices (a label and a line under it) and a line to type or say their own (the keyboard's own microphone; Vyre speech is a later hook); `ask.answer` (a person's own surface, never a model) gives the answers once, `ask.get` waits for them, `ask.cancel` puts the card away. The card is a `questions` block in the chat stream (the same tool id patches it as it is answered). The answers decide nothing: the act that follows is filed at the Gate as any send and is the person's one yes. One to six questions, eight choices each, 20 waiting; a restart ends the wait. Tests: core/ask/ask.test.js, apps/app/src/chat/question-model.test.js; shots in team/0.3.1/shots/questions/.
- feat(previews): the preview card in the chat (R031-22). A `thread.preview` event from the previews module becomes one `preview` block in the thread's stream (a new block kind in core/stream/protocol.js; the same tool id patches the card as its state changes; the block carries a title and a state, never an address). The card shows a calm poster, the name, one word for its state, the access in a line, and one verb: Open when it is up, Restart or Look at the log when it is not; Share opens a sheet (Only me, Project, Everyone) and a menu holds Keep it running, Restart, the log and Stop. `previews` is allowed the `thread.*` events. Tests: apps/app/src/chat/preview-model.test.js, core/stream tests; shots in team/0.3.1/shots/previews/.
- feat(previews): a server an agent starts on a port becomes a preview (R031-22, R031-23; team/0.3.1/DESIGN-previews.md). The new `previews` module keeps a row per preview, opens it on its own origin `pv-<id>.<the host Vyre is served at>` through the SAME apps' front, one-time ticket and cookie that installed apps use (core/appmods/proxy.js now also resolves a preview's host through `previews.resolve`, forwards a preview's own cookies and its WebSocket upgrades, and tells its server its own address), and decides who may open it before asking appmods for the ticket (`appmods.ticket`, `appmods.drop`; modules only). Access is me, project or team; anyone-with-the-link waits for the public ingress (0.3.2). An agent calls `previews.open { port, title }` (never a command: Vyre runs a command only on a person's own call); `previews.keep` runs the command the agent said it started with on a leased port (5100 to 5999, given as PORT) so it survives the session and a restart of vyred; a supervisor restarts a crash three times in two minutes, keeps the last 200 KB of output, and kills only the process group it started. Tools: previews.open, list, get, url, keep, restart, stop, remove, log, share, resolve. Tests: core/previews/previews.test.js.
- feat(vault): search, and shared vaults with their people (R031-75). The Vault items list has "Search the vault": every word must match a name, a note, a site or a kind, names first, across tabs, never a value. The Shared page lists shared vaults (people, items, your role, what needs rotating or settling, each member's role and fingerprint) and the people Vyre shares with (card checked, pinned, or changed key). Reading only: making and changing a shared vault stays at the command line until the app's device may ask for it (the vault tools admit cli and local only).
- feat(vault): two-factor codes by camera or paste (R031-75). Import page, "Two-factor codes": scan the QR (the phone's camera, one code at a time, the same code once) or paste otpauth:// and otpauth-migration:// addresses; it shows by name what would be added, what is already there and what could not be read (and which parts of a split export are still missing), and adds on one yes. Names only come back, never a seed. A one-time-code address is now read whole by the scanner (up to 4 KB) instead of cut to the length kept for other codes.
- feat(runner): the UX half of "run on my computer" (R031-95), against session-transfer's runner contract (placement, move, settings, here, pause). A chip on each session in the chat status line ("On this Mac" / "On the server", with why and a tap to move it), one quiet line in the chat when it moves ("Moved to the server: lid closed."), and Settings, This computer, "Run on this computer": a switch, plugged in only, processor and memory limits (whole numbers in a range, checked before they are sent) and the sessions running here with Pause all. A box without the runner shows none of it. Words and rules are `screens/runner/runner-model.js` (tested); pictures in the gallery.
- feat(vault): a password generator and health on the home (R031-75). The Add item sheet has "Generate a strong one" (length 16, 20 or 32, optional no symbols): made on the device from the Web Crypto source, without look-alike characters, typed into the field and sent nowhere until the person saves. The Vault home shows one line when items need attention ("2 items need attention: 1 weak, 2 reused.") with a Fix button to the Health page.
- feat(vault): emergency access (R032-12) on the Vault's Shared page: who can ask, where each request stands in plain words (can ask, asked and opens on a date unless denied, denied, opened), Deny while one waits, Remove at any time, Add someone with a wait of 1 to 30 days, Rebuild. Names and dates only. Also: `ListView` is gone; the tag page draws its lists with the table block's typed cells.
- docs: the vault page's agent-grant example uses the sample world's names (juniper-drive, drive.juniper.example), not a client's (test/docs-rulings.test.js).
- refactor(approvals): readers move onto the one waiting list (R031-00c part 3). A card in `approvals.items` now carries `facts`, a named subset of its owner's row (who asked, thread and its name, kind, via, where a draft goes, the questions and their choices; never a draft's words or the agent's reason), for the person's own surfaces; `waiting.list` drops it, so it never reaches every device. `vyre needs`, the terminal live screen, the Slack adapter's already-held lookup, and the rollover seed read approvals.items and no longer call gate.held or threads.asks. The phone app's Now list moves in a separate change. A model caller (thread, agent, assistant, harness) is refused approvals.items, tested.
- test(tools): description lint (R031-00m). `test/description-lint.test.js` caps the descriptions an agent sees at 25 words. The 250 of 412 that are longer today are on `test/description-baseline.json` (12,460 words) and may only shrink; a new tool, or one that shrinks under the cap, is held to it. The baseline is rewritten with `UPDATE_DESCRIPTION_BASELINE=1` on the test box. Shortening them is the work this ratchet now makes visible.
- refactor(credentials): one secret detector (R031-00c, part 2). The private-key forms (header, whole block, block with a clipped END line, the PuTTY head) and the Anthropic token kind are written once in lib/credential-shapes.js (`PRIVATE_KEY_HEAD`, `hasPrivateKey`, `privateKeyBlock`, `anthropicKind`); lib/sanitize.js, core/mcp/hub.js, core/vault/sweep.js, core/files/safety.js, core/glass/guard.js and core/onboard use them instead of their own regexes. The phone app's redactor and the siteops/extension copy cannot import the table, so `test/credential-pins.test.js` pins them to it. `test/one-mechanism.test.js` is the "grep finds one of each" check for all four jobs: roles and secret detector pass, the grant model (connect-anything) and approval path (session-transfer) are `todo` until their owners land.
- refactor(roles): one role list (R031-00c, part 1). kernel/contracts holds the five roles, `ROLE_RANK`, `ROLE_LABELS`, and now `ROLE_MAY_SET` (who may set whom) and `ROLE_DEMOTE_TO` (what an owner who hands a Space over may keep). lib/spaces/members.js loses its second, inverted rank and its own manageable table; kernel/grants reads the same tables; two literal role lists in core/spaces become `roleAtLeast`. `test/one-role-list.test.js` greps the source for the owner/admin sequence and allows only the contracts and four named special lists (wink pairing admins, publish approvers, assistant makers, the vault's own sharing roles).
- feat(chats): one persistent chat each for your assistant and for @Engineer (R031-94), on the one chat UI. `work.chat.persistent { kind }` says which chat is yours (or none yet, and whether you may have one) and `work.chat.pin { kind, chat }` makes a chat of yours the one: a second, different chat of a kind is refused and names the first, so there is one per person per kind and it stays the same chat as the session rolls over. The Engineer's is for an owner or an admin and must be a chat with the engineer agent. `work.chat.list` rows carry `pinned`. The app starts the assistant's chat the first time you open Chat and pins it at the top ("Your assistant"); the Engineer's chat is not in the list and opens from Settings, Engineer (owners and admins). Lumen and any other surface reach the assistant's chat with the same two calls (`work.chat.persistent`, then `stream.send` into it); the native Lumen change is not part of this commit. Fix: the work module's internal template-change tools answer `unavailable` without a kernel.
- feat(flows): `flows.kit.credentials { task }`, the question the vault asks before `vault.connections.lend`: which installed Kit version a task is from and which Connections that version names for its template, found by record type, stage and title (`KitManager.credentialsFor`). Callable by `module:vault` only; a task no installed Kit names credentials for is `not_found`, so the vault lends nothing. Also: `recall.marks` declares its reach (modules).
- fix(eval): the paid eval's harness hang. The fake vendor runs in its own process (`scripts/eval-honest/vendor.mjs`; the plain Claude Code arms never depend on the daemon's event loop), a heartbeat supervisor in `scripts/eval-honest.mjs` ends a harness whose event loop has not beaten for `--stall-min` (default 3) minutes and prints what it was doing and whether its main thread was spinning, every run has a wall-clock cap (`--run-cap-min`, default 10) after which it is INVALID ("timed out") and re-run once, and `--disclose "text"` puts a line in the report. Proved on the stand-in: a deliberate stall (`--stall-proof`), a forced timeout, and 40 parallel GETs beside an unfinished POST (test/eval-vendor.test.js). When it ends a stalled harness it now also pauses it over its inspector and prints the function and line it was on (`scripts/eval-honest/stall.mjs`, test/eval-stall.test.js), records the run it was in as an INVALID row in rows.json, and the same command with `--again` carries on from there (finished runs are kept, the invalid one is re-run once; run numbers stay the same across the resume). `--first N` takes the first N runs of the plan; `--stall-proof N` stalls on purpose at run N. Proved on the stand-in with the first 8 cells of Eval A: a stall at run 3 was named (evalMain, run.mjs line), run 3 was recorded INVALID, and the resume finished the other cells and re-ran run 3 as #40. The stall of the first paid run did not reproduce on the stand-in (cells 5 and 6, h3-todo then flow, ran clean), so its cause is still not known; the supervisor will name it next time.
- feat(eval): the honest eval (R031-00v). `scripts/eval-honest.mjs` with `scripts/eval-honest/{prereg,heldout}.json` sealed by `PREREG.sha256` (a paid run is refused if either changed or the tree is not a commit), the pure parts in `scripts/lib/eval-honest.js`, the runner in `scripts/eval-honest/run.mjs` on the token-proof world. Eval A: plain Claude Code as given, plain Claude Code given the data as files and curl, and Claude Code with Vyre, on the ten tasks plus three held-out ones, 3 reps each. Eval B: nine scripted messages with a forced roll after the fifth, arms Claude's own /compact, Vyre seed only, Vyre seed with the sheet and link, and no roll. Checks read the world (values computed from the seed data, the vendor's request log, the todo list), never a model; fresh-thread, process-count, model and roll guards make a run invalid (listed, re-run once, both reported); the world reset between runs is read back and a non-empty read-back stops the run (`--prove-reset`); order is a seeded interleave; every run is in the report. `VYRE_ROLLOVER_LINK=off` is an eval-only switch to leave the link header out of the seed.
- feat(rollover): rollover v2 (R031-00u). A session rolls at 80 percent of its window (was 60; `sessions.rollover_at` default 80, an estimate from characters at 67), at a turn boundary, and is forced at 90 whatever is running. A hard guard (`ROLL.guard` 0.92): before a message goes to an idle session, if the window used plus that message would reach 92 percent, Vyre rolls first, so one turn cannot overflow; Claude Code's own compaction is never switched off and stays the backstop. The person sees no seam: the "Continued in a fresh session" notice is gone and `thread.rolled` carries `quiet: true` (`threads.rolls` still lists rolls). The seed now opens with a link: the earlier windows' session ids, how to read them (`memory_turn {session, from, to}`, the one tool) and "do not mention the handover unless asked". New owner-only `recall.marks {sessions, at[]}` maps moments to `session:turn` pointers by index reads alone. A deterministic reference sheet (`sheetCalls`/`sheetOf` in `core/switchboard/rollover.js`: tools called with outcome and ids, research with sources, notable facts and decisions, each with a pointer, capped at 24,000 characters, never any output text) rides in the seed only when `VYRE_ROLLOVER_SHEET=on` (or the managed-context switch); it turns on by default only if the eval (R031-00v) shows it helps.
- feat(chrome): learned website operations, wave B. `chrome_op` (kit, list, scout, learn, save, call, heal, check, versions, rollback, forget) and the extension capability `ops` (`ops.learn`, `ops.call`, `ops.heal`, `ops.scout`, `ops.check`). The login is resolved inside the page and never leaves it: a credential reference becomes a value in the extension's worker, rides into the page's own fetch, and the answer returns as extracted data. A write is taught with its request blocked after the person's yes, held for a yes on every call, made once, and not retried when the outcome is unknown. A drift of a read is repaired once and kept only after a replay answers; each kept version is rolled back in one step. The standalone playbook has the method.
- feat(connectors): a website is a Connection (wave C). `transport: "site"` in the declaration, a vault credential with `auth.type: "browser"` (the host and the route rules, no key; the vault hands the call to the browser instead of the network), and `connectors.site.*` (connect, sync, propose, operations, list, rows, rollback, limits, limits.set, resume). Flows, watchers (polls), views and assistants call a learned operation like any Connection's operation; a send is held at the Gate and made once with the approval. Two Capsule views, Websites and Website operations, through the existing views engine. An assistant's proposal waits for the person's card.
- feat(connectors): the rungs (wave D). The cheapest rung that works answers and the event `connectors.site-ran` says which: `public` (a plain fetch from the box for an operation that needs no login), `page` (the person's Chrome on this machine), `box` (an agent's own Chrome on a box, over CDP, 24/7 with the Mac off; `modules/hands-chrome` `chrome.op.run`), `mac` (a box asks the person's Chrome on a paired Mac through the link: `chrome.op.call` in `core/link/allow.js` CALL, only operations the person allowed with `link.ops.allow`, an outward one only with the box's signed assertion for exactly that call). The sign-in-again state is the event `connectors.site-needs-signin` and the Connection's light.
- feat(flows): a service step on a Mac that is off waits. The box announces `link.mac-online` when a paired Mac asks again; a Flow step whose Chrome is on that Mac waits on the engine's durable event wait, shows as `attention.kind: "device"` ("Needs your Chrome"; Retry tries now, Stop ends it), and tries the same step again when the Mac is back or fails plainly at the longest wait.
- feat(connectors): the account governor (wave E). Every call to a watched account (LinkedIn by default; any site on request) goes at a person's pace, one at a time, within daily read and write caps, outside quiet hours, and the first security check stops the account until a person resumes it (`connectors.site.resume`). Every number is a setting per account (`connectors.site.limits.set`). The LinkedIn site kit (`lib/siteops/kits/linkedin.js`) is a teaching recipe that says plainly it is against LinkedIn's terms and at the user's own risk; `chrome_op kit` lists it; the trial ran on a replica of a professional network's web app.
- feat(sessions): a Codex session is given the Space's approved skills (R031-19). The switchboard asks the skills module to write the library for the thread's provider and tells a Codex run where (`VYRE_SKILLS_DIR`); the Codex driver runs it with a CODEX_HOME of its own beside the account's (`.codex-lib/<content id>`: the sign-in linked, Vyre's config, the skills linked), so sessions with the same skills share a home and none sees skills that are not its project's or agent's. Proved against the real Codex CLI (`codex debug prompt-input` lists the skill in that home and not in the account's). Grok is not wired yet (its skills folder and CLI are windows-setup's R031-86).
- fix(app): a project's page title is its name (the sample world's view table named records by `title`, which the Space's own Project has not got); the template studio no longer prints a person's id. `scripts/app-walk-projects-shots.mjs` takes the screenshots of the studio and project pages.
- feat(skills): one skills and plugins library at four levels (R031-18..21). A skill or plugin is a `skill` record per version (level space, personal, agent or project; draft, approved or retired). Anyone drafts (`skills.draft`: a person, their assistant, an agent for itself, @Engineer); nothing uses a draft; the level's owner approves (`skills.approve`, or one card from `flows.propose { what: "skill" }`), the one before is retired, and `skills.rollback` writes an earlier version again. `skills.list/find/get` include the approved ones the caller may see, the narrower level winning a name; a secret-shaped text is refused. Each AI is given the approved library in its own layout (`skills.materialise`: a Claude and Grok plugin folder, a Codex skills folder, checked against the real Codex CLI with `codex debug prompt-input`); Claude threads get it through `--plugin-dir` beside the Harness. A plugin with code (a hook or an MCP server) is approved only with the acknowledgement of exactly what it declares; its hooks run in the watchers' script sandbox (`skills.hook.run`: no network of its own, only the declared hosts, reads only; an undeclared host is refused, proved under bubblewrap), and its MCP servers become Connections. Not yet: Codex and Grok SESSIONS are not started with the materialised folder (the layout and tool are there), hooks are not yet registered with Claude Code's own hook runner, and the learn module still installs by its own path.
- feat(engineer): @Engineer does the setup by conversation (R031-16). It was a Flows-only proposer; its toolbox now holds the template tools (`work.template.define`, `test`, `list`, `get`, `library`, `install`, `from-project`), `flows.patch`, `flows.cheatsheet`, `flows.test.*`, `agents.versions` and the docs and skills finders, and nothing that applies (`work.start-project`, `work.template.golive`, `flows.approve`, `agents.update` and permissions stay a person's). Its instructions teach the draft, try, propose order; a home still on the earlier shipped text is brought up to date and one an admin edited is left alone. The `build-a-template` skill and `docs/using/project-templates.md` teach the template shape. Fix: the tool list an agent that only proposes is held to (`meta.agentOnly`) was applied only on the path without the kernel retrofit, so a daemon with the kernel on never applied it; it is now judged before either path (`core/modules/index.js`). Test: `test/engineer-daemon.test.js` (scripted; a live-model eval is a paid run, not made).
- feat(app): the template studio and project pages (R031-11, 14, 15). `/u/templates` lists the project templates (and the ones Kits ship, to add as drafts); `/u/templates/<id>` is the studio: the tree of stages and tasks with who does each and who may move a stage early, Test mode (every brief and doer on a sample, nothing created or sent), Go live (a draft, by its owner or an admin), the versions, and an editor that saves a NEW draft version. A project page opens on its chats (a template project on its stages first) with Files, Memory and Team beside them; from 1100 points wide the panes sit side by side, two at 1440 and three from 1700 (`screens/projects/panes.ts`). Files are the project's sealed `Projects/<id>/files`; Memory is `memory.space.recall` for the project.
- feat(projects): templates, the stage engine for them, and "start a project" (R031-06, 10, 12, 13). A project template is a record per version (`project-template`; `lib/project-template.js` checks it, writes every task's brief from its own choices and compiles it): stages with "moves on when" (the next stage's entry condition) and who may move one early, tasks with doer, checker, checklist, what needs a yes, who to ask, Connections it may use, and roles filled by roster agents with at most one lead. `work.template.define` writes a draft, `work.template.test` tries it with nothing created or sent, `work.template.golive` (its owner or an admin) puts it live and retires the old one, or an agent proposes it (`flows.propose { what: "template" }`, one card). `work.start-project` (also the Flow step "Start a project from a template") makes the project, its teammates and lead from the roles, pins the stages on the project (`template_snapshot`, so a running project keeps its version) and makes the first stage's tasks; the Flows stage module drives them (`template_stage`), enters each next stage itself and accepts the stage owner's early move. `work.template.from-project` saves a template from a project that ran one; `work.template.library` / `install` ship Kit templates (law-firm: Estate plan). The work module's declared Project type was missing the wave A fields (personal_of, tags): regenerated, with a test that fails when it drifts from the core type.
- feat(agents): subagents and agent records (R031-07, R031-02). `agents.spawn { task, label?, tools?, project? }` starts a short-lived helper from an agent's own thread: it runs as its parent (same credentials, projects and kernel actor, so it holds nothing the parent does not), its tool list can only be shorter (a list outside the parent's is refused, and with none it inherits the parent's), `agents.scope { name, thread }` holds that thread to it, a helper starts no helpers (at most five at once), and its row nests in the parent's conversation as one hand-off row with the helper's steps under it (the `summon.*` events teammates use). Agents are mirrored as `agent` records, a derived view written by one path (`core/agents/mirror.js reconcile`, run on start, after every roster change and after any hand edit of an agent record, which is put back): tags go in through `agents.update { tags }`, so an agent takes a tag like any record and shows on a tag page.
- feat(agents): owners, versions and changes by conversation (R031-09). Every agent has an owner (the person who made it). A person's own `agents.update` of instructions, skills, model, effort or tags is a version; `agents.versions` lists them and `agents.update { rollback: n }` restores version n (0 is how it began) as a new one. A model never edits an agent: the error teaches `flows.propose { what: "agent", agent, patch }`, which stores a draft and puts ONE card in front of the owner (else an admin); their yes applies it as a version, only if the agent has not changed since. The proposals path (`kernel/flows/proposals.js`) takes registered kinds, so templates and skills use the same card, hash and approve-and-apply; tests in `kernel/flows/proposal-kinds.test.js`, `core/agents/versions.test.js` and the real-daemon `test/agent-change-daemon.test.js`.
- feat(models): the model registry (R031-84). A new `models` module keeps every model Vyre can offer, filled from each provider's own `/models` with the account's key (the switchboard asks, with `threads.models-fetch`; the key never leaves it), from what each CLI or subscription login reported when a session started, and from OpenRouter's public metadata for price, context length and capabilities; an entry says which source gave each field. Refreshed daily and on demand (`models.refresh`, at most once a minute); a source that fails keeps its last rows and says so on `models.status`; a model no source lists for three refreshes is marked unavailable, never deleted. The only hardcoded list is the Claude aliases, used when nothing else is known. `models.list`, `models.get`.
- feat(models): the new-model eval card (R031-87). A model first seen after the first fill proposes its evals once: each eval type with a dollar estimate worked out from the model's own price (or "cost unknown"), as one `eval` card in Needs you. `models.eval-approve` (a person's own) queues the chosen types and `models.eval-decline` is remembered; nothing runs and nothing is spent by Vyre on its own. A runner reports with `models.eval-record`, and the score lands on the model's entry.
- feat(sessions): harness capabilities are detected at session start (R031-85) from what the harness says about itself (Claude Code's init; an ACP agent's `initialize`: version, loadSession, images, MCP, sign-in methods) and stored per harness (`sessions.harness.get`); a capability is true, false or not shown, and only a false ever hides anything. `skills.list` and `skills.find` take a `harness`: a skill that declares `needs` (frontmatter) and needs what that harness showed it lacks is left out and named with the reason in `hidden`, one that gives a `degrade` line stays with `works: "degraded"` and what it loses.
- feat(skills): adapters per harness (R031-86). `lib/skill-adapters.js` places a SKILL.md where each harness reads skills (the table is a driver fact, core/sessions/drivers/skill-homes.js), turns a skill into plain instructions for a harness that has none, and routes a plugin to its own vendor's harness first and to another only where its needs are met, with the reason where not. Vyre copies nothing a harness already reads and re-implements no plugin.
- feat(chat): a key in a person's own message is held as a card instead of bounced (R031-68, lead ruling). `threads.send` from the person's surfaces (CLI, Deck, Capsule, local) holds the message at the Gate as a `threads:key` send: the card reads "Save this Anthropic key to your Vault and send the message with it?" and shows the words with `vault://anthropic-key` where the key was. The raw key lives only in the threads module's memory under a random ref for 30 minutes. The person's yes on the card (the Gate's outward approval) lets the Gate call `threads.key-release`, which saves the key with vault.put and sends the message with the reference; a no, a restart or the timeout sends nothing and keeps nothing. A model, an unknown surface, `threads.start`, `threads.edit-retry` and `stream.send` are still refused. `vyre threads send` prints the card id and how to approve it. Test: core/switchboard/key-guard.test.js.
- feat(vault): the phone picks an export from Files with the system file picker (expo-document-picker, one line of why in test/allowed-dependencies.json); the Import page works the same on every surface. Brand names are spelled as the brands spell them in the project list, and a message with several secured keys shows one tag. A sample-world page (app/shots-vault.tsx) and apps/app/scripts/vault-shots.mjs make the screenshots in team/0.3.1/shots/vault-ux/.
- feat(chat): a key in a message never reaches a model, from any surface (R031-68, lead review). `threads.send`, `threads.start`, `threads.edit-retry` and `stream.send` refuse text that holds a vendor-shaped key (the one detector, `lib/secure-paste.js` `keyInText`), before anything is stored or handed to a turn, with `secret_in_message` naming the kind and never the value; a `vault://name` reference passes. The app's catch is the same library as a fast path: it saves the key (the Vault's yes) and sends the reference, so the person never meets the refusal. The server does not save on its own, because the Vault's floor needs the person's yes on that exact save and a module call is exempt from it. Test: core/switchboard/key-guard.test.js.
- chore(golden): the app's new callers for vault.import, vault.import.preview and (phone) vault.env.scan are named as a surface ruling in scripts/gen-allow.mjs (SURFACE_RULINGS, person callers only, the one refusal `denied`), written to kernel/golden/presence.json; docs/reference regenerated. golden.json itself is for the gate to re-record: `node kernel/golden/index.js --write` on this base also refuses on 33 added tools (appmods.*, connectors.connection.*) that were not named before this branch.
- feat(vault): an Import page in the app (R031-66, R031-67). Vault, Items, Import: pick one of fifteen places your passwords are now (1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Keeper, NordPass, Proton Pass, Enpass, KeePass, Apple Passwords, Chrome, Edge and the other Chromium browsers, Firefox, Safari, a .env file), see how to export from it, choose the file, read what would come in (new, already here, differs, by kind and name) and import with one button. A differing password is kept as it is unless you choose the file's; the old one stays in history. Below it, "Your projects" asks the box for the .env files that hold keys (vault.env.scan), lists them by project with a switch per file and a warning for files git holds, and moves them in and rewrites them to vault references under one yes.
- feat(vault): `vault.import.preview` and `vault.import` take the bytes of a file (`content` base64 with its `filename`) as well as a path, because the file the app picked is on the person's computer, not always on the box; Claude cannot pass bytes (a value never goes through Claude). `vault.import` takes `files` (up to 100 absolute .env paths) for one yes over a scan. The import, preview and env.scan tools are open to the Deck, Capsule and phone as well as the CLI.
- feat(chat): paste a key in a message and it is secured before anyone reads it (R031-68). The app finds the key with the one detector (`locateSecrets` in lib/credential-shapes.js), saves it to the Vault (the Vault's own yes), and sends the message with `vault://name` in its place; the chat draws a small "Secured in the Vault" tag under the words, and a "Securing your Anthropic key in the Vault" tag while it saves. If the Vault does not take the key, nothing is sent. The transcript never holds the value. Tests: apps/app/src/chat/secure-paste.test.js.
- feat(projects): wave B (R031-04, 08). A project's own files (`Projects/<id>/files/`) are stored sealed under a key the server derives for that project from the Space's pool key and never stores (`kernel/storage/sealed-drive.js`, `kernel/home.js`), names hashed like a chat's. They open only for the project's members (its owner and its team-member people), a member's default assistant, and a teammate agent only while it has a ready or working task in that project; an owner or admin who is not a member, another member, an outside agent and another module get not_found before the Drive is touched (`kernel/core/folders.js`, `kernel/gateway/project-members.js`). Every read is the existing `file.accessed` event with the agent in its chain. Space memory facts take a `scope`: `memory.space.file { scope: "agent" }` keeps a lesson with the agent across projects, `scope: "project:<id>"` keeps a fact in one project it may reach; `memory.space.recall { project }` returns the Space's facts, the agent's own and that one project's, never another project's or another agent's.
- feat(projects): wave A of Projects (R031-01, 02, 03, 05). The `project` type takes `template`, `template_version`, `lead` and `personal_of`; every core type takes a free `tags` text (a JSON list, `lib/tags.js` is the one reader and writer; the Task type did this first) and `/u/tags/<tag>` lists everything with a tag and pins as a sidebar view. One private "Personal" project per person replaces the single shared "General": a chat started with no project is filed in its creator's, `work.chat.list` hides other people's Personal, and `hub.migrateGeneral` moves each old General chat to its creator's Personal once and archives General. The default assistant already holds the person's own access and never a sealed vault action (kernel/delegate.test.js proves it). Kit JSON regenerated for the new core field.
- feat(siteops): learned website operations, wave A (pure core, `lib/siteops`). Ported from api-anything (MIT, credited in NOTICE and Settings, About, Open-source credits): the layered request codec (path, query, form, JSON, JSON in a string, base64), two-example learning with the diff (inputs, constants, nonces), the failure classifier (ok, drift, auth, rate, blocked, input, error, each with a next step), extract and pick, the outline and a scout. No Buffer, no I/O, no dependency, so it runs in the extension, the standalone and the daemon. A login never enters an operation: credentials are references (`cookie:`, `session:`) the page resolves when it signs the call, and example values leave the template.
- feat(site-knowledge): the `ops` part. A learned operation is kept in the one site record (extension, standalone files, Vyre Memory) with the same allowlist (a secret shape or an email refuses the whole patch), heal by outcome, quarantine, tombstones and union. A new verified version keeps the old two for a one-step rollback (`rollbackOp`). The record bound is 1 MB.
- refactor(chrome): one learner. `apilearn.js` (the shape catalog) and `redact.js` now live in `lib/siteops` and are generated into the extension by `scripts/sync-copies.mjs` (`extension/shared/sk/siteops/`); importers follow.
- feat(flows): "Turn this into a Flow" (R031-42). `flows.from-chat { name, calls, variables?, propose? }` turns the calls an assistant made by hand into a stored draft: record writes and finds become steps, a variable becomes an input read from the trigger, an id one call returned and a later one used becomes a read of that step, and what cannot be a step is listed. With `propose` it goes through the checked `flows.propose`. A skill, `turn-this-into-a-flow`, tells the assistant how. The draft is never approved.
- feat(flows): Connections list their Flows (R031-43). `flows.connections` answers, per Connection, the Flows that use it with their health line; `flows.list` rows carry `connections`.
- feat(waiting): one "Needs you" place (R031-45). Stuck tasks join approvals, asks, drafts and failed runs as `task` cards (the reason in the detail, answered by `tasks.move`); `waiting.count` has a `task` count. The Flows host reads them and says `task.*` changes on the event bus.
- feat(update): "What's new" after an update (R031-47). `update.whats-new` gives the running version's release notes once to each person, only after an update (a new install records its version in silence); `update.whats-new-seen` clears it. `release/notes` now ships in the package.
- feat(sidebar): pin anything (R031-48). `sidebar.pin { what: project | flow | connection | records | view, id, label }` and `sidebar.unpin` add and remove an entry in the caller's own sidebar; pinning twice pins once.
- test(vault): the keychain test waits up to 60 s for vyred to answer (a loaded box took 25 s), not 15 s.
- feat(projects): wave A of Projects (R031-01, 02, 03, 05). The `project` type takes `template`, `template_version`, `lead` and `personal_of`; every core type takes a free `tags` text (a JSON list, `lib/tags.js` is the one reader and writer; the Task type did this first) and `/u/tags/<tag>` lists everything with a tag and pins as a sidebar view. One private "Personal" project per person replaces the single shared "General": a chat started with no project is filed in its creator's, `work.chat.list` hides other people's Personal, and `hub.migrateGeneral` moves each old General chat to its creator's Personal once and archives General. The default assistant already holds the person's own access and never a sealed vault action (kernel/delegate.test.js proves it). Kit JSON regenerated for the new core field.
- feat(flows): the Needs-attention inbox (f3). A run that stopped, is stuck, is paused or a stage gate held back is a `run` card in the one waiting queue (`waiting.list`, `waiting.count` and `approvals.items` count it; a stale wait is a quiet row that does not push). `flows.attention` lists them in plain words with the message redacted; `flows.settle { run, action }` is the one answer (retry, skip with a value, stop, or advance for a gate), a person's, answered from any device. The Flows host now says `flow.finished`, `flow.stuck`, `flow.stale`, `flow.paused`, `flow.cancelled`, `flow.retried`, `flow.started` and `stage.gate-opened` / `stage.gate-closed` on the event bus (ids and a state only), so the card appears and closes on every device. The gate events were named `gate.*` inside the runner; they are `stage.gate-*` so they do not meet the Gate module's own `gate.*`.
- feat(design): a screen reaches Lumen (R031-57). `capsule.view` for a command that declares a `screen` answers its glance (up to three blocks, an approval kept) written as a `list` frame (the numbers and facts lead as rows) or a `detail` frame, the frames every Lumen already draws, so no Swift changes and every Lumen build shows it. Read-only: an action would need the block it belongs to, so the frame says to open Vyre. A row opens as a detail through the block that has one. Also: Chrome flags on the render launch, the plain-session and environment lists, the architecture map for `core/design`, `core/brand` and `design-refs`, and a `golden-refresh` workflow that records the golden decisions in the CI environment.
- feat(design): typed cells, and the records LIST drawn from the table block (R031-58). A `table` cell may be text, a number or `{ k, v, f, s }` typed by a field kind of the registry (text, money, date, choice, stage, link, actor, sealed...) or `title`; the app draws each with that kind's own renderer, so a value reads here as it does everywhere. A `sealed` cell is `{ k: "sealed", on }` and nothing else: `tableFromRecords` stops a sealed value (by kind, by the definition's seal, or a seal reference) before it reaches the block, and the validator refuses a sealed cell that carries one (tests cover both). `/u/records/<type>` in list mode is a table block with the list's own sorting, filter and sort menus, chips and phone rows; the board, calendar and dashboard stay on their views until 0.3.2. Evidence: before and after pictures of Matters, Contacts and a stored view at 1280 and 390, dark and paper, 0 pixels differ in all 12 (shot with reduced motion); a test shows the same order for every sortable column, both directions, with and without a filter.
- feat(design): the records page is a screen in the design language (R031-58, proof of one key route). `/u/records/<type>` is now one `records` block (data source: the space's own records) drawn by BlockScreen; the block reuses the records views (ListView, BoardView, CalendarView, DashboardView) as they were, so sorting, filters and stored views behave identically. Before and after pictures of Matters and Contacts at 1280 and 390, dark and paper: 0 pixels differ on desktop, animation-timing noise only on the phone. `registerBlock` lets the app register block types that need its store and router. `test/key-screens.test.js` now counts 3 of 66 routes on blocks and names the other 63 with a reason. The remaining routes move in 0.3.2 with their owners (team/BACKLOG.md).
- feat(design): the owner's Design changes page (`/u/design`). Each proposal from an agent or the Engineer is drawn before and after with the same renderer the app uses (`views.preview`), custom styling as text, with a plain line of what it reads and runs and who proposed it; Yes makes it the space's, Not now keeps what was there. A screen drawn in a narrow place (a pane beside another, a chat card) now stacks its rows and splits by its own width, not the window's.
- feat(design): the brand profile and the guarded CSS hatch (R031-60, R031-61). `core/brand` keeps the space's identity (names, colour, fonts, density, logos, letterhead), all optional, as SPACE-level data: `appearance` is a per-person and per-device preference, so brand is not a section of it. `brand.resolve` is what everything reads (a colour that cannot be read as text is moved to the nearest one that can, with a note), `brand.draft` makes a draft from a website's markup (the caller fetches the page), and only a person saves with `brand.set`. A new artifact the person sees (private view, download) carries the brand by default; a document's own theme wins; a public share carries none (it is stripped of who and where). The app's space theme follows the brand. `design.css.propose` takes custom CSS for the space or one screen from the Engineer only: `lib/design/css.js` lints it (hooks `[data-screen]` and `[data-block]`, design tokens only, no @import, url(), !important or properties that hide or move), the owner sees it before and after, it is drawn on the web app only, and `design.css.verify` (also at every start) turns off one that no longer passes, with the reason. `design_brand` joins the Design MCP.
- feat(design): the design language, one registry for screens (R031-56 to R031-64). `lib/views/blocks.js` holds 23 blocks (props, data, content, and each one's phone and chat form), layouts (col, row, grid, split, tabs, stack), a validator that names the path and the fix, and the shrinks for a phone and a chat card. A v1 frame is a one-block screen. `views.get` and `views.act` take `surface` and `block`; a view may declare `screen`. `apps/app/ui/blocks` draws any screen (`BlockScreen`), `ViewHost` uses it, and `ChatCard` draws the glance form. `views.show` puts a read-only card in a thread (an agent may call it; the module's tool runs as that agent) and `views.shown` tells the chat what it was shown. A row can carry a status tone by name (`tones`). `module-sdk` checks a module's screens. `core/design` keeps the space's own screens and the proposals to change them (propose, owner's yes or no), `views.preview` resolves a proposed screen for the owner's before and after, and `vyre mcp design` serves the Design and Module MCP (catalogue, validate, render, propose, scaffold, check, test, stage). Picture tests (`design-refs/`, 162 pictures, made in a pinned Playwright image by CI) and `/gallery` fixtures generated by `scripts/gen-gallery`.
