If the Vault does not take the key, nothing is sent. The transcript never holds the value. Tests: apps/app/src/chat/secure-paste.test.js.
- feat(flows): stage gates on the same runner (s1). A stage with tasks is a run on the Flows runner, synthesized at stage entry from the stage as the Space defines it (no Flow is stored): `tasks`, one `task:<title>` for each task, `condition` (the next stage's entry condition) and `move`. It is written down, so a restart takes the open gates back and makes no task twice; it shows in `flows.runs`, `flows.describe` and the timeline; a stuck task or a held entry condition raises attention; and a gate held back by the next stage's entry condition now moves on once the record meets it (the host's tick looks again). `flows.advance { run, reason }` moves a record on early, for the stage's owner or an admin in their own name; who and why stay on the ledger. A gate is not cancelled or retried like a Flow run.
- feat(flows): task briefs and checklists checked by the gate (s2). A stage task template takes `brief` (filled from the record into the task's note), `checklist` (`field`, `answer`, `status` and `poll` checks) and `credentials` (the Connections the doer may use). A task the doer calls done counts only when its checklist holds; the gate says what is missing. Status and poll checks are reads through a declared Connection, authorized as reads (nothing a check does can send), and a poll is bounded and spaced. A Kit with a bad brief, checklist or credential is refused at install with the place and the fix. Enforcing `credentials` as narrower vault grants for the doer is not done yet; today it is declared, shown in the task and checked at install.
- feat(flows): template test mode (s3). `flows.kit.test` walks a Kit on a sample, or a real record read only, with nothing sent: each stage's tasks and filled briefs, checklists, what holds the record, what the next stage's condition says of it, and what each Flow that starts at a stage would do, then a totals line.
- feat(flows): the active version keeps running when a saved test case starts to fail, and its health line turns red ("a saved test fails").
- feat(flows): the lines form (e1). `flows.code { format: "lines" }`, and `format: "lines"` on `flows.define` and `flows.compile-text`, read and write a Flow as one line a step (`kernel/flows/lines.js`): lossless against the stored form, so text and canvas stay in sync, with parse errors that name the line. The shipped Kit Flows come to about a third fewer tokens than the TypeScript form (their long descriptions are the same in both); a Flow of steps alone gains more.
- feat(flows): edit by patch (e2). `flows.patch { id, base, ops }` applies named edits (set, insert, replace, remove, move, trigger, meta) to the newest version and stores a new draft; a patch made against an older version is refused, never merged, and an unknown step says which ids there are.
- feat(flows): validate and simulate before propose (e5). `flows.propose` for a Flow compiles it, runs its saved test cases and replays the last week of events with every action stubbed before a person is asked, and puts one line on the card. An assistant cannot skip it; a person can with `unchecked: true`, and the card says so.
- feat(flows): a generated cheat sheet (e6). `flows.cheatsheet` lists every trigger, step kind with a real example, retry and failure keys, check, expression name and function and limit, built from the code; each example is checked against the schema.
- fix(flows): the records store now answers `flowRow`, so a draft Flow's newest version can be found (patch and test cases need it).
- feat(flows): saved test cases (t2). `flows.test.save` / `run` / `list` / `remove` keep a trigger and what the Flow is expected to do (`state`, `writes`, `outward`, `asks`, `steps_ran`, `steps_not_run`); a case can be kept from a real run as a baseline. Cases run through the simulation, so nothing is done for real, and approving a Flow version is refused while one fails. An assistant adds cases and never changes or removes one.
- feat(flows): explain this run (t3). `flows.describe { run }` answers `explain`, at most four sentences: why it ran, what it did, what happens next. No step data.
- feat(flows): errors name the place and the fix (e4). Every Flow problem leads with the step ("Step 3 (make_letter): ...") and carries `step` and `fix` ("did you mean client?", or the choices) for record types, fields, stages, actions, roles, teammates, pools, templates, connectors, step references and expression names.
- fix(tools): `tasks.create` says it is a work item on a record and that a to-do or reminder is `planner_add` (the compact `work_tools` sent a model to it for "add a todo"). A by-reference summary keeps the signals beside the list (`more`, `next_cursor`, `capped_at`), so a reader of the summary alone knows there is more.
- change(context): the rollover seed's receipts and ledger (R031-00q) are OFF unless `VYRE_MANAGED_CONTEXT=on`. Token proof round 5 could not show they help: the long task was one message, a window rolls over only between turns, so no rollover fired in any arm and the ledger arm differed from the others only by chance. The proof's long task is now two messages with a roll between them (the daemon's own, or `threads.roll` if it does not come), so the next run can tell.
- change(tools): results by reference is OFF by default (lead ruling, 9 Oct, after token proof round 4): a session offers `tools_run` and returns big results whole. `VYRE_MCP_FEATURES` still turns it on for measuring (`""` both, `ref`). `vault_list` and `vault_request` now share one check (`modelMayRead`), so a list shows exactly what a request would allow for that caller, and no more.
- fix(tools): the causes round 4 of the token proof found. `work_tools` lists names, risk and one line for each tool (a full catalog of shapes was most of 30,000 characters, and the environment text sends every session to it first); give `tool` for one tool's shape or `schemas: true` for all, and it is never handed out by reference. A record `find` now says `more` and `next_cursor` when there are more, `capped_at` when a limit was cut to 50, and takes `cursor` and `sort`, so "the first three by name" is one call. `results_read` can narrow a list before paging it (`where`, `sort`, `fields`), and a handle's summary names the list to read (`result.records`), its count and its fields. `vault_list` shows the person's assistant the api-credentials it can already call (name, kind, description, hosts; never a value), where it read an empty vault and gave up. A learned Vyre skill's description now says in words what it does ("look up clients, then look up matters, then add to the planner"), not tool ids no request ever names.
- fix(proof): the token proof world's vault seed failed on every round since round 3 (hosts must be origins), so the vault task could not pass in any arm; and its clean-up deleted nothing (`planner.delete` takes `item`), so the second arm of the long and repeat pairs was judged with the first arm's todos still there. Both fixed, with a check that proves the clean-up, and rows now say how many Claude processes a run took.
- fix(agent-paths): what round 3 of the token proof showed an agent could not find. A Connection's record now says how to call it (`use`: vault.request with `conn-<id>`, not the key item it is made from; the docs said connectors.operation.run, which assistants are not offered); team_ask's two errors say what to give and where to find it (the Project record id, from team_list { all: true }), and its tools_find example carries `project`; flows_start and flows_run get ready examples with the id to pass. The proof's world gives the Acme key a host and a description, and the Orbit key a description, so an agent can see which host and which item.
- fix(token-proof): round 2 was measured from two proofs at once. Two worlds wrote to the same out folder, so each run's file held lines from a second thread (another home's juno, resumed), and a helper session (memory) could be read as the run. The copy of a claude process's output is now one file per process (`<tee>.<pid>.part`), and the world reads only the files whose session began in this proof's agent folder, so a helper, a teammate or another proof is never counted; a proof refuses to start where another is running (a lock) or where a round's rows.json already exists (unless --again); the teammate the `teammate` task asks is stopped between runs. The `connection` task asked for a Stripe connection the world never made: it now names the Orbit CRM connection the world seeds (and the vault task's Acme key no longer shares a name with the connection's key), and checks the count in the answer.
- feat(learn): repeated work becomes one step (R031-00s). The learn module's own detector (learn_procs: a 3 to 6 step run clean in three sessions) now sees Vyre tool calls: a call is the step `vyre:<tool>` by the tool that really ran (tools_call, work_call and each call of a tools_run unwrapped), named from the PreToolUse hook and never from an argument (lib/vyre-steps.js; the finders and results_read are not work). A failed Vyre call (PostToolUseFailure now passes on Vyre tools) keeps its turn's Vyre steps out. A Vyre-run thread's started tool event gains `steps`, `argKeys` and the id-shaped `argIds` (never a value). The draft is written from the three runs' receipts (lib/skill-skeleton.js): the argument names, and the data flow every run agrees on (a later call's id argument was an earlier call's returned id); a skill whose steps are all Vyre calls ends in `## One call`, a tools_run script with `<placeholders>` and an `{ expr }` for the agreed flows, and a model's own draft keeps that ending. No value from any session reaches a skill. A terminal session, with no thread log, gets the plain steps. The assistant's glance says, as a count only, when drafts wait. Offering a Flow stays with R031-42. The token proof gains the task `repeat` and the arms `skill-off` and `skill-on`.
- fix(token-proof): each paid run is a fresh thread that runs to its final answer. The first paid round showed three faults: agents.ask answers as soon as a thread stops to ask the person, so the row was read before the turn ended (runs made one call and no text); the agent's last thread was resumed for every task (SessionStart:resume), so input tokens grew by about 500 a run; and a run whose second permission ask was unanswered ended at the first result. The world now deletes the agent's threads before each run, waits for the run's own result line, and fails a row that resumed an old session or ended with no text. The stand-in gains `toolseq-ask` (two asked tool calls, then a final answer), used for the `record` task, so a run that stops after one call fails for nothing.
- feat(flows): a decide or a repeat takes `on_fail` and `verify` like any step. A step failing for good inside the block, or a check over its output (`branch`, or `count`) that fails, goes to the block's failure path, which reads `error`; `then: continue` lets the run go on, and the block's ledger entry makes the failure path replay-safe. A block still refuses `timeout_ms` and `retry`, which the runner would ignore.
- fix(flows): a Flow tool that needs an id says so. flows.start with no `id` (an agent passed `flow`) answered "that Flow is not running", which sent the agent the wrong way; start, get, run, retry, cancel, timeline, diff and rollback now answer `bad_input: id is required: the Flow's id (flows.list ...)`.
- fix(flows): a run on its own can never take the server down, and two events about one record take turns. A detached run's rejection (a store that fails while it is written, a bug) is caught where it starts: the run is marked failed if it can be, `flow.error` says why, and there is no unhandled rejection (tested with a throwing step, a throwing failure path and a failing store). A Flow with no `lock` of its own now takes an implicit one per record when the run was started by an event about a record (the event's subject): two runs for one record take turns, runs for different records go together, and an event that is not about a record has no key. Each run's ledger is its own, so a crash repeats neither run's write (tested).
- feat(flows): reliability wave 3, read it, compare it, go back (f8, f12, f11, describe). **Health (f8):** `flows.health` and a `line` on every `flows.list` row say how a Flow is in one sentence and a few numbers: last run, ok of total this week, what needs a person, what is held, the next run (in the Space's zone), and red when a Connection its service steps use is red (the host passes the lights of the Space's Connections into the catalog). It is read from the runs the runner already keeps; nothing new is stored. **Timeline (f12):** the ledger now keeps, per step, when it started and finished, every attempt, the input of an effect step with credential-shaped strings and secret-named keys hidden and the whole cut to 2 KB (a sealed placeholder stays a placeholder), the verify result, who answered a card and who gave a substitute value; `flows.timeline { run }` reads it back as one line a step (`#2 Create letter  ok  1.4s  3 tries (timeout, timeout, ok); verify ok`), `step` for one in detail. **Compare and go back (f11):** `flows.diff { id, from, to }` names the steps added, removed, moved and changed by id, with the keys that changed, the trigger and the Flow-level keys, and a summary in words; `flows.rollback { id, to }` approves the earlier version again as the person who asks (their presence, nothing inherited from the old approval), says what changes, leaves runs in flight on their version, and with `retry_failed: true` moves failed runs that still match onto the restored version. **`flows.describe`** gives a Flow (the trigger, one line a step with its limits, tries, failure path and check, how it is doing) or a run (state, where it stopped and what you can do) in a few lines.
- feat(flows): reliability wave 2, the runner's control (f5, f6, f7). A run executes on its own now (`void #exec`), so a slow step no longer holds up the delivery of every other trigger. **Concurrency (f6):** a Flow runs at most `concurrency` runs at once (the setting `flows.concurrency`, 8; a Flow's own `concurrency` 1 to 32 wins) and the box at most `flows.concurrency_box` (32); a run holds a place only while it executes a slice, never while it waits for a person or a timer. The rest are `queued` (a new run state, durable: a restart keeps them) and start oldest first as places free. A Flow's `lock` (an expression giving a key such as `"client:" + trigger.client`) keeps runs with the same key from executing at the same moment, across Flows. **Pause (f7):** `pauseAll` / `resumeAll` (flows.pause with all: true or drain: true, flows.resume with all: true): paused holds what arrives, in order, and a run in flight stops at its next step boundary; draining lets running runs finish and starts none. An event that arrives while ONE Flow is paused is held too (it was silently dropped before: a paused or runaway-paused Flow lost every event). Resume runs what was held in order (`backlog: "run"`, the default) or drops and counts it (`"drop"`); held runs are bounded per Flow (`flows.backlog_cap`, 200) and an event past the cap is refused, counted (`dropped`) and the control line shows the count first (`flows.control`). **Watchdog (f5):** the scheduler's own `tick()` runs a run that has not moved for `flows.stuck_minutes` (5, or a Flow's `stuck_after_ms`) once more, and flags it `stuck` if it still does not move (the flag goes on the live run, so a hung step cannot hide it behind its own lock); a run waiting on a person past `flows.stale_days` (3) is flagged `stale` and left waiting; both clear when the run moves; `nextWake()` carries the deadlines, so there is no new timer. New setting `flows.retry_attempts` caps the default tries. The Space's settings are read through the settings tool by the host and re-read every 30 seconds.
- feat(flows): reliability wave 1, the runner as a beast (f1, f2, f4). Every step now runs under a time limit and a retry rule, defaults per kind in `POLICY` (runner.js; the host can override per kind): find/pick 30 s and 3 tries, record writes 60 s and 3 tries, a module tool or a service write one try (retried only when the Flow says so), classify/extract 2 tries, code 10 s. Only `timeout`, `unavailable`, `rate_limited`, `upstream_5xx`, `connection_reset` and `busy` are ever retried (`RETRY_CODES`; the schema refuses any other name); the wait between tries is a durable sleep, so a restart repeats nothing and loses nothing, and a retried write carries the one idempotency key. New optional step keys `timeout_ms`, `retry`, `on_fail { steps, then }` and `verify { check, essential, say, readback }`, and Flow keys `on_failure`, `concurrency`, `lock` and `stuck_after_ms` (the last three arrive with waves 2 and 3; the schema takes them now). A failed step's ledger entry records `status: failed`, its tries and error; `on_fail` steps read `error`, `then: continue` records `failed_handled` and the run goes on, `stop` fails it after the handler; a Flow-level `on_failure` runs once before the run is called failed, and survives a restart without repeating its work. A failure path's steps count for the Flow's declared powers and names (`walkSteps`, `needs`, the connection expansion) and cannot have a failure path of their own. VERIFY: an expression over `output` after the step acted, essential by default (`verify_failed`, never retried) or `essential: false` (flagged on the ledger and on the run's new `attention` field); `readback: true` re-reads a written record. A model-written Flow is warned for each write with no verify. `retry(run, { skip, value, version })` resumes at the failed step: skip refuses when a later step reads the output unless a value is given (recorded with who supplied it; an assistant's call cannot carry the value, the person accepts it), `version: "latest"` re-pins only when every done step still exists with the same kind. New `cancel(run)` (the `cancelled` state is now set), and `flows.cancel`. A `decide` or `repeat` takes none of these keys yet (the schema refuses them rather than ignore them).
- feat(context): receipts and a facts ledger in the rollover seed (R031-00q). Vyre already rolls a session over before its window fills and starts a fresh one with a seed; the seed now also says what the closed window did and what it established. Each tool result leaves a receipt on its `thread.tool` event (lib/receipt.js, made in core/switchboard/translate.js): one word (ok, held, refused, error), a count, a size and up to three id-shaped values under id-like keys; never output text, never a sealed placeholder or a credential-shaped string. The seed gets "Work done so far" (the last 60 calls, one line each, older ones counted) and "Established so far" (ids folded to the last value per tool and key, the facts the thread was told to keep from memory.writes, reminders it set, items held at the Gate), both quoted as data, derived at seed time from the event log and existing stores with no new store and no memory write. Only at rollover, so the prompt cache is rebuilt anyway; nothing changes between rollovers. A person's own terminal session (`vyre roll`) gets the ledger parts Recall and memory give but no receipts. VYRE_MANAGED_CONTEXT=off leaves both out (only the token proof sets it). The token proof gains the task `long` and the arms `roll-off`, `roll-seed` and `roll-ledger`.
- feat(tools): tools_find follow-ups (a), (b), (d). (a) It returns five: the best three in full with a ready call, the next two compactly (name, 80 characters, the arguments they need); on the held-out set B the right tool is in the top five for 90% of intents (top three 86%). (d) A weak answer (nothing found, a top score under 25, or the top two within 10%) adds a line pointing at vyre_core, the map of modules, so the model can browse; about half of such answers are wrong. (b) It learns from what happens next: when the call that follows a find is one of the tools it showed, the pairing (the ask's word stems from the tool vocabulary, never a name or a number, and the tool) is written to tools-learned.json in the Vyre home (mode 0600, 400 pairings, least recently used out, not synced), and a similar ask later scores that tool up to 60% higher: a habit lifts a near neighbour, not a poor match over a clear one (lib/tools-learn.js).
- fix(token-proof): the proof's thread no longer dies at its first tool call. Claude Code asks the host before an agent uses a Vyre tool (can_use_tool, raised as a permission ask); in a real thread the person answers at the Deck, and nobody did in the proof, so the run ended with "Tool permission request failed" and no usage. The world now answers for the person (allow the Vyre tools, refuse the rest, as the owner). The stand-in claude gains `tooluse-ask`, which raises the same request and fails the same way when unanswered, and the tasks' stand-ins use it, so this is caught for nothing next time. `parseStream` now sums usage and cost from each message's last message_delta when no result event arrives, takes the answer from the last assistant words, and reports `firstTurnIn` (Claude Code's own prompt plus the listing, before any work) separately. --stand-in no longer needs VYRE_PROOF_PAID.
- feat(tools): tools_run, many steps in one call (R031-00o), and results by reference (R031-00p). `tools_run { steps, return }` takes up to 20 steps as JSON: `{ id, call, input, when? }` or `{ id, fn, inputs? }`, with `{ expr }` values read from earlier results in the Flows expression language (kernel/flows/expr.js; no eval, a step counter), and `fn` as the Flows Code step in its OS sandbox (no network, no files, no tool calls). It is written in lib/batch.js and runs in the MCP server: each call step is its own request to vyred's tool door under the agent's own identity and call id, so the same grants, reach, presence rules and Gate judge it, and there is no second door (this replaces the design's `POST /v1/batch` route, which would have needed the router's identity derivation copied). A held step ends the script and the answer gives the step and the held id; a refused (`presence_required`, `denied`, `not_found`) or failed step ends it; `tools_run`, `tools_call`, `tools_find`, `results_read`, `threads.*` and `agents.ask` do not run inside it; 20 steps and 60 s at most. A tool result over about 2,000 tokens is kept in the MCP server's memory (lib/results-store.js: 30 minutes, 64 MB per identity, oldest out, nothing on disk, gone on restart, bound to the caller and session that made it) and the model gets `{ handle, tokens, summary }`; `results_read { handle, select?, offset?, limit? }` returns a path or a page, capped at about 3,000 tokens, and `tools_call results_drop` frees one. Reads whose whole text is the answer (`docs.read`, `memory.turn`, `skills.get`, `artifacts.get`, `recall.thread`, the previews) are never turned into handles. The listing is 28 tools and 4,527 tokens (was 26 and 4,266). The token proof gains the arms `core-run`, `core-ref` and `core-both` (VYRE_MCP_FEATURES: `run`, `ref`, empty for both, `none` for neither; only the proof sets it) and the tasks `chain`, `biglist` and `both` on a world with 215 clients and 217 matters; the first ten tasks are the control.
- feat(tools): tools_find generalises beyond the intents it was tuned on (R031-00q). Every tool an agent has now carries everyday asks (`lib/tools-asks.js`, two lines per tool, 368 of 368), the ranker also scores the closest single ask by idf-weighted cosine, drops request filler ("let me know", "I have put"), expands a few multi-word phrases ("roll back", "put away") and a small set of everyday words (diary, ping, revert). Scores on held-out sets, pinned in test/tools-find-quality.test.js: before the work 47% top-1 / 69% top-3 on 51 new intents; an independent author's 51 (fresh4) scored 75% / 88% with the ask table and before it was tuned on its misses; an independent author's 49 written afterwards (fresh5, scored once) scored 71% / 86%. The 85% / 95% target is not met. The vault's development network seam now goes through `devSwitch`, so a release-kind build ignores it even with VYRE_SEAL_DEV=1.
- fix(mail)!: the mail adapter no longer dials a host without an address check (the IMAP/SMTP follow-up on consolidation inventory item 1). The default dial of `core/mail/imap.js` resolves the person's host through `lib/netguard.js` `resolveUserHost` and connects to the address it checked (a `lookup` on the socket, so a name cannot change its answer between the check and the dial). The person's own host is user-given, so a public address, a private-network address (192.168, 10, 172.16/12) and a tailnet address pass; loopback passes only when the host is itself a loopback name or address (a public name that resolves to this machine is refused); link-local (the cloud metadata address 169.254/16, fe80::/10), unspecified, multicast and the other special ranges never pass, and every answer for a name must pass. New helper `isLinkLocal` in netguard.
- refactor(presence)!: one yes at the floor, no proof headers, no presence sessions (one-yes, consolidation inventory item 4, step B). Only the three moments take a yes (`MOMENT_OPS` in `lib/one-yes.js`: pairing or widening reach, a vault secret or grant, an outward send; `gate.approve` and `apps.send` are named outward); every other tool the floor used to guard (about ninety) now needs only that the call is the person (a person surface or a signed-in person session), with no proof. A moment is given a yes in one of three forms, all ending in `yes()`: an approved card (`approvals.ask`, answered on the phone or by `approvals.local-yes`: Touch ID on a Mac through vyred's own dialog, or a code written to the person's login terminal), a device's signed yes (`x-vyre-yes`, bytes given in the refusal's `sign`), or a five-minute reuse (`vault.reveal`, `vault.copy`, `vault.totp` only, one device, never an agent) that a yes may ask for. The refusal names the moment and the exact request (`presence_required { moment, request, sign }`); a request with a long or nested input (a vault import) is bound by a digest of the whole input. Removed: the 30-minute presence session (`x-vyre-presence-keep`, `x-vyre-presence-session`, `presence.session.open`/`close`), the CLI terminal window, `core/presence` `SESSIONABLE`/`TERMINAL_WINDOWED`, and vyre-core's `presence.session.open`. Kept, named: signing in (`presence.person.start`) still takes its passkey or device-key proof, and enrolling the first key still takes its one-time code. A 0.3.0 client's `x-vyre-presence` header is checked at the server's edge and turned into a card admitted through `approvals.admit`, so `yes()` is still the only thing that says ok; each method is logged once as deprecated and the adapter goes in 0.3.2. Clients changed in the same release: the CLI (`core/cli/presence.js`: ask a card, confirm here or wait for the phone, retry with the card), the Deck (`web/js/api.js`), the app (`apps/app/src/real/box.ts`, the phone signs a yes with its own key; the Mac window asks vyred for Touch ID), the Mac's link to its box (`core/link/mac.js`), the relay bridge (passes `x-vyre-yes` and `x-vyre-approval`), the Capsule (`VyredClient.swift` and tests) and vyre-core (no sessions). The final split of tools, yes versus person only, is in the commit message and `team/0.3.1/SPEC-one-yes-clients.md`.
- fix(mail)!: the mail adapter no longer dials a host without an address check (the IMAP/SMTP follow-up on consolidation inventory item 1). The default dial of `core/mail/imap.js` resolves the person's host through `lib/netguard.js` `resolveUserHost` and connects to the address it checked (a `lookup` on the socket, so a name cannot change its answer between the check and the dial). The person's own host is user-given, so a public address, a private-network address (192.168, 10, 172.16/12) and a tailnet address pass; loopback passes only when the host is itself a loopback name or address (a public name that resolves to this machine is refused); link-local (the cloud metadata address in 169.254/16, and fe80::/10), unspecified, multicast and the other special ranges never pass, and every answer for a name must pass. New helper `isLinkLocal` in netguard.
- fix(mail)!: the mail adapter no longer dials a host without an address check (the IMAP/SMTP follow-up on consolidation inventory item 1). The default dial of `core/mail/imap.js` resolves the person's host through `lib/netguard.js` `resolveUserHost` and connects to the address it checked (a `lookup` on the socket, so a name cannot change its answer between the check and the dial). The person's own host is user-given, so a public address, a private-network address (192.168, 10, 172.16/12) and a tailnet address pass; loopback passes only when the host is itself a loopback name or address (a public name that resolves to this machine is refused); link-local (the cloud metadata address the cloud metadata address, fe80::/10), unspecified, multicast and the other special ranges never pass, and every answer for a name must pass. New helper `isLinkLocal` in netguard.
- refactor(approvals)!: what waits on the person is one queue (one-yes, consolidation inventory item 4, step C). The Gate's held drafts, a session's asks and the vault's pending grants, passes and requests are cards in the approvals queue (`core/approvals/items.js`, new tool `approvals.items`): a card appears when its owner holds the item, carries the owner's tool that settles it, and closes with the outcome the owner's event gave (`recent` keeps ten minutes of them); a card is rebuilt from the owner's own list on start and after its events, so a restart or a missed event leaves none behind, and an owner that cannot be read is named in `partial` with its cards kept. A yes waiting on the phone (the registry's held outward calls and the device cards) is a card of the same list (kind `approval`). `core/waiting` now reads that one source plus the planner's ringing reminders and the link's pairing requests; its asks and drafts adapters moved to the queue, the shared title cleaning is `lib/waiting-text.js`, and the list gains the kinds `approval` and `access` (the vault's requests, which no surface listed before). The detail screens stay with their modules (`gate.get`, `threads.asks`, `vault.pending`); `vault.pending` is now readable by Vyre's own modules. The one-yes walk lists the held card in `waiting.list`.
- refactor(vault)!: the vault's value tools stop asking a second time (one-yes, consolidation inventory item 4, step A). `core/vault/prove.js` (the interim presence gate, its `confirm: true` Deck form and its Touch ID cooldown) is deleted: reveal, copy, totp, resolve, render, inject, git get, native fill, session open, device code and unlock, and backup are held at the registry's floor like every other moment, which asks the one yes (`lib/one-yes.js`) once. The `confirm` input those tools took for the Deck's old proof is gone (nothing sent it). The tools that were only checked by prove.js's own list join the vault moment (`vault.git`, `vault.fill.native`, `vault.session.open`, `vault.device.code`, `vault.device.unlock`, `vault.backup`, `vault.export`), so a device's yes or an approved card covers them. `core/vault/touchid.js` stays: it is the enclave wrapper that unlocks the vault's own key, not a proof path. `scripts/one-yes-walk.mjs` walks the pair, vault and outward moments on a real daemon with a device yes.
- feat(http)!: one guarded client for requests that leave the machine, `lib/http.js` (consolidation inventory item 10): `httpFetch(url, init)` and `guardedFetch(defaults)`. It resolves the host itself, needs every answer to be a public address (lib/netguard.js), connects to the address it checked and checks the connected socket again, allows https only and no user:password in the URL, gives every request a deadline (30 s) and a size cap (4 MB, enforced while the body streams), follows at most 3 redirects (never https to http, re-checking each hop, dropping Authorization and Cookie across origins), and retries with backoff (250 ms doubling, Retry-After honoured to 5 s) on a network error, a timeout or 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE only (a POST only when the caller says `idempotent: true`). A test that replaces `globalThis.fetch` is honoured under the same URL and size rules. The module egress (kernel/modules/egress.js) and the credentialed API client (lib/api-endpoint.js `pinnedFetch`) now use its transport (`requestOnce`) instead of each writing the pinned request again.
- fix(http)!: production requests are public https only; the `"auto"` allow mode and `allowFor` are gone (they let rotation, pairing, voice, Google and the updater reach the daemon's own loopback ports, a way in for a request-forgery attack). A test that runs its fake on loopback calls `allowLoopbackForTests()` in lib/http.js, a switch only test files call: no environment variable or setting turns it on, and test/http-seam.test.js scans the source and starts a fresh process with every plausible switch set to prove it. `stream: true` answers at the headers (an event stream, with the deadline for the headers only).
- refactor(http): the MCP client, the S3 storage backend and the drive bridge (kernel/storage), the voice provider WebSocket handshake (address checked through lib/http.js `pin`) and the watcher child's host-side fetch (lib/sandbox/fetch.js, now on the shared `requestOnce` transport with the same cap-and-flag, host list and credential rules) go through the guarded client. test/http-single.test.js now also finds `lib.request(`.
- refactor(http): the GitHub calls (core/github: repos, mentions, pull requests, the connect flow) go through lib/http.js: api.github.com is reached by a checked public address, with a deadline, a size cap and a retry for the reads.
- refactor(http): the Google API client, the Google sign-in, the service-account token call (lib/connectors/auth.js), the ACME client and the connector OAuth discovery go through lib/http.js. Google and ACME may point at this machine in a test or a development setup (`autoFetch`: public, except loopback); OAuth discovery of a server the person connected is `userHostFetch`.
- refactor(http): the name directory and the identity directory (vyre.run), the Space-level deps (the VPS driver's DigitalOcean calls), the update check and the CLI's release downloads (1 GiB cap, loopback allowed for a local release server) go through lib/http.js.
- refactor(http): the vault's breach check, rotation and relay calls, the voice providers (64 MB cap for audio), the apps' weather adapter, the Wink relay resolve, the S3 storage client (the person's own endpoint, 512 MB cap) and the CLI's server probes (`userHostFetch`) go through lib/http.js. What still makes a raw request, and why, is the list in `test/http-single.test.js`, which fails on any file not in it.
- feat(watchers): the person is told when a watcher's schedule moved with the time zone. The first tick after the zone a watcher's cron runs in changes (the Space's zone differs from the machine's, which is what schedules used before), every enabled cron watcher is re-aimed at its next time in the new zone, and the watchers that really fire at another moment are named in a `watcher.schedule-moved` event and one planner to-do ("Watcher schedules now follow the Space's time zone ... 2 fire at a different time than before: ..."). Said once; a watcher whose time did not move is not listed.
- refactor(bytes)!: base32 and canonical JSON are each written once (consolidation inventory item 7). base32 (RFC 4648, lower case, no padding) is `lib/bytes.js`, promoted from relay/client/bytes.js; the device client's copy is generated from it by `scripts/sync-copies.mjs` because the Windows capsule ships relay/client/*.js alone. The copies in core/relay/wire.js, core/names/rules.js, core/wink/grants.js, core/vault/crypto.js (in capitals), core/vault/otpmigration.js, lib/identity/directory.js and both recovery-code generators (core/spaces and the app) are gone. Canonical JSON is `kernel/core/canonical.js`: the copies in the app's payload hash and the iPhone signer, core/link (assert and companion), kernel/flows/schema.js, core/vault/crypto.js and lib/publish/util.js now import it (a value that is undefined at the top still reads "null"). Stricter: NaN, Infinity and class instances now throw instead of encoding as null or {}. The few that stay are named with their reason in `test/bytes-single.test.js` (the pinned identity files, which import nothing but node:crypto, the sealing protocol's reference form, the presence input hash pair, the two Cloudflare Workers, the relay's browser app, hashes already stored over values that can hold bytes), and a corpus holds every one of them to the kernel's bytes.
- refactor(cron)!: a cron schedule is parsed and stepped in one place, lib/cron.js (consolidation inventory item 12): `parseCron`, `nextCron(src, after, tz)` and `describeCron`. Flows (kernel/flows/compile.js, whose `parseCron`/`nextCron` are now re-exports; kernel/flows/zone.js keeps only the zone check) and the watchers (core/watchers/cron.js is a thin shape of it) use the same code, so a watcher and a Flow with the same schedule fire at the same moment. One behaviour changes, by ruling: a watcher's schedule now runs in the Space's time zone (the planner's configured zone, else the server's own) instead of the machine's local time; on a server whose zone is its Space's zone nothing moves, and `watchers.list` names the zone beside a clock time ("every day at 09:00 (Europe/Berlin)"). Daylight saving follows lib/time for watchers too (a skipped wall time runs once, moved on; a repeated one runs once). `test/cron-single.test.js` fails when a source file outside lib/cron.js parses cron fields of its own.
- refactor(ws)!: RFC 6455 framing is written once, in lib/ws.js (consolidation inventory item 13). `FrameParser` now parses both directions (`{ masked, max }`: a client's masked frames or a server's unmasked ones, with a size limit and the close status code), `encodeFrame(payload, opcode, mask)` frames both ends, and `upgradeHead(key, extra)` is the whole `101` answer. local/voice/ws.js (its own frame encoder and parser), core/relay/wsclient.js (the bridge's client half) and the seven hand-written `101` answers in Glass, the stream router, the terminal, the relay and voice are thin users of it. core/computers/image/computerd/ws.js, the computers image's copy, is now generated from lib/ws.js by `scripts/sync-copies.mjs` (which also writes the extension's shared/sk copies; it replaces `scripts/sync-sk.mjs`, and `test/sk-sync.test.js` is `test/generated-copies.test.js`). `test/ws-single.test.js` fails when a source file outside a short list writes a handshake or a frame header of its own.
- refactor(ids)!: a record id is minted in one place, lib/id.js (consolidation inventory item 11). Thirty local `prefix_` + random-bytes mints are gone: artifacts (`a_`), goals (`g_`), the planner (`i_`, `f_` ...), vault agents, items, connections, sharing, emergency access and the `said` log (`ag_`, `cn_`, `e_`, `s_`, the item ids), Flows (`fl_`, `run_` ...), the importer (`plan_`, `imp_`), publishing holds (`hold_`), undo (`u_`), streams (`st_`), sign-in asks (`si_`), recovery requests (`rec_`), connection proposals (`prop_`), the GitHub, Google and OAuth connect flows (`gh_`, `gc_`, `oa_`), hook deliveries (`hd_`), memory (`iq_`, `mw_`), module-list reset asks (`rr_`), plugin agents (`pa_`), recall watches (`w_`) and the SSH agent's requests. New ids are `prefix_` + a time-ordered uuid (sorting them sorts by creation, and an id says when it was made); ids already stored are never rewritten, so the artifact id check now accepts both shapes. Secrets, tickets, nonces and passwords are not ids and stay random bytes, and a few ids keep their own shape for a stated reason (Space ids, invite ids, the sealing process, terminal socket names, a short code a person types; each is named with its reason in the test). `test/ids-single.test.js` fails when a source file mints a record id of its own.

## Unreleased
- feat(kernel): step A of the one grant model (team/0.3.1/DESIGN-one-grant.md). Three access levels for credentials in kernel/seal/uses.js (use: fill, totp, read, call; reveal: use and show the value; manage: reveal and change, delete, share, rotate and pass access on), with `vault.edit` and `vault.delete` as actions; an assistant can hold use and nothing more, whoever gives it. Teams are a grant subject (`{ kind: "group", id }`): an owner or admin makes one, a grant to it reaches each person in it and their assistants by association, never more than the person. Named vaults (`gw.grants.vaults`): any member makes one and holds manage on it, shares a part of it as a child grant (a manager passes on what they hold, nothing more), and a personal vault is its owner's alone. A project's people and assistants are a group (`project:<id>`) for the one-step offer "also let this project's members use it"; the person's own key is still needed. A grant can now name the exact origins a login may be used at (`conditions.where.origins`, `authorize` input `origin`). Nothing existing changes: the Vault and Connections move onto this in step B.
- feat(vault)!: step B of the one grant model: lending a login to an agent (`vault.agent.grant`, `.grants`, `.revoke`) is a kernel grant now, not a table of the vault's own. The grant is the agent (its stable id), `vault.fill`, the item's address under the owner's personal vault, one exact origin (`where.origins`) and an expiry; the person's own session makes it (as the child of their `manage` on the vault), an assistant's request still waits for `vault.approve` as a request row that carries no authority, and taking one away needs no one (the kernel lets the vault module end what it lent, `takeBack`, also when the login is deleted, so a login made again under that name inherits nothing). The older `vault_agent_grants` rows are carried over once at start: a row that passes its MAC becomes the same grant (same agent, login, origin and expiry), one that fails is dropped, and the table is emptied. A model can no longer list what a person lent; it sees the logins it may use and where (`vault.agent.grants` as an assistant asks the kernel one login and one host at a time). Grant ids are the kernel's (`gr_`); a request keeps `ag_`. A project's people are read from its `project.reach` grants (an agent given every project is on all of them), so "also let this project's members use it" follows the real project; a grant to `project:<id>` names a project that exists. Deletes the agent-grant table code of core/vault/agents.js (MAC rows, pending, approve, revoke, list, grantFor: about 120 lines).
- feat(vault): the Vault MCP for outside agents (R031-77). A person makes a pass for chosen api credentials (`vault.mcp.pass.create`, from the Vault's New pass sheet: who, how long up to 90 days, which credentials, which hosts, how many calls, whether it may ask to see a value) and gets a token once and the line to give the outsider (`claude mcp add --transport http ...`, or Codex). The outsider's agent talks to POST `/vault-mcp` (off unless `vault.mcp.port` is set; the relay carries it out) with three tools, `vault_list`, `vault_request` and, only when allowed, `vault_reveal_ask`: a call runs at the vault's home through the same relay as `vault.request` (the credential's own hosts and rules, the key added there, never returned; a read runs, anything that changes something is held for its owner), and a value is never sent. A pass is kernel grants (`vault.read` and `vault.call` on its items, an expiry, a rate) to its own actor `ext_<id>` inside what its issuer holds, so taking the issuer's access away stops it. The token is stored as a hash, compared in constant time; a pass has a rate, a source that sends five wrong tokens is locked out for ten minutes, and every refusal is a `vault.mcp-refused` event; every use is an audit row and the kernel's decision. `vault.mcp.pass.revoke` ends a pass at once. `vault_fill` is deferred to 0.3.2. The public gate carries it: exactly POST `/vault-mcp` with a JSON body of at most 64 KB reaches the vault's loopback listener, the Authorization header kept, the gate's own per-source limit (60 a minute) in front of the vault's, every other path under the gate unchanged (core/wink/control/gate.js, one more ingress shape beside `/hooks/<route>`); the gate's address is what a new pass names. Reveal: when a pass allows it, an ask to see a value waits for the owner (vault.pending mcpReveals; `vault.mcp.reveal.allow` with a fresh yes, `vault.mcp.reveal.clear` to decline); once allowed the agent's next `vault_reveal_ask { id }` poll returns the value a single time and it is gone, logged as `vault.revealed-to-pass` with the pass and the item, never the value. The New pass sheet: filled-with-a-check choices, a switch for "May ask to see a value", "Call limit (optional)", and two copy buttons over one-line code boxes in the made state. A pass's grants record the owner's manage as their parent and the owner as issuer, so taking the owner's access away cuts the pass.
- feat(vault)!: an agent's or the assistant's call through an API credential (`vault.request` from a model) is decided by a kernel grant, not the credential's static `scope`, and the assistant is no longer exempt. The kernel is asked of the agent's stable id (never the default assistant's delegate shortcut): `vault.read` for a read (runs at once under a grant), `vault.call` for anything outward (still held for a person), no grant means refused, not held. A model's `vault.list` shows exactly the credentials it holds a grant for. Existing scopes are converted to grants once when the vault first runs with agents up (`vault:scope` grants, a named agent each, a project's group, every agent for a scope of everyone), the assistant is carried over for every credential that existed, and each conversion is an audit row (`scope-converted`) and a `vault.scope-converted` event; a credential made later is reached by grants alone. A task's doer can be lent Connections for that task (`vault.connections.lend { task, agent, connections, until }` and `.end { task }`, the flows module only): the vault asks `flows.kit.credentials { task }` for the approved Kit version and the credentials it names, refuses any other or missing Connection, makes use-only grants on the Connection (read runs, outward still held) that end at `until` or at `.end`, are idempotent per task, agent and Connection, record the Kit and version, and hang from the owner's manage (a fourth `carryOver` shape, `lease`, with `takeBack` by source). A build with no kernel keeps the older scope check.
- feat(vault)!: step B, module release, on the one grant model: which module may be handed which item (`vault.grant`, `vault.revoke`, `vault.granted`, `vault.pending`/`approve` for them, the module check of `vault.totp` and `vault.request`, backups) is a grant in the kernel's shape: the module's service actor, the new action `vault.release`, the item's address (`watcher/<w>/` for one watcher, a `project` predicate for one project), source `install:<module>:vault`. One format and one checking code, in two homes: on a server the kernel holds the grants (the vault asks it to lend them, and takes them back); in vyre-core, which does not trust vyred's kernel (ADR 0040), the same grants sit in the vault's own `vault_grants` table (a `body` column, written only by core). Both ask `matchGrant`, now the pure core of the authorizer (kernel/core/authorize.js, which `evaluate` uses too). The older rows are converted in place when the vault opens (a row that passes its older check becomes its grant, one that fails is dropped, a waiting request moves to `vault_grant_requests`, where an assistant's requests wait without authority). `vault.revoke` is async. Shared vault roles (owner, admin, member, read-only) stay the signed words peers verify, written once as the access levels (`ROLE_LEVEL` in core/vault/shared.js, with a round-trip test); the limit that people in a shared vault hold its key is in DESIGN-vaults-named.md. The kernel cap is 9440 (one grant model C plus module release).
- feat(vault)!: step C of the one grant model: where a Connection may be used is a kernel grant. Opening a connection to a surface (`vault.connections.grant`) is a grant to the group `surface:<capsule|chat|agents|phone>` at the connection's address (`vyre://<space>/connection/<id>`), at the use level, made by the person on their own session with no fresh proof (the tool still asks for Touch ID before it hands a credential to `agents`); closing one (`vault.connections.revoke`, still only a surface's own) takes the grant back, and a connection that is removed or fails its check loses what was granted on it. The group reaches any chain that came in through that surface (`SURFACE_GROUPS` in kernel/seal/uses.js: capsule, mobile, mcp, harness), so a caller with a real chain can ask `authorize` directly. The row's `surfaces` column now holds only the seed it started with (capsule and chat for a row a person saw coming) until that is changed. A connection's grants are listed with every other grant.
- refactor: one list of Space roles. kernel/contracts exports ROLE_RANK and ROLE_LABELS beside ROLE_IDS; the app's roles and Rules screens, the planner's types, the core record types, the Flows host (which left out `temp`, so a temp member could not be assigned), a Kit's CORE_ROLES (which listed three of the five), the grants' MAY_SET, the members' MANAGEABLE and the Kit and Flows fixtures import them instead of typing the five again. The vault's sharing roles are VAULT_MEMBER_ROLES and Wink's invitation roles WINK_PAIR_ROLES, so nobody mistakes them for Space roles. test/one-role-list.test.js fails on a source file that types the five again.

## 0.3.0 (9 Oct 2026)
- fix(box): `box/vyre` is shellcheck-clean again (need_docker names the verb from VYRE_VERB only; the app-line split is marked as intended).
- docs(site): the vyre.run direction page and the home direction section say what 0.3.0 ships (watch the work, one yes for a group, connect any app, signatures inside Vyre, modules that feel built in, back online by itself) and name the backup gap (records are not carried yet); Next reads 0.3.1 (projects with AI teammates, backups that carry records, your own app modules) and Screen Share moves to Later in llms.txt to match. Generated by scripts/gen-site.mjs; the pages are written at release time (VYRE_SITE_VERSION=0.3.0).
- perf(harness): tool answers to agents are compact JSON (no indentation), so every tool call costs fewer tokens.
- fix(ci): the J2 upgrade, J2c cosign-refusals and J8 data matrix scripts seed the way the J2b ones now do (they failed on a bare box: the candidate was unsigned so no module booted, and planner and personal memory need the record store and a person). The candidate is signed with a throwaway key pinned in the runner checkout (`scripts/matrix/j2-pin-key.mjs`), boxes install on the built-in store, and J2 and J2c seed two files in the home volume; J8 seeds a planner note on the built-in store, so its export and import carry real data (memory is no longer part of its world). Test setup only.
- fix(ci): the J2b update-refusals run is green again. Its candidate was unsigned, so the box (a packaged, kernel-on daemon) booted no module and the installer, which now fails loudly when none start, stopped the install ("Vyre is running but none of its modules started"); it had failed this way on main since 4 Oct. The candidate is now signed with a throwaway key pinned in the runner checkout (`scripts/matrix/j2-pin-key.mjs`, CI only), installs on the built-in store (no Records stack on a runner), and seeds two files in the box home volume (planner and personal memory need the record store and a person). Case 5e (default pin) is the wrong-signer case once the candidate is pinned to that key.
- fix(app): Vault in plain words (issue #64). The device's confirm prompt says what is being done ("Save Juniper Drive") and never the tool name; a login's Username is required and every empty required field shows its error under the field; "Who has it" says what holding means; a Held fields note explains sealed values; the Unlock card goes away once a save has gone through.

A Contact's e-mail may be a list. The Space helper's app tests ran 470 s in one file against a 300 s limit and were killed as hung in the full run; they are now four files of 55 to 180 s.

The seven read tools that reach anyone say why (reach-anyone.json), appmods relaying the person to `connectors.connection.create` and `.delete` is listed as a person-proxy with its reason, `lib/views/engine.js` and `core/connectors/index.js` are on the reviewed list of computed calls (the views engine moved out of local/capsule), and the appmods family is in the sessions brief's families.
- feat(appmods,records,app): the app is called **Documents**, never by the engine's name, wherever a person reads it: the card, the views, the events (`documents.signed`, `documents.form-completed`), the app's address (`documents.<name>.vyre.run`), its Connection and the notices. Settings, About, Open-source credits names DocuSeal with a link to its source (AGPL-3.0); its own small attribution on the signing pages is left as it is. The app ships a Kit: a **Document** record (name, status, template, signer's e-mail, signed, file, submission, linked to the signer's Contact and to a Project) and a ready Flow that, when `documents.signed` arrives, finds the Contact by the signer's e-mail, files the Document linked to them (the signed copy is already in the Drive) and stamps the Contact's "last signed". The install proposes the Kit as the installing person; the owner's yes in Now defines it. A Contact with an e-mail gets **Send for signature** in the app when Documents is installed: it opens the send view with the e-mail already in the form (`views` field defaults and a `q` on the module route). Tested on the live DocuSeal rig (docuseal-live.test.js): the Document is filed and linked to the Contact, the Contact lists it, and its timeline has it. NOT done: the engine's open-source build has no logo or colours setting (its account has no such field; personalisation is its paid edition), so the Space's logo and colours are not applied to the signing pages.
- fix(gate,approvals,modules): a send the person already approved with a card is not held a second time. When the registry spends an approved outward card (`yes()` ok for the exact tool, input digest and asker), the call carries a registry-only Symbol mark (`lib/covered.js`; never from input, not serializable, gone after the call) that a first-party module's nested `gate.request` inherits. The Gate trusts it only when it asks `approvals.cover` (internal, Gate only) and the approvals module confirms that card was redeemed for this tool, input digest and asker within 2 minutes and not yet used by the Gate, and only the module that owns that tool may use it (a card for billing.email cannot release a send reminder.send files in the same turn); the card is then spent and the send goes out at once as `card:<id>`, recorded in the Gate's audit log. One card covers one send: a second send in the same call, another email, a forged `covered` field, a made-up card id, a client, or an added module is held as before. `test/gif-story.test.js` (4 tests) walks the README story end to end and these cases.
- fix(connectors,modules,appmods): a view over a wrapped app's Connection now works against the real app (proved with the live DocuSeal test: the "Waiting for signature" view shows a document just sent and "Send for signature" lists the template). Three things stood between the view and the app: `connectors.operation.run` could not relay the person to `vault.request` (the relay check allowed only a credential write and delete; it now also allows `vault.request` of a Connection's own `conn-<id>` credential by operation, never a free-form url or another credential), the views read the app's answer at `body.data` (the request tool's envelope), and `templates.list` declared no `limit` for the query the view sends.
- fix(appmods,views): an app's Vyre views are listed only while its Connection exists (a view that names a Connection other than `self` is hidden until one is made, and goes when it is removed). Found by the test for it: DocuSeal's Connection was refused by the Connections module (`submissions.get` and `submissions.documents` name `{id}` in the path but declared no params), so every install had silently ended with "no Connection yet". Both operations now declare their `id`, and the install makes the Connection.
- fix(gate): a send the person already approved with a card is not held a second time. When the registry spends an approved outward card for a tool call, a first-party module that files a send through the Gate for that call is told so, once; the Gate sends it at once. One card covers one send, a second send in the same call, another kind, or a module that is not Vyre's own is held as before. Before, the group yes was followed by a second yes per email at the Gate. test/gif-story.test.js walks the README gif's whole story on a real daemon.
- fix(app): the group card's closing line names what was sent from the tool the card is for (`request.op`), not from the signed act, which is `task.outward_act` for every outward call.
- feat(box,appmods): the app's `APP_URL` is its public address, `https://<module>.<name>.vyre.run:<port>`, when the box has a name on vyre.run (root reads the name and the public gate's port through the vyre container's node and keeps them only if they fit that shape; otherwise the internal address stays). The same value goes to the setup script. Opening DocuSeal's signing links for people outside the team is NOT built: the app's origin is for the owner and admins.
- feat(appmods,connectors): DocuSeal feels built in. The appmods module declares two Vyre views over DocuSeal's Connection, drawn in Vyre's own look and run as the person who opened them: "Waiting for signature" (the pending submissions, by template and signer) and "Send for signature" (the templates, each with a form for the signer's e-mail; the send is outward, so it shows its exact words first and waits for the person's yes). `connectors.operation.run` also takes `self` (the calling module's own app) or an app name where a Connection id goes. `purge-app` removes the app's image too, unless another app that still has a folder runs the same digest. The DocuSeal card says outside signers come with the public address.
- fix(app): chat polish from the shots review: a step shows its plain words and the tool name one tap away; Copy, Highlight and Reply sit in one row that shows on hover (desktop) or a long press (phone); the composer chip names the model (no fit score); thought, step and hand-off rows are denser; the hand-off row has the teammate's avatar and the project.
- feat(app): the chat draws a hand-off ("Asked kit (billing)", its state, the report-back as quoted data) with the teammate's own steps nested under it (data.via), the sample world has an activity scenario (/chat-demo?scenario=activity), the held-group card can draw a given group (sample prop, /shots-approval), and a chat-shots workflow photographs them in dark and light at desktop and phone width.
- refactor: the view engine and frames live in lib/views (the Capsule and core/views both use them), the Mac server's always-online rules in lib/online.js, and the peer door asks the sidebar module's handle for its service by name: three boundary edges gone, none frozen.
- feat(modules): a view can run a Connection's operation. Where a view's list, detail, action or form names a tool it may name `{ connection, operation, input }` instead; it is written out as the new `connectors.operation.run`, so a wrapped app's everyday screens ("Documents waiting for signature") are Vyre views in the Capsule, the app and Lumen like any module's. A module reaches only the Connection of its own app and only the operations that Connection declares (never the generic request); a send, change or delete is the vault's own outward call, held for the person's yes. docs/MODULES.md says so.
- fix(mac-app): the Mac app keeps its identity key, Secure Enclave key, key-agreement key and presence key as ONE Keychain item, read once per launch and held in memory, so a build signed ad hoc asks for the Keychain once (and Always Allow covers the rest) instead of up to four times (IR-33, item 1.10). An older install's four items move in on the first read and are taken away.
- feat(app): Now shows "Vyre <version> is out" with an Update now button (or the command, when the box cannot update itself from the app), and Settings, About shows the version with one button: Check for updates, or Update to <version> when a release is out (item 1.9). The update is still the box's own signed one (update.apply).
- fix(always-online): the Mac server installer checks FileVault before installing anything and stops in plain words unless the line is run with VYRE_ACCEPT_FILEVAULT=1 (--yes alone no longer accepts it); the app card and `vyre doctor` say the same.
- feat(always-online): a Mac server says whether FileVault is on (system.info filevault), and the Add a server card warns when it is: "FileVault is on: after a power cut this Mac waits for someone to sign in. For a server, turn FileVault off, or keep it and accept that."
- feat(always-online): the app says "Your server has been offline since 14:02" with what to check (a Mac server that restarted may be waiting at its login window) when it cannot reach its server for a minute or more, instead of a screen that hangs; a Linux box's installer makes Docker start at boot so the restart policy brings the server back; install.md says how a server comes back by itself.
- feat(always-online): a Mac server comes back by itself. The server install sets the power settings (pmset: start after a power cut, never sleep, wake on network, no Power Nap) and boot-tests the LaunchDaemons (loaded, RunAtLoad, KeepAlive); install-mac-server.sh stops and asks before installing on a Mac with FileVault on (it never changes FileVault); `vyre doctor` checks both and `vyre doctor --repair` fixes the power settings; core/vyre-core/online.js holds the rules (and the authrestart choice for a planned restart).
- fix(box,appmods): found by the first run on a real server. The Space helper's watcher is a long-running process of the wrapper that was installed when it started, so after an update or a re-install it kept re-walling with the old code and knew no apps: an update and `space-helper install` now restart it. A running app whose walls fail their proof right after the vyre container restarts is looked at again twice, four seconds apart, before it is stopped. DocuSeal's setup script is safe to run twice (a reinstall over the data an earlier removal kept): it reuses the account, the user, the certificate and the token, sets the password and the webhook again, and prints the same lines.
- fix(box,appmods): the root helper no longer writes into an app's container. The one-time setup script reaches the command on its stdin (`docker exec -i ... bin/rails runner -`) instead of `docker cp`, so a third-party container (and, later, a person's own image) cannot turn root's copy into a symlink race. Catalog images are no longer pulled at every install and update: the line is recorded, and `app-up` pulls the pinned digest when it is not on the machine. `sudo vyre admin purge-app <app>` (a terminal and a typed word, never a request) removes the rules, the app, its volumes and root's folder for it, and `admin wipe` removes every app too.

- fix(security): an added module can never name a tool that pairs, admits or drops a device or sets the server up (the relay, link, wink and presence families, except their read-only status tools). `vyre module check` and the loader refuse a manifest that lists one, and a call to one from an added module is denied whatever its needs.tools say. test/added-module-never.test.js runs real added modules in a real daemon with the real presence check.

- feat(chat): ask another model on an answer (`stream.second-opinion { chat, message, to }`). - feat(app): the held group is a card (11.8). On Now and in the conversation, an assistant's waiting calls read as one card with each item's exact words, a Drop or an Edit on any, and one yes that signs each approved item over its own hash (src/real/group-approve.js, screens/shell/GroupApprovals.tsx); an item shown only in part is left out of the yes. The closing line says what went out ("Sent 3 emails. Each is logged on its client." where the sent mail is filed).
- feat(app): notices when you are not looking (11.8, 12.8). src/native/notices.ts asks the server over the connection the app already keeps for what waits for your yes and for a turn that finished, and shows each once as a local notice (no push service, no token); an iPhone shows it when the app opens. Delivery while the app is closed on Android needs the foreground service named in native-core's notes, which is not built.
- feat(chat): ask another model on an answer (`stream.second-opinion { chat, message, to }`). The chat shows one short line from the person, a reply to the answer, and the other assistant or model is given the question, the whole answer and the earlier turns, all read from the chat's own log, and told to answer from scratch and say where it differs. It works where the first answer was made and goes through the chat's ordinary send, so the Gate, membership and accounting are the usual ones. The other model must already be in the chat.
- feat(stream): a hand-off to a teammate is a row in the asker's conversation (a `handoff` frame: queued, running with the teammate's session, done or failed with its report), and the teammate's tool steps are appended to the same conversation with `via`, so a screen nests them under the row. They are cursored like every frame, so a closed screen opens from its last cursor and gets what it missed. The team module says `reply_to`, `role`, `text` and `result` on `summon.*` events and emits `summon.thread`. Frames and rules: team/0.3/IFACE-activity.md.
- feat(gate): grouped approval. An assistant's outward calls held within 90 seconds of each other are one group in `approvals.pending`, each card with every value the yes covers, flattened with its path (`to[0]`, `headers.bcc`, `attachments[1].name`, `amount`). A call too large to show whole is `partial`: its card says part of it is not shown, and it cannot be approved inside a group yes, only on its own. `approvals.answer-group` takes one decision per item and one proof per approved item, each over that item's own request, so a yes cannot cover another item or a later one; an item with no decision stays waiting and a dropped item is not held against the asker. `approvals.edit-item` lets the person change the words of one text field before approving, which makes the card again over the new call, and the call that runs is the edited one.
- fix(approvals): a card the registry held now names its asker as its device. Before, the asker's retry with the approved card was refused as a wrong request.
