- feat(modules): an added module may ship a Kit (`does.kits`), in the records language's stored form or the kernel's. `vyre module add` proposes it under the rules a module's Kit has (its id is the module's name, its types are named for the module, no roles, no teammates, no project type), and a record type relates to projects with a link to `project`. A real-daemon test installs a module with a Kit, links records to a project, upgrades the module and its Kit, and checks nothing is lost.
- feat(chat): the one pass over the chat screen (12.1 copy, 12.2 find, 12.3 keyboard, 12.4 header, 12.7 optimistic send). Copy and Copy as Markdown on each finished answer, and one Copy code per fenced block; Cmd/Ctrl-F finds in the conversation (count, next and previous, the match scrolled to and lit); Up in an empty composer edits the last message, Esc stops (or closes find), Cmd-Enter steers a working assistant, Cmd-K opens the chat list, Cmd-1..9 open the nth chat; the header says the project and which AI answers and never an id or a path; a sent message shows at once, dimmed, and the box's echo replaces it (a refused send takes it back). Pure rules in src/chat/polish.js; the folder owns the placeholder (frames.js addOptimistic).
- feat(lumen): the conversation view (11.5). A conversation with an agent is drawn from its activity feed: a header with who, the project and the state, a thinking line that shows the latest thought and opens to the whole, step rows that tick from running to done, "Asked kit (billing)" hand-off rows with the teammate's own steps nested under them and the report-back as quoted data, follow-ups typed in the same bar, and ⌘O to open the whole conversation in Vyre chat. ActivityFeed (Core) folds the stream frames of IFACE-activity.md; ActivityLink (Host) follows the chat's stream from the first frame the log holds; stills of four moments are in the lumen-screens artifact.
- feat(views): a module's screens drawn by Vyre in the app. `views` in the manifest (list, detail, form, and the new `board` and `summary`) is the Capsule's `view:` language promoted to the whole app; shows.capsule's `view:<id>` entries are the older name for the same declaration and the status folds them together. New core module `views` (views.list, views.get, views.act) shares one engine with capsule.* (core/views/engine.js, frames.js); the app draws the frames with its own components (ViewHost) and no module code runs in its window. An outward action previews its exact words and sends only with the preview's token. A view is a sidebar screen (`view: true` in sidebar.get's modules), so a pin is { kind: "module", module, screen: <view id> }. The Capsule lists only the views it can draw.
- test(proof): `scripts/proof-install.mjs --live --host <ssh host>` is the real walk: a throwaway name reserved and claimed on names.vyre.run, the relay at relay.vyre.run, and a real server installed over ssh with the exact line the app's Add a server shows (the published installer), once with Records and once without, with the team-space step and a full wipe at the end. `scripts/proof-live-drop.mjs` frees the names it made with the support admin drop. `--expect-version X.Y.Z` makes the walk update the first server from the app as Settings does (waits for the release to be offered, requests it, checks the same app signs in again and records answer), and `scripts/proof-live-droplet.mjs` runs the whole walk on a fresh droplet it makes and always destroys.
- feat(names): the support-only admin drop also frees a name an IDENTITY holds (its keys lost, the person starting again), with no tombstone, so it can be reserved afresh.
- feat(records): a sent email is logged on the client it went to. When the Gate sends a held email, core/daemon/sent-mail-log.js files one Communication (subject and the first words of the body, not the body) on every Contact the recipients belong to, by main address then contact point, keyed on the Gate item so a repeat files nothing new. A failure is a log line; the email has already gone.
- feat(records): a sent email is logged on the client it went to. When the Gate sends a held email, core/daemon/sent-mail-log.js files one Communication (subject and the first words of the body, not the body) on every Contact the recipients belong to, by main address then contact point, keyed on the Gate item so a repeat files nothing new. It reads the Gate's own email shape and a Gmail send made through a Connection (the raw message in the held request). A failure is a log line; the email has already gone.
- test(lumen): "Lumen on a Mac paired to a server with an assistant" runs on Wink. test/wink-world.js pairs a real box vyred and a real Mac vyred the way Wink leaves them (the paired-server record and an open peer session, through the new peerSeams test seam in core/wink/serverlink.js), scripts/capsule-paired-check.mjs drives the built Lumen against it, and the capsule-mac step is back.
- fix(security): only first-party modules may reach another machine. wink.server.call, wink.server.home and ctx.remote refuse an added module before any pairing check or forward; Vyre's own modules are unchanged. test/remote-first-party.test.js covers every model, hook and added-module caller; the HD-3 test now runs with the device machine, where the tool exists.
- refactor!: the 0.3.0 cleanup lands on the current main (work/cleanup-tailnet merged as cleanup-tailnet-2): Mac federation, every tailnet caller kind, the mounted-folder Drive (Taildrive), the old owner wizard (web/onboard) and the old Deck onboarding page are gone, and main's newer code wins everywhere else. The no-tailscale ratchet falls from 197 files to 110, known-red loses the three test files that went with federation and the link (federation-answer, federation-send, link), and kernel/golden matches cells by caller and world name so a dropped caller no longer reads as every later caller changing.
- fix(site): assemble-site.sh leaves release files over the 25 MiB Cloudflare Pages limit out of /box (the apps are linked from the GitHub release), and refuses if one the installers fetch is over it; the v0.2.12 site deploy stopped on the dmg and APK.
- fix(release): the Android release-notes line no longer ends the release job with an apostrophe inside a single-quoted printf; every bash run step in the workflows is now checked with bash -n (test/workflows-yaml.test.js).
- feat(appmods,wink,names): the front door for an app module's own host, `<module>.<name>.vyre.run`. The names Worker's `publish` takes `apps: true` and then also points `*.<name>` at the same address (cleared when the last app is removed, and with the name); the public gate orders a certificate for `[name, *.name]` (same key, so the pin does not move) only while an app is installed, publishes the wildcard only once that certificate is in hand, and answers `appsChanged()` when the first app is installed or the last removed. The gate has a new ingress kind: a request whose Host is exactly one label under the box's name (and, over TLS, whose SNI is that same host) is matched against the installed RUNNING apps before any of it is read; an unknown label is the gate's plain 404 and its body is never read, a known one is carried to the apps' loopback front with the Host kept, any method and path, up to 64 MB streamed, under its own per-address budget (600 a minute); WebSocket stays refused. The install card says a server with no public address has no app screens but still runs the app for Flows and webhooks. Tests: gate, publicgate, netd, names Worker, lib/acme `covers`, and a whole path through a real gate to the apps' front in core/appmods/module.test.js.
- feat(appmods,box): app modules on a server whose vyred has no Docker. The root helper (box/vyre `space-helper`) takes three new requests, `app-up|app-stop|app-down <module>`, for a module root recorded out of the vyre image (`private/app-modules`, written at install and at every update: thirteen fields each from its own pattern, names and hook ports unique, no hook port that the vyre container listens on). It writes and lints its own compose file from core/appmods/host-plan.js, makes the app's keys itself (never given to the daemon), joins the vyre container to the app's internal network, walls it in both directions in the container's namespace (OUTPUT: only the daemon's uid reaches the app; INPUT on the app network's interface: tcp to the hook port from the app's subnet and the answers to what the daemon asked, DROP for the rest), proves both walls (a throwaway container on the app's network must time out at every other vyre port), then runs the app's one-time setup from an env file, not a command line, and hands its outputs to the daemon once in a file only the daemon's uid reads. `sp_attach`, `sp_fw_apply` and `sp_probe` are now thin wrappers over network- and comment-parameterised versions with Twenty's exact strings, and the Space helper's own tests pass unchanged. The daemon side is core/appmods/helper-driver.js; manifests may carry `app.hookPort` (43000 to 43999). Tests: test/space-helper-apps.test.js, core/appmods/{host-plan,helper-driver}.test.js.
- fix(release): the published Android app is signed with Vyre's own release key (the release job re-signs the APK from the `release` environment's ANDROID_KEYSTORE_B64, ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS and ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD), never with Expo's public debug key, which anyone could use to install over Vyre and inherit its data; check-release-dist.mjs --android-release refuses an APK not signed by the pinned release certificate, and a publish stops while none is pinned.
- feat(connect): a Connection to an app module's API on this machine (`app: "<module>"` instead of an address; for the app modules of part 8). The vault gives such a credential the one sentinel host `<app>.app.invalid` (nothing on the internet answers it), asks the app module for its origin (`appmods.origin`, only while it runs), and sends the key only to exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (port 1024 and up) with the connection pinned to 127.0.0.1, following no redirect and reaching no other address; an origin of any other shape is refused. A held call shows and binds the stable name, so an app that restarts on another port keeps its approvals. The `appmods` module may relay the installing person to `connectors.connection.create` and `.delete` and to nothing else (`checkRelayTool`). No polls or webhooks for an app's connection yet.
- feat(connect): the API description import reads YAML as well as JSON. New dependency: `yaml` 2.9.1 (eemeli, ISC licence, no dependencies of its own), pinned exactly, bundled with the release, and loaded only when an import is not JSON (never in the kernel). It reads with the core schema, no custom tags, strict, unique keys, at most 100 alias expansions (an alias bomb is refused in well under a second), only the first document, and the same 5 MB cap as JSON. Why: OpenAPI files in the wild are mostly YAML, and a hand-written YAML reader in a place that reads untrusted files is a worse risk than a small, audited one.
- feat(connect): `connectors.connection.import { url }` reads an API description from its public https address, for a person only (a model's request for an address is refused before anything is fetched). vyred does the fetch through the vault (`vault.fetch.public`, callable only by the connectors module): a plain GET with nothing of the person's, the address resolved and checked against private, loopback, link-local and metadata ranges at every hop, the connection pinned to the checked address, at most 3 redirects (https only), 5 MB, 20 seconds.
- feat(connect): an assistant can propose a Connection (`connectors.connection.propose`, same fields as create): it names the Vault item that holds the key (it never sees the key), the host and the operations, gets the plain-words card back, and nothing is made or called until the person approves it from their own screen (`connectors.connection.approve`, person only, written as that person). Whatever only the person may say is taken out of a proposal first: a relabeled operation and any kind but the method's, so an assistant's POST is a change on the card and in the Gate.
- feat(connect): `connectors.connection.import { text }` turns an OpenAPI 3 or 2 or Postman v2 file (JSON) into a draft Connection: the operations with their parameter, query and body shapes, the host from the file's https server, never saved or called, a POST always a change, no example value or key carried over. The Connections screen has an Any app tab to connect an app from a key in the Vault and see its light.
- feat(connect): the generic request. Every Connection reaches any method and path on its one pinned host: GET and HEAD read, POST PUT PATCH are held like a send, DELETE is a delete, and the operations the person declared sit on top and win (a POST that only reads, such as a search, is a read when the person relabeled it: `relabeled: true`; nothing else makes a write a read). `vault.request` takes `{ credential, operation, input }` for a Connection: a declared name is built from its path and shapes (input it does not declare is refused), `request` is the generic one; the result is judged exactly as the plain request it stands for.
- feat(flows): "Call a service" for a Connection: a service step may name `{ connection, operation, input }`. When the Flow is defined it is written out as the one service step the runner already runs (connector conn-<id>, method, path, query, body), so the approval card shows the destination, the Gate sees the operation's kind, and the ledger, idempotency and read-back are the service step's own. Path parameters must be written out; query, headers and body may be expressions. Unknown Connections and operations, input an operation does not take and missing required input are named at define time.
- feat(connect): a Connection's operations and polls in the form (kind from the method, the person may relabel, a `poll` makes a read operation a watcher source) and `watchers.preset { kind: "connector", connection }` builds the generic read-only watcher from the Connection's own declaration with its credential (conn-<id>) as the one way out. An inbound webhook on /hooks/conn-<id> (opened with hooks.open) is told to listeners as `connectors.connection-received`. `connectors.connection.export` gives a template without the key's item, the typed values, the id or the dates.
- feat(flows): a module extends Flows with one manifest declaration, `flow.steps` and `flow.triggers`. A step is one of the module's own tools (a Flow's call step runs it, an outward step is held for the person's yes), a trigger is an event it emits or a watcher it hosts, offered by name and stored as the `event` or `watcher` trigger that already exist. Added modules may declare both, and the install card lists them. `flow` and `flowAction` on a tool are deleted with the kernel's registerFlowActions, registerActions and installFlowActions and core/daemon/module-actions.js; test/flow-action-guards is now test/flow-step-guards.
- feat(flows): a module extends Flows with one manifest declaration, `flow.steps` and `flow.triggers`. A step is one of the module's own tools (a Flow's call step runs it, an outward step is held for the person's yes), a trigger is an event it emits or a watcher it hosts, offered by name and stored as the `event` or `watcher` trigger that already exist. Added modules may declare both, and the install card lists them; an added module's step is always outward (held for the person's yes whatever its manifest says), only Vyre's own modules are believed. `flow` and `flowAction` on a tool are deleted with the kernel's registerFlowActions, registerActions and installFlowActions and core/daemon/module-actions.js; test/flow-action-guards is now test/flow-step-guards.
- feat(planner): the planner's one scheduler escalates tasks. A task's `escalate_after` and `escalate_to`, stored and never read, now put a "Late: <title>" to-do in front of `escalate_to` once, and say `planner.escalated`; it is a wake hook on the existing timer.
- feat(kits): the law-firm Kit gets stage tasks (a paralegal's and an attorney's) for leads, clients and projects (personal injury and estate planning), and roles attorney and paralegal. A stage may name an `owner` (role:x or person:x): each of its tasks with a due offset escalates to the owner when not done by then. A role two Kits define (attorney) is one role that holds both Kits' grants, and it stays until the last Kit that holds it is removed. `vyre kit` lists the Kits and `vyre kit deploy <kit>` proposes the Kit, and the base Kit it needs first, in one step.
- feat(team): `team.ask` takes an optional `model` (a provider such as codex or grok, `provider/model`, or a Claude model name; `vyre team ask --model`). The request runs in a session made for it alone on that provider, through the same launch, Gate and spend as any teammate session, and the teammate's standing thread is left as it was. The request records its model and its thread.
- feat(app): the sidebar is a list each person arranges (SPEC-0.3.0 part 9): built-in places, an installed module's screens (manifest `screens`) and saved views, with groups, an order and hidden entries. The Space's default is set by its owner or admin role (sidebar.team; an assistant's request to change it is held for their yes); each person's own list sits on top, kept per member on the team's server through the Space kernel's new `sidebar` service so it follows them across devices (sidebar.edit, `reset` to go back to the team's order). Settings, Sidebar edits it (drag on the web, Up and Down everywhere); the assistant does "put Documents in my sidebar"; "Add to sidebar" on a records list or saved view; a module install can offer "for me or for the team". A module screen opens on the module's own origin (pane or new window). With nothing stored the sidebar is today's NAV.
- feat(appmods): part 8, apps from the open-source world as modules. core/appmods reads an app module manifest (app, connection, events, screens: manifest.js), runs the app as a container pinned by digest with memory, CPU and process limits, no capabilities, a folder of its own and no way out but the hook door (runtime.js, docker-direct driver), keeps its keys in the Vault, sets it up with its own bootstrap (no browser), turns its webhooks into Vyre events and a Flow's web trigger (flows `handleWeb` is now reachable from the Flows host), and installs only on the owner's yes. DocuSeal 3.3.1 is the first app (catalog/docuseal.json).

The app's own screens are on the app's own origin, `<module>.<the host Vyre is served at>` (core/appmods/proxy.js), never on Vyre's: Vyre's sign-in buys a one-time ticket (`appmods.open`, owner and admins only) that the app's host trades for a cookie for that host alone; the app is signed in for the person with the credentials the install kept in the Vault; its cookies and Vyre's never cross; nothing of the app is rewritten; Vyre's routes do not exist on that origin. App modules run on servers only. The install relays the person to the Connections module to make the app's Connection (`app:` form, IFACE-connection.md). test/appmods-origin.test.js proves a same-site request carrying Vyre's cookie from the app's origin is not the person's.
- fix(daemon,test): the three failures on lead-cand 81fa2bd7b. A merge had put serveDeck back (deck/ is gone), so an unbuilt app at / answered no_deck instead of no_app: serveDeck is removed again and / answers 404 no_app when no export built for the root exists. The setup tool list moved to lib/setup-gate.js and the release-build helpers to lib/release-build.js, so core/modules no longer imports core/relay and core/spaces no longer imports core/wink; the unused core/onboard -> core/names frozen edge is dropped; wink.phone.enrolled is classed person-only in agent-reach.
- fix(app): on Windows a refused passkey (no usable Windows Hello) falls back once to the computer's own key with a plain notice, and the paste screen promises Windows Hello only where it is there.
- fix(app): the Windows app's window is a boxless window like the Mac's server-Mac window (setup gate), so its first run opens on the install flow instead of "Now did not load".
- feat(windows-app): one origin for the life of the app: the window is always the bundled app at https://vyreapp.localhost (before and after pairing), a Windows build without the web build fails, and the app starts hidden in the tray once the page says setup has finished (setup_finished).
- feat(names): the names Worker accepts the Windows app's window origin (https://vyreapp.localhost) for the self-proving claim, finalize, append and update routes, beside the hosted app and the Mac window. The live Worker is not redeployed by this change (the lead's go).
- docs: Install now uses the app's Same and Not the same buttons, names Windows Hello (with its fallback), the Mac server's Touch ID and boot start, the My Home to My Cloud upgrade, and `vyre words`.
- refactor(installer): the Docker and Mac installers no longer pair a server at the terminal (the QR, long code, typed code and three-word questions are gone, and so is VYRE_PAIR_TO); run by hand without the app's code they say: Open the Vyre app, choose "Add a server", and run the line it shows. Setup pairs in one place, the app.
- fix(records): with Records on (Twenty), every gated call from a space whose record store was not up yet when its gateway was built failed as "no such record" (the owner app's team invite among them): the not-yet-attached store handed the gateway a refusing function where its attribute map belongs. It now holds a real map, replays it onto the store when that attaches, and forwards to it after.
- test: every workflow and composite action must parse as YAML with a trigger and jobs (test/workflows-yaml.test.js); an unquoted colon in a step name had made release.yml invalid.
- fix(release): the release workflow parses again (a step name with an unquoted colon made the whole file invalid, so no release or dry run could start).
- feat(copy): the first run, the installers and the reserve page use the approved plain wording (no internal names); the installer ends on "Go back to the Vyre app to finish"; new `vyre words` prints the four words to compare with the app; the Windows paste-code screen says the key is made with Windows Hello; Mobile and the phone page now describe the sideloaded apps (Android APK, iPhone build) instead of the home-screen web app.
- feat(mac-server): a Mac server's core ends with one key, the Mac app's Secure Enclave key as its Capsule key. The setup key (software, core's only key after the first-key step) signs the Capsule key's enrolment once, within the first key's hour; vyre-core checks that signature itself (presence.enroll.capsule), enrols the key as `capsule` and removes the setup key in one transaction. A capsule proof counts as a Touch ID gesture (hardware strength), so presence-required acts on the release server (Add a device, vault put, approvals) can be proved; a software key still cannot. The Mac app offers its Secure Enclave key as `presenceKey` kind capsule with `core_proof`/`core_name` in the pairing hello, the relay carries them, and devicePresence takes a `method` so the same key signs `capsule key=...` headers.
- docs: Install and the vyre.run start page now walk the new first run (reserve your name, install the Mac or Windows app, paste the code, join a team or add a server or use My Home, check four words, add your phone); the old browser setup, terminal QR and web-app-on-your-phone steps are gone from them.
- feat(release): a release now carries the Mac app (Vyre-Lumen-aarch64.dmg and Vyre-Lumen-x86_64.dmg, on every channel, ad hoc signed until a Developer ID is in place) and the Android APK (Vyre-android.apk, signed with Expo's fixed debug key); both are listed in the signed SHA256SUMS, required by check-release-dist, and the release notes say plainly that both are sideloaded.
- refactor(app): the Mac window's "type your server's code" screen (MacServer) and the where-Vyre-runs copy are removed; a Mac adds a server with the install line.
- refactor: the setup claim is gone (relay.setup.claim and claim-token, the session's mint/take, the claim message and TTL, the page's claim link, callWithGrant), with the old browser-setup CI journey (matrix J1) and the staging override for the setup page; the first-owner grant stays for a device's own enrol.
- feat(windows): a Windows PC claims its name with its Windows Hello passkey (identity/windows-claim.js) and uses that one passkey as its identity, its presence key and the signer of list changes. Its entry is a full device, not held, so a team's server takes it at the invitee door, a release sealing process takes its assertion as the yes (work/passkey-presence merged: webauthn_platform with a verified WebAuthn assertion, marked unattested), and it can add a phone to its own name. The door takes a passkey entry's hello as a WebAuthn assertion (one Hello prompt per new member stream); a held key is still refused. The shell makes a passkey for the bundled page (https://vyreapp.localhost) and the paired server's page only. Where Hello is not available the PC claims with the DPAPI key as before. This reverses IR-32 for Windows only. Unproven until a Windows build keeps its window: that WebView2 accepts vyreapp.localhost as a relying party id, and the real Hello prompt.
- feat(app): a team space is made in the order name, add a server (the same add-a-server step), invites with Skip; the Where will it live, On this computer and Mac server-code steps are removed, so no space is made without a server.
- feat(mac-app): the bundled setup passes --login-only (My Home: a LaunchAgent as the person, no admin password); a Mac that stays on as a server is added with the install line.
- feat(app): adding a server asks whether it is a Linux machine or a Mac that stays on; a Mac gets the Mac installer's line, and install-mac-server.sh takes VYRE_STORE, shows the four check words and ends with "Back in the Vyre app" when the app made the code.
- feat(app): after a name the first run offers Join a team, Add a server (your own Cloud) and, on a Mac, My Home; Windows says Home is coming.
- fix(app): a server paired by the typed code from the Mac or Windows app is an app device with a paired session (the hello said kind web, so presence.person.pair-challenge was "no tool"), and the typed path finishes with the server's adopt and the owner (IR-35).
- feat(app): an identity with no server can join a team. The app reads the invite itself (src/real/join-team.js): the space's record from the names directory gives the home's route, a throwaway invitee channel opens the home's invitee door with a hello signed by the identity key, the join card comes from the home's kernel with the home proving it holds the space, and the person's yes (their hardware key over exactly that card) is accepted there; the accept enrols the device's key on that server. The member row is kept so the app reaches the space with a member call. install.ts previews and accepts here whenever the app holds the name. Test: test/wink-paired-2.test.js (two identities, one real server and relay).
- feat(windows-app): the TPM key's refusals carry the provider's status code, the app logs its start, setup and exit, and the Windows proof drives the shell's own yes/no box for a list change.
- test(install): scripts/proof-install.mjs walks the new install and pairing flow end to end, one PASS or FAIL line per step: reserve a name, become yourself in the app, Add a server with the install line, the real installer, the four words in the app, adopt, a tool call, Add a device, a team space and an invite, and a server paired from its own terminal (long code, typed code, a browser with and without the owner's identity proof), with and without Records; the team invite and Join steps run the app's own team-invite.js, join-team.js and kernel-wire.js against a development sealing process; `--live-relay` runs the same walk over the real relay.vyre.run as transport only (names stay on the stand-in). The Mac walk uses a test release with a signed module list (scripts/lib/proof/mac-release.mjs); the Linux installer walk forwards a loopback relay into the box's network namespace. The app side is the app's own modules driven headless (scripts/lib/proof/app.mjs); the names directory and the relay are local stand-ins. CI: .github/workflows/install-proof.yml (the Linux installer, and the Mac mini server on the hosted macOS runner).
- ci(windows-app): the installer carries the app's web build (capsule-win.yml), and a dispatch-only proof job in capsule-win.yml builds and drives the Windows app on windows-latest against a stand-in names directory (first run, identity bridge, app log, restart keeps the identity and relay keys).
- feat(windows-app): the Windows app opens the app's own web build in its window with no server (a vyreapp scheme served by the shell, origin http://vyreapp.localhost), so reserve, become yourself, Join or Add a server can run on Windows; the page has identity.has and identity.forget; every key failure goes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Vyre\logs\app.log with its real reason, and the claim screen shows the shell's reason instead of one generic line.
- fix(pairing): an app with no server of its own finishes a typed-code pairing. The Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android apps redeemed the typed code and stopped, so a server's pairing never got its owner (wink.server.adopt, with the typed ack as the yes and the name's proof) and a phone's never got its wink.phone.wait; the server let the half-paired device go and the app, which had saved the pairing anyway, was refused every few seconds. relay/client/join.js joinWithCode now finishes the pairing (relay/client/finish.js, shared with the long code and the add-a-device flows); the box names the gate in its pending reply; the owner's proof binds to a typed code's tag; a typed-code server device gets its paired session from the key it offered; and a saved pairing the server no longer knows is let go before a new server is paired. Tests: test/pair-fix.test.js.
- fix(setup): the reserve page and the app's paste check accept every character the directory puts in a reservation code (A-Z without I and O, 2-9); they refused any code with an 8 or 9.
- feat(vyre-core): a Mac server takes its first presence key without a Capsule. The full Mac install tells core it is a server (plist VYRE_CORE_SERVER, only the root installer can) and names the fingerprint of the app's key, the last 16 bytes of the install line's setup code (public; the secret half never reaches core). Core then takes ONE device key (P-256), only that key, within the hour, from a process outside every Claude session (presence.enroll.first); a same-uid process that read the code still cannot enrol a key of its own. Every later key needs a proof from an enrolled key over the exact enrol input, which core already required. The relay forwards a paired device's key to core (with `presenceKey.core_proof` when the app sends one); people and the CLI keep core_owned.
- feat(app): joining a team on a release server. The app asks for the invitee's key enrolment with the invite id and, on an iPhone, attaches App Attest over "join:" plus that id (the sealing process's token for a join); a secure-chip key without it is taken marked unattested, a software key is refused and the accept fails whole. Tested at the sealing process (kernel/seal/appattest.test.js: the app's bytes equal the process's, another invite's attestation is refused) and end to end on a release-rule sealer (test/wink-paired-2.test.js).
- feat(app): an owner whose name lives in the app invites people to a team space on their server from the app (src/real/team-invite.js, kernel-wire.js): the server holds no identity, so the app asks the space's own kernel over its paired session and answers the home's one-use challenge with the name's key (the proof now names the home and the challenge, in the Mac, Windows and phone signers). Create, list, confirm and cancel work this way; the kernel wire gained grants.invites.list and grants.invites.revoke, and revoke takes its proof like every other grants call. The Invite screen uses it whenever the app keeps the name.
- test(pairing): the computer app serving a phone's enrolment is tested with the real chain (apps/app/src/real/enrol-serve.test.js; the steps moved out of enrol-phone.ts into enrol-serve.js), and the three-minute enrolling timeout of a phone added to a server with no identity is tested in core/wink/pairing.test.js.
- fix(vyre-core): the Mac installer mints the first enrolment code again (up to 6 tries) when core is still making its database; the two migrations collided on the hosted runner ("UNIQUE constraint failed: _migrations") and ended the install.
- fix(mac-server): a Mac installed with the server install line comes up as a server: install-mac-server.sh sets machine "server" in config.json (a choice or role already made is kept), and a machine set up as a server is role box so wink and the server side of the relay run (before, wink.server.code did not exist and custom record types were refused).
- fix(mac-server): the installer ends as the Linux one does with the app's install line: the four check words, then "Done. Back in the Vyre app."; the old wink.server.code text stays only for an install with no setup code. The Records choice (VYRE_STORE) now reaches vyre.env, auto by default.
- fix(vyre-core): the vault module failed to start on a vyre-core Mac ("paths[0] ... Received undefined"): a core tool's module was judged first party by a folder the manifest never carries; it now uses the module record's folder. A module that fails to start also logs where.
- feat(site): vyre.run/setup checks a name, reserves it and shows the code for the app; the browser setup flow (key, install follow, claim, AI, devices) and its relay client copies are removed; staging override and build scripts follow.
- feat(app): a first name is made by pasting the code from vyre.run/setup; one add-a-server step (install line with a one-time owner token, With Records or Without Records, the words checked in the app) replaces the question, server and VPS screens; My Home upgrades to My Cloud and moves everything.
- feat(names): a server holds no name: `names.serve` and `names.unserve` replace names.claim and names.release, the directory points a space's name at a server only when the space lists it, spaces.create on a paired server lists it and tells it; `vyre setup --name`, `vyre name claim|release` and onboard.name claim are removed; the installer takes VYRE_STORE (auto or sqlite) and ends with "Back in the Vyre app"; the setup channel offers wink.server.setup-offer and system.info only.
- feat(names): a person's first name is reserved on the web (POST /v1/ids/reserve, a VYRE-code good for 24 hours, once) and finished in the app with its own key (POST /v1/ids/finalize); a space lists the servers that serve its name (POST /v1/ids/server, at most 8); the box routes names.claim, release and admin rebind are gone (Worker not deployed).
- feat(connect): a Connection is an app the person connects themselves from a key already in the Vault (spec part 4, piece 1): `connectors.connection.create/update/check/list/get/rebuild/delete`. The quick form (label, https host, how the key is sent, Vault item, fixed headers, one check request) becomes a declaration the existing connector format checks; the record is the only source and the vault credential `conn-<id>` is derived from it (config only, the key stays in its own item), written only in a person's act and shown out of step if changed behind the record. New vault auth: basic, an api-key in a query parameter, and fixed headers vyred adds that a caller cannot override. The check says green or "the key was refused (401)", "that id was not found (404)", "no answer from the host (timeout)".
- fix(names): the directory takes identity claims from the Mac app's window (origin vyreapp://box) as well as app.vyre.run (IR-32).
- fix(app): the Mac app's window claims a name with the Mac's own key, not a browser passkey ("Open app.vyre.run to create your name", IR-32).
- fix(mac-app): the ad hoc Lumen package is signed again after the version stamp and web build, and must verify; an invalid signature made the Keychain refuse the identity key ("This Mac would not keep your key", IR-31).
- fix(lumen): a failed identity key step says the shell's own reason on screen and in ~/Library/Logs/Vyre/app.log, and `defaults write sh.vyre.capsule inspect -bool true` makes the window inspectable (IR-31).

## 0.2.11 (8 Oct 2026)

## 0.2.10 (8 Oct 2026)
- fix(lumen): an ad hoc signed Mac app keeps the identity key in the login Keychain when macOS refuses the this-device-only class (errSecMissingEntitlement); before, "This Mac would not keep your key" and no name could be claimed.
- feat(names): support-only POST /v1/names/admin/drop takes a name back from a server, so an identity or a space can claim it (names belong to identities and spaces; an older setup named servers).
- test: known-red burn-down 1.3, the 8 with no recorded cause: stdin-hygiene, within-hygiene, peer, screen-live and agents are green (fixes above and in their tests); sessions, golden and federation-send now each carry a written cause and owner in test/known-red.json; the list is 18 files.
- fix(hygiene): known-red burn-down 1.3: the confinement probe listens for errors on its child's stdin (EPIPE could take vyred down), and the three Wink relay waits (homecall, netd, netjoin) race through lib/within.js instead of an unref'd timer; test/stdin-hygiene and test/within-hygiene go green.
- fix(kernel): the event log's `iterate` asks the disk for the rows its caller's limit needs, not a whole batch of 500: a consumer far behind the window read 500 rows to deliver one event.
- fix(flows,watchers): IR-18 on a Space with its own records store the Flow types and the watcher definitions are defined: def-flow's `name` is now Twenty's title column (a text field called name is the title), and the watcher definition's `name` is no longer unique, so neither type is refused ("collides with a name Twenty uses"); the Flows timer starts only after the Flow types exist and runs are recovered, so a tick no longer reads "no type flow-state" every minute. A test plans every type Vyre defines.
- fix(doctor): IR-17 `vyre doctor` no longer says Claude is not signed in right after the setup page signed it in: onboard.status counted only the Claude step's own token, and now also a signed-in Claude account made by the sign-in tool.
- fix(setup): IR-11 what the setup channel may call is one list: the registry's class check read its own copy of it (SETUP_REACH), which lacked network.wink.status, so the page's network step got "no tool network.wink.status" from a healthy box. SETUP_REACH is now built from core/relay/setup.js (SETUP_REASONS), classReach asks setupToolAllowed, and kernel/retrofit/gates.js reads the same classReach. test/setup-gates.test.js drives every tool site/setup calls through a real registry as a setup caller.
- fix(setup): IR-14 the setup page's "What is happening" log is one list in the order things happened, new lines at the bottom: the page's own lines (words matched, claimed, signed in) were drawn above the install lines, so the log looked quiet after the install.
- fix(release): REL-1 scripts/patch-release.mjs keeps the first commit argument when --base is not given (the filter skipped index 0 whenever the flag was absent).
- fix(box): IR-8 a root run of the vyre wrapper writes its run files through its own temp names, so two at once (the update path unit and `sudo vyre name status`) no longer print "mv: cannot stat .../compose.env.new".
- fix(installer): IR-7 Docker's own install output goes to a log file; the screen shows one progress line, and the log's path only if Docker does not install.
- fix(installer): IR-4 the installer and the box wrapper name no internal part to a person (Twenty, kernel, vyred): "room for 2 spaces (each needs about 3.1 GB)" replaces "room for 2 space(s) on Twenty"; a test keeps the printed lines free of them.
- fix(installer): IR-2 with a setup code (a browser install) the terminal shows the four check words only: no pairing QR, long code or typed code, which was a second pairing path beside the page's.
- fix(installer): IR-3 the installer starts vyre with `vyre up --quiet`, so a fresh install no longer reads "vyred is already running" or "not paired yet, run vyre call wink.server.code"; the installer says what comes next itself.
- fix(installer): IR-1 the check words are read through sudo when the account cannot reach the box itself, and the terminal names the command that shows them when they cannot be read.
- fix(acme): the public gate waits for public DNS (Cloudflare's and Google's resolvers) to carry the _acme-challenge record before the CA looks (lib/acme/dnswait.js); 0.2.10 asked the CA two seconds after writing it and every issue failed with NXDOMAIN.
- fix(wink): the public gate's ACME challenge reaches the name directory as the challenge value; 0.2.9 sent the name instead, so no box got a certificate or a published <name>.vyre.run address (nameDirectory, with a test).
- fix(perf-check): a refused memory.curate (personal memory answers only a proven person) no longer fails the check; the quiet wait covers curation. test(wink): the linked-root test removes its link.
- fix(kernel): a log consumer that ran before a restart goes on from its durable cursor instead of from 0, so a restart no longer hands every consumer the whole log again, read back from disk (about 9 s of a busy vyred after boot in a thread test, and the cause of the threads-watch restart test timing out on the CI runners); tested.
- feat(sessions): a switch of model carries the rollover seed (decisions, plan, open tasks, the files touched, the working folder, Recall pointers, the last turns) and nothing else; handoffBrief is gone. A model that ran the thread before and resumes its own session gets the seed with what was said while it was away, as one message ahead of the person's words, which fixes Claude to Codex to Claude coming back without the Codex turns. Tests: the switch eval (a recorded Claude, Codex, Claude conversation, ten questions).
- fix(release): vyre.tgz carries its three @noble packages (bundleDependencies), so a Mac server, which unpacks the tarball with no npm step, starts vyred instead of failing on a missing @noble/hashes; build-site.sh refuses a tarball without them; the pack check counts the bundled packages as shipped on purpose.
- fix(mac-server): the vyred wrapper writes its output to logs/vyred.out, since the system LaunchDaemon sets no output path and a crash left no trace.
- test: the runner removes each test process's temp folders on exit; the macOS watch-restart test gives the resumed thread's first send 75 s; the clipboard test reads the fake helper's state only once it is written; the Android capture skips a push that has no green build yet.

## 0.2.9 (7 Oct 2026)
- fix(store): a Space store still starting past 20 s leaves the Space a waiting store and finishes in the background, so a first install no longer deadlocks on the root helper.
- fix(flows): the Flow types and recover wait for a store that is still starting, instead of stopping vyred at boot.
- fix(modules): a module that failed only because the store was still starting starts again when it joins (startStoreWaiting); a started module clears its earlier error.
- fix(storage): the sealed Drive keeps the Drive's pool, so paired drives join the Space's pool again.
- fix(agents): agents.ask relays the asker's verified facts to threads.send and threads.release, so the chat gate admits a person's ask and gives the keyboard back.
- fix(peer-door): a paired device's call carries its verified peer, so an approval card names the device.
- fix(threads): a session socket that finishes opening after vyred began stopping is closed at once.
- fix(upgrade): the chats port steps aside when My Cloud is on another server; the upgrade goes on.
- fix(box): uninstall stops every Space's containers, keeping their data; the encrypted swap's mkswap and swapon in an if.
- feat(brand): the halftone V with a folded corner (scripts/gen-mark.mjs) is the app icon, the splash (expo-splash-screen, added for the splash) and every favicon.
- docs: the README tells Vyre as one product, with a panel film and an app tour (docs/images/readme); known gaps gain the model switch-back and a remote My Cloud's chats.
- test: the integration's test fixes (chat gate callers, the kernel log, the Deck screens, PW-1, split space-helper) and the known-red list with reasons.
- refactor(app): the Team tab, the Teammates tab and the Assign picker key teammates by the Project record's id, as the team.* tools now take it (cleanup's work/cleanup-team d45d3b8df; the box refuses a short name). A project with no slug has a team; projectSlug is gone; the Assistants page names each project through work.project.ref. Needs that branch on the box side: team.list, team.add, team.retire and the other team.* tools with a `project` input now want the id or the vyre:// address; team.default.get and team.default.set take the id too.

- feat(records,comms): plan item 6's relation. `communication.contacts` is a many-to-many link to Contact with the named reverse "Communications" on the Contact (windows' relations, from work/hub-kernel-on). The Log communications Flow adds each matched or made contact to it with one `update` step beside the Participant, by address, so a contact's page lists every email and meeting; a stranger with no contact adds nothing, and logging the same item twice does not double the links. Tested in records/comms/log-flow.test.js.
- fix(watchers): reviewer-4 G-3. The Google read matches a vault grant to exactly this watcher (as `vault.release` does), so a grant to the watchers module as a whole reads nothing; tested.
- fix(watchers): reviewer-4 G-1. A watcher that reads a Google account (`net.<host>.google`) reads nothing until a person grants the account's vault item to that watcher (`vyre vault grant <item> watchers --watcher <name>`), checked in the runtime for a dry run and for a run alike; `watchers.preset` answers with that grant command. Before, the read went through `google.api` with no grant, so a model could write and dry-run such a watcher and read the owner's mail.
- fix(google): reviewer-4's hold on calendar-live. `google.api` takes an exact caller (`module:leases` for the calendar sync, `module:watchers` for reads only), and refuses a write whose `sendUpdates` is not none unless the body names attendees. Tests: another module is denied; a change to a pulled event that has guests is held for a yes (the pull keeps attendees as people).
- fix(calendar): the sync re-checks an approved Google write as the task's doer (the Flows service under the owner) with the request's bind, the rule platform-3's approval fix makes real (merged work/approval-token-verify). On the real kernel the approved write now goes out once and the approval is spent; before, it was never allowed. Real-daemon test in core/daemon/calendar-sync-google.test.js.
- feat(calendar): a synced Event keeps the zone it was made in. `time_zone` is Google's `start.timeZone`, else the calendar's own zone (the list's `timeZone`); times stay UTC ISO, so a screen can show "9:00 am PT" beside the viewer's own time. An all-day event is date only and has no zone; a push writes `time_zone` back (and invents none when there is none, where it used to send UTC). Tested with an America/Los_Angeles event, in records/calendar/sync.test.js.
- refactor(connectors): one Google path, the google module (the lead's ruling, 5 Oct 2026). The `google-api`, `gmail-api` and `google-calendar-api` OAuth presets, the vault credentials on the Gmail and Calendar declarations (`auth.type: "google"` now, with no `also`, and `connectors.declare` refuses it), and the vault-connector branch of the calendar sync are deleted; the declaration format and Stripe stay. The calendar sync runs for each Google account through `google.api`. `google.api` also reads Gmail (GET of the profile, the message list, a message or a thread; never a write). A Log communications watcher names the account, `net: { "gmail.googleapis.com": { "google": "work" } }`, and the runtime reads through `google.api` as a module, so the watcher holds no credential and its card says "your connected Google account, read only"; `watchers.preset` takes `google` for a Google connector, `connectors.logging` takes `google` (default: the account whose address it is). `connectors.declared` lists a Google connector as installed when an account is connected. New `mergedParts` in records/connectors/format.js. "Vyre can write drafts; sending asks you first" is now the first line of the google module's mail tip. Reviewer GC-1 to GC-3: `google.api` refuses a path segment that is or decodes to `.`, `..` or hides a slash; only `module:leases` (the calendar sync) may write and `module:watchers` may read; the sync passes the request's `bind` when it re-checks an approval, so an approval for one write is not accepted for another.

- fix(calendar): the Space's calendar sync now runs for the Google accounts people actually connect (the google module's, signed in with a service account or OAuth), not only for vault connectors: each account is pulled into Event records (source google, calendar google-<account>) and Vyre's own events are pushed back only through the approval path (held for the owner's yes, the approval checked for that act before the write). The new `google.api` tool (Vyre's own modules only; Calendar events paths only, narrowest scope per method, If-Match allowed) is how the sync reaches Google, so the token is still minted only by the google module from the vault. A connector name with a colon made the kernel refuse the resource (wrong_space), so accounts are named google-<account>. Tested in a real kernel-on vyred against the fake Google.
- feat(identity): claim a name from a browser with a passkey (0.2.9, gap A29). `claimIdentityWithPasskey` (apps/app/src/identity/claim.js) makes a WebAuthn credential (P-256, user verification required) as the identity's first device and signs the genesis and the claim's record with it; `createPasskeyKey` and `restorePasskeyKey` (apps/app/src/identity/passkey.js) read the attestation with a small CBOR reader, normalise the high-s twin an authenticator may return, and keep only the credential id and public key. A passkey is a full device (unlike a key a page can reach). The directory could verify a passkey's signature on a chain op but not on a name record or an act; `verifyWith` now takes the signing entry (`signing` from `signerKey`) and checks a passkey's assertion as one, in the Worker, the client directory, the audit key, the seal's bindings and spaces. The pinned hash of kernel/identity/chain.js is updated; merging with work/no-labels needs it recomputed.
- fix(kernel): one rule for an outward approval, no older looser path. Every producer of a held outward act records `form.bind` (the Flow runner now does: `requestBind` of a service step's request, `actBind` of any other call step's action, resource and input; the calendar sync already did), every consumer passes the same bind (leases now bind lent-computer sessions too), and `approvedAct` refuses an outward approval that recorded none. `actBind` is new in kernel/seal/uses.js. test/outward-flags.test.js checks that every registry-held outward tool binds its card to a digest of the whole input.
- fix(kernel): `approvedAct` compares the bind. An approved task that recorded the bind of what the person saw (`form.bind`, a digest of the request as it would be sent) releases only a request that carries the same bind; approve A and send B is refused, and a request that states none is too. It holds for every outward act, not only the calendar sync (which checked it for itself). `authorize` passes the request's `input.bind` through, and the service lease passes the bind it computes from the request it is about to send. An approval that recorded no bind is judged as before. Test: approve A, send B with that approval, refused.

- feat(one-yes): `wink.code.open` is a pair moment, so a headless walk or a dev build signs the owner's yes over it (`dev-sign-proof --yes pair --tool wink.code.open --input '{"flow":"W2"}'`) and a browser or server typed pairing can start; `records.seal-put` and `records.reveal` are the vault moment (filling or revealing a sealed field, ruling 7cc004d). A prefix never counts.

- fix(team): team.role.fill no longer gives an agent a project from inside the module (that is the person's own signed act and the module call carries no person); an agent that does not reach the project is refused with the way to grant it (projects.access.grant), and the team tests grant through the person's chain.
- feat(team): an upgrade step re-keys team rows from short name to Project record id. At start, `rekeyLegacy` (core/team/rekey.js) moves every row of team_teammates, team_requests, team_duties and team_project_settings whose `project` is not a record id to the id Records gives for that short name (retried while Records starts); a name Records does not know is left as it is and logged once, never dropped, and a settings row already under the id wins. Released migration text is untouched.
- feat(modules): one keying scheme for projects. Every tool that declares `projectArg` takes the Project record's id or `vyre://` address as well as the short name: the registry turns an id into the short name (through `work.project.ref`) before the agent grant check and the tool, so threads.start, the brief, artifacts, goals, memory, projects and github tools need no change; an id Records does not know is `not_found`. A tool that keys by the id itself (the team.* tools) says `"projectIsRecord": true` in its manifest and is handed the id back after the grant check. `work.project.ref` answers the registry's own door call.
- refactor(team,work,harness,said,cli): the team.* tools and tables are keyed by the Project record's id, not its short name. `team_teammates.project`, `team_requests.project`, `team_duties.project` and `team_project_settings.project` hold the record's id (a v4 uuid); every team.* `project` input is that id or the record's address (`vyre://<space>/project/<id>`), and a short name is `bad_input`, except for team.default.get and team.default.set, which the settings module still calls with its project level's short name. A teammate's agent name is made once, from the short name at the time it is added. New `work.project.ref` (`{ project: id | address | short name }` to `{ id, urn, slug, name }`, nothing made, read again under the caller's own chain) is how a part that holds only a short name (the CLI, the harness, the Said recorder, a thread's own project column) gets the id; sessions, the agents' project lists and the watchers keep taking short names, so team asks Records for the slug where it calls them. A teammate is also a team-member record linked to the Project (`work.team.member`, the teammates module only; the work module gains `records.remove` for it). `lib/project-id.js` gains `isProjectRecordId` and `projectRecordIdOf`. Rows written by an earlier build under a short name are not converted: there are no installs.
- fix(work)!: reviewer-5's HIGH on the chat upgrade: `work.chat.upgrade-move` and `work.chat.history-import` are the person's own act. Both refuse (denied) unless the caller's chain is exactly one person hop (their own device, or their own session, which the spaces module relays after the person's one approval); an assistant's or a model's session (an agent hop), a viewer or a delegate chain is refused before anything else is looked at. A chat the mover was NOT in no longer moves with its project: network-2's `carryFiles` refuses the files of a chat the mover is not in, and a record never moves without its files, so it stays in the source Space (record, files, people) and the move names it in `chats_left_behind`, along with the chats nobody in the target was part of.
- feat(work,stream,switchboard): a chat's HISTORY travels with the Personal to My Cloud upgrade (windows asked where transcripts live; they were not covered). A chat's logged frames and member rows live in the stream's tables, its runs and their events in the switchboard's and the events table, none of them records or files, so the records carry could not reach them. Now module-only `stream.export-chat` / `stream.import-chat` and `threads.export-chat` / `threads.import-chat` read and put them back; `work.chat.upgrade-move` writes the bundle into the chat's own folder as numbered chunks of at most 8 MB (`.history/000001.json` and so on, in the order they must come back: runs, who answers, events, frames; one item larger than a chunk is a chunk of its own, up to 64 MB) and, last, `.history/manifest.json` with each chunk's hash, so it travels sealed with the chat's files and no chat is left behind for its length; the new `work.chat.history-import { chat }` (the person, in the chat) reads the manifest on the other device, checks each chunk against its hash and puts it back in order (frames, member rows, the runs as stopped, their events), resumes where it stopped (`work_history_imports` keeps which chunks are back), and leaves a chat that already had frames of its own there as it is. Nothing of it is written anywhere but the sealed chat folder and the engine's own tables. `work.chat.upgrade-move` also takes windows' `upgrade_id` and passes it to `carryFiles`. NOT carried: the provider's own session file (a resumed run starts from the brief, not from native context). Tests: one device to another through the module tools, and the file read as the person.
- feat(work): Personal to My Cloud chat upgrade (core/work/chat-upgrade.js; windows' contract). `work.chat.upgrade-plan { to }` answers `{ counts: { chats, files, bytes }, blockers, chats }` (read only; a chat that is working blocks it) and `work.chat.upgrade-move { to, move_id? }` moves the chats the caller is in to their other Space under the caller's own chain in both: each keeps its chat id (a key ring is bound to it), title, started and last_active, is filed under the target's General project, its record and files move (files sealed through the move's `carry`), people who are not members there and missing agents go to `former`, and a chat that cannot move is named in `left` while the others still move. Resumable. Tool names start with `work.`; the spaces module relays the person to these two.
- feat(stream): grouped run steps and the returning view. The tool frames of a run step (the calls between two of an assistant's messages) carry `data.step`; when the assistant starts its next message, or the turn ends, one `chat.step-summary` frame `{ step, count, kinds, summary, ok }` closes the step ("Read 3 files, ran a command", from counts, never invented), so a screen folds the step's tool frames into one collapsible block. `stream.catchup { chat }` answers what happened since the caller's read marker: `{ chat, since, head, unread, messages[last 10: { message, author, text<=140 }], steps[last 10], steps_total, open_asks, joined, left }`, from the chat's own log, with no model summary. Relay path measured on testbox6 (core/stream/relay-perf.mjs, real relay code and Noise, box and client on one host): emit to client p50 1.25 ms, p95 4.1 ms, p99 6.35 ms for 1500 frames at 100 per second; kill to first resumed frame p50 150 ms, p95 185 ms over 30 cuts, no gap and no repeat. A phone adds its own network time; the boxes could not reach each other's relay port, so no cross-host number.
- feat(work,stream): `unread` (a number) on each `work.chat.list` row the caller is in: the messages others made after the caller's read marker (`stream.mark-read`), counted from the stream's own tables. The carry never gives the mover a chat they were not in: a chat nobody who was in it is a member of the target for stays in the source Space (record, files, people), is dropped from the target, and the move names it in `chats_left_behind`. Time zones go through lib/time (`zoneFrom`, `validZone`) with no copy: `stream.send` and `threads.send` take the device's zone from `tz`, else from the validated `x-vyre-zone` header (`meta.zone`); a frame's `tz` is the sender's zone, and the screen shows `showTimes(frame.time, { person: viewerZone, space: frame.tz })`.
- feat(work,kernel,lib): a chat with a person in it is never in the clear on disk, even when started on the server (CLI, a Flow). With no ring from a device, `work.chat.create` makes it: a chat key wrapped to each participant device's public agree point (`spaces.identity.devices`, `holdersOf` in lib/chat-keys.js; no private key needed), kept only as the session lease (`chats.keys.adopt`, process memory, same lifetime rules as a lent key). A participant with no agree point stops the start (`no_agree_point`), named. Test: core/work/chat-server-ring.test.js (the disk holds no plaintext).
- feat(work,memory): exact recall (the user's ruling, 5 Oct 2026, in 0.2.9). `work.chat.span { chat, from, to?, slot? }` reads a span of a chat word for word by line range: the user's and the assistant's lines of each run (or one slot) as the Space's memory already keeps them (core/work/memory/lines.js, scrubbed on the way in, so a sealed value is a placeholder), each with its line address; at most 200 lines and 96 KB a call, `more`/`next` to continue; tool output stays out. The one gate is the chat: the kernel's `chats.read` on the asker's own chain, so a person or an assistant the chat lists reads it and anyone else is told "no such chat", the same answer as for a chat that does not exist. No second store: `engine.lines.exact` reads the existing table for the chat's own runs only. Test: core/work/chat-span.test.js.
- feat(work,memory): exact recall (the user's ruling, 5 Oct 2026, in 0.2.9). `work.chat.span { chat, from, to?, slot? }` reads a span of a chat word for word by line range: the user's and the assistant's lines of each run (or one slot) as the Space's memory already keeps them (core/work/memory/lines.js, scrubbed on the way in, so a sealed value is a placeholder), each with its line address; at most 200 lines and 96 KB a call, `more`/`next` to continue; tool output stays out. The one gate is the chat: the kernel's `chats.read` on the asker's own chain, so a person or an assistant the chat lists reads it and anyone else is told "no such chat", the same answer as for a chat that does not exist. No second store: `engine.lines.exact` reads the existing table for the chat's own runs only. A terminal session in the chat (`threads.of-chat` now also returns `terminals`, from the table `term.open` fills) is read the same way, slot `terminal:<first 8 of its id>`. Test: core/work/chat-span.test.js.
- feat(work,kernel,lib): a chat with a person in it is never in the clear on disk, even when started on the server (CLI, a Flow). With no ring from a device, `work.chat.create` makes it: a chat key wrapped to each participant device's public agree point (`spaces.identity.devices.read`, the module twin of `spaces.identity.devices`; `holdersOf` in lib/chat-keys.js; no private key needed), kept only as the session lease (`chats.keys.adopt`, process memory, same lifetime rules as a lent key). A participant with no agree point stops the start (`no_agree_point`), named. Test: core/work/chat-server-ring.test.js (the disk holds no plaintext).
- feat(kernel,work,lib): per-chat keys end to end (team/0.3/DESIGN-chat-keys.md), on chat's passed head. A chat's key ring rides in `chat.created` and `chat.changed` (kernel/grants: an add or remove needs the ring that change made, a removal a higher epoch, the epoch never goes back; `chats.epoch(id)` is 0 for a chat in the clear). The gateway lends a chat's key to the process only through a participant's own device (`chats.keys.begin / finish / lock`, kernel/gateway/chat-keys.js; the keys live in memory only, a rotation makes a lent key stale, `finish` is async because opening the bundle uses the device's agree key). A chat's folders are stored sealed (kernel/storage/sealed-drive.js): path segments become HMAC ids, bytes are sealed under a key of each file's own, names and file keys sit in one sealed index, a file shared to a project is wrapped to the project's ring and found through the project's own sealed index; the gateway authorizes, grants and logs on the stored path so no name reaches the log. `work.chat.create` and `work.chat.change` take `ring`, `work.chat.get` returns it to a participant, and `work.chat.keys.begin / finish / lock / status` are the person-only tools a device uses. New dependencies with exact pins and lockfile integrity: @noble/ciphers 1.3.0, @noble/hashes 1.8.0, @noble/curves 1.9.7 (lib/databox.js, lib/keywrap.js, lib/chat-keys.js). Tests: kernel/gateway/chat-lease.test.js (a ring made on a device, the lease, a rotation, and the whole path on a real Drive: ciphertext on the disk, names included, readable by a participant, nothing for a non-participant with the disk), chat-sealed.test.js, kernel/storage/sealed-drive.test.js, lib/chat-keys.test.js.
- fix(switchboard,kernel)!: every threads tool a person can call is gated by the chats they are in, at ONE point (a wrapper over this module's `ctx.tool`), not tool by tool (reviewer-5 HOLD on 92494bcd3). A tool that takes a thread, an ask, a watch or a session answers not_found for a run in a chat the caller is not in; `threads.list`, `threads.asks`, `threads.live` and `threads.history` leave such runs out; `threads.pids` is empty for a non-module caller; with no person chain only runs in no chat show. First-party modules are exempt. `threads.answer` is covered through the ask's thread. A walker test calls every threads tool from the registry's own schemas as a member outside the chat. Merged flows' aecc0f8cc: its SL-1 (a session's agent is never a model slot name) is kept, and the daemon's own door opens a slot with `slot_open: true` (`lib/kernel-session`, `core/daemon`), which nothing a model or a module can supply.
- feat(work): a chat moves with its project (core/work/chat-carry.js, run by the move's own `chats` step under the mover's chain in the target): the chat is made again in the target Space under a NEW chat id with the same title and project; its people are those who are members there (the mover only if they were in it, or nobody else is left), its agents those that exist there, everyone else is listed in the new `former` field of the chat-record and gets nothing; the target record's `chat`, `people`, `agents`, `former`, `drive` and `location` are rewritten; the chat's sealed files land under the NEW id (`mapChatPath`, old id to new in the move's `chatMap`); those fields are the carry's, not compared by content at verify. The move's sides carry the Space's own `chats` and `members`.
- feat(stream,switchboard): the device's time zone rides with every message. `stream.send { tz }` (an IANA name; an unknown one is dropped, never stored): the `chat.user-message` frame carries `tz`, `threads.send` keeps it as the thread's current zone (`threads_runs.tz`, read by `threads.get().thread.tz`) and `thread.sent` says it. The brief and `lib/time` read the person's current zone from there. Showing a message's time in the viewer's own zone is the screen's (frames carry `time` in epoch ms).
- feat(stream): quoted replies, WhatsApp-style, in the same timeline. `stream.send { reply_to: <message id> }`: the user-message frame carries `reply_to` and `quote: { message, author, text }`, which the box reads from this chat's own log (a person's message, or an assistant's whole message), `text` cut to 140 characters. A message the log does not hold answers not_found, a private message cannot be quoted. The run is told what it answers (`Replying to <author>: "<quoted text>"` then the person's words), the same for every provider because it is plain text.
- feat(kernel,work): `chats.mine(chain)`, the one answer to "which chats am I in": the chat ids a chain may read (a person in it, or an assistant or model slot acting for them), joined with each chat's record (project, location, title) when the Records type is defined. `work.chat.list` uses it for `open`; any module with a kernel handle (the files search) calls `kernel.chats.mine(chain)` on the caller's own chain instead of keeping a copy of the rule. Kernel side: `grants.chatMine` / `chats.mineIds`.
- feat(stream): one Chat, the live-experience items. `stream.send` takes `mode: "steer" | "queue"` (default steer: words sent while the run works join the running turn at its next step, as `threads.send` always did; `queue` waits for the turn's end and can be taken back). `threads.chat-stop` stops every busy slot of a chat, or one by its slot id. Presence is now produced: `chat.presence` frames (ephemeral, never logged) say `{ who, state: "doing", doing: <tool summary> }` while a slot works on a tool, `{ who, state: "idle" }` when its turn ends, and `{ who, state: "typing" }` from the new `stream.typing { chat, on? }` (`on: false` clears it). One line per author, at most once a second.
- fix(switchboard)!: the chat gate on every `threads.*` call that names a run in a chat now fails CLOSED (reviewer-5): with the kernel on, a call needs a person chain that passes the kernel's chat read; a chain that could not be built (a bad token, an unenrolled device) or whose first hop is not a person is not_found. Only a first-party module's call is exempt. Tests that call `threads.*` as the local owner with no meta use `asOwner(d, root)` (test/helpers.js), which gives the call the facts the real socket would. A run with no agent is a model slot: its kernel session's agent hop is `model:<provider>/<model>#<n>` (minted once, stored in `threads_runs.slot`, narrowed to the run's project), no longer the default assistant's.
- feat(stream)!: one Chat, frame types are `chat.<kind>` (was `session.<kind>`: `chat.user-message`, `chat.text-delta`, `chat.text-done`, `chat.participant-joined` and the rest). The envelope field `session` (the log's id) is unchanged. A new chat with nobody in it who answers starts the default model slot on the first `stream.send` (a chat of one person only), working in `<home>/chats/<chat id>/work` when it has no folder of its own. A chat's status follows its runs (`working` while any run works, `idle` after the turn, `stopped` or `failed` when every run has ended that way), from `thread.status`, which now says its chat.
- feat(stream): one Chat, step E3b: a chat started outside the stream continues in it. - feat(seal): moving sealed values to a Space on another server (the Personal to My Cloud upgrade). The target's sealing process holds an X25519 wrapping key per Space (`wrapKey`); `exportApprove` takes the person's one proof over the move's list of refs, then `export` wraps each listed ref once to the target's key (HKDF, AES-256-GCM, bound to the target record and field) and `import` stores it there. The plaintext is only ever inside the two sealing processes. gateway.seal.wrapKey, exportApprove, export, import; wrapKey and import are on the wire; new action `seal.export` (owner and admin). The sealing line cap is 960 (budget.test.js, awaiting reviewer-3).
