- fix(relay): the Worker relay now keeps a typed code for a 90 s grace when the box's control socket drops (the Node relay got this in 0446ada12): same route key reconnecting keeps the code, a DO alarm frees it after the grace, requests meanwhile are refused. `CODE.graceMs` is in the Worker's constants too.
- refactor(acme): the ACME client, csr and certificate store moved from core/names to lib/acme, so the public gate (core/wink) and lib/publish use them with no core/names edge; docs reference and index regenerated.
- feat(wink): a paired server falls back to the relay when the direct path is down. The home, when it adopts a server, admits the server's own relay key (derived from the peer secret both hold, `relayKeyPair` in core/wink/directkey.js, so nothing is sent) as a relay row of kind `server` (`relay.devices.admit-server`, modules only; the device list never shows it; `relay.devices.drop-server` and the `wink.removed` event take it away), and hands it the relay, its route and its key in the hand-over. The server's `netjoin` opens a `peer` stream to the home's door through that route; `core/relay/index.js` gives a server's channel no HTTP-like door at all and a peer door (`acceptServer` in core/daemon/peer-door.js) that asks "is this still a paired server" on every call and lets it read `network.wink.status` and `network.wink.whois`, nothing else. A hand-over with only the relay (no network address, or no node program) links through the relay alone. Proved on two real machines (scripts/e2e-wink-net.mjs, 17 checks): with the home dropping the server's UDP and its TCP to the gate, the link falls back to the relay, a call still crosses and is still limited to the status read, and the link prefers the direct path again once the block is lifted. Not proven: a NAT between the boxes; the hosted Cloudflare relay (only the Node relay was used).
- fix(relay): a box's published relay address is always wss:// outside a development build (walker: a ws:// record fails on https pages as mixed content). `lib/relay-url.js` is the one check: the pairing ticket's record, the pairing link, the hand-over to a server and `relay.enable` / `relay.apply` refuse a plain ws:// relay in a release build, saying why; a development build still allows ws:// (the tests and walks run a relay on 127.0.0.1).
- fix(wink): reachability maps a router port only for a gate that listens in public (NW2-2). With a configured control address the gate port is mapped at once; with a named box the PUBLIC gate's port is mapped only once that gate is up with its certificate; with no name, or the public gate off, only the loopback gate exists and nothing is mapped. The relay's outside check then lets the name be published as before.
- Public ingress (network): the public gate (core/wink/control/gate.js, publicgate.js) now carries exactly two shapes from the internet to loopback listeners on the box: `POST /hooks/<route>` (a signed webhook, 256 KB at most, length declared, JSON or form; the signature is checked at the home by core/hooks) and `GET|HEAD /s/<token>` (a public share link, core/artifacts/share-server.js). No query, no upgrade, no other path or method: every other request is the same 404 bytes and reaches nothing (tests list the refused shapes and prove no other loopback service is asked); 120 requests a minute per address. `wink.network.status` reports `ingress` (up with the origin, or why not: no name, getting a certificate, waiting for the name to point at the box); the origin is set as the artifacts public base, and `hooks.status` gives each route its address. Honest limits: it exists only once the box has its name and its public port is reachable from outside (or `wink.publish`), and a home behind NAT that cannot be reached stays relay-only; verified with a real hooks listener and the real share server behind a TLS gate on a testbox, not through a name and a real router.
- Glass egress over Wink moved out of this branch (reviewer-4: no dead code): the Mac-side agent, home tunnel and fail-closed SOCKS gate live on branch work/network-egress (core/wink/egress.js) until 0.3.1 wires them.
- feat(wink): a paired server joins its home's network for real. The hand-over (controlUrl, one-time join key, the node name the home gave it, and now the home's door address `peerAddr`) is consumed by `core/wink/netjoin.js`: the server starts its own Wink node, joins the home's Headscale as that name, waits a few seconds for the home to give the node its door rule, and dials the door (direct; retried every 5 s). The server proves itself on the door with an Ed25519 key derived from the peer secret the home holds for it (`core/wink/directkey.js`), so only that server can sign and nothing is added to an identity list. The home admits such a server through `peers.directEntry` and the peer door lets it read `network.wink.status` and `network.wink.whois` as the daemon on its behalf, nothing else. `adopt` now accepts `hostname`, `peerAddr` and `pin` in the hand-over (they were refused as unknown fields). `wink.gatePort` fixes the gate's port behind a configured control address. Proven by `scripts/e2e-wink-net.mjs` on two real machines (testbox6 home, testbox2 server): real pairing with an identity claimed at a stand-in directory, the server's link is direct, a call crosses as device:<sid>, the home's node host admitted it on the direct leg, and after the device row is removed the next call cannot cross. NOT proven: a NAT between the boxes (both have public addresses), a name with the TLS gate (the test uses a plain http control address), IPv6. NOT built: the relay fallback for a server's link to its home (the hand-over carries no relay route for the home and the home has no relay device row for a server), so with the direct path down the link reports `relay: failed, no relay path is configured`.
- feat(wink): the public gate. A box with a claimed name serves its network's control address itself: a second, TLS gate (core/wink/control/publicgate.js, default port 7443, `wink.publicPort`) in front of the same Headscale, with a certificate for `<name>.vyre.run` obtained by DNS-01 through the name directory (core/names/acme.js and certs.js reused; the names module signs, three internal tools `names.directory.acme`, `.acme-clear` and `.publish`, the Wink module only). The certificate key is made once and reused at every renewal (checked daily, renewed inside 30 days), so the pin the pairing hands out stays the same; a renewed certificate takes effect for the next handshake (`gate.setTls`). netd sets Headscale's address from the name (`wink.controlUrl` still overrides and then no second gate is made), restarts the network when a name is claimed or released, passes the gate's port to the reachability helper, and the pairing hand-over carries `controlUrl` and `pin` only once the name points at this box. The name's A record is published (new Worker call `POST /v1/names/publish`: the public IPv4 the directory sees the box at, never one the caller names, never private, CGNAT or documentation ranges; `names.directory.publish`) only when the outside check says the port answers, or when the person says so (`wink.publish: true`). `VYRE_ACME_DIRECTORY` or `wink.acme` picks staging or a test CA. Honest states in `wink.network.status` as `publicGate`: `no-name` (loopback only, the relay carries everything), `getting-cert`, `up`, `failed` with the reason. Risks: a box with no name has no public gate; home NAT is untested here (the testboxes have public addresses), and the hosted relay has no outside check so against it nothing is published by itself; the Worker must be deployed for publish to work. Tests: control/publicgate.test.js and netd.test.js (fakes), names/worker/worker.test.js (publish), and control/publicgate.real.test.js against Pebble (a real DNS-01 order, a real TLS listener, a real renewal that keeps the pin) under `VYRE_PEBBLE=1`.
- feat(install): Headscale and the Wink node program on a Mac server. `scripts/install-mac-server.sh` (`setup_wink_net`) installs the pinned darwin Headscale 0.29.4 (sha256 per architecture) and the release's `wink-forwarder-darwin-<arch>` (listed in the signed SHA256SUMS; built by release.yml in the same pinned Go image as the box image) into Vyre's own bin and exports `VYRE_HEADSCALE_BIN` and `VYRE_WINK_FORWARDER_BIN` to vyred. They run natively beside vyred, not inside the Colima VM: netd supervises them over unix sockets and files, which do not cross the VM. A bad sum or a missing file installs nothing and the relay carries everything. `VYRE_FORWARDER_FILE` uses your own build. Not yet run on a real Mac: the walk is team/0.3/WALK-MAC-HEADSCALE.md.
- fix(relay): a typed Wink code no longer dies when the box's relay link is re-made. The relay (relay/node/server.js) freed a box's typed-code rendezvous the moment its control socket closed or was replaced, so after a link flap (the box's screen still showing the code) every redeem was refused with "That is not a Vyre code" until a relay restart gave the box a fresh code. The code now stays with the route for a 90 second grace (`CODE.graceMs`) after the socket drops and is kept when the same box (same route key) reconnects; what was in flight on the old socket is refused, the code's own 10 minute expiry still applies, and a box that stays gone loses it after the grace. Test: relay/node/server.test.js "a box whose control socket drops and reconnects keeps the code". The reach check endpoint (POST /v1/reach/check) is a separate path and was ruled out.
- refactor(network): another VPN product is gone from the person's view and from start-up (TAILSCALE-removal steps 5, 6 and 9, in reach). The network module starts nothing and holds only `network.wink.*`; `network.tailscale.*`, the guest tools and the funnel tool are deleted (a guest is the space role "temp"). `core/names/tailscale.js`, `identity.js`, `guests.js`, `cloudflare.js` and the names listener are deleted: a name is claimed, recovered, released and watched through the directory and held ("named"); its address is published once the built-in network has one, and `names.connect`, `.owner`, `.fallback`, `.claim-code` and `.domain.serve` are gone. Onboarding's `tailscale` step is `pair` (`onboard.pair`, read from `network.wink.status`; lock and policy actions removed), the setup page's Tailscale stage is a "Your network" stage that reads `network.wink.status` once, `relay/tailnet.js` and the relay's tailnet-key minting are deleted, hooks no longer read or print another product's commands (a route says it is not reachable from the internet yet), `vyre send` and `files.deliver` say they come back with VyreDrop, `core/link/health.js` reads only the Wink node, the vault relay listener's whois identity modes are retired, `vyre up --system` no longer writes a tailnet socket unit, `vyre phone add` is the relay's single-use offer only, `vyre box` and `vyre up` no longer need or look for another VPN, and the site, README, DigitalOcean listing and package keywords say the network is built in. `test/no-tailscale.test.js` keeps it that way with a shrinking ratchet (`test/no-tailscale.ratchet.json`).
- feat(wink,cli): the typed code ships in release and is the way in (user ruling, 5 Oct 2026). One lifetime: core/wink/code.js states ten minutes and three wrong tries (CODE_TTL_MS, MAX_ATTEMPTS) and core/wink/index.js imports them instead of restating them (it said 10 minutes and 3 tries while code.js had 5 and 10). The typed code is on by default and shown beside the QR and long code (`typedCodeDefault` follows `typedCodeOn`); the kill switch is `VYRE_WINK_TYPED_CODE=0` or `wink.typedCode: false`. `wink.server.code { qr: true }` answers `code`, `code_expires` and `code_tries` beside the QR's own `expires`. - feat(app): the proof a paired phone's key lives in the OS key store (platform-3's `attest` field on the entry, held "web" until it verifies). iPhone: `entryAttestation(entryPub)` has an App Attest key vouch for SHA-256("vyre-enrol\nentry:" + the entry's Ed25519 key + "\n" + the chip key's SPKI base64), the same bytes as `enrolClientData`. Android: a new native `attestationChain(alias)` returns the Keystore certificate chain, and `ensureKey` takes an `attestChallenge` (a Keystore key is attested only as it is made, before its public point exists, so the challenge is SHA-256("vyre-enrol\nentry:" + entryPub + "\n") and the leaf's own point must equal the entry's `enclave`); `enclavePublic(entryPub)` makes the key with it. The add-device flow makes the entry key first, then the chip key, then the attestation, and the pairing entry (relay/client/phonepair.js) carries `enclave` and `attest`. scripts/appattest-check.mjs reads that blob (`--attest ... --entry-pub ... --enclave ...`) and can write the sanitised fixture that flips APPATTEST_VERIFIED. Unrun on a real device; Kotlin compiles on the box at the next APK build.
- fix(app): a browser publishes an agreement point. `agreePublic` and `agree` (src/identity/agree.ts) answered null on the web, so a browser device's claim, recovery and add-device entries had no `agree` and a browser-only person could not be in a private chat. On the web they now use app-wire's non-extractable IndexedDB key (src/crypto/agree-key.ts, imported only there), so the point on the entry is the key that opens the chats; browser recovery (`recoveryKeyOptions`) carries it too. Test: src/identity/agree-web.test.js (the published point opens a peer's ECDH; the callers pass it into the entry).
- refactor(mac): the Swift Capsule asks its paired server through Wink, not `link.*` (the lead's ruling). One file names the tools (Sources/Vyred/WinkServer.swift): `wink.server.home` for linked, reachable, name and address, `wink.server.call {tool, input}` for the server's tools. BoxLink, the Planner, history import and VyredClient go through it. The Glass server-address read (`Glass.address`) is deleted; the box address memory links use now comes from the pairing (`BoxLink.boxAddress`). Assumed from network's code (work/network 2f9cbb665, which only calls these two tools; neither is in core/wink/module.json yet): the `home` answer keeps link.status's `{linked, reachable?, box: {name, address}}` shape, an unreachable server answers `server_unreachable` as well as the old codes, and server events still arrive on /v1/link/events. No health, sleep or wake tool exists: the menu bar's link line and the sleep and wake hellos stay behind `has(...)` and say nothing. - fix(mac,windows): KP-3 (reviewer-3, MED). The shell, not the page, says what the person signs. Before, the page chose both the bytes and the Touch ID words, so a team server's JavaScript could ask for an add-device signature under "Unlock Drive". Now the Mac's `enclave.sign` reads the bytes itself (Host/SignSummary.swift): an identity-list change ("Add a device: Ana's iPhone", "Make Sam an owner", "Remove a sign-in (...)", replace-code, recover, genesis) or a yes-moment proof whose card fields (passed with the call) hash to the proof's payload_hash, the check the phone's card does (the canonical form matches kernel/seal and the shared vectors). The summary is the Touch ID sheet's text; the page's `prompt` is never shown, and bytes with no summary are not signed. Windows: `enclave_sign` reads a list change the same way (`identity::chain_summary`, Rust-tested) and asks in a native Windows message box before the TPM key signs; Windows yes-moment proofs are not summarised there yet, so a development build's Windows yes signer will be refused. Tests: Tests/SignSummaryTests.swift, native-win tests and Rust unit tests. Unseen on a real Windows machine: the message box.

- fix(app): on a release build a Windows computer has no yes-moment signer (reviewer-3 and platform-3: no prompt per signature has been shown on a TPM computer, so page JavaScript could mint yes proofs with no person present, and the verifier refuses a tpm key on release too). `WINDOWS_YES_ALLOWED` is false in production; a development build keeps it for walks; a Mac's Secure Enclave key is unaffected. The test names the gap. Also: memory's fixed agree vector (lib/vectors/keywrap.json, from work/memory-noble) is checked through the page adapter and, in Swift, through the Mac's software agreement key.
- fix(windows,mac): reviewer-3's three holds on the Windows capability. (1) Each of the six commands now checks the Origin of the frame that made the call, exactly the pinned origin (`Pinned::is_origin`, tested with lookalikes, http, another port and a missing header), not only the top-level page: the capability admits any https frame, so a cross-origin iframe inside the pinned page would otherwise have passed. (2) The TPM key's comment no longer claims a Windows Hello prompt on every signature, which nobody has shown (the Platform Crypto Provider's consent may not be Hello's; Hello's per-use consent is the Passport provider's). (3) A key a page's script can reach is held as a web key (`held: "web"` on the entry, so it cannot change who speaks for the identity, kernel/identity/chain.js KP-1): a computer app with no hardware key to ask the person, and every Windows key until a TPM computer has shown a prompt per signature (`shellKeyHeld` in src/identity/mac-key.ts; claim, recover and add-device carry it; the pairing code that builds the entry must read `held`: platform). The Windows presence proof now says signer "tpm" (platform-3's class, work/agree-key), never "secure_enclave".
- feat(app): the agreement key, on the Mac and Windows and in the page (the lead's rulings: a second hardware key per device of kind agree, no prompt per use, a software key in the OS keystore where there is no hardware, an `agree` field on the device entry from platform-3). `agree(epk)` is ECDH on P-256: the 32-byte shared secret (the raw X coordinate) between the device's agreement key and a peer's raw uncompressed point; HKDF and AES-GCM stay portable code (lib/keywrap.js). Mac: Host/MacAgree.swift (Secure Enclave key agreement without a biometry flag, else a software key in the Keychain) with bridge calls `identity.agreePublic` and `identity.agree`. Windows: ncrypt.rs makes an ECDH_P256 key in the TPM, else CNG's software provider (DPAPI for this user), and `agree_public` and `agree_secret` join the capability's commands (now six, each behind `from_pinned`); the little-endian raw secret CNG gives is reversed. Page: src/identity/agree.ts (`agreePublic`, `agree`, `validPoint`); claim, recovery and add-device put the point in the entry as `agree` (claim.js, restore.ts, add-device-core.js, relay/client/phonepair.js); kernel/identity/chain.js and PINNED.json are taken from platform-3's work/agree-key. iPhone and Android modules follow.
- feat(app): the yes moments on a computer with a hardware key. `shellSigner()` (src/real/shell-signer.ts) is the phone signer's twin for the Mac window and the Windows panel: it refuses a card whose fields do not hash to its payload_hash, then the enclave key (Secure Enclave with Touch ID; the TPM behind Windows Hello) signs the proof bytes in the low-s form, with the key id of that key; `PhoneApprovals` uses the phone's signer or this one and now also shows on a computer that has one. A computer with no hardware key has no signer. (Web passkeys, which Windows Hello answers inside WebView2, stay the other route.) The Windows app says "Lending this computer comes in a later update." on Share a computer (`WINDOWS_LATER`, `isWindowsShell`). The proof's `signer` field says "secure_enclave", the one hardware class the kernel's verifier knows: a TPM class is a platform question. Tests: src/real/shell-signer.test.js.
- feat(app): every device sends its IANA time zone with every call (the lead's ruling, option B). The app's direct and relay-fetch calls already carry `x-vyre-zone` (src/api/client.ts, read at each call so a trip is followed); this adds it to the peer wire (relay/client/peerclient.js: a `zone` field in the call frame, which the server must read: platform), and to every request Lumen makes to vyred (`x-vyre-zone` in `VyHTTP.requestBytes`, from `TimeZone.autoupdatingCurrent`; Tests/MacIdentityTests.swift zoneHeaderSuite). The Mac app's window and the Windows panel are the web page, so they send it through the app's client.
- feat(windows): the Windows app has an identity key and a TPM key, the way the Mac's window does (parity item 6; ruled by the user's team lead). The main panel (the person's own server's page) gets `window.__vyreShell` of kind "windows" with `identity.public`, `sign`, `enclavePublic` and `enclaveSign` (the Mac's shape; no presence, menu or notices), through exactly four commands (identity_public, identity_sign, enclave_public, enclave_sign) that a narrow capability (capabilities/main-identity.json, https origins) permits for the main window, and that each refuse any page that is not on the pinned origin before a key is touched. The Ed25519 seed is DPAPI-protected on disk and signs in Rust (`vyre_capsule_win::identity`, tested against RFC 8032); the page gets public keys and signatures only. The `enclave` key is a P-256 key in the TPM (CNG's Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider, ncrypt.rs) with a UI policy that makes Windows ask the person (Windows Hello) for every signature; it returns a raw 65-byte point and raw r||s signatures like MacEnclave. A computer with no TPM or no Hello has none and its entry signs alone. Page side: `shellIdentity()` in src/shell/shell.ts serves the Mac and Windows shells alike (mac-key.ts reads it). Presence proofs for tools (x-vyre-presence) and the in-window menu stay the Mac's; lending and agents on Windows are not offered. Tests: local/capsule/native-win/tests/windows-identity.test.js and Rust unit tests; capsule-win CI builds it. Unseen on a real Windows machine: the TPM key and the Hello prompt.

The typed-code pairing (`finish_typed_pair`) now holds its address and handle to the shell's pin rules (`shell::pin_from_offer`, with its tests), and `pairTicket` also returns the box's `handle`. capsule-win CI builds it.

- fix(app): passkey origin rules (walker's finding on app-wire 9aac110af). A passkey belongs to its relying party, so it is made only on https://app.vyre.run in a release build, and also on http://localhost (any port) in a development one (`passkeyRp` in src/identity/passkey.js; any other origin, a lookalike, http, another port or 127.0.0.1 gets none). A browser on any other origin (a space's own web app, a custom domain) is `claimBlocked()`, so it pairs as its own device with the typed code, the one way to pair; the Mac app's window is never blocked. If a claim is still tried there it is refused before the browser is asked or any key is made, with the words "Open app.vyre.run to create your name." (code `wrong_origin`); a browser's own SecurityError for the passkey gives the same words instead of "could not make a passkey". Tests in src/identity/passkey.test.js and src/real/rc.test.js.

- feat(mac): the Mac's device entry carries a Secure Enclave key, as a phone's does (NK-2; the user's ruling: nothing waits for 0.3.1). `Host/MacEnclave.swift` makes a P-256 key in the Secure Enclave with `.userPresence` (Touch ID, or the Mac's password), in its own Keychain item (not the Capsule's presence key, which is enrolled with vyred and must not change a name's entry); the bridge adds `identity.enclavePublic` and `identity.enclaveSign` (the raw 65-byte point; a raw r||s signature after Touch ID). A Mac with no Secure Enclave has none and keeps an Ed25519 entry that signs alone (no software key claims a hardware guarantee). Page side: `macEnclavePublic`, `macEnclaveSign` (the low-s form the chain accepts) and `macSignListChange` in src/identity/mac-key.ts; keys/index.ts gives the Mac `enclavePublic`, `signListChange` and `listChangeSigners` (one Touch ID for both signatures), `hasKeys().presence`, and `keyStorage().presence` "secure-enclave"; claim and recover put `enclave` in the entry; the server pairing signs sig and esig together and reports the device as a computer. Tests: Tests/MacEnclaveTests.swift (a software key and a yes or no stand in for the enclave and Touch ID) and src/identity/mac-key.test.js. Typechecked, not run on a Mac; Touch ID and the enclave are unseen.

A ring that is not a code says so in plain words. `PairEntry`'s own camera view (the old QR reader) stays off with CAMERA_SCAN: no plain QR. The earlier `onTicket` prop on PairEntry is removed. Round trip tested: code to 8 bytes to mark levels to the page's decoder to the same code. Camera and speed in a real WebView are unseen until a phone walk. relay/client/avatarcode.js and its test are taken from work/avatar-code (5abcd7613); the box side (`wink.phone.open` `avatar`, `spaces.invites.create` `code_avatar`) is platform-3's.

- feat(mac): a Mac can claim, recover and sign for a name in the app window (parity item 3; the user's ruling: the seed never reaches the page). `Host/MacIdentity.swift` keeps an Ed25519 seed in the login Keychain (this device only) and signs in Swift (CryptoKit); the bridge's `window.__vyreShell.identity` has `public(create)`, `sign`, `has` and `forget`, which carry only the public key and signatures. Page side: `src/identity/mac-key.ts` makes that a DeviceKey like the phone's; the store keeps `{ kind: "mac-keychain" }` instead of a seed and reads the key back from the shell; `createIdentity` and `recoveryKeyOptions` hand it to claim and recover; `claimBlocked()` is false in the Mac app's window (and its server-only window); `keyStorage()` says `mac-keychain`. A Mac key signs a list change alone (the chain asks for an enclave signature only of an entry that names an enclave key), so no Secure Enclave key is added to the entry; the Mac's hardware-held proof is the later PI-1 item. - fix(calendar): the calendar sync no longer decides outward in code (the code audit's drift). Whether an event write is outward is the Calendar declaration's own flag (the op's kind: change, send, delete), so an event with nobody invited is held for the owner's yes exactly like one that invites people; the shortcut that wrote it without asking is gone. A write that goes out is done safely from the declaration, the Flow runner's safe-write rules: a ledger (kept in the sync's state file) records what an exact change already sent so a repeat sends nothing, the declared rate per minute is kept (a 429 waits for the next look), and the write is read back through the declared pairing and compared with what was sent, stopping with a log line on a mismatch. Reads still go through the google module's `google.api` (the one Google path), not the vault's forward: the vault has no Google connector route to forward to. Tests: core/daemon/calendar-sync.test.js (an event write is held whoever is invited, and read back after the yes).

- fix(app): passkey origin rules (walker's finding on app-wire 9aac110af). A passkey belongs to its relying party, so it is made only on https://app.vyre.run in a release build, and also on http://localhost (any port) in a development one (`passkeyRp` in src/identity/passkey.js; any other origin, a lookalike, http, another port or 127.0.0.1 gets none). A browser on any other origin (a space's own web app, a custom domain) is `claimBlocked()`, so it pairs as its own device with the typed code, the one way to pair; the Mac app's window is never blocked. If a claim is still tried there it is refused before the browser is asked or any key is made, with the words "Open app.vyre.run to create your name." (code `wrong_origin`); a browser's own SecurityError for the passkey gives the same words instead of "could not make a passkey". Tests in src/identity/passkey.test.js and src/real/rc.test.js.

- feat(mac): the Mac's device entry carries a Secure Enclave key, as a phone's does (NK-2; the user's ruling: nothing waits for 0.3.1). `Host/MacEnclave.swift` makes a P-256 key in the Secure Enclave with `.userPresence` (Touch ID, or the Mac's password), in its own Keychain item (not the Capsule's presence key, which is enrolled with vyred and must not change a name's entry); the bridge adds `identity.enclavePublic` and `identity.enclaveSign` (the raw 65-byte point; a raw r||s signature after Touch ID). A Mac with no Secure Enclave has none and keeps an Ed25519 entry that signs alone (no software key claims a hardware guarantee). Page side: `macEnclavePublic`, `macEnclaveSign` (the low-s form the chain accepts) and `macSignListChange` in src/identity/mac-key.ts; keys/index.ts gives the Mac `enclavePublic`, `signListChange` and `listChangeSigners` (one Touch ID for both signatures), `hasKeys().presence`, and `keyStorage().presence` "secure-enclave"; claim and recover put `enclave` in the entry; the server pairing signs sig and esig together and reports the device as a computer. Tests: Tests/MacEnclaveTests.swift (a software key and a yes or no stand in for the enclave and Touch ID) and src/identity/mac-key.test.js. Typechecked, not run on a Mac; Touch ID and the enclave are unseen.
- feat(app): the Wink camera reader is on (DRAWN_CODE_SCAN). The drawn avatar carries the typed code (platform-3, relay/client/avatarcode.js: byte 0 0xC1, five bytes of code symbols, "WK"), so `TypeCode` (Type the code: Add a device, Join a space, the browser start, the phone's connect step) shows a "Scan the code" action on a phone that opens the camera view; a code it reads fills the field and runs the typed code's own pairing, with the ack typed back on the showing device. A ring that is not a code says so in plain words. `PairEntry`'s own camera view (the old QR reader) stays off with CAMERA_SCAN: no plain QR. The earlier `onTicket` prop on PairEntry is removed. Round trip tested: code to 8 bytes to mark levels to the page's decoder to the same code. Camera and speed in a real WebView are unseen until a phone walk. relay/client/avatarcode.js and its test are taken from work/avatar-code (5abcd7613); the box side (`wink.phone.open` `avatar`, `spaces.invites.create` `code_avatar`) is platform-3's.
- refactor(app): `replaceRecoveryCode` and its two tests are gone: the box side drops the recovery code and instant recovery is the only path. The camera page's backdrop colour is a placeholder the component fills from the theme, so no literal colour is in the generated page (raw-colours test).
- feat(app): `PairEntry` takes an `onTicket` prop and, with CAMERA_SCAN on, a platform reader (a phone) and that prop, shows a "Scan the code" action above the typed field that opens the WinkScan camera view, says why when it is slow or the camera is refused, and hands the 8-byte ticket on once. CAMERA_SCAN is still false and no screen passes `onTicket` yet: what a drawn ticket redeems on the box (resolveTicket then pairOffer, or the wink.phone path) waits on platform-3's answer.
- feat(mac): a Mac can claim, recover and sign for a name in the app window (parity item 3; the user's ruling: the seed never reaches the page). `Host/MacIdentity.swift` keeps an Ed25519 seed in the login Keychain (this device only) and signs in Swift (CryptoKit); the bridge's `window.__vyreShell.identity` has `public(create)`, `sign`, `has` and `forget`, which carry only the public key and signatures. Page side: `src/identity/mac-key.ts` makes that a DeviceKey like the phone's; the store keeps `{ kind: "mac-keychain" }` instead of a seed and reads the key back from the shell; `createIdentity` and `recoveryKeyOptions` hand it to claim and recover; `claimBlocked()` is false in the Mac app's window (and its server-only window); `keyStorage()` says `mac-keychain`. A Mac key signs a list change alone (the chain asks for an enclave signature only of an entry that names an enclave key), so no Secure Enclave key is added to the entry; the Mac's hardware-held proof is the later PI-1 item. Tests: Tests/MacIdentityTests.swift (a memory seed store: stable key, signatures verify with CryptoKit, forget) and src/identity/mac-key.test.js. Typechecked, not run on a Mac; the Keychain store is untried.

The app's deck imports now read src/vendor/deck (Find's command parser, session titles and answer-with added there; commands.js typed so tsc is clean).
- fix(wink): a pairing that fails after the server was adopted gives back the channel it wrote (restoring any earlier one), and the home server is the newest COMPLETED pairing: a `paired:<server>` mark is written when a pairing finishes, `homeServerId()` picks the newest mark (a channel with no mark, from before this, counts as the oldest), and removing a server drops its mark. Before, a failed pairing's channel stayed and `homeServerId()` took the first channel by key, so a later pairing could leave calls going to the dead server (found in the live drop run).
- feat(relay-client): `joinFromPhone` (relay/client/browserjoin.js), the counterpart of pairServer for a browser with no box: paste or scan the phone's long code (`wink.phone.open`, "Add a device"), both sides show three words, the person at the phone picks them, and the browser's entry goes on the identity list with its key, its key-agreement point (`agree`, required: 65-byte uncompressed P-256) and `held: "web"`. Only the long code is taken; the short typed code, an avatar and a server's code are `bad_code`; a missing or misshapen agree point is `bad_key`. `addThisDevice` now passes `held`, `enclave` and `attest` through in the entry. Tested over a real relay and daemon.

- feat(files): the receiver opens a drop's wrapped key through `spaces.identity.unwrap-drop { wrap, aad }` (platform-3: purpose-bound, only the file key comes back, the aad starts with `vyre-drop-wrap\n`), replacing the raw `spaces.identity.ecdh`. The wrap's aad is `vyre-drop-wrap\n<drop id>\n<receiving entry id>`. Merges work/entry-fields3 751cdc71c.

- fix(wink): pairing passes a device's agree point on only when it is a real P-256 point: 65 bytes, uncompressed, and on the curve (noble's decoder throws off-curve), so a made-up point never reaches the identity list (reviewer-4's LOW). Test: an off-curve point, a short one and none are dropped.

- feat(files,wink): VyreDrop seals to the receiving computer's key-agreement key on the person's identity list (the ruling to replace the interim drop key). The sender reads the receiver's `agree` point from the list (`spaces.identity.devices.read`), wraps a fresh file key to it with lib/keywrap.js (`wrapForDevice`, ECDH-ES), and seals the chunks under a key derived from it; the receiver opens it with its own key through `spaces.identity.ecdh` (the private key never leaves the identity module). A computer registers only its entry id (`files.drop.register { eid }`); the server can no longer name a key, and a drop sealed to another entry does not open on the real receiver. Deleted: the X25519 drop key and its file, `wink.identity.sign`, `wink.identity.check` and core/wink/drop-identity.js (the signing oracle reviewer-4 flagged). Takes lib/keywrap.js, lib/databox.js and the @noble dependencies from work/memory-noble 5d7eb572f, on work/entry-fields3 2deef60cd.

- feat(memory): `memory.identity.status` also returns `space`, the id of the Space whose kernel chain the grant's proof is verified in (the Space the phone signs the payload over). Public data.
