- fix(memory)!: an unlock ask is signed over sorted-key canonical JSON (kernel/core/canonical.js), not plain `JSON.stringify`: field order never decides validity. `finish` now checks on the server that a standing grant matches the asking server's fingerprint (before, any grant let any ask finish); a grant for server A cannot finish an ask from server B. Test: core/memory/identity/grant-server.test.js.
- feat(memory): `memory.identity.status` also returns `server_key` (this server's public JWK, which the phone pins when the person says yes to the grant) and `id` (the identity id the grant proof is over). Public data only.
- fix(memory): `memory.upgrade.plan` and `memory.upgrade.move` answer only the spaces module (`module:spaces`), not any module caller (reviewer-5 LOW).
- fix(memory): `memory.upgrade.move` calls `spaces.storage.*` with `{ relay: true }`, so the storage calls reach as the person the spaces module relayed (a plain nested module call carries no person). Needs windows' ctx.call relay (work/spaces).
- feat(kernel,lib): the sealed stores run unchanged on a phone and in a browser. New dependencies, exact pins with lockfile integrity: `@noble/ciphers` 1.3.0, `@noble/hashes` 1.8.0 and `@noble/curves` 1.9.7 (the last for the device-key ECDH in lib/keywrap.js; the first two synchronous, pure JS, audited; chosen over node:crypto because the sealed store's write-through hooks are synchronous and the same code must run on Node, a phone and a browser). `lib/databox.js` is the data cryptography (AES-256-GCM boxes `{ v: 1, iv, ct, tag }` identical to lib/keywrap.js's, HKDF-SHA256, HMAC-SHA256 names, SHA-256, base64 and base64url over Uint8Array); `kernel/store/sealed.js`, `core/memory/identity/remote-backend.js` and `spaces-transport.js` import it and no longer touch node:crypto or Buffer (a test enforces it). Device-key operations (ECDH with the agree key) stay asynchronous elsewhere. The injectable primitives are gone. Tests: `kernel/store/sealed.test.js`, the live put-if in `core/memory/identity/spaces-transport.test.js`.
- feat(stores): one Space on a 4 GB server, automatically. The memory profile is chosen by the machine (`autoProfile`: `tiny` under about 6 GB, `small` above; "auto" is now the default and the person sees no setting). `tiny` caps server 1200, worker 900, db 192, redis 64 MB and lets a container spill half its cap into swap; measured on a real Twenty in a 3 GB cgroup (a 4 GB server less the OS and the daemon): no restart or kill, peaks 1196, 892, 109 and 25 MB, 2221 MB in all (the earlier 1024/640 caps crash-looped the worker; an uncapped Space peaked at 3105 MB). The fit check uses that measured need (`requireFor`, `MEASURED`), and when a server has no room the answer is one plain line, "This server is full. Use a bigger server for another space." The root helper (box/vyre) turns on a 2 GB swapfile once on a Linux server under 6 GB with no swap, and gives the compose generator the host's memory. `stores/twenty/live/measure-live.mjs` (with `CGROUP_PARENT` and `PROFILE_JSON`) and `latency-live.mjs` are the measurement scripts. Not measured: the first start takes about 270 s and the first define about 500 s on a shared 8 GB box; swap use was not exercised (the test box has none).
- feat(spaces): the Personal to My Cloud upgrade (the user's ruling, 5 Oct). `spaces.upgrade.plan { to }` shows what would move (records by type, what cannot be carried, the hash the one approval is bound to); `spaces.upgrade.run { to, plan_hash }` does it with ONE approval (kernel act `space.upgrade`, proof request `upgrade`), carrying every record with its id (`records.create` takes `{ import: true, id }`, a new admin action `records.import`), links rewritten to My Cloud in a second pass, sealed fields named as not carried, a rerun finishing what stopped, chats and memory through their owners' ports (`chats.upgrade.*`, `memory.upgrade.*`, module callers only), and a report of what moved and what did not. Afterwards the Personal space keeps its records readable, takes no new writes (`moved`), and its row says `upgraded_to`. Tests: lib/spaces/upgrade.test.js (SQLite into Twenty over a fake Twenty), core/spaces/spaces.test.js.
- chore(stores,records): the estate planning kit's welcome email and the stores' live scripts and spike notes say Juniper Studio (launch's sweep, team/0.3/HARLOW-SWEEP.md); test fixtures are left alone.
- feat(stores): a record's kernel attributes are written WITH its create (conformance revision 7). `store.create(type, id, data, { attrs, urn })`: the Twenty store puts the four mirror columns in the same Create mutation (one fewer Get and one fewer Update per create, no queued follow-up, and a record never exists without its owner attributes), the built-in SQLite store writes them in the same unit, and the memory store has nothing to write. The gateway passes them at create and its follow-up `kattrs.set` no longer sends a second mirror write (the store remembers what the create wrote); a later attribute change still goes through `mirrorAttrs`. New conformance case: attributes given at create are found by `attr_filter` on the first read. Found while measuring create latency (median 137 ms through the gateway, 3 requests per create against 88 ms and 2 at the store).
- feat(seal): moving sealed values to a Space on another server (the Personal to My Cloud upgrade). The target's sealing process holds an X25519 wrapping key per Space (`wrapKey`); `exportApprove` takes the person's one proof over the move's list of refs, then `export` wraps each listed ref once to the target's key (HKDF, AES-256-GCM, bound to the target record and field) and `import` stores it there. The plaintext is only ever inside the two sealing processes. gateway.seal.wrapKey, exportApprove, export, import; wrapKey and import are on the wire; new action `seal.export` (owner and admin). The sealing line cap is 960 (budget.test.js, awaiting reviewer-3).
- fix(modules): a sandboxed module's SQL stays in its own file (no ATTACH, VACUUM, PRAGMA, extensions; reads only through `query`); a Flow's call of a module tool claims the owner's surface only when the run's person is the owner; the outward kind-word hold is one `Registry.outwardRefusal()` used by both the registry and the retrofit gates, so a held act resolves placeholders and tells the card either way.
- fix(data-stores): the kernel's counters, the text index's shadow tables, the shipped Engineer agent, the sealer's own folder, the box's pairing key and `membership.read` are named as not the person's data (each with its reason); an agent the person made still counts.
- feat(time): the device's time zone reaches `meta.zone` from the `x-vyre-zone` header (the CLI sends it) and from the peer-wire call frame; every harness brief opens with one `timeLine()` (lib/time).
- feat(modules): an added module written against the SDK runs in the sandbox: its ctx is the host-side one and each door is a message (core/modules/sandbox-ctx.js, kernel/modules/child.js); its own database file with async store exec/query/migrate; `needs.kernel.records` and `needs.kernel.files` (narrow verbs, an external label, no handle); `does.kits` (proposed by `vyre module add`); `does.tools[].flow` (a module tool is a Flow step: registered action, owner/admin role grants, the flows `call` port); a Now card from `shows.deck: now:<tool>` in the app; examples/modules/forms and docgen. ADR 0047 addendum.
- refactor(events): the event bus is kernel/bus.js over the kernel log alone (the events table and core/events are gone); an event's id is its log position; the daemon attaches the home's log.
- feat(kernel): the daemon wires the inference door, every reveal is logged before it is shown, every tool's gates go through authorize (the compiled legacy rules; the outward rule now mirrors the registry), the VYRE_KERNEL switch and the kernel-off start path are deleted, sealer.api.reseal moves a sealed value between Spaces inside the sealing process.
- feat(presence): per-person switches presence.confirm_pairing, presence.confirm_vault and presence.confirm_outward (default on; Settings > Privacy).
- refactor(vault,watchers): reviewer-4 G-3, properly. The grant check is one function, `Vault.granted`, which `release` now calls; a new module-only tool `vault.granted` answers it without handing over a value, and the watcher's Google read asks that instead of reading the vault's grants and matching them itself. A grant to the watchers module as a whole is still not a grant to a watcher.
- fix(watchers): reviewer-4 G-3. The Google read matches a vault grant to exactly this watcher (as `vault.release` does), so a grant to the watchers module as a whole reads nothing; tested.
- fix(watchers): reviewer-4 G-1. A watcher that reads a Google account (`net.<host>.google`) reads nothing until a person grants the account's vault item to that watcher (`vyre vault grant <item> watchers --watcher <name>`), checked in the runtime for a dry run and for a run alike; `watchers.preset` answers with that grant command. Before, the read went through `google.api` with no grant, so a model could write and dry-run such a watcher and read the owner's mail.
- fix(google): reviewer-4's hold on calendar-live. `google.api` takes an exact caller (`module:leases` for the calendar sync, `module:watchers` for reads only), and refuses a write whose `sendUpdates` is not none unless the body names attendees. Tests: another module is denied; a change to a pulled event that has guests is held for a yes (the pull keeps attendees as people).
- fix(calendar): the sync re-checks an approved Google write as the task's doer (the Flows service under the owner) with the request's bind, the rule platform-3's approval fix makes real (merged work/approval-token-verify). On the real kernel the approved write now goes out once and the approval is spent; before, it was never allowed. Real-daemon test in core/daemon/calendar-sync-google.test.js.
- feat(calendar): a synced Event keeps the zone it was made in. `time_zone` is Google's `start.timeZone`, else the calendar's own zone (the list's `timeZone`); times stay UTC ISO, so a screen can show "9:00 am PT" beside the viewer's own time. An all-day event is date only and has no zone; a push writes `time_zone` back (and invents none when there is none, where it used to send UTC). Tested with an America/Los_Angeles event, in records/calendar/sync.test.js.
- refactor(connectors): one Google path, the google module (the lead's ruling, 5 Oct 2026). The `google-api`, `gmail-api` and `google-calendar-api` OAuth presets, the vault credentials on the Gmail and Calendar declarations (`auth.type: "google"` now, with no `also`, and `connectors.declare` refuses it), and the vault-connector branch of the calendar sync are deleted; the declaration format and Stripe stay. The calendar sync runs for each Google account through `google.api`. `google.api` also reads Gmail (GET of the profile, the message list, a message or a thread; never a write). A Log communications watcher names the account, `net: { "gmail.googleapis.com": { "google": "work" } }`, and the runtime reads through `google.api` as a module, so the watcher holds no credential and its card says "your connected Google account, read only"; `watchers.preset` takes `google` for a Google connector, `connectors.logging` takes `google` (default: the account whose address it is). `connectors.declared` lists a Google connector as installed when an account is connected. New `mergedParts` in records/connectors/format.js. "Vyre can write drafts; sending asks you first" is now the first line of the google module's mail tip. Reviewer GC-1 to GC-3: `google.api` refuses a path segment that is or decodes to `.`, `..` or hides a slash; only `module:leases` (the calendar sync) may write and `module:watchers` may read; the sync passes the request's `bind` when it re-checks an approval, so an approval for one write is not accepted for another.

- fix(calendar): the Space's calendar sync now runs for the Google accounts people actually connect (the google module's, signed in with a service account or OAuth), not only for vault connectors: each account is pulled into Event records (source google, calendar google-<account>) and Vyre's own events are pushed back only through the approval path (held for the owner's yes, the approval checked for that act before the write). The new `google.api` tool (Vyre's own modules only; Calendar events paths only, narrowest scope per method, If-Match allowed) is how the sync reaches Google, so the token is still minted only by the google module from the vault. A connector name with a colon made the kernel refuse the resource (wrong_space), so accounts are named google-<account>. Tested in a real kernel-on vyred against the fake Google.
- feat(identity): claim a name from a browser with a passkey (0.2.9, gap A29). `claimIdentityWithPasskey` (apps/app/src/identity/claim.js) makes a WebAuthn credential (P-256, user verification required) as the identity's first device and signs the genesis and the claim's record with it; `createPasskeyKey` and `restorePasskeyKey` (apps/app/src/identity/passkey.js) read the attestation with a small CBOR reader, normalise the high-s twin an authenticator may return, and keep only the credential id and public key. A passkey is a full device (unlike a key a page can reach). The directory could verify a passkey's signature on a chain op but not on a name record or an act; `verifyWith` now takes the signing entry (`signing` from `signerKey`) and checks a passkey's assertion as one, in the Worker, the client directory, the audit key, the seal's bindings and spaces. The pinned hash of kernel/identity/chain.js is updated; merging with work/no-labels needs it recomputed.
- fix(kernel): one rule for an outward approval, no older looser path. Every producer of a held outward act records `form.bind` (the Flow runner now does: `requestBind` of a service step's request, `actBind` of any other call step's action, resource and input; the calendar sync already did), every consumer passes the same bind (leases now bind lent-computer sessions too), and `approvedAct` refuses an outward approval that recorded none. `actBind` is new in kernel/seal/uses.js. test/outward-flags.test.js checks that every registry-held outward tool binds its card to a digest of the whole input.
- fix(kernel): `approvedAct` compares the bind. An approved task that recorded the bind of what the person saw (`form.bind`, a digest of the request as it would be sent) releases only a request that carries the same bind; approve A and send B is refused, and a request that states none is too. It holds for every outward act, not only the calendar sync (which checked it for itself). `authorize` passes the request's `input.bind` through, and the service lease passes the bind it computes from the request it is about to send. An approval that recorded no bind is judged as before. Test: approve A, send B with that approval, refused.
- feat(wink): pairing passes the phone's key-agreement point (`agree`) into `spaces.identity.enrol` beside its key and label (platform-3's daemon-agree), so a newly paired device can open private chats at once. The phone's wait call and the phone client (relay/client/phonepair.js) carry `entry.agree`; only a 65-byte uncompressed P-256 point is passed on, anything else is dropped and the pairing still completes.

- fix(runner): the home keeps a lent session's chat id only when the lender's person is in that chat (the kernel's chat read decision), and otherwise drops it, so a lender can no longer make someone else's chat show as running on their computer (reviewer-4's LOW on runner.places).

- feat(runner): `runner.places { space }` (reach person) answers where the caller's chats run: `[{ chat, session, computer, device, online }]`. `runner.start` takes an optional `chat` id (checked for shape, kept in the home's lent table, never on the wire); the home lists its lent sessions to the daemon only. Only chats the caller is in (kernel chats.mine) appear; no chat list means no rows. The computer's name and online state come from relay.devices.all.

- fix(daemon): a home with no storage key of its own for a Space (no Drive, no pool) refuses to hold a lent computer's work, in plain words, instead of keeping the checkpoints in the clear (reviewer-5): every call of the lent service answers `unavailable` and nothing is written. Test in core/daemon/lent-service.test.js.

- feat(runner,kernel): a lent session's checkpoints are encrypted at rest on the home (launch's finding: the home's store kept them in the clear). The checkpoint store takes the Space's own key (derived from its pool key, kernel/storage/keys.js, held per kernel and out of reach of modules) and seals every file, version, checkpoint record and the commit pointer with AES-256-GCM under it with its place in the associated data; each transcript line is sealed inside its JSON line (the log's shape and offsets stay); a file's folder is named by a keyed hash, not its path. A restart reads it, another Space's key and a file copied to another name open as nothing. Seen on testbox6: after a lent session the home's lent/ folder holds no readable text and no file or folder named for what is in it. Without a key (tests, a home with no sealing process) the store is plain as before.

- fix(runner): a restart reconciles what the last runner left (lead's gap). Each session's process group is recorded (`run/<space>.<session>.pid`, with its start time) and a restarted runner ends any that outlived it; each workspace names its Space beside the encrypted folder (`space.id`), and at start the runner asks that Space's home whether this computer still has access: access that ended while the daemon was down (an Offer withdrawn, the member removed or gone) deletes the workspace, as a pushed revoke does, and access that stands leaves it locked and encrypted for `runner.start` to resume from the home's checkpoint; a home that cannot be reached is asked again each minute. Test (core/runner/lent-wire.test.js): a session outlives its runner, the restart ends it and keeps the locked workspace, the Offer is withdrawn while the daemon is down, the next restart leaves nothing. The test rig's lease key is now the same for the same member and computer, as the real sealing process gives it.

- fix(runner,daemon): no part of a credential is logged on its way to a lent session (reviewer-4): the credential resolver's debug line (it printed the first 11 characters of the key) and the whole `VYRE_DEBUG_LENT` scaffolding (the lender's credential-call stderr, the proxy's upstream 4xx text, the runner's event log) are removed; `VYRE_LENT_AGENT` and `VYRE_LENT_AGENT_ARGS` are honoured only on a development build with `VYRE_LENT_AGENT_DEV=1`. A test fails if any of them comes back.

- feat(files,wink): VyreDrop over Wink, no Tailscale. `files.send` (a computer to another of the person's computers) and `files.deliver` (the server's file to a computer) move a file through the person's server: it is sealed on the sender to the receiving computer's own drop key (X25519 + HKDF + AES-256-GCM per chunk, a fresh key per drop, the chunk's place in the associated data), held on the server as ciphertext only (bounded: 2 GB a file, 10 GB in all, 7 days, all configurable under `files.drop`), and taken by the receiver, which opens every chunk, checks the whole file's hash, writes it into its inbox (guard-checked, never over an existing file) and tells the server to delete it. A receiver that is asleep gets it when it connects: the server offers what waits when a computer connects (`files.drop.push`) and down the held connection when a drop is finished (`wink.drop.offer`, accepted only from the paired server). Receiving is off until `files.receive` is turned on, which makes the computer's drop key (`drop-key.json`, 0600) and registers its public half. Only the person's own paired computers can send or receive (the server admits only the owner's devices); a browser is no target. The Taildrop code (core/files/drop.js) and its tests are gone; `vyre send <file> [--to <computer>]` uses the new path. New internal tools: `relay.devices.all`, `wink.home.id`, `wink.device.call` (drop offers only). Proved on testbox6 over the real relay: a 2 MB file and a small one from the server to a computer arrived with the same hash and the server kept nothing; a drop for a stopped computer waited on the server as ciphertext and arrived when the computer started. Not built: sending to another person's computer by an explicit grant (needs a registered kernel action), and a direct path between two computers (everything goes through the server).

- fix(wink,spaces): `wink.lent.revoked` is accepted only from the paired server that hosts that Space (reviewer-3 NW2-1): the device's peer session now tells the handler which server it is, and the handler asks the spaces module (`spaces.server.of`, internal) which server hosts the Space; any other server or connection is refused, so nobody else can end a computer's grant or stand in for the home (core/wink/lent-revoked.js, tests). Lending a computer again no longer relies on the lender's own record to know it must be reinstated: the home's answer to a lease probe (revoked) decides, so a computer whose member was removed from the Space entirely and lent again is reinstated under the admin's yes; real-process test for that case (kernel/gateway/leases.real.test.js).

- feat(kernel): every hosted Space has its own Drive from the moment it is created, like the home Space (kernel/storage/provision.js, used by kernel/home.js and kernel/spaces). Before, only the home Space had one: a Space hosted on a server had no Drive, so no files, no versions and no place for the per-chat keys. Each Space gets its own pool under its own folder and its own pool key (the sealing process derives it per Space; a file-held kernel key derives it from that Space's key), so one Space's chunks are not in another's pool and are not openable with another's key (test). `retire` still takes back a Space that was only started: an empty provisioned Drive is not content.

- feat(runner,daemon): the provider route takes a subscription sign-in token. A claude account of kind setup-token becomes a route that sends the token upstream as `Authorization: Bearer` with `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` added to the program's own beta list (route-level static headers, validated), resolved at the home per request; the session still holds only its per-session token. The model route is only for the home owner's own account. An owner's or admin's approval of a lend gives no key of the member's: a lease needs the member's own acceptance (test). Development builds can start a one-shot agent turn with `VYRE_LENT_AGENT_ARGS` and print the upstream's own 4xx text with `VYRE_DEBUG_LENT`.

- feat(runner,vault,daemon,kernel): a lent session reaches the model with the member's own provider key, held at the home. The home's default definition builds the provider route from the member's claude account (`sessions.accounts.key`), the lender's proxy asks the home per request (`leases.use`), and the home answers from the vault through a new narrow credentials-port method, `apiKey`, that returns only the key of an API-key item. The kernel's `resolveCredential` was never wired in the daemon, and a hosted Space's kernel was not given one; both are. A route marked `provider` (set only by the home's own definition) may make exactly POST /v1/messages, POST /v1/messages/count_tokens and GET /v1/models without a per-call yes; every other call, and every other route, still asks. The runner takes the key lease before it asks for the definition (the home binds the routes to that lease). Proved on testbox6 with a fake upstream: the right key reached it on every call, the key is not on the lender's disk or in the sandbox, and nothing is sent after removal. A real Claude turn is not proved yet.

- feat(spaces,kernel): lending a computer again after its access ended works. `leases.reinstate` is on the remote wire (the home's challenge covers op `lease.reinstate` over the member and the computer, the same one yes as every other act), and `spaces.devices.lend` runs it with the new lend when the computer was lent to that Space before, under the kernel's own role check (an owner or admin). Proved on testbox6: a computer removed from a Space, lent again, got a working runner (`runner.start` answers a pid; before, "access to this space has ended").

- feat(runner,spaces,daemon): lending a computer works end to end between two machines. A member's own session for a Space runs on their computer instead of the server (the agent by name, found on the lender: `VYRE_CLAUDE_BIN` or PATH; the Space's definition is `lentSpec` or the member's own agent with the provider as the only network), the work sits in an encrypted workspace (gocryptfs, key from the Space's lease, memory only), every turn is checkpointed to the Space's home, and when the grant ends (an Offer withdrawn, the member removed or left) the home tells that computer down the connection it holds (`wink.lent.revoked`, `runner.revoke`): the sessions stop and the whole workspace is deleted within about two seconds while the home keeps everything. Also fixed: the home names the computer calling (`lent.whoami`, from what the transport proved) and the Offers are made under that id (the identity entry id never matched what the home sees, so a lent computer was never allowed); the home's challenge for an offer call carried no op or payload (WIRE_TO_PROOF), so no device could sign it; `spaces.devices.lend` answers a server's challenge with this computer's key on a development build; an owner or admin can stop a member's computer from the Space's own home (`member`, the id the Space gives it); a revoked runner is made again after a new grant. Not wired: reinstating a computer whose lease was revoked is an admin act on the home's sealing process with no tool on the wire, so a computer removed from a Space cannot be lent to it again until that is done.
- fix(box): three release blockers from a fresh install of trunk (network). (1) A record store that cannot be set up no longer crash-loops vyred: the Space gets a store that answers `unavailable` in plain words (stores/twenty/deferred-store.js), the daemon stays up, `<dir>/store-state.json` and `/v1/health` `records_store.unavailable` say why and when the next try is, and the setup is retried in the background (30 s, doubling to 15 min); when it works the definitions the kernel made at start are applied and the store forwards. No retry tool yet: `registry.deps.storeRetry` tries now (a tool is the follow-up). A hosted Space's deferred store keeps queueing definitions. (2) An explicit `VYRE_STORE=sqlite` in vyre.env is honored on a packaged server (it was ignored; `auto` still means Twenty). (3) The Space helper's lock names its run and is taken over when that run is gone; `space-helper install` (a fresh install and every update) clears stale locks, claims, the up-rate window and old answers, never a Space. The install failure itself (the helper could not record `${TWENTY_IMAGE_REF:-...}`) is fixed by merging work/network-twenty (9310c9822). Also: wink/forwarder is in the pack, and test/box-pack-covers-dockerfile.test.js checks every Dockerfile COPY source is in it.

- fix(planner): one importer for the 0.2.x upgrade. legacy.js keeps platform-2's append-only migration list (the five released steps and planner_moved) and the idempotent importer: no table is dropped, a run that carried everything records "~complete" and each carried id in planner_moved, and later starts do nothing. The upgrade test builds its database through the real migrate and checks the fixture's steps equal the released ones.
- fix(planner,gateway): an event or reminder a person adds through the planner is theirs in the Bin. The planner writes on its own chain and names the person with `on_behalf` (their own kernel-built chain, honoured only on a module's service chain, so `created_for` is never a value a caller types: a plain chain that passes `on_behalf`, or a chain-shaped object the kernel did not build, is refused, and `created_for` in `attrs` stays refused). The member who deletes it finds it in `planner.bin` and restores it; another member, and an agent with no person, see nothing. Tests: kernel/gateway/bin.test.js (forgery), core/planner/events-delete.test.js (the full path with two members).

- fix(planner,gateway): planner.bin reads under the caller's own chain, not the planner's service chain, so an agent no longer lists every deleted event; the gateway's Bin rule matches the person on the creating chain (a new `created_for` attribute) instead of the chain's last hop, so a person sees what their assistant removed and another person through the shared assistant id sees none (6 gateway bin tests).
- feat(records,planner): the Bin. records.query takes `include_deleted` (records.list passes it): removed rows are listed under the same read rules, to whoever made them or an owner or admin; sealed values stay sealed. planner.bin lists the person's deleted events for planner.delete restore. A live Twenty test covers an event's rrule and url (create, update, clear, remove, bin list, restore, expansion).
- test(planner): the upgrade from a 0.2.x planner is tested on a real database: `core/planner/legacy-fixture/store-0.2.3-rc.2.js` is the 0.2.3 planner's own store and migrations (`git show v0.2.3-rc.2:core/planner/store.js`), which build a file database, and `legacy-upgrade.test.js` carries it, restarts, carries a second copy of the same rows, and crashes before every write; every carried row is in the records exactly once. A to-do that sat under another to-do keeps its parent (the import goes parent first); one that sat under a reminder is carried without a parent, since a Task's parent is another Task.
- perf(twenty): a new Space starts from a saved, already migrated database instead of migrating and defining from nothing. Measured on a real Twenty on the test box: provisioning plus the first define of the core types took about 790 s (393 s provisioning, 394 s define); a Space made from the saved database is ready in about 62 s and its first define is a no-op (0.8 s). Where the time went: the server's three first-boot steps (about 31 s each plus the migrations themselves), one serialised Twenty call of 1.2 to 1.6 s for every field (116 calls) and 2.6 s for every type, and 101 view-field position writes. `stores/twenty/live/build-golden.mjs` builds the saved database once per Twenty image (a 1.1 MB `pg_dump` plus what the store knows of the types); `findGolden` (stores/twenty/provision.js) uses it when its image is exactly the Space's (`VYRE_TWENTY_GOLDEN_DIR`, else `stores/twenty/golden`, git-ignored, shipped with a release). A one-shot `restore` step in the Space's compose file loads it before the server starts, drops the saved signing key (sealed with other secrets), and puts the Space's own password on the saved user, so nothing shared stays valid; the server skips its migration steps (`DISABLE_DB_MIGRATIONS`), an upgrade still migrates; then one sign-in makes the Space's own API key. Without a saved database the old path runs. `defineCore` (stores/twenty/space-store.js) is the one place a Space's core types and base Kit are made. A type that is exactly as it was costs no view or field-order work on a define. A view's id no longer carries the Space's name (a Space has its own Twenty).
- perf(twenty): the view-field order writes only what differs (relative order, not absolute position: 101 writes became about 44 on a first define); a create no longer reads first (the primary key is the answer). Records through the store: 15 to 20 a second one at a time, 40 a second in parallel; through the gateway 12 a second after a Space's first use (a type's four mirror columns are made when the saved database is built, not at a person's first record). `stores/twenty/live/profile.mjs` counts every Twenty call by operation.
- feat(tasks): a task due in a space that keeps a time zone (`spaces.tier` answers `time_zone`) carries `due_shown` ("9:00 am PT · 9:00 pm your time") and `due_zone` in `tasks.list`, `tasks.get` and `tasks.request` results; the reader's zone is the device's. No zone, or the reader in it, adds nothing. `spaceZone` in lib/cloud-gate.js reads it. fix(twenty): a type's views are made after its relations exist (a view may name a link); the task's `stage` is plain text.
- fix(lib/time): JSDoc types on every parameter, so a strict `tsc` over the library (the app's) is clean (23 implicit-any errors fixed). test(kernel/tasks): a task's parent and project read back as `{ urn }` whether the caller sent `{ urn }` or plain text.
- refactor(kernel/tasks): the one `task` type is objects' `TASK` in records/core-types.js; kernel/tasks/type.js is gone. A task's parent, project and record are link fields holding `{ urn }` on the record (the kernel still keeps a parent as an id and a project as a urn; the gateway takes `{ urn }` or plain text from a caller). The task's `stage` has no options: it names a stage of the record the task concerns, which is any Kit's. Merged work/objects 0c9455cb1.
- feat(planner): the Cloud gate refuses only a person with no Cloud membership at all. A Basic personal space with a team (or My Cloud) is let through, and the home's own space never counts as the Cloud space. The message is "Planner needs a Cloud space: join a team or set up My Cloud" (`needs_cloud`, `detail.spaces` empty). The task tools gate on the space the call resolves to. Custom fields and views on personal tasks stay My Cloud only: the Basic limit (cleanup, `cloud_required`) is the one guard. One engine, one store port (`store`): Twenty on a Cloud space, memory's encrypted store on Personal. Tests: lib/cloud-gate.test.js, core/planner/{gate,records}.test.js, kernel/tasks/records.test.js.
- feat(lib/time): the one shared time library (the user's time-zone ruling, option B). Three clocks (the person's, from the device in use; the space's; the server's, never used), everything stored as UTC ms. API: the zone functions the planner had (`validZone`, `systemZone`, `localParts`, `offset`, `toUTC`, `localDate`, `addDays`, `parseDate`, `parseWall`, `dateString`, `wallString`, `checkRepeat`, `nextOccurrence`, moved to lib/time/zones.js; core/planner/time.js re-exports them); `ZONE_HEADER` ("x-vyre-zone"), `zoneFrom(value, fallback)`, `personZone(meta, set, fallback)`; `scopeZone({ scope, person, space })` (a personal thing in the person's zone, a space's in the space's, an unclear one in the space's with both said); `resolve("tomorrow at 9", { now, zone })` to a UTC instant on the wall of the zone, daylight saving included, or `{ ambiguous }` ("5" with no am or pm); `showTimes(ms, { person, space })` ("9:00 am PT · 9:00 pm your time", a different day says which), `clock`, `zoneLabel` ("PT"), `stamp`; `timeLine({ now, person, space, contacts })`, the line every model brief carries. Tests: lib/time/time.test.js (7).
- feat(daemon): a call carries the zone of the device making it. The CLI sends `x-vyre-zone` (its own zone); the daemon believes it only if it is a real zone and hands tools `meta.zone`; nothing a module passes can set it.
- feat(planner): personal reminders follow the person. A call from the person's own device that carries a zone moves the planner's zone (which floating alarms are read in) and the alarms' next rings to it; a zone that is not one, an agent's call and a shell on a server are not followed; `planner.settings { follow_device: false }` turns it off. Test: records.test.js.
- fix(test): `vyre agenda`, `alarm`, `todo` and `notes` answer `unavailable` on a home with the kernel off (the planner keeps its records there), which core/cli/consistency.test.js now allows.
- test(planner): the Cloud gate on a real daemon (core/planner/gate.test.js, with windows' `spaces.tier`, merged from f8478c492): a Basic device refuses `planner.add`, `planner.list` and `tasks.list` with `needs_cloud` and "Planner needs a Cloud space" (the Cloud spaces the person is in listed, never "Pro" or "server"), `planner.parse` still answers, and a server runs them. A Mac paired with a box hands the call to the box without asking its own tier.
- feat(planner): a to-do's fields are real fields of its `task` record. List, priority, tags, pinned and repeat are fields of the type (the person sees and filters them like on any task); the planner's own bookkeeping (time of day, who added it, a plain project name) is one hidden `planner` field (hidden from every role). `form.planner` is gone. The planner writes a to-do's words and fields with one `records.update` (the kernel routes words, due time, parent and project through `tasks.edit`), and reads a change made on the task record in the app (words, list, priority, tags, due time, state) back through the kernel's task events; a due time set in the app moves the ring. Loading finds the planner's to-dos as the task records that carry the hidden field. Tests: records.test.js (to-do changed in the app).
- feat(kernel/tasks): Tasks are Records for every Space, with no flag and no old path (the user's decision). The kernel always defines the `task` type, `request` always makes the record, `tasks.migrate()` always runs at start, and the gateway always routes `records.create/update/remove` of a task. A bare `createTasks` (a test rig) gets a memory store with the type defined. `stage` and `record` are kernel-owned fields on the record, like `status` (the kernel keeps its synchronous copy, written by its own calls; `records.update` refuses them). A task's title and note are the record's: the task text store no longer holds them (it keeps only the doer's answer, a Flow's form and a block's reason), and the log's snapshot carries neither the words nor due, parent or project. A task logged the old way still verifies and its words migrate. `scrubTexts` (forgetting a record, or a value that moved into a sealed field) is async and also clears the words on the task record, including every custom text field, and finds a value there. Tests: kernel/tasks/records.test.js (6), the two Kit tests now expect the kernel's own `task` type.
- fix(planner): the engine's own fields on Reminder and Note are hidden with the contract's `hidden_from` (all five roles) instead of a new flag: a person's read leaves them out and no role writes them; the planner's own chain has no role and reads and writes them.
- feat(planner): the engine's own bookkeeping fields on Reminder and Note (`next_fire`, `created`, `updated`, `source`, `added_by`, `wall`, `date`, `floating`, `run_count`, `last_result`, `waits_on_fired`) carry `internal: true` in their field definition, so a record page, table or form lists only what a person sets; the Reminder type offers a calendar view laid out by `at` (`views` on the type, the shape of `defineView`) and a list view sorted by `at`. Test: records.test.js.
- feat(lib): `cloudGate` (lib/cloud-gate.js). Planner and the task tools ask the spaces module's internal `spaces.tier` for the space they act in; on a Basic personal space they answer `needs_cloud` with the message "Planner needs a Cloud space" and `detail.spaces`, the Cloud spaces the person is in (id, name, label), so the screen can offer one. No answer from the spaces module is not Basic. The words never say Pro or server. The spaces team owes `spaces.tier` (reach modules: `{ tier, cloud }`). Tests: lib/cloud-gate.test.js and records.test.js.
- feat(kernel/tasks): Tasks as Records, phase 1 (DESIGN-tasks-records, behind `createKernel({ tasksAsRecords: true })`; off, nothing changes). The `task` record type (`kernel/tasks/type.js`: title, note, due, status, parent, project, contact, repeat, priority, list, tags, pinned, plus any custom field) is the source of truth for what a person reads and edits; the kernel keeps what decides who may act, keyed by the same id. `request` makes the record and the authority together (and `fields` carries custom fields); every state change writes the record's `status` (a field the kernel owns: `records.update` refuses it, `field_not_allowed`, via a new `owned_by: "kernel"` field flag); `get`, `list`, `needsYou` and `card` lay the record's fields over the kernel's task; `edit` writes the record first. Through the records calls: `records.create` of a task by the person (or their assistant acting as them) makes a plain to-do through `tasks.request` (anyone else uses `tasks.request`), `records.update` routes words, due, parent and project through `tasks.edit` (same who-may rules) and other fields as plain updates, `records.remove` is refused (skip it). `tasks.migrate()` runs at start: it makes a record for every task that has none, keyed by id, so it is safe to run again and a crash is finished by the next run, and writes one `tasks.migrated` event. The held act's body, the approvals and the doer stay kernel-side. `record` and `stage` stay with the kernel in this phase (stage gates read them); the old text store is still written for rollback. Tests: kernel/tasks/records.test.js (5), and the whole of tasks.test.js passes unchanged with `VYRE_TASKS_RECORDS=1`.
- fix(test): kernel/home.test.js lists `memory` among the first-party kernel handle's keys (added with the Space memory path).
- feat(kernel): `actsAsPerson(chain)` in kernel/core/chain.js: the person's own chain, or the person's default assistant acting AS them (`chain.via === "assistant"`, windows' 2b080cefd). Tasks use it for a person doer and for edit, reopen, skip, so a to-do the assistant made for the person is the person's own act and the assistant can finish it; a space or project agent still cannot, and decide (an approval) stays `isExactlyPerson`. Tests: tasks.test.js and planner records.test.js, both cases.
- feat(kernel/tasks): a Task names its project as a link to a Project record of this Space (`project` at `request` or `edit`; `list` takes `{ project }`). The chain must be able to read it and it must exist (`projectExists`); another Space's, a made-up or a non-Project reference is bad_input. The planner passes a Project reference through (a plain project name stays in the to-do's form) and now declares `project/*` among the prefixes it reads.
- feat(kernel/gateway): a Space's own memory, `gateway.memory` (also `ctx.kernel.memory` and the remote wire): `file(chain, { text, source, kind?, topics? })`, `recall(chain, { q, topic, kind, source, limit })`, `retire(chain, id)`. Who may file and read is a grant (`memory.file`, `memory.read`, `memory.retire`; owner and admin hold file and retire, every member reads, an agent only where a grant names it, and a grant may be narrowed to some facts). A fact keeps its source (a record, task or file of this Space the filer may read, or `session:`, `thread:`, `chat:`), who filed it (from the chain, never the caller) and the labels of the chain that filed it. The text is free text, so the event log carries its hash only (`memory.filed`, `memory.recalled`, `memory.retired`). A source that names another Space is refused and a chain built in another Space is absence, so nothing crosses Spaces. Stored as a protected system record type `memory_fact` that the records calls never read or write. Tests: kernel/gateway/memory.test.js.
- feat(kernel/tasks): a Task can be edited and reopened, and can have a parent. `edit(chain, id, { title, note, due, form, parent })` is for the doer, a person, or whoever assigned the task (not one waiting for its check); `reopen` opens a done or skipped task with no checker and no outward act. Done and skipped stay terminal in the transition table; reopening is its own act (`TASK_REOPENS` in the contracts), written as `task.reopened`; `task.edited` carries the text only by its hash, like every task text. `parent` is set at `request` or by `edit` (a cycle is refused) and `list` takes `{ parent }`. Tests: tasks.test.js.
- feat(planner): to-dos keep everything they had, as Tasks. Edit words, list, priority, tags, time and note; reopen a done to-do; delete and restore; sub-items (`parent`); a repeating to-do makes the next Task when one is finished; the person can give a to-do to an assistant (`assignee`) and that assistant finishes it as its doer, while a to-do an assistant made for the person stays the person's to finish (the kernel refuses the assistant). The records.reference RF-1 filter is exact. The planner's change filter compares the actor exactly (`service:planner`), and the planner no longer declares the Event type: it reads the Space's shared one (and answers an empty calendar where a Space has none yet).
- fix(planner): `removed_at` replaces `deleted_at` on Reminder and Note records (Twenty reserves that name on every object), and a create leaves an empty field out (Twenty keeps an empty field as no field, so a create that said null read back as something else and the gateway refused it). Both found by running the planner on a real Twenty.
- test(planner): `core/planner/live-twenty.test.js` and `live-twenty.sh` run the planner on a real, pinned Twenty (v2.44.0) through the kernel's gateway: the `starts_at` range filter returns exactly the events in the window, in time order, across pages; reminders, a to-do and an event ring; a restart reads everything back. Skipped unless VYRE_TWENTY_LIVE_URL is set.
- fix(kernel/gateway): `records.reference` treats a field as a room placeholder only when it equals exactly the token a room view makes for that record and field. A text field a member filled with `{{field:<other record>#ssn}}` was echoed as a placeholder (reviewer-3 RF-1) and could steer an action to another record's sealed value; it is now plain data with its braces broken. Test added.
- feat(switchboard): the kernel validates a `record` mention on `threads.send`, `threads.start` and a queued edit (`core/switchboard/record-tags.js`). The id must be a record reference in this Space and is read under the sender's own chain through `records.reference` (a service chain, a stranger, a made-up or foreign reference tags nothing and the words stay plain text); a tag carries the record as data with sealed parts as placeholders, marked outside text. Non-record mentions go to their providers as before. Tests: record-tags.test.js.
- feat(planner): a planner that kept its own tables (0.2.x) carries what it held into the Space's records at its first start with the kernel, then drops the tables, and a crash part way is safe. Reminders, alarms, timers and chained tasks become `reminder` records, notes `note` records, the planner's own events `event` records, open to-dos Tasks, rings `planner_firing` records and settings `planner_state` records (done to-dos, deleted items and the connected calendars' copy are not carried; Google events are read again within 15 minutes). Every record made carries the old id (`legacy_id` on a Reminder or Note, `external_id` "planner:<id>" on an event, `form.planner.legacy_id` on a Task) and the import reads what is already there first, so a re-run after a crash at any of the ten writes of the test planner makes no second copy; the tables are dropped only when every write has succeeded. A chained task's wait follows the new record. 3 tests.
- feat(planner): the planner's own events can be deleted and restored. planner.delete on an event moves its record to the records' bin (records.remove) and stops its rings; planner.delete with restore: true (the event's id, or one occurrence's) brings it back through records.restore, so it works after a restart and the Records screens see the same bin. An event on a connected calendar is not deleted here ("delete it there"), and an agent may not delete one. The planner module now needs `records.restore`. 4 tests.
- feat(planner,records): an event can repeat and carry a link. The Event type gets `rrule` (an RRULE such as FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO: daily, weekly, monthly by date or nth weekday, yearly, INTERVAL, COUNT or UNTIL, read in the event's own zone so 09:00 stays 09:00 across a clock change) and `url` (the event's page on its calendar, which the Google sync now fills from htmlLink instead of leaving it out). The planner expands a rule into occurrences: each rings on its own key (`<record>~<start>`), an unanswered one gives way to the next, and the agenda and planner.upcoming list them. planner.add, planner.calendar.create and planner.update take `rrule` and `url` (null clears); a bad rule or link is refused in words. Updating an occurrence changes the event's record. 8 new planner tests and 8 for the rules.
- feat(planner): the Planner is built on Vyre Records. It has no tables and no migrations. Alarms, timers, reminders and /later tasks are `reminder` records and notes are `note` records (declared by the module, listed in Records); to-dos are the kernel's Tasks assigned to the person (a Task's `form.planner` carries list, priority and tags); the calendar is the Space's `event` records, the ones a connector's sync writes, with the planner's own events made as source `vyre`; rings and settings are `planner_firing` and `planner_state` records (system types, left out of the Customize list). The scheduler stays in the engine and reads a working set loaded from the records, so ringing is as exact and synchronous as before, `planner.fired`, `planner.acked`, the ring keys and the box ringing when the Mac is shut are unchanged; every change is written through to the gateway in order and a tool answers once it is saved. A record changed from the app, a Flow or a connector is read back through the kernel's `reminder.*`, `note.*`, `task.*` and `event.*` events (a changed time moves the next ring, a finished one stops ringing). `planner.calendar.sync` reads the window again; the planner's own Google calendar copy and its 15-minute poll are gone (a calendar with events is refreshed every 15 minutes; with none there is no timer). Needs the kernel: with it off every planner tool but `planner.parse` answers `unavailable`. `core/planner/store.js`, `calendar.js` and their tables are deleted (no data to migrate). Behaviour changes: a to-do's words, list and time are fixed once made, it does not repeat or reopen, has no sub-items, and only the person finishes it (an assistant adds one, the doer closes it); an item's id is its record's id (the CLI reads both forms); `planner.add` of kind event makes an Event record. Tests: planner.test.js moved onto a real kernel, events.test.js replaces calendar.test.js, records.test.js is new.
- feat(records-tools): `records.reference`, the tool behind the `#` chip. It takes a urn, reads under the caller's own chain through `gateway.records.reference`, and returns the record as data with sealed (and room-hidden) parts as `{{field:urn#name}}` placeholders. Person-reach like `records.get`, open to the person's assistant (named in `core/modules/agent-reach.js`, so `kernel/golden/allow.json` is regenerated), and added to the remote wire's records calls.
- feat(kernel/placement): node placement is decided by node descriptor records. `kernel/placement` holds the descriptor shape (capabilities, resources, residency, posture, lend policy), its signature by the node's own key (an edited or unsigned record decides nothing), and one scheduler: two-way consent (Space policy and lend policy), capability, resource, residency and posture fit, online, power, awake and CPU and memory ceilings, then locality, the preferred node, load and uptime. It answers with `workload.placed` (and what it passed over) or `workload.refused` with a code and plain reasons. `core/runner/placement.js` no longer has its own rules: it builds this computer and the server as node facts and maps the answer to here, server or wait with the same words as before. The scheduler is named non-base in `kernel/size.test.js` (a decision, never an enforcement).
- feat(kernel/gateway): `records.reference(chain, type, id)`, the kernel side of `#contact`: one read under the caller's grants, then every sealed part (and any part a group room may not read) is a `{{field:urn#name}}` placeholder in `fields` and `text`, whoever asks, so the AI reasons over the rest and can use the token in an action. A value cannot forge a token (its braces are broken in the text). Declared in `kernel/contracts/gateway.d.ts`.
- feat(spaces): member storage matches memory's remote backend: `spaces.storage.list` also answers `entries` ({ name, sha, size }), `spaces.storage.delete` takes `expected` (sha256 or null) and deletes only on a match, answering { ok, deleted, sha256 }, and `put` answers { ok: true, sha256 }. A delete is never refused for the cap.
- feat(spaces): the team server's per-member object storage (lib/spaces/member-storage.js), for the ciphertext of a member's encrypted personal items and identity home: `spaces.storage.put`, `get`, `list`, `delete`, `usage` and `put-if` (an atomic compare-and-set on the object's sha256, or null for "not there yet"; a loser is told the sha256 that is there now), and `spaces.storage.set-cap` for an owner (default 1 GiB per member, 0 for none; a write is refused once the member's bytes reach it). The caller is the member themself (the chain's one person, a member of that hosted space); each call reaches only that person's own folder, `<space>/member-storage/<person>/`. Objects are base64 text of at most 8 MB per call. Atomicity is the single daemon's: the check and the write are synchronous.
- fix(kernel): the conformance suite's linked-records paging case (revision 6) looped without a bound, so the "teeth" test with a store whose pager repeats the first page forever grew memory until the heap was gone (kernel/conformance/memory.test.js died even at 4 GB). The loop stops after 10 pages with "paging did not finish", like the cursor case above it.
- feat(kernel): `moves.outMany`, the batch form of `moves.out` for an upgrade that moves several projects: ONE approval and one plan hash cover the target, the plan and the exact sorted list of projects (proof call `moveOutMany`), at most 100, each project then gets its own `project.move_started` and is received with the ordinary `in` (single use, one-hour window). `moves.in` also refuses evidence whose event carries `acted_via` (reviewer-3 LOW).
- fix(spaces): the person's own (home) space is always listed with a name: label "personal" and display name "Personal" (device) or "My Cloud" (server) with its tier, on a fresh home too (app-wire's live walk showed null names). `spaces.tier` also answers `personal_host`: this server's own home space when the machine is a server (My Cloud), else the Cloud space the person chose with `spaces.personal-host.set` while they are still in it, else the earliest one they joined, else null.
- fix(modules): the ctx.kernel handle with `for(space).call` is an own-key frozen copy (getters live), not an Object.create over the kernel's handle, so `Object.keys(ctx.kernel)` shows exactly the actions the manifest declared again (reviewer-3 HOLD on a50ad3bef, kernel/home.test.js).
- fix(spaces): `spaces.host-here` needs no presence proof (walker): making a space is not one of the yes moments, so it rides on the owner's authenticated call and the owner check stays. A passkey browser that has just paired a server can create its first space. The tests that used host-here as the presence-gated act use `spaces.retire-here` now.
- feat(spaces): a space's home time zone (an IANA zone, checked with lib/time `validZone`). It starts as the creating device's zone (`meta.zone`, else the machine's), an owner or admin changes it with `spaces.time-zone.set`, and `time_zone` (null when none) is in `spaces.list`, `spaces.get` and `spaces.tier`. lib/time (zones.js, index.js) comes from platform-2's branch, unchanged.
- feat(modules): every hosted Space gets each module its own store (03:45Z ruling). `ctx.store.db` and `ctx.store.dir()` follow the Space the running call is for (`meta.in_space`, set only by `ctx.kernel.for(space).call`, inherited by the calls it makes): the home's Space keeps vyre.db, every other hosted Space gets `<home>/kernel/spaces/<space>/modules/<module>.db` with the module's own migrations replayed, and its own data folder. `ctx.kernel` follows the Space the same way (that Space's `kernelFor`, so its own records, log, grants and service chain). A module that prepares a statement once at start belongs to the home's Space; it reaches the right one by using `ctx.store.db` inside the call. `ctx.kernel.for(space).call` now carries the caller's origin as `ctx.call` does.
- fix(kernel): SL-1 (reviewer-3). `model:` is a Switchboard slot name, and only a `model_slot` fact makes one: an `agent_session` fact under a `model:` agent name gets no chain, and `surfaces.open` refuses that agent name, so a narrowed agent can no longer shed its narrowing by having a session opened under such a name. The built-in stores report conformance revision 6, which the suite now expects.
- feat(kernel): a model slot is the person's authority narrowed to its chat's Project (one Chat, reviewer-3 G1). `surfaces.open(person, { chat, agent: "model:<provider>/<model>#<n>", project? })` writes the Project into the token (a slot lives in a chat; only a slot takes a Project; the id must be a slot id), `chainFor` builds windows' `model_slot` chain with `chain.project`, and authorize refuses another Project's resource (`outside_project`) for it; a resource of no Project is judged as before. `chatRead`, `chatHas` and the room checks accept a `model:` hop when the person on the chain is in the chat, so the slot ends when its person leaves.
- feat(spaces): `spaces.tier`, an internal tool (reach modules) for the modules that refuse on a Basic personal space (Planner, tasks): `{ space? }` (the home's own when omitted) answers `{ tier: "basic" | "cloud", cloud: [{ id, name, label }] }`, the tier from the same rule as `spaces.list` and the Cloud spaces the person is in. An unknown space is `not_found`.
- feat(modules,kernel): `ctx.kernel.for(space).call(tool, input, chain)` runs a module tool in a hosted Space's own instance, under the chain the caller holds there (`kernel.chainIn(space, meta)`), after THAT Space's `authorize` allows the kernel action the tool declares (`crossSpace` on its manifest entry; a tool without it is refused with `not_declared`). First-party modules only, never on the wire. The tool sees `meta.in_space` and `meta.in_space_chain`, set only by the registry (a symbol key; whatever a client sends under those names is dropped). A chain with no right in that Space, or built in another Space, is refused with `denied` before the tool runs. The other Space's store is never read from the caller.
- feat(spaces): `spaces.list` rows carry `tier` ("basic" or "cloud"), the same machine role `storeMode` reads: a space whose home is a server is cloud; a space on this computer is cloud on a server machine and basic on a device. The app reads only that field.
- feat(stores): a personal space has two tiers (the user, 5 Oct). A device install (laptop or desktop, not a server) is Basic: no Twenty, no Docker or Colima, no Records refusal; the default store mode is the built-in index. Twenty is provisioned only on a server install (`config.isServer(cfg.machine)`), a packaged build ignores `VYRE_STORE` (a server is always Twenty, never sqlite or auto; a device is always Basic, the built-in store with the fixed personal types), and only a development build honours it. `storeMode(env, { server })`, `createStoreFor({ server })` and `storeStatus({ server })` take the machine role.
- feat(kernel,stores): links are real relations (plan item 9). A link to a type gets a named inverse shown on the other record and may be a list (`many`); the gateway checks that the target is a live record of its type; Twenty holds a link as a RELATION field (a list through a hidden junction object) and the built-in store as before, and the conformance suite (revision 6) holds them to the same answers. Links stored as urn text move onto relations when a Space's store opens, without changing any record's version.
- feat(sessions): every model brief carries a time line (lib/time `timeLine`, from platform-2): what time it is for the person in the zone of the device in use, for the space in its zone, and for any contact in context, and the rule that a relative time is read in the person's zone for personal things and the space's for space things (the space's, with both said, when unclear). `sessions.environment` and `sessions.prompt.compose` take `zone`, `space_zone`, `contacts` (and `now`); `threads.start` takes `zone` (kept for resumes, defaulting to the calling device's) and passes it to the brief; the quick answer (Vyre IQ) carries it too. The spaces brief passes each Space's `zone` when it has one. Test: a brief built on a UTC server shows Asia/Karachi's local time (`core/sessions/environment.test.js`).
- feat(kernel,memory): the encrypted personal records store (`kernel/store/sealed.js`, team/0.3/DESIGN-personal-records.md). A Personal person's Planner, reminders, notes and personal to-dos on a team server: the reference Store with its state in process memory only and ciphertext on the server beside the identity home (a records key sealed under the identity memory key, one sealed blob per record named by an HMAC, a sealed change log), only the fixed personal types, and a per-member cap the space owner sets (`memory.personal.set-cap`; default 1 GiB; a write over it is refused, reads are not). `memory.personal.status` returns `{ host, used_bytes, cap_bytes }` and counts the storage while the store is locked. It passes `kernel/conformance/suite.js` like any store (it reports `store: "sealed-personal"` and the suite revision). Tests: `kernel/store/sealed.test.js` (the whole conformance suite; admin or root reading the disk sees ciphertext only; a second device opens it with the laptop off; wrong key and locked refuse; the cap), `core/memory/space-memory.test.js`.
- feat(lib): per-chat keys, `lib/chat-keys.js` (team/0.3/DESIGN-chat-keys.md), over `lib/keywrap.js`. A chat's or project's ring is epochs of a random key wrapped to device keys; `addHolders` (with or without history) and `removeHolders` (rotate, drop the removed holder's wraps); each file has its own key under the ring, `shareFile` wraps it to a project ring (a grant, not a copy), `unshareFile` rotates the file key and re-seals the content; names get a stable HMAC index id and a sealed display name; `bundleFor`, `openBundle` and `ProcessKeys` let an agent work in a chat on a server with keys in process memory only. Not wired to the chat or Drive stores yet (flows). Tests: `lib/chat-keys.test.js`.
- feat(memory): `memory.room.offer` and `memory.room.import` declare `crossSpace: "project.move_in"`, so flows' project move can run them in the target Space's own memory instance (`ctx.kernel.for(space).call`); export and forget run in the Space the move starts in. The backup source list is filtered once more on the way in (dependency and build folders, caches, logs, `.DS_Store`, vault and sealed paths, files over `memory.backup.max_bytes`, default 2 GB; `.git` is kept). Test: `core/memory/space-memory.test.js`.
- fix(memory): review of the backup and the room move. A backup run is one at a time, here (a second call gets the same run) and across devices (a lease on the server), and the manifest is written only when every chunk it names is on the server (a lost chunk fails the run and the next uploads it again), so concurrent runs no longer trim each other's chunks. The backup key is sealed under the identity memory key, so a second device and the recovery code open it, and `memory.backup.restore` rebuilds the newest backup into a folder from a device key or the recovery code; with the identity home not set up the status is none. A project that changed between room export and forget no longer wedges the move: `memory.room.import` takes the export's `digest`, checks it, and a newer export replaces the rows and gives a new receipt (the move's key is kept for its hour). `memory.room.*` are reach modules (callers module). The user-facing name is Personal, not Basic. Tests in `core/memory/backup/backup.test.js`, `core/memory/move.test.js`, `core/memory/space-memory.test.js`.
- feat(memory): the Personal encrypted backup (core/memory/backup, team/0.3/DESIGN-basic-backup.md). A person's personal projects and chats (the device's row files and the projects' folders) are kept as ciphertext on a team server: one backup key in a key ring (device keys and recovery code, lib/keywrap.js), files cut into 4 MiB chunks sealed under it with ids that are HMACs of the content (incremental, and the server cannot confirm a known file), a sealed manifest written last (an interrupted run leaves the last one newest and resumes by skipping the chunks already up), the last three manifests kept. `Backup.restore` rebuilds every item from the newest manifest and checks it by hash, naming any chunk missing or damaged. `memory.backup.status` returns `{ to, last, state }` (ok: nothing older than an hour is missing; behind: such changes are waiting or the last attempt failed; none: no team server) and `memory.backup.run` backs up now; it also runs every hour. It has no store and no key of its own: it lives beside the identity home in the same server storage (`memory.identity.home`, `backup/<identity>/`) and opens with the device key the identity home uses (`memory.identity.deviceKey`); with no identity home there is no backup. `memory.backup` only tunes it (`every_ms`, `max_bytes`, or false). Tests: `core/memory/backup/backup.test.js`, `core/memory/space-memory.test.js`.
- feat(memory): the Space layer's memory tools, thin doors over the kernel's `memory.file` / `memory.read` / `memory.retire`: `memory.space.file`, `memory.space.recall`, `memory.space.retire` (and the agent tools `memory_space_file`, `memory_space_recall`). The caller's own chain goes to the kernel, which decides by grant; a refusal reaches the caller, and a kernel with no Space memory answers unavailable. Work's fact extraction now also files each note (a fact that fits no field) into the Space's memory under the person's chain alone, with the record as its source; best effort, the note on the record stands either way. Tests: `core/memory/space-memory.test.js`, `core/work/memory/engine.test.js` (outcome 1b).
- feat(memory): a project's memory moves between Spaces (core/memory/move.js): `memory.room.offer` (target, a one-use P-256 key held in process memory), `.export` (source, sealed to it), `.import` (target, one transaction, returns a receipt), `.forget` (source, needs the receipt, refuses if the project changed since export, leaves `moved_to` in the new `memory_moves` table). Each refuses unless this Space's log holds the kernel's `project.move_started` / `project.move_in` for that move id, project and plan hash. Carried: filed writes, decisions and their fixes, corrections; the graph is derived again from the arriving sessions. The key code is now one library, `lib/keywrap.js` (moved from core/memory/identity/crypto.js; adds a key ring: `newRing`, `ringKey`, `ringAdd`, `ringRotate`) for the identity home and per-chat keys (team/0.3/DESIGN-chat-keys.md). Tests: `core/memory/move.test.js`, the ring in `core/memory/identity/home.test.js`.
- fix(memory,sessions): the environment brief is cut to the asking agent (ENV-1). Only the identity-level assistant and the person's own session are told of all their Spaces; a project or space agent hears of the current Space, the connectors it holds a tool of, and teammates only if it may `team.list`. `memory.markers` shows a scoped agent only the projects it may follow (ML-1): others are not named or counted, and `memory.follow` answers not found; the assistant and the person see all. `sessions.environment` and `sessions.prompt.compose` take `artifacts_dir`, which adds one Files line (`$VYRE_ARTIFACTS_DIR`) to every driver's brief. Tests: a scoped agent's brief holds no other Space, connector or unlisted teammate; the assistant's holds them all.
- feat(memory): the identity home (core/memory/identity). A person's identity memory (the personal tables) and the private assistant's state can be kept as ciphertext on any space server they belong to, so an admin or root there reads nothing at rest. One identity memory key (IMK) encrypts the snapshot (AES-256-GCM, bound to the identity and revision) and is wrapped to each of the person's device keys (P-256 ECDH-ES) and to their recovery code (Argon2id); the server holds ciphertext, wraps and hashes, never the key. `memory.identity.enroll` (the person's act) seals it and removes the rows from the database (`secure_delete`, log truncated); locked, the memory tools answer "locked". `memory.identity.grant` is the one yes per server (a new vault-moment op `memory.identity.unlock` in lib/one-yes) that lasts until revoked from the phone (`memory.identity.revoke`); the phone then answers that server's signed unlock requests, including after a restart, with no re-ask, and a person's own devices unwrap with their device key without a prompt (`.unlock.begin` / `.finish` carry the request). Unlocked, the rows live only in an in-memory schema, never written back or logged in the clear; new facts are saved as ciphertext (autosave, lock, stop), so after a kill the disk holds ciphertext only. `.lock` saves and seals again; `memory.identity.move` moves the ciphertext to another server (the person's own, say) checked by hash with only a marker left behind, nothing decrypted or re-keyed. Off unless `memory.identity` in config.json names the home. Tests: root reading every byte of the home finds nothing; a process killed while unlocked leaves no fact on the disk and nothing sealed is lost; the assistant reads after the yes and a wrong or missing yes opens nothing; the move keeps it.
- feat(sessions): the environment brief lists the person's Spaces and the Space's record types through the kernel: new internal tools `spaces.brief` (names and roles, modules only) and `work.space-brief` (the Space and the types with their field names, definitions only).

- feat(seal): a passkey says yes for a browser-only person. A key of signer `webauthn_platform` (with its `rp`) is admitted on a release build, marked `unattested` like a phone's chip key, and its proof is a WebAuthn assertion over the same proof bytes: the sealing process checks it with the identity chain's own verifier (`verifyWebAuthn`, now exported), once per request in `Presence.preverify` before the synchronous `refuse` reads the result (remembered by object identity, so nothing a request says can mark a proof checked). The `rp` rides enrolment, recovery and join end to end. kernel/seal/passkey-proof.test.js covers yes once, another act, another person, a copied proof, another site and a missing user verification.
- fix(wink): a browser whose identity is a passkey can pair a server (walker, 5 Oct). Three drops: the server capped the identity proof's signature at 200 characters (a WebAuthn assertion is longer, so it answered denied_no_proof); it checked it as a bare signature instead of the assertion the chain's own `verifyWith` reads; and the identity ports (`spaces.identity.state`, the peer door's entry) dropped the entry's `rp`, which the assertion check needs. A passkey is now hardware-class for owning a server (user presence and verification are checked), recorded as owner_proof "passkey". The software authenticator moved to apps/app/src/identity/soft-authenticator.js; test/wink-paired.test.js pairs a fresh server from a passkey identity.
- feat(identity): claim a name from a browser with a passkey (0.2.9, gap A29). `claimIdentityWithPasskey` (apps/app/src/identity/claim.js) makes a WebAuthn credential (P-256, user verification required) as the identity's first device and signs the genesis and the claim's record with it; `createPasskeyKey` and `restorePasskeyKey` (apps/app/src/identity/passkey.js) read the attestation with a small CBOR reader, normalise the high-s twin an authenticator may return, and keep only the credential id and public key. A passkey is a full device (unlike a key a page can reach). The directory could verify a passkey's signature on a chain op but not on a name record or an act; `verifyWith` now takes the signing entry (`signing` from `signerKey`) and checks a passkey's assertion as one, in the Worker, the client directory, the audit key, the seal's bindings and spaces. The pinned hash of kernel/identity/chain.js is updated; merging with work/no-labels needs it recomputed.
- feat(memory): identity memory has classes (`classOf`, personal/profile.js): each profile line is `stack` (a tool you use), `writing_style`, `pm_style` or `working_style` (a preference, by its words) or `life`, by rule and never by a model; `memory.profile` takes `class` to read one. `memory.markers` says which layer the caller holds (`identity` for the person and the assistant, `project` for an agent). The environment brief explains the layers to every agent from its own side: a project agent its own layer and that nothing crosses, the assistant the identity layer and how to follow markers. Not built yet, for the kernel owners: filing a fact into a Space's own memory (a `note` record through the Work engine) and a Space-scope `memory.write`.

- feat(memory): the three layers of memory, first piece (team/0.3/DESIGN-memory-layers.md). Identity, Spaces and Projects each own their facts and nothing learned in one is copied into another; a layer holds markers that point down. `memory.markers` (agents: `memory_markers`) lists the markers of the layers below: one per project's memory, derived on every read from the rooms (name, counts of facts, decisions and sessions, topics, a summary of at most 200 characters, never a sealed value), and the Space's own. A marker the caller may follow carries its summary; one it may not follow is only named ("exists"), with no summary, counts or topics. `memory.follow` (`memory_follow`) follows a marker into that project's memory (or the Space's own records and session lines) and asks it a question under the caller's own grants, refused with the reason when they do not reach it. The person and the identity-level assistant follow every marker; a project agent only its own. First test: a Northwind agent cannot retrieve Harlow's memory by any question, is told only that it exists, and cannot follow its marker (core/memory/layers.test.js).

- feat(sessions): one environment brief for every agent, on every model and driver (core/sessions/environment.js, team/0.3/DESIGN-agent-environment.md). `sessions.environment` builds it from live reads, never by hand: what Vyre is, the Space this session is in and the person's role, the other Spaces they belong to (and that data does not cross a Space unless moved or shared), the record types and fields, how sealed fields arrive as placeholders, the Project hub, Tasks and Flows, approvals (outward acts are held for the person's yes, so propose), teammates, Memory (personal and per project, memory_search, memory_turn and the rest, what is remembered by itself), connectors and the vault (used, never seen), and the agent's own reach, cut to the registry's own tool list for its caller class. It is layer one of three (environment, then the role, then the project's context) in `sessions.prompt.compose`, within 6,000 characters (lower-priority parts drop first; what Vyre is, the agent, approvals, memory and "to learn more" never do), and a replacing role prompt replaces only the role layer. Claude gets it as the system-prompt append; Codex and Grok get it, with the project's own context, as the first prompt block of every process, a resumed session's too. FAMILIES names every tool family an agent can reach as taught or "learn more"; a test fails on a family in neither.

- fix(security): every container image Vyre runs as root on a box or builds the edge from is pinned by digest (reviewer-3 SC-1, SC-2): the backup and restore helper (`alpine tar` over the data volumes, now alpine:3.20@sha256 as `HELPER_IMAGE`), the edge's Caddy base and its derived Dockerfile's alpine, and BuildKit. The publish image check accepts `name:tag@sha256:...`. test/image-pins.test.js fails on any unpinned image reference in core/cli/commands/box.js and lib/publish/edge.js. The manual restore example in docs/using/box-care.md is pinned too. The digests are the multi-arch index digests of 5 Oct 2026; bump them on purpose.
- feat(names): the old 72-hour recovery rebind is removed (0.2.9, gap A10); instant recovery (the identity's own chain) is the only path. The directory Worker drops `POST /v1/names/recover` and `/recover/cancel`, the pending rebind and its landing, the recover rate limits and `mine`'s `pending`; `core/names` drops `names.recover` and `names.recover.code`, the `name.recovered`, `name.recovery-pending` and `name.recovery-cancelled` events, the `recovering` config key and the hourly cancel; the relay's setup channel no longer takes a recovery code. A pending rebind a record still carries from before is cleared on release or admin rebind, never landed. Support's admin rebind stays. The recovery code a claim returns and `/v1/names/code` stay for now (BACKLOG: retire recovery codes).

- fix(app): Shared leaves More until the user decides whether it is a tab in Drive; /u/shared stays reachable by address but unlinked.

- refactor(app): the provider marks file lives in apps/app/ui/marks/provider-art.js (copied unmodified), so the app no longer reads deck/js/provider-art.js.

Filling and revealing go to the box as held calls: the owner's phone answers the ask and the call goes again with the approval, as the Vault's held fields do. The simulated Face ID proof is gone from the record page.

- feat(app): one Find. /u/search is web-2's Find page; the Search button and Cmd-K (Ctrl-K) open it as a command bar from <FindHost/> mounted once in UiShell; the app's own search screen is gone. Shared joins More. Now greets by name or not at all ("Good afternoon"), never "there".

- fix(app): Records and Customize findings from the walk. Add a field shows its kinds as chips (the menu did not open inside the web sheet) and a Link field asks what it links to; more than five types become a Type picker instead of clipped tabs; the timeline says who and what in words ("You created this"), never a raw id; a space with no name reads Home, never spc_ ids; Devices reads "Your phone and computers"; Templates leaves More per the app map.

- feat(app): a real chat's composer is filled from the box (0.2.9), not the sample world: the models and accounts that can answer (providers.list; a model of the answering account switches with threads.model, another account's with threads.switch), the people and assistants to @mention (this chat's, records.actors, agents.list), and the records to # tag, each with how many sealed fields it holds (src/chat/real-composer.js, useRealComposer.ts).
