- feat(app): the look is kept across a restart (0.2.9): the person's density, font, reduced motion and larger text, and each space's accent, row tint, density, font and corners, are kept on this device (localStorage on the web, the secure store on a phone, src/state/keep-appearance.ts) and come back on start; the theme (dark, paper, system) is read from the settings hub on the box at start, not only when Appearance is opened.
- feat(app): chat shows which provider wrote a reply (0.2.9). A reply that says its provider carries that provider's own published mark at its avatar's lower right (ui/components/ProviderBadge.tsx, ui/marks/provider.js over deck/js/provider-art.js), a model's face is its provider's mark when the name says which (Claude, Codex, Grok), never a guess, and the thinking is its own folded row ("Thought ▸") instead of being dropped. - feat(app): the new shell is the app (0.2.9). `/` opens Now in the @vyre/ui shell, on a phone as on the web; the legacy tab screens (Now, Chats, Agents, Places sheet) and their EmptyHere are retired (app/places and app/new-chat redirect). New routes the shell already pointed at: /u/chats (the box's sessions, those needing you first, New chat), /u/chats/new, /u/search (the person's records, which never read a sealed value, plus mentions.search groups: files, vault names, artifacts, GitHub) and /u/assistants. Now shows what is missing on this device and the assistants' asks and the Gate's held items ("Waiting on you", the old Needs list) above the tasks. The swipe-to-approve row and its perf marks (open.cold, approve.collapse) are gone with the old Now: .github/scripts/app-perf.mjs reports them "not measured".
- fix(app): copy rules on the phone: no "A server" kind in Add a device on a phone or browser, no "Make a space on your server" or "to invite people, make a space on your server" there, no "alex" or "harlow.vyre.run" in real screens ("You", "Paste the invite link"). scripts/app-walk-shell.mjs walks the shell at 390 px against awbox.

- fix(app): a device paired by a typed code now keeps the pairing, marks the server as the way it reaches its box, opens its paired person session and reconnects over the relay (src/real/pairing.ts afterPaired; used by the browser's Type the code, the Mac's boxless server and add-this-device). A browser the owner has not trusted yet cannot start the session: the pairing stays and the session starts once it is trusted. test: scripts/app-walk-records-ui.mjs, app-walk-records-shots.mjs, app-walk-paired-records.mjs, and the paired-device walk now also defines a case type (text, choice, link, sealed) and adds two records.

- fix(records): the core Project's `client` links to a contact (`to: "contact"`, ruling R2), so a link with no target is no longer allowed in the Kit SDK or the Kit checks (undoing the allowance made for it).

- fix(daemon): the home serves the lent-computer wire. A Space's home now registers the `lent` service (core/runner/lent-home.js, built by core/daemon/lent-service.js) on its remote server, so a member's computer can start a lent session, checkpoint it and resume it over the peer wire; until now only tests built it and every `lent.*` call answered no_such_call. The Space's definition of a session comes from the daemon option `lentSpec`; with none the home answers not_found rather than inventing a program. Boundaries: `core/daemon -> core/runner` gains lent-home.js.
- feat(identity): a device entry on an identity's list may carry `agree`, a raw P-256 point for key agreement (ECDH), the key a chat key is wrapped to. It is part of the signed entry like `enclave`: immutable once listed, device entries only, validated at genesis and at every add (so enrolment, recovery and join all carry it), and read back by `spaces.identity.state` and the identity ports. chain.js is re-pinned in kernel/identity/PINNED.json (needs the reviewer's gate).
- feat(records): the one Task type (records/core-types.js; the kernel imports it): `status` (required), `stage` and `record` are `owned_by: "kernel"`, a `planner` text field hidden from every role holds the planner's bookkeeping, `tags` is a JSON list in a text. Contact gets `time_zone`, an IANA zone: a text field may say `format: "time_zone"`, checked by every store with the runtime's own zone list (`validZone`, kernel/store/values.js), refused at define for any other format.

- feat(records): Task is a core Records type (team/0.3/DESIGN-tasks-records.md): title, note, due, status, stage, parent, project, record, contact, repeat, priority, list, tags, pinned, the planner's zone and wall-time fields and source, with a default board by status and a list and calendar by due, and the usual custom fields, stages and views. A field may say `owned_by: "kernel"`: `records.create` and `records.update` refuse a write to it unless the chain carries the kernel's own service (`field_not_allowed`), and define refuses any other owner; `status` is the first. The tasks service (platform-2) must write it under the service `kernel`.

- feat(records): no legal words in the base Kit (the user, 5 Oct, replacing R4's split). Practice area is not a field on any base type; the base stages are New, Active, Review, Done for a Project and "Meeting booked" for a Lead; an Appointment is a Meeting, Follow-up or Call. Practice area, the legal stage sets and the accident date, trust name and hearing date are all in the `law-firm` library Kit, which restates Lead, Appointment, Client and Project (a type is defined whole) and installs per account. Stage sets that vary by a field remain a capability with no example in the base. A test greps the base Kit's source and stored form for legal words.

- feat(records): the Records' own screens read as ours. `store.define` gives each field the icon of its kind and its description, and puts the type's fields in the object's default table in the order of the definition (a hidden field is not shown): `syncFieldOrder` and `FIELD_ICON` in stores/twenty/views.js. A field has no position of its own in the Records; the order is the position of its view fields. Checked live (views.live.test.js).

- feat(records): Law firm Kit and generic base Kit (R4), hidden bookkeeping types (R6), base Kit for every new Space (R1), title menu and Filtered row (map). (R4) The base Project keeps generic stages (Intake, Active, Review, Done); the personal injury and estate planning stage sets and the accident date, trust name and hearing date are in the new `law-firm` library Kit, which restates the Project and keeps the base board. (R6) `kit-proposal`, `kit-install` (and Flow, definition and goal types) are not a screen in Records or Customize (`isHiddenType`); `person` and `file` are no longer link targets a Kit may name. (R1) A new Space on any store gets the base Kit's types when its Flow and core types are defined (core/daemon/flows-host.js), as the owner's setup act with no card; one on its own Records store has had them since the store was made. (map) The Records screen has the named-view menu on its title (shown when a type stores more than one view), a "Filtered: ..., 3 of 9" row with Clear for a view's stored filter (Clear is for the visit only, the view is not edited), and `view` and `noFilter` props on List, Board and Calendar.

- feat(records): views live in the Records too, every view per type is supported, the base Kit installs on every new Space, and the person-facing words say Records. (a) `stores/twenty/views.js` writes a type's stored views as the Records' own views (list as a table, board as a kanban on the grouping field, calendar on the date field, columns as view fields, a sort as a view sort, a filter of fields, literals, and/or and empty() as a filter group), under one deterministic id per view; `store.define` keeps them in step (new, changed, removed). A filter outside that form stays in the definition only and the change says so. Probed and tested on a live Twenty v2.44.0 (stores/twenty/live/views.live.test.js, probe-views*.mjs). (b) `storeFor` defines only the core types a Space lacks (a Kit-extended contact is no longer put back to its bare shape on restart) and, once, when a Space is new, the base Kit's types with their views. (c) `viewDefOf(def, table, viewName)` and `storedViewsOf(def, kind)`: the first stored view of a kind is the default and a name picks another; `ListView`, `BoardView` and `CalendarView` take an optional `view` prop. (d) The messages a person can meet (store errors, preflight reasons, key warnings, `vyre daemon status`) say Records, not the engine's name; the credits line in settings is unchanged.

- feat(records,kernel,app): objects layer, items 10 to 13 of the 0.2.9 platform gaps. (10) A field takes `visible_if` and `required_if`, Expressions over the record's other stored fields: the language (`defineField.*({ visible_if, required_if })`, checked and printed back), the gateway (`field_not_shown` when a value is written to a field the record does not show, `field_required` when a visible required_if field is left empty; a create is judged whole, an update only where it touches the field or what its condition reads) and the record page (hidden fields are not listed, a required empty one shows a Required chip and cannot be saved empty). (11) A type stores its `views` (list, board, calendar, columns, grouping, sort, filter), validated by `records.define`; `viewDefOf` lays the first stored view of each kind over deck/ui/view-defs.js, which stays as the default for a type that stores none; a Kit's views are folded into the type they show when the Kit is installed (the Kit's own list stays for the install card); list, board and calendar apply a view's filter. (12) A `base` Kit in the library: Contact, Lead, Appointment, Client, Subscriber, Project; Lead, Client and Subscriber are roles linked to the one Contact; practice area is a choice. (13) A stage takes `enter_if` and a type takes `stage_sets` (`defineStage([...], { sets: [{ name, when, stages }] })`): the first set whose `when` holds gives that record's stages, the default stages otherwise. The gateway refuses a stage outside the record's set (`stage_not_in_set`) and an entry whose condition fails (`stage_entry_refused`); kernel/flows/stages.js advances along the record's own set and holds a record whose next stage cannot yet be entered. One new module, kernel/expr/conditions.js, is the single judge for the gateway, the stage module and the app. No new permission, log, table or runner.

The directory Worker drops `POST /v1/names/recover` and `/recover/cancel`, the pending rebind and its landing, the recover rate limits and `mine`'s `pending`; `core/names` drops `names.recover` and `names.recover.code`, the `name.recovered`, `name.recovery-pending` and `name.recovery-cancelled` events, the `recovering` config key and the hourly cancel; the relay's setup channel no longer takes a recovery code. A pending rebind a record still carries from before is cleared on release or admin rebind, never landed. Support's admin rebind stays. The recovery code a claim returns and `/v1/names/code` stay for now (BACKLOG: retire recovery codes).

- fix(app): Shared leaves More until the user decides whether it is a tab in Drive; /u/shared stays reachable by address but unlinked.

- refactor(app): the provider marks file lives in apps/app/ui/marks/provider-art.js (copied unmodified), so the app no longer reads deck/js/provider-art.js.

- feat(app): a record's sealed field has a Fill (Replace once filled) button and the line "Hidden from AI; your assistant sees a placeholder". Filling and revealing go to the box as held calls: the owner's phone answers the ask and the call goes again with the approval, as the Vault's held fields do. The simulated Face ID proof is gone from the record page.

- feat(app): one Find. /u/search is web-2's Find page; the Search button and Cmd-K (Ctrl-K) open it as a command bar from <FindHost/> mounted once in UiShell; the app's own search screen is gone. Shared joins More. Now greets by name or not at all ("Good afternoon"), never "there".

- fix(app): Records and Customize findings from the walk. Add a field shows its kinds as chips (the menu did not open inside the web sheet) and a Link field asks what it links to; more than five types become a Type picker instead of clipped tabs; the timeline says who and what in words ("You created this"), never a raw id; a space with no name reads Home, never spc_ ids; Devices reads "Your phone and computers"; Templates leaves More per the app map.

- fix(app): a server that belongs to another Vyre name is refused in words the person can use: the page says "This server belongs to <name>.vyre.run. Ask them to add you to a space, or reset the server to start over." (a phone: "This Vyre belongs to <name>..."), instead of "The pairing did not finish". The name is cut out of the server's sentence and checked, never the server's text itself. test: app-walk-claim has `--save-state` and `--use-state` so a second run can pair as the same, existing identity.

- feat(app): a real chat's composer is filled from the box (0.2.9), not the sample world: the models and accounts that can answer (providers.list; a model of the answering account switches with threads.model, another account's with threads.switch), the people and assistants to @mention (this chat's, records.actors, agents.list), and the records to # tag, each with how many sealed fields it holds (src/chat/real-composer.js, useRealComposer.ts). A # tag picked from the list goes to the box beside the words as `{ kind: "record", id: <urn>, name }` (threads.send `mentions`; stream.send in a group chat), and only tags still in the words are sent. The kernel side (a record's sealed parts reaching the assistant as placeholders, a `record` mention provider) is platform's.
- test(app): render check. apps/app/scripts/render-check.mjs draws 24 main screens at phone and desktop width from a sample-world export in headless Chromium and fails on a page error, an unmatched route or a blank screen; CI runs it in the web job (`npm run render:check` locally after `EXPO_PUBLIC_VYRE_MOCK=1 npx expo export -p web --output-dir dist-mock`).

- feat(app): the look is kept across a restart (0.2.9): the person's density, font, reduced motion and larger text, and each space's accent, row tint, density, font and corners, are kept on this device (localStorage on the web, the secure store on a phone, src/state/keep-appearance.ts) and come back on start; the theme (dark, paper, system) is read from the settings hub on the box at start, not only when Appearance is opened.
- feat(app): chat shows which provider wrote a reply (0.2.9). A reply that says its provider carries that provider's own published mark at its avatar's lower right (ui/components/ProviderBadge.tsx, ui/marks/provider.js over deck/js/provider-art.js), a model's face is its provider's mark when the name says which (Claude, Codex, Grok), never a guess, and the thinking is its own folded row ("Thought ▸") instead of being dropped. The stream's text frames do not carry the provider yet (core/stream/adapter.js), so replies show no badge until they do; frames.js reads `provider` and `model` on a text-delta as soon as the box sends them.

- feat(app): the new shell is the app (0.2.9). `/` opens Now in the @vyre/ui shell, on a phone as on the web; the legacy tab screens (Now, Chats, Agents, Places sheet) and their EmptyHere are retired (app/places and app/new-chat redirect). New routes the shell already pointed at: /u/chats (the box's sessions, those needing you first, New chat), /u/chats/new, /u/search (the person's records, which never read a sealed value, plus mentions.search groups: files, vault names, artifacts, GitHub) and /u/assistants. Now shows what is missing on this device and the assistants' asks and the Gate's held items ("Waiting on you", the old Needs list) above the tasks. The swipe-to-approve row and its perf marks (open.cold, approve.collapse) are gone with the old Now: .github/scripts/app-perf.mjs reports them "not measured".
- fix(app): copy rules on the phone: no "A server" kind in Add a device on a phone or browser, no "Make a space on your server" or "to invite people, make a space on your server" there, no "alex" or "harlow.vyre.run" in real screens ("You", "Paste the invite link"). scripts/app-walk-shell.mjs walks the shell at 390 px against awbox.

- fix(app): a device paired by a typed code now keeps the pairing, marks the server as the way it reaches its box, opens its paired person session and reconnects over the relay (src/real/pairing.ts afterPaired; used by the browser's Type the code, the Mac's boxless server and add-this-device). A browser the owner has not trusted yet cannot start the session: the pairing stays and the session starts once it is trusted. test: scripts/app-walk-records-ui.mjs, app-walk-records-shots.mjs, app-walk-paired-records.mjs, and the paired-device walk now also defines a case type (text, choice, link, sealed) and adds two records.

- feat(identity): claim a name from a browser with a passkey (0.2.9, gap A29). `claimIdentityWithPasskey` (apps/app/src/identity/claim.js) makes a WebAuthn credential (P-256, user verification required) as the identity's first device and signs the genesis and the claim's record with it; `createPasskeyKey` and `restorePasskeyKey` (apps/app/src/identity/passkey.js) read the attestation with a small CBOR reader, normalise the high-s twin an authenticator may return, and keep only the credential id and public key. A passkey is a full device (unlike a key a page can reach). The directory could verify a passkey's signature on a chain op but not on a name record or an act; `verifyWith` now takes the signing entry (`signing` from `signerKey`) and checks a passkey's assertion as one, in the Worker, the client directory, the audit key, the seal's bindings and spaces. The pinned hash of kernel/identity/chain.js is updated; merging with work/no-labels needs it recomputed.

- fix(switchboard,kernel)!: every threads tool a person can call is gated by the chats they are in, at ONE point (a wrapper over this module's `ctx.tool`), not tool by tool (reviewer-5 HOLD on 92494bcd3). A tool that takes a thread, an ask, a watch or a session answers not_found for a run in a chat the caller is not in; `threads.list`, `threads.asks`, `threads.live` and `threads.history` leave such runs out; `threads.pids` is empty for a non-module caller; with no person chain only runs in no chat show. First-party modules are exempt. `threads.answer` is covered through the ask's thread. A walker test calls every threads tool from the registry's own schemas as a member outside the chat. Merged flows' aecc0f8cc: its SL-1 (a session's agent is never a model slot name) is kept, and the daemon's own door opens a slot with `slot_open: true` (`lib/kernel-session`, `core/daemon`), which nothing a model or a module can supply.
- feat(work): a chat moves with its project (core/work/chat-carry.js, run by the move's own `chats` step under the mover's chain in the target): the chat is made again in the target Space under a NEW chat id with the same title and project; its people are those who are members there (the mover only if they were in it, or nobody else is left), its agents those that exist there, everyone else is listed in the new `former` field of the chat-record and gets nothing; the target record's `chat`, `people`, `agents`, `former`, `drive` and `location` are rewritten; the chat's sealed files land under the NEW id (`mapChatPath`, old id to new in the move's `chatMap`); those fields are the carry's, not compared by content at verify. The move's sides carry the Space's own `chats` and `members`.
- feat(stream,switchboard): the device's time zone rides with every message. `stream.send { tz }` (an IANA name; an unknown one is dropped, never stored): the `chat.user-message` frame carries `tz`, `threads.send` keeps it as the thread's current zone (`threads_runs.tz`, read by `threads.get().thread.tz`) and `thread.sent` says it. The brief and `lib/time` read the person's current zone from there. Showing a message's time in the viewer's own zone is the screen's (frames carry `time` in epoch ms).
- feat(stream): quoted replies, WhatsApp-style, in the same timeline. `stream.send { reply_to: <message id> }`: the user-message frame carries `reply_to` and `quote: { message, author, text }`, which the box reads from this chat's own log (a person's message, or an assistant's whole message), `text` cut to 140 characters. A message the log does not hold answers not_found, a private message cannot be quoted. The run is told what it answers (`Replying to <author>: "<quoted text>"` then the person's words), the same for every provider because it is plain text.
- feat(kernel,work): `chats.mine(chain)`, the one answer to "which chats am I in": the chat ids a chain may read (a person in it, or an assistant or model slot acting for them), joined with each chat's record (project, location, title) when the Records type is defined. `work.chat.list` uses it for `open`; any module with a kernel handle (the files search) calls `kernel.chats.mine(chain)` on the caller's own chain instead of keeping a copy of the rule. Kernel side: `grants.chatMine` / `chats.mineIds`.
- feat(stream): one Chat, the live-experience items. `stream.send` takes `mode: "steer" | "queue"` (default steer: words sent while the run works join the running turn at its next step, as `threads.send` always did; `queue` waits for the turn's end and can be taken back). `threads.chat-stop` stops every busy slot of a chat, or one by its slot id. Presence is now produced: `chat.presence` frames (ephemeral, never logged) say `{ who, state: "doing", doing: <tool summary> }` while a slot works on a tool, `{ who, state: "idle" }` when its turn ends, and `{ who, state: "typing" }` from the new `stream.typing { chat, on? }` (`on: false` clears it). One line per author, at most once a second.
- fix(switchboard)!: the chat gate on every `threads.*` call that names a run in a chat now fails CLOSED (reviewer-5): with the kernel on, a call needs a person chain that passes the kernel's chat read; a chain that could not be built (a bad token, an unenrolled device) or whose first hop is not a person is not_found. Only a first-party module's call is exempt. Tests that call `threads.*` as the local owner with no meta use `asOwner(d, root)` (test/helpers.js), which gives the call the facts the real socket would. A run with no agent is a model slot: its kernel session's agent hop is `model:<provider>/<model>#<n>` (minted once, stored in `threads_runs.slot`, narrowed to the run's project), no longer the default assistant's.
- feat(stream)!: one Chat, frame types are `chat.<kind>` (was `session.<kind>`: `chat.user-message`, `chat.text-delta`, `chat.text-done`, `chat.participant-joined` and the rest). The envelope field `session` (the log's id) is unchanged. A new chat with nobody in it who answers starts the default model slot on the first `stream.send` (a chat of one person only), working in `<home>/chats/<chat id>/work` when it has no folder of its own. A chat's status follows its runs (`working` while any run works, `idle` after the turn, `stopped` or `failed` when every run has ended that way), from `thread.status`, which now says its chat.
- feat(stream): one Chat, step E3b: a chat started outside the stream continues in it. At a `stream.send`, the runs of the chat (`threads.of-chat`) become its members (an agent's run is that agent's slot, a run with no agent is a model slot `model:<provider>/<model>#<id>`; stored with `kind = 'run'`, kept whatever the kernel's list of assistants says), their history is read into the chat's log (the person's words as said, the replies through the kernel like any), and the message goes to the run that is already there: no second run starts. A person speaking in the chat takes the run's keyboard from the surface that started it, once, instead of the send being silently dropped (`sent: false`). Test: the last case of core/switchboard/one-chat.test.js.
- test(daemon): the SIGTERM-during-start test gets a 120 s budget. A stop takes 7 to 9 s on a loaded test box on every revision tried (bd047118b and 47e64264a alternated on testbox6: 33.6 to 37.9 s for the four stops on the first, 33.7 s and one 51.6 s outlier on the second; the same with the work module disabled), so four stops sit at or over the old 30 s whatever the hub does. Nothing in the hub was found to delay a stop. fix(work): the memory engine is one per Space and the move tools read the running Space's own log (windows' per-Space module stores).
- fix(work): the Work lines' forget no longer wedges a resumed move (reviewer-5). `forgetKnow` is idempotent (nothing left to drop is a success, but never without a receipt while lines remain); the engine saves the receipt as soon as the lines are imported, and a forget that meets a line written meanwhile (`conflict`) copies the lines again and forgets against the new receipt, once, in both the same-home and the remote move (`ports.know.repull`). Tests: a crash between import and forget resumes and completes; a late line is carried again.
- feat(work,kernel): the plan carries every file's content hash (the Drive's own record, `drive.stat`; the chat folders' hashes come sorted and nameless from `survey`), covered by the hash the person approves, and a file edited after the approval stops the move. The remote move now carries the memory room (sealed to a one-use key the target made, forgotten at the source only against its receipt, re-carried once on a conflict) and the Work engine's lines (in the pull, `pulled.know`), so nothing is left behind across homes. The Personal to My Cloud upgrade is ONE approval for all the projects (`approveAll`: the set of plan hashes approved once, a move id per project, a retry keeps its move id and is not asked again); it needs windows' batch `moves.out`.
- feat(flows): schedules run in the Space's time zone through lib/time, the one time library (platform-2's b85d3eb72; lib/time/ is copied here byte for byte until that branch merges), never the server's (the user's option B). kernel/flows/zone.js is now a thin wrapper over lib/time's `toUTC` and `localParts`, so a cron has one daylight-saving rule, as a phone does: a time the clocks skip moves on by the gap (02:30 runs at 03:30), a time that happens twice runs the first time. `describeSchedule` (kernel/flows/schedule-words.js, used by the canvas `graph(flow, cat, { person, now })`) shows a schedule's next run on both clocks ("next 9:00 am ET · 6:00 pm your time"). Tests: a weekday 9am flow across both clock changes, passing under TZ=UTC, Asia/Karachi and America/Los_Angeles.
- fix(work,agents,projects): reviewer-3's MV-1 to MV-4 and reviewer-5's F1 and F2. `work.project.move` is outward (one yes in the approvals queue; moves.out already refuses any chain with an agent or model hop). A move is saved as it goes (`work_moves`: the id map, move id, plan and what is done) and a retry resumes it, finds an earlier attempt's project by its pointer back, and never copies a record twice; every copied record is read back and compared by content before the source records go; the plan hash covers record versions, and a listed file outside the project's folder or with a dot segment is refused; `state.verified` is set only after the chat files are carried. A memory room that changed between export and forget is carried again and forgotten against the new receipt. An agent's reach grants and actor are keyed by a stable id (`agt_<uuidv7>`, `agents.uid`), never the name, so a deleted agent's name given to a new agent inherits nothing, and `agents.delete` with no person is refused (the plugin agent's revoke relays its person's own verified facts and proof).
- feat(work): the remote form of a project move and the Personal to My Cloud upgrade built on it, coded to windows' design (core/work/project-move-remote.js). `planRemoteMove` is the same plan with a target on another server that is not readable from here; `runRemoteMove` drives out, the signed evidence, the target's receive and its server-to-server pull, checks counts against the plan, empties the source only then, and finishes both sides, every step resumable behind a saved state; `upgradePersonal` runs it per project (one approval each), skipping moved ones and continuing past a failure. It runs through ports the remote kernel client supplies (moves.out, evidence, in, finish and the pull), none of which exist yet, so it is exercised with stand-ins only. The memory room and the Work engine's lines are reported as not carried.
- feat(work): a Basic personal space keeps a project as a plain device folder. On a kernel with no Drive the project hub makes the Project record in the device's own store and sets its `drive_path` to this computer's home folder for it (learned when the computer adopts the project), skips the Drive marker, and files sessions under that folder; with a Drive nothing changes (id-named `Projects/<id>`). Tests: core/work/hub.test.js (stand-in kernel) and test/project-hub-basic.test.js (a real kernel with no Drive).
- feat(kernel,work): a project moves whole, chat folders included, without the mover reading a byte (lead's ruling, 5 Oct). The Drive gateway gains `survey` (counts a project's chat files and bytes, owner or admin only, for the plan), `inventory` (path, size and hash of every file of the moved project, never a byte, resting on the move's own `project.move_started` and an owner or admin) and a `removeMoved` that now confines itself to the moved project's folder and removes chat files for that same admin. The engine counts the chat files in the plan (a kernel with no sealed carry reports a blocker), carries them through `from.carry` (pool to pool inside the sealing processes, `moves.carryFiles`, not built yet), checks every hash on what arrives, and removes them with the rest. Tests: kernel/gateway/chat-folders.test.js and core/work/project-move.test.js.
- feat(work): the Work engine's session lines move with a project (core/work/memory/move.js; tools `work.know.move-export`, `move-import`, `move-forget`, each refused unless this Space's log holds the move's own event): the lines filed under the project's records go to the target with `record` rewritten through the move's id map and the source Space replaced by the target in their labels; the index, suggestions and proposals are derived and dropped with them; forget needs the receipt and refuses if the lines changed since. The move engine runs them between the memory room and the marker. Not run end to end yet.
- feat(stream)!: one Chat, step E3a. The stream tools (`stream.send`, `react`, `pin`, `keep`, `mark-read`, `open`, `open-peer`) take `chat`, not `session`. `stream.open` and `stream.open-peer` answer `{ chat, session, ... }`: `chat` is the id asked, `session` the log served (a chat nobody has spoken in through the stream, whose one run the CLI, a terminal or a Flow started, is served as that run's own log). With the kernel on, a thread id is no longer a way in: the person must be in the chat. Tests follow; the app's stream calls follow in app-wire.
- feat(work,switchboard): one Chat, the tools the app builds on. `work.chat.create` and `work.chat.change` (a person acting directly, the kernel's own chat functions; models are not accepted yet, a model joins when first asked); `work.chat.list` rows carry `project_name`, and for chats the caller is in `providers` and `last_line`, from the engine and never on the record; `threads.chat-switch` and `threads.chat-stop` reach a run by its slot. Every `threads.*` call a person makes on a run is checked against the run's chat with the kernel's chat read on their own chain (not_found otherwise; first-party modules and calls with no person chain are as before). Tool names start with their module's name, so these are `work.chat.*` and `threads.chat-*`, not `chats.*`.
- feat(kernel): a chat's folders (`Projects/<project id>/chat/<chat id>/` and `.../made/<chat id>/`) are its participants' only, decided at the authorizer from the kernel's own chat membership (kernel/core/folders.js): a participant, or the assistant the chat lists acting for one, reads and writes the files with no grant of their own; an owner, an admin, a project member or anyone holding the exact path is refused as absence on get, history, put, delete, move and listing, and a person who leaves loses it on the next call. A module's service chain may write them and never reads them. Share to project is a kernel grant of `drive.read` on exactly that one file to the project's members (never the folder, another file, or a write). One refusal test per Drive-gateway path in kernel/gateway/chat-folders.test.js.
- feat(projects): `projects.backup.sources` (the memory module's own) lists this computer's projects for the Basic encrypted backup: each project's folders file by file as { kind: "file", name, size, mtime, path }, the project rows as `rows/projects.jsonl`, and notices. Ignore rules (.git is kept): node_modules, build output (dist, build, out, target, .next), venvs, caches, logs and .DS_Store; a file over 2 GB is skipped with a notice; symlinks are never followed.
- fix(agents,work): an agent given a project by a call that carries no person is refused (`denied`) instead of silently left without its kernel grant; the plugin agent's own module call is the one exception. The plan hash is 43-character base64url, the form the kernel's moves and memory's room move require, and the move engine drives the memory room (`ports.memory`: offer, export, import, forget) between the file verification and the marker. Tests that depend on reach make their agents through `kernelCaller`.
- feat(work,kernel): the move engine removes the source files itself after every hash matches (`drive.removeMoved`, bound to the move's own `project.move_started`, checked per file under the mover's chain, no second ask) and a resume after verification does not re-plan; record types the target lacks are installed under the same approval and are part of the plan hash (only a missing Drive blocks). The core Project type gains `owner` and `due` and its client links to a Contact (no practice area). WIP, tests pending on the test boxes.
- feat(projects,kernel)!: one permission system for agent reach to a project (the user's ruling): the `projects_access` table, its seeding, `projects.access.migrate` and `.clear` are gone. An agent reaches a Project only by a kernel grant of the new read action `project.reach` on the Project record (lib/project-reach.js); a person holds it by role, an agent only by a grant of its own. `projects.access.grant` and `.revoke` make and revoke those grants as the person's own act with the kernel's proof (an agent is added as a kernel actor the first time it is given something; revoking one project from an agent that held the every-project grant keeps all the others as explicit grants); `projects.access.check` and `projects.reach` ask the kernel through the new handle method `agentMay` (needs.reach), which builds the [owner, agent] chain inside the kernel and answers allow or deny for a READ-risk act only, so no module can mint an agent chain. An agent whose `projects` is `*` holds ONE grant on every project (`vyre://<space>/project/*`), so a project made later is reached too. The agents module keeps an agent's `projects` list in step with its grants in the person's own create, update and delete (a call with no person, such as the plugin agent's, grants nothing; the plugin agent makes its own every-project grant in the person's call). New tools `projects.record` (agents only) and `work.project.ensure` (projects only). A grant needs the kernel's presence proof, so a test that makes an agent with projects does it through `kernelCaller` (test/helpers.js).
- feat(work,switchboard,daemon,records)!: one Chat, step E2 (team/0.3/CONTRACT-one-chat.md). The `session-summary` record type is replaced by `chat-record` (label "Chat"; not named `chat` because the kernel's own `chat.created` and `chat.changed` events would then share names with the Records events and break the kernel's replay of them): title, project, `chat` (the kernel chat id, unique), people and agents (mirrors of the kernel's list, put back if edited, kernel membership untouched), started, last_active, status (working, idle, stopped, failed), `drive` and `location` (`Projects/<project id>/chat/<chat id>/`). Nothing the engine keeps (models, providers, transcript files, summary) is on it. The writer (core/work/hub.js) follows the kernel's `chat.created` and `chat.changed` (the daemon reads them as the owner, who alone may see them, and says them on the module bus), the switchboard's `thread.started`, `thread.stopped` and `thread.renamed` (which now say their `chat`) and `thread.chat` (a terminal session's chat). Tools: `work.chat.list`, `work.chat.get`, `work.chat.rename`, `work.chat.move` replace `work.session.*`; the switchboard gains `threads.of-chat` and `threads.chat-of` (first-party modules only). A chat's Drive folders are named by the chat id.
- feat(projects)!: the folder-based project is gone; a project is a Project record. core/projects keeps its tool names but no longer reads or writes a marker file (`.vyre/project.json`), walks folders, or moves homes: the project's name, picks, people and watchers are rows of `projects_projects`, and the folders on THIS computer that belong to a project are rows of the per-machine table `projects_folders` (a path is a fact about one computer), which `projects.of` reads, longest match first. New tool `projects.adopt` (the work module only) gives this computer a local row and a home folder for a Project record; the work module writes the record for a project made through the old list (`project.created`), and archive and rename follow through `project.changed`. Removed: `core/projects/markers.js` and `move.js`, `projects.move`, `vyre projects move`, the `projects.moved` event. Agent reach (`projects_access`) is unchanged and is still its own table.
- feat(work): moving a Project to another Space (core/work/project-move.js, team/0.3/DESIGN-project-move.md). `planMove` reads what would move (records by type, files, bytes, sealed fields, blockers such as a record type the target lacks) and hashes it; `runMove` re-plans (a changed project is refused), creates a NEW project with a new id and folder in the target, copies the linked records with links rewritten and the files one by one under the mover's chain in each Space, verifies every file by hash, and only then leaves the old Space a `moved` marker pointing at the new record; it resumes after a crash from its id map. Sealed fields move only through the sealing process's own transfer (`ports.reseal`); with sealed fields and no such port nothing runs. Tools `work.project.move-plan` and `work.project.move` (the second answers `unavailable` until the kernel's compound move act exists). A Project gains status `moved` and the fields `moved_to` and `moved_from`.
- feat(kernel): the kernel is ON by default (KERNEL-default-on, branch work/kernel-default-on, not merged until the walk passes kernel-on). `VYRE_KERNEL=0` turns it off in a development build only; a packaged build ignores it, says so (one log line at start and a line in `vyre status`: "VYRE_KERNEL=0 is ignored: this build always runs with the kernel on") and keeps the kernel on (MA-5; a stray variable must not take a server down). package.json `files` gains `kernel` and `names/worker/chain.js` so a release ships them. The tripwire test core/memory/legacy-labels.test.js is deleted; the `SHIM(legacy labels)` branches stay for their owners to remove (assistant: core/memory; windows: core/spaces), because a call with no chain still reads its label there.
- feat(switchboard,daemon,kernel): one Chat, step E1b and the assistant ruling. A terminal session's SessionStart (the Harness's `thread.started` with a session and no thread of ours) leaves a chat of the person's, remembered in `threads_terminal_chats` and taken by a later adopt. The person's own assistant is never a listed participant of a chat (`chatFor` stops listing it); `kernel/core/room.js` and `chatRead` no longer require the default assistant hop to be in a chat's list, because it acts as the person and the chat checks the person (the same pass-through `authorize.js` already gives it). Any other agent in a run's chat must be an actor of the Space (grants.addActor, with the owner's yes); one that is not is a refusal, logged, never an owner-only chat that drops it. Tests in core/switchboard/one-chat.test.js.
- feat(watchers): watcher definitions are hidden records (`def-watcher`, like `def-flow`) where the kernel is on (core/watchers/defs.js): the record holds the settings (watcher.json) and the code (watch.js); the folder stays as the cache a sandboxed run reads. Existing folders are migrated into records once and idempotently, a record edited by a person is written back to the folder (the watcher then shows changed and waits for a new dry run and a yes), a folder edited by Claude's skill is written into the record, and a lost folder is restored from the record. Run state (schedule, cursor, failures, items) stays in the module's SQLite tables.
- feat(work,kernel): the move engine removes the source files itself after every hash matches (`drive.removeMoved`, bound to the move's own `project.move_started`, checked per file under the mover's chain, no second ask) and a resume after verification does not re-plan; record types the target lacks are installed under the same approval and are part of the plan hash (only a missing Drive blocks). The core Project type gains `owner` and `due` and its client links to a Contact (no practice area). WIP, tests pending on the test boxes.
- feat(projects,kernel)!: one permission system for agent reach to a project (the user's ruling): the `projects_access` table, its seeding, `projects.access.migrate` and `.clear` are gone. An agent reaches a Project only by a kernel grant of the new read action `project.reach` on the Project record (lib/project-reach.js); a person holds it by role, an agent only by a grant of its own. `projects.access.grant` and `.revoke` make and revoke those grants as the person's own act with the kernel's proof (an agent is added as a kernel actor the first time it is given something; revoking one project from an agent that held the every-project grant keeps all the others as explicit grants); `projects.access.check` and `projects.reach` ask the kernel through the new handle method `agentMay` (needs.reach), which builds the [owner, agent] chain inside the kernel and answers allow or deny for a READ-risk act only, so no module can mint an agent chain. An agent whose `projects` is `*` holds ONE grant on every project (`vyre://<space>/project/*`), so a project made later is reached too. The agents module keeps an agent's `projects` list in step with its grants in the person's own create, update and delete (a call with no person, such as the plugin agent's, grants nothing; the plugin agent makes its own every-project grant in the person's call). New tools `projects.record` (agents only) and `work.project.ensure` (projects only). A grant needs the kernel's presence proof, so a test that makes an agent with projects does it through `kernelCaller` (test/helpers.js).
- feat(projects)!: the folder-based project is gone; a project is a Project record. core/projects keeps its tool names but no longer reads or writes a marker file (`.vyre/project.json`), walks folders, or moves homes: the project's name, picks, people and watchers are rows of `projects_projects`, and the folders on THIS computer that belong to a project are rows of the per-machine table `projects_folders` (a path is a fact about one computer), which `projects.of` reads, longest match first. New tool `projects.adopt` (the work module only) gives this computer a local row and a home folder for a Project record; the work module writes the record for a project made through the old list (`project.created`), and archive and rename follow through `project.changed`. Removed: `core/projects/markers.js` and `move.js`, `projects.move`, `vyre projects move`, the `projects.moved` event. Agent reach (`projects_access`) is unchanged and is still its own table.
- feat(work): moving a Project to another Space (core/work/project-move.js, team/0.3/DESIGN-project-move.md). `planMove` reads what would move (records by type, files, bytes, sealed fields, blockers such as a record type the target lacks) and hashes it; `runMove` re-plans (a changed project is refused), creates a NEW project with a new id and folder in the target, copies the linked records with links rewritten and the files one by one under the mover's chain in each Space, verifies every file by hash, and only then leaves the old Space a `moved` marker pointing at the new record; it resumes after a crash from its id map. Sealed fields move only through the sealing process's own transfer (`ports.reseal`); with sealed fields and no such port nothing runs. Tools `work.project.move-plan` and `work.project.move` (the second answers `unavailable` until the kernel's compound move act exists). A Project gains status `moved` and the fields `moved_to` and `moved_from`.
- feat(kernel): the kernel is ON by default (KERNEL-default-on, branch work/kernel-default-on, not merged until the walk passes kernel-on). `VYRE_KERNEL=0` turns it off in a development build only; a packaged build ignores it, says so (one log line at start and a line in `vyre status`: "VYRE_KERNEL=0 is ignored: this build always runs with the kernel on") and keeps the kernel on (MA-5; a stray variable must not take a server down). package.json `files` gains `kernel` and `names/worker/chain.js` so a release ships them. The tripwire test core/memory/legacy-labels.test.js is deleted; the `SHIM(legacy labels)` branches stay for their owners to remove (assistant: core/memory; windows: core/spaces), because a call with no chain still reads its label there.
- fix(kernel,work): a session move is all or nothing. `drive.moveFolders(chain, pairs)` checks every file of every folder (`drive.read` and `drive.write` on the source, `drive.write` on the destination) under the mover's chain before any file moves, so `work.session.move` can never leave a session's chat and made folders split across two projects; `moveFolder` is the one-pair case.
- fix(work): a rename is only a title, so anyone allowed to update the record may rename and it reaches the project list and the thread; the `drive.read` stand-in check is gone (nothing in Drive depends on a name any more).
- feat(switchboard,daemon): one Chat, step E1 (team/0.3/DESIGN-one-chat.md). Every run lives in a chat: `threads_runs.chat` (new column), `threads.get` and `thread.started` say which. A start the stream makes keeps the chat it names; any other start (CLI, a Flow, the assistant) and a resumed older thread get a chat made by the daemon under the home owner's own chain (`deps.chatFor`, the owner plus the assistant it runs as, or the owner alone for a named agent that is not an actor of the Space). Tests: core/switchboard/one-chat.test.js; kernel-turn.test.js and threadsock.test.js follow the new fact that a person's own run has a chat of its own.
- feat(work)!: Drive folders are named by id, never by title (the user's decision, which also removes PH-3 at its root). A Project's folder is `Projects/<project id>` and its session folders `chat/<session id>` and `made/<session id>`; a rename of a project or a session changes only the title (on the record, the old project list and the thread) and never touches Drive. The rename-to-folder sync is gone. Moving a session to another project moves its two folders under the target project's folder as the person who moved it (`drive.moveFolder` checks `drive.read` and `drive.write` on every file under that person's chain and aborts the whole move on one refusal; the record is relinked only after the files moved). `drive_path` stays system-only: a person's edit of it is put back.
- fix(work,kernel): PH-3 and MV-1, and the last two rename paths. A rename made directly in Records no longer moves a folder as the service: only an edit by a person who holds Drive access (`drive.read` on the folders, asked of the person plus the service; owners and admins by role) moves it or reaches the project list or a thread, and the folder moved is the one the record named BEFORE the edit. The system fields (`slug`, `drive_path`, `memory_scope` on a Project; `thread`, `transcript`, `transcript_file`, `machine`, `drive`, `started`, `ended` on a session) are put back if a person edits them, and the hub moves only folders under `Projects/`. `drive.moveFolder` checks `drive.read` and `drive.write` on every source file and every destination under the caller's chain BEFORE anything moves, and one refusal aborts the whole move. A `/rename` inside Claude Code reaches the session record: at each turn's end and at the session's end the transcript's name (from Recall) is compared with the last one seen, and only a change counts, so a stale transcript name never overwrites a title set in Records. A kernel chat has no title of its own (its title is its thread's name), so `threads.rename` is the chat-title path.
- fix(work): PH-1, a Project's Drive folder marker is written under the CALLER's own chain, so a caller who cannot write Drive cannot make a project (and none is left half made); a rename, a move and a session rename done through the work tools run their record updates and Drive moves under the caller's chain too. A session's files live under its project's folder in `chat/<title>-<id6>` and `made/<title>-<id6>` and those folders follow the session's rename and its move to another project. `test/reach-anyone.json` now says why `work.project.create`, `work.project.rename`, `work.session.rename`, `work.session.move`, `threads.rename`, `flows.budget` and `harness.end` are safe.
- feat(work,switchboard,kernel): the Project hub's index and name sync. Every session is a `session-summary` record with its id (`thread`), start and end times, Drive folder, the kernel address of its transcript, and the transcript file path with the machine it is on; a session with no project is filed in the Space's General project (made with the Space), and `work.session.move` files it elsewhere (id, times and transcript pointer stay). A rename made anywhere reaches the others, ids unchanged, in both directions: the Project record, the old project list (`project.changed`), the Drive folder (named after the project; the new `drive.moveFolder` moves its files and tombstones the old paths) and every session's `drive`; a session's record title and the thread's name (new `threads.rename`, event `thread.renamed`). `work.project.rename` and `work.session.rename` rename from Records' side. The model-door summarizer is dropped: a summary is a plain facts line.
- feat(work,harness): terminal sessions are in the Project hub too. The Harness's SessionStart hook already said `thread.started` with the session and folder; the hub now finds the Project by folder (`projects.of`) and writes the summary, and a new SessionEnd hook (`harness.end`) says `thread.stopped` once so the summary closes (a second end changes nothing). `work.situation` with `context` adds the Project's memory (read for the named assistant, quoted as data) when the record is a Project or links to one. The core `project` type is `kind: "project"` with `slug` unique but not required, so Kits and imports can extend it (Objects' base kit extends this one type).
- feat(work): the Project hub, first slice (team/0.3/DESIGN-project-hub.md). Two core record types, `project` (name, short name, status, client, Drive folder, repo, memory scope) and `session-summary` (title, project link, people, agents, provider, model, account, started, ended, status, summary, thread, transcript address), defined by the work module. The tool `work.project.create` makes a Project with its short name, its Drive folder (`Projects/<short name>`, with a marker file holding the record's address, since Drive has only path prefixes) and its memory scope. The work module writes a session summary record from the switchboard's `thread.started` and `thread.stopped` (a resumed session is the same record, working again), linked to its Project, made on first sight for a slug the old folder projects still name; it holds no transcript text.
- refactor: the pure expression language and its conditions (conditions.js, expr.js, errors.js, with conditions.test.js) move from kernel/expr to lib/expr/. The kernel (kernel/expr/index.js, the gateway, the stage module), records/language and the app (ui/views/logic.js) all import that one copy, so the app and the kernel judge a record by the same rules. The copy under apps/app/ui/views/expr is deleted. expr.js gains the JSDoc types the app's type check needs.
- refactor(app): Find no longer imports anything from deck/. The command grammar, the p/t/u prefixes and the session merge are typed in screens/find/commands.ts (with the Deck's tests ported), so the app's type check passes and deck/ can go. The vendored expression language in ui/views/expr is marked as copied, and the view definition's types gain `sortDir` and `filter`, which the views already read.
- fix(app): the Vault's Held-fields reveal asks the box for `records.reveal` through the app's own call (the passkey, or the phone's yes), as the vault reveal does, instead of passing the Deck's simulated proof, which never worked on a real box.
- feat(app): Find takes the arrow keys on the web (Down and Up move through the rows, Enter opens the highlighted one, Up from the first goes back to the box) and adds `mentions.search` as sections after memory: vault names, Drive, artifacts and GitHub, names only, with a note for a provider that was late.
- feat(app): Find on every device (parity row 13), at /u/search and as a Cmd-K command bar (`FindHost`, `openFind()` in screens/find, for the shell to mount): one box over chats (names, then what Recall found in them), projects, people (assistants and Contact records), other records, Go-to places, files (files.search, with a preview) and memory (memory.relevant), the p, t and u prefixes, and Enter runs the line the way the Deck's Find does (`@agent` asks it, `tell <chat> to ...` types into it and watches it, `watch <chat>` watches it, anything else asks the assistant and opens the thread). A sealed field is never searched. The grammar, prefixes and session merge are the Deck's own modules. Logic tests in screens/find (12 pass on testbox2). No arrow-key row selection yet.
- feat(app): Glass in the web app (parity row 8; web only for 0.2.9, phone and Mac in 0.3.1), at /u/glass/<agent> (and /u/glass/box for files): watch an agent's computer live, take over the keyboard or sign in privately, hand back with a note, and a Files tab (list, preview, download, upload with progress, new folder, rename or move, trash). The picture is the Deck's vendored noVNC in an iframe page (src/glass/frame.js, copied with it to public/glass/ by `scripts/glass-assets.mjs`, run by `export:web`), with the Deck's rules: view only unless this surface holds the keyboard, fewer frames over a relay or a slow link, reconnect at 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s, pause while the tab is hidden and keep the last frame. The Glass mini card opens it on the web. On a phone or the Mac app the route says Glass is in the web app. Logic tests in screens/glass (11 pass on testbox2). Not yet seen in a real browser: no browser on the test box.
- feat(app): Connections follows connectors-029's connect answers: a token step carries the vendor's guide (steps and https links), and the OAuth-client step carries its guide, redirect and the two fields, so the app can be typed in directly (`connectors.connect { app }`) or picked from the vault (`client`). Removes the unused `clearClipboard` source call from Vault.
- feat(app): Connections in the app (parity row 5), at Settings, Connections (/u/connections): Add (the connector catalog with who can use it, the vendor sign-in with a paste box for another browser, token and OAuth-client steps; the one Google sign-in for Gmail and Calendar is the catalog's own `google-api` preset, so it needs no special case), MCP servers (add, test, restart, remove, per-tool Read, Held or Off), Google accounts (Sign in with Google, service account, refresh-token item, scope test), GitHub (device code or a pasted token, a shared repo picker `RepoPicker` for Projects to use) and Access (which surfaces may use each connection, Agents grants asking for the person). A typed token goes to the box once and any echo of it is masked. Nothing polls except while a sign-in is open. Logic tests in screens/connections (13 pass on testbox2).
- feat(app): Vault in the app has the Deck's other pages (parity row 6). Real mode gets Items, Passes, Shared, Devices and Health sections: Passes (what waits for the person with Approve and Deny, New pass with relayed or sealed and the ticket, Revoke naming what to replace, Offboard a person), Shared with you, Devices (revoke), Watchtower (weak, reused, rotate, old, 2FA, unprotected, and the opt-in breach check), an item's History (versions, who, when; earlier passwords counted, never shown), Change (replace a value or make a new one on the server, vault.update) and Make an SSH key (vault.ssh.generate). No value is read by any of these. The app never calls `vault.copy` (a copy goes to the phone's own clipboard), so `vault.clipboard.clear` has no screen. Logic tests in screens/vault/more.test.js (25 pass in the folder on testbox2).
- feat(app): Memory in the app has the Deck's other three parts (parity row 12). Real mode gets Facts, Lessons and Sites tabs: Lessons (learn.lessons, stats, skills; Accept, Edit, Relax, Retire, Decline, skill Install and Dismiss, a loosening asks for the person through the app's box call), Sites (memory.site.list, detail, forget, restore: Forget never asks first and Undo lasts a day; a family and Forget all ask once), and "Where this came from" on a fact (memory.why: the turns behind it by thread, the modules that taught it, never an invented source). Logic tests lessons, chrome-sites and why in screens/memory (26 pass on testbox2).
- feat(kernel): a model slot is the person's authority narrowed to its chat's Project (one Chat, reviewer-3 G1). `surfaces.open(person, { chat, agent: "model:<provider>/<model>#<n>", project? })` writes the Project into the token (a slot lives in a chat; only a slot takes a Project; the id must be a slot id), `chainFor` builds windows' `model_slot` chain with `chain.project`, and authorize refuses another Project's resource (`outside_project`) for it; a resource of no Project is judged as before. `chatRead`, `chatHas` and the room checks accept a `model:` hop when the person on the chain is in the chat, so the slot ends when its person leaves.
- feat(spaces): `spaces.tier`, an internal tool (reach modules) for the modules that refuse on a Basic personal space (Planner, tasks): `{ space? }` (the home's own when omitted) answers `{ tier: "basic" | "cloud", cloud: [{ id, name, label }] }`, the tier from the same rule as `spaces.list` and the Cloud spaces the person is in. An unknown space is `not_found`.
- feat(modules,kernel): `ctx.kernel.for(space).call(tool, input, chain)` runs a module tool in a hosted Space's own instance, under the chain the caller holds there (`kernel.chainIn(space, meta)`), after THAT Space's `authorize` allows the kernel action the tool declares (`crossSpace` on its manifest entry; a tool without it is refused with `not_declared`). First-party modules only, never on the wire. The tool sees `meta.in_space` and `meta.in_space_chain`, set only by the registry (a symbol key; whatever a client sends under those names is dropped). A chain with no right in that Space, or built in another Space, is refused with `denied` before the tool runs. The other Space's store is never read from the caller.
- feat(spaces): `spaces.list` rows carry `tier` ("basic" or "cloud"), the same machine role `storeMode` reads: a space whose home is a server is cloud; a space on this computer is cloud on a server machine and basic on a device. The app reads only that field.
- feat(stores): a personal space has two tiers (the user, 5 Oct). A device install (laptop or desktop, not a server) is Basic: no Twenty, no Docker or Colima, no Records refusal; the default store mode is the built-in index. Twenty is provisioned only on a server install (`config.isServer(cfg.machine)`), a packaged build ignores `VYRE_STORE` (a server is always Twenty, never sqlite or auto; a device is always Basic, the built-in store with the fixed personal types), and only a development build honours it. `storeMode(env, { server })`, `createStoreFor({ server })` and `storeStatus({ server })` take the machine role.
- feat(stores): a server has one record store, Twenty; a device keeps its own, limited one (cleanup, ruling 5 Oct 03:08Z). VYRE_STORE is `twenty` or `sqlite`; `auto` is gone and a packaged server refuses `sqlite`. A server that cannot run Twenty makes no new Space (the person's server is offered, no create-in-the-built-in-store choice in spaces, the app or the installer) and its own Space boots with a store that refuses every record call in one plain line (kernel/store/refusing.js, shown by `vyre status`). A Basic device boots on its SQLite store with no refusal and only project and chat-record, plus the hidden system types they need (records/basic-types.js): records.define of any other type answers "Custom types need a Cloud space." The installer writes VYRE_STORE=twenty.
- feat(stores): a personal space has two tiers (the user, 5 Oct). A device install (laptop or desktop, not a server) is Basic: no Twenty, no Docker or Colima, no Records refusal; the default store mode is the built-in index. Twenty is provisioned only on a server install (`config.isServer(cfg.machine)`), and `VYRE_STORE` still overrides. `storeMode(env, { server })`, `createStoreFor({ server })` and `storeStatus({ server })` take the machine role.
- fix(spaces): `spaces.host-here` needs no presence proof (walker): making a space is not one of the yes moments, so it rides on the owner's authenticated call and the owner check stays. A passkey browser that has just paired a server can create its first space. The tests that used host-here as the presence-gated act use `spaces.retire-here` now.
- feat(spaces): a space's home time zone (an IANA zone, checked with lib/time `validZone`). It starts as the creating device's zone (`meta.zone`, else the machine's), an owner or admin changes it with `spaces.time-zone.set`, and `time_zone` (null when none) is in `spaces.list`, `spaces.get` and `spaces.tier`. lib/time (zones.js, index.js) comes from platform-2's branch, unchanged.
- feat(modules): every hosted Space gets each module its own store (03:45Z ruling). `ctx.store.db` and `ctx.store.dir()` follow the Space the running call is for (`meta.in_space`, set only by `ctx.kernel.for(space).call`, inherited by the calls it makes): the home's Space keeps vyre.db, every other hosted Space gets `<home>/kernel/spaces/<space>/modules/<module>.db` with the module's own migrations replayed, and its own data folder. `ctx.kernel` follows the Space the same way (that Space's `kernelFor`, so its own records, log, grants and service chain). A module that prepares a statement once at start belongs to the home's Space; it reaches the right one by using `ctx.store.db` inside the call. `ctx.kernel.for(space).call` now carries the caller's origin as `ctx.call` does.
- fix(kernel): SL-1 (reviewer-3). `model:` is a Switchboard slot name, and only a `model_slot` fact makes one: an `agent_session` fact under a `model:` agent name gets no chain, and `surfaces.open` refuses that agent name, so a narrowed agent can no longer shed its narrowing by having a session opened under such a name. The built-in stores report conformance revision 6, which the suite now expects.

An unknown space is `not_found`.
- feat(modules,kernel): `ctx.kernel.for(space).call(tool, input, chain)` runs a module tool in a hosted Space's own instance, under the chain the caller holds there (`kernel.chainIn(space, meta)`), after THAT Space's `authorize` allows the kernel action the tool declares (`crossSpace` on its manifest entry; a tool without it is refused with `not_declared`).
