A device install (laptop or desktop, not a server) is Basic: no Twenty, no Docker or Colima, no Records refusal; the default store mode is the built-in index. Twenty is provisioned only on a server install (`config.isServer(cfg.machine)`), a packaged build ignores `VYRE_STORE` (a server is always Twenty, never sqlite or auto; a device is always Basic, the built-in store with the fixed personal types), and only a development build honours it. `storeMode(env, { server })`, `createStoreFor({ server })` and `storeStatus({ server })` take the machine role.
- feat(kernel,stores): links are real relations (plan item 9). A link to a type gets a named inverse shown on the other record and may be a list (`many`); the gateway checks that the target is a live record of its type; Twenty holds a link as a RELATION field (a list through a hidden junction object) and the built-in store as before, and the conformance suite (revision 6) holds them to the same answers. Links stored as urn text move onto relations when a Space's store opens, without changing any record's version.
- feat(identity): claim a name from a browser with a passkey (0.2.9, gap A29). `claimIdentityWithPasskey` (apps/app/src/identity/claim.js) makes a WebAuthn credential (P-256, user verification required) as the identity's first device and signs the genesis and the claim's record with it; `createPasskeyKey` and `restorePasskeyKey` (apps/app/src/identity/passkey.js) read the attestation with a small CBOR reader, normalise the high-s twin an authenticator may return, and keep only the credential id and public key. A passkey is a full device (unlike a key a page can reach). The directory could verify a passkey's signature on a chain op but not on a name record or an act; `verifyWith` now takes the signing entry (`signing` from `signerKey`) and checks a passkey's assertion as one, in the Worker, the client directory, the audit key, the seal's bindings and spaces. The pinned hash of kernel/identity/chain.js is updated; merging with work/no-labels needs it recomputed.
- fix(kernel): one rule for an outward approval, no older looser path. Every producer of a held outward act records `form.bind` (the Flow runner now does: `requestBind` of a service step's request, `actBind` of any other call step's action, resource and input; the calendar sync already did), every consumer passes the same bind (leases now bind lent-computer sessions too), and `approvedAct` refuses an outward approval that recorded none. `actBind` is new in kernel/seal/uses.js. test/outward-flags.test.js checks that every registry-held outward tool binds its card to a digest of the whole input.
- fix(kernel): `approvedAct` compares the bind. An approved task that recorded the bind of what the person saw (`form.bind`, a digest of the request as it would be sent) releases only a request that carries the same bind; approve A and send B is refused, and a request that states none is too. It holds for every outward act, not only the calendar sync (which checked it for itself). `authorize` passes the request's `input.bind` through, and the service lease passes the bind it computes from the request it is about to send. An approval that recorded no bind is judged as before. Test: approve A, send B with that approval, refused.

- feat(one-yes): `wink.code.open` is a pair moment, so a headless walk or a dev build signs the owner's yes over it (`dev-sign-proof --yes pair --tool wink.code.open --input '{"flow":"W2"}'`) and a browser or server typed pairing can start; `records.seal-put` and `records.reveal` are the vault moment (filling or revealing a sealed field, ruling 7cc004d). A prefix never counts.
- feat(names): the name recovery code is gone (0.2.9, no existing installs). A claim no longer makes or returns a one-time recovery code and the directory stores no code hash (the claim answer is `{ name, mine, fresh }`); `POST /v1/names/code`, `directory.rotate` and `codeHash` are deleted; `vyre setup --name`, `vyre name claim` and the setup channel stop printing one. Instant recovery through the identity (its own recovery code and contacts) and support's admin rebind are the only ways back to a name. The identity's recovery code (spaces.identity) is a different thing and stays.

- fix(kernel/gateway): `records.reference` treats a field as a room placeholder only when it equals exactly the token a room view makes for that record and field. A text field a member filled with `{{field:<other record>#ssn}}` was echoed as a placeholder (reviewer-3 RF-1) and could steer an action to another record's sealed value; it is now plain data with its braces broken. Test added.
- feat(switchboard): the kernel validates a `record` mention on `threads.send`, `threads.start` and a queued edit (`core/switchboard/record-tags.js`). The id must be a record reference in this Space and is read under the sender's own chain through `records.reference` (a service chain, a stranger, a made-up or foreign reference tags nothing and the words stay plain text); a tag carries the record as data with sealed parts as placeholders, marked outside text. Non-record mentions go to their providers as before. Tests: record-tags.test.js.
- feat(planner): the Planner is built on Vyre Records. It has no tables and no migrations. Alarms, timers, reminders and /later tasks are `reminder` records and notes are `note` records (declared by the module, listed in Records); to-dos are the kernel's Tasks assigned to the person (a Task's `form.planner` carries list, priority and tags); the calendar is the Space's `event` records, the ones a connector's sync writes, with the planner's own events made as source `vyre`; rings and settings are `planner_firing` and `planner_state` records (system types, left out of the Customize list). The scheduler stays in the engine and reads a working set loaded from the records, so ringing is as exact and synchronous as before, `planner.fired`, `planner.acked`, the ring keys and the box ringing when the Mac is shut are unchanged; every change is written through to the gateway in order and a tool answers once it is saved. A record changed from the app, a Flow or a connector is read back through the kernel's `reminder.*`, `note.*`, `task.*` and `event.*` events (a changed time moves the next ring, a finished one stops ringing). `planner.calendar.sync` reads the window again; the planner's own Google calendar copy and its 15-minute poll are gone (a calendar with events is refreshed every 15 minutes; with none there is no timer). Needs the kernel: with it off every planner tool but `planner.parse` answers `unavailable`. `core/planner/store.js`, `calendar.js` and their tables are deleted (no data to migrate). Behaviour changes: a to-do's words, list and time are fixed once made, it does not repeat or reopen, has no sub-items, and only the person finishes it (an assistant adds one, the doer closes it); an item's id is its record's id (the CLI reads both forms); `planner.add` of kind event makes an Event record. Tests: planner.test.js moved onto a real kernel, events.test.js replaces calendar.test.js, records.test.js is new.
- feat(records-tools): `records.reference`, the tool behind the `#` chip. It takes a urn, reads under the caller's own chain through `gateway.records.reference`, and returns the record as data with sealed (and room-hidden) parts as `{{field:urn#name}}` placeholders. Person-reach like `records.get`, open to the person's assistant (named in `core/modules/agent-reach.js`, so `kernel/golden/allow.json` is regenerated), and added to the remote wire's records calls.
- feat(kernel/placement): node placement is decided by node descriptor records. `kernel/placement` holds the descriptor shape (capabilities, resources, residency, posture, lend policy), its signature by the node's own key (an edited or unsigned record decides nothing), and one scheduler: two-way consent (Space policy and lend policy), capability, resource, residency and posture fit, online, power, awake and CPU and memory ceilings, then locality, the preferred node, load and uptime. It answers with `workload.placed` (and what it passed over) or `workload.refused` with a code and plain reasons. `core/runner/placement.js` no longer has its own rules: it builds this computer and the server as node facts and maps the answer to here, server or wait with the same words as before. The scheduler is named non-base in `kernel/size.test.js` (a decision, never an enforcement).
- feat(kernel/gateway): `records.reference(chain, type, id)`, the kernel side of `#contact`: one read under the caller's grants, then every sealed part (and any part a group room may not read) is a `{{field:urn#name}}` placeholder in `fields` and `text`, whoever asks, so the AI reasons over the rest and can use the token in an action. A value cannot forge a token (its braces are broken in the text). Declared in `kernel/contracts/gateway.d.ts`.
- feat(wink): the camera reader's code (0.2.9, replaces 0.3.1). The drawn avatar carries the SAME eight symbols the person would type, so the camera reads the code and the pairing that follows is the typed code's own (CPace, the ack typed back): no second secret and no second way to pair. relay/client/avatarcode.js maps a code to the 8 bytes deck/vyrecode already protects with a CRC-8 and Reed-Solomon (`codeToAvatarBytes`, `avatarBytesToCode`; version byte 0xC1, forty bits of symbols, a magic that keeps an identity mark's fingerprint from reading as a code). `wink.phone.open` returns `avatar` (base64url of the 8 bytes) beside `code`, `spaces.invites.create` returns `code_avatar`, and `addThisDevice({ avatar })` takes the decoded bytes in place of typing. Native decoders (iPhone, Android, web) turn camera pixels into the 8 bytes (deck/vyrecode/decode-core2.js is the reference); this is what they hand to the app.

- fix(security): every container image Vyre runs as root on a box or builds the edge from is pinned by digest (reviewer-3 SC-1, SC-2): the backup and restore helper (`alpine tar` over the data volumes, now alpine:3.20@sha256 as `HELPER_IMAGE`), the edge's Caddy base and its derived Dockerfile's alpine, and BuildKit. The publish image check accepts `name:tag@sha256:...`. test/image-pins.test.js fails on any unpinned image reference in core/cli/commands/box.js and lib/publish/edge.js. The manual restore example in docs/using/box-care.md is pinned too. The digests are the multi-arch index digests of 5 Oct 2026; bump them on purpose.
- feat(names): the old 72-hour recovery rebind is removed (0.2.9, gap A10); instant recovery (the identity's own chain) is the only path. The directory Worker drops `POST /v1/names/recover` and `/recover/cancel`, the pending rebind and its landing, the recover rate limits and `mine`'s `pending`; `core/names` drops `names.recover` and `names.recover.code`, the `name.recovered`, `name.recovery-pending` and `name.recovery-cancelled` events, the `recovering` config key and the hourly cancel; the relay's setup channel no longer takes a recovery code. A pending rebind a record still carries from before is cleared on release or admin rebind, never landed. Support's admin rebind stays. The recovery code a claim returns and `/v1/names/code` stay for now (BACKLOG: retire recovery codes).
- feat(records,kernel,app): objects layer, items 10 to 13 of the 0.2.9 platform gaps. (10) A field takes `visible_if` and `required_if`, Expressions over the record's other stored fields: the language (`defineField.*({ visible_if, required_if })`, checked and printed back), the gateway (`field_not_shown` when a value is written to a field the record does not show, `field_required` when a visible required_if field is left empty; a create is judged whole, an update only where it touches the field or what its condition reads) and the record page (hidden fields are not listed, a required empty one shows a Required chip and cannot be saved empty). (11) A type stores its `views` (list, board, calendar, columns, grouping, sort, filter), validated by `records.define`; `viewDefOf` lays the first stored view of each kind over deck/ui/view-defs.js, which stays as the default for a type that stores none; a Kit's views are folded into the type they show when the Kit is installed (the Kit's own list stays for the install card); list, board and calendar apply a view's filter. (12) A `base` Kit in the library: Contact, Lead, Appointment, Client, Subscriber, Project; Lead, Client and Subscriber are roles linked to the one Contact; practice area is a choice. (13) A stage takes `enter_if` and a type takes `stage_sets` (`defineStage([...], { sets: [{ name, when, stages }] })`): the first set whose `when` holds gives that record's stages, the default stages otherwise. The gateway refuses a stage outside the record's set (`stage_not_in_set`) and an entry whose condition fails (`stage_entry_refused`); kernel/flows/stages.js advances along the record's own set and holds a record whose next stage cannot yet be entered. One new module, kernel/expr/conditions.js, is the single judge for the gateway, the stage module and the app. No new permission, log, table or runner.
- feat(mac): a Mac server's Spaces run Twenty in Colima's own Docker with the same pinned images and compose as a server: `stores/twenty/mac.js` (`macStoreOptions`, spread into `createStoreFor`) points docker at Colima's socket (DOCKER_HOST from vyre.env; no `docker context use`), makes the preflight ask `vyre-runtime room N` (a full VM says so plainly and offers the person's server), and makes a new Space call `makeRoom` first ("Making room for a new space"). `realRunner` takes an optional `{ env }`. On a Mac Twenty is published on 127.0.0.1 only, at a random port recorded in reach.json and store.json, through a pinned proxy container (Docker cannot publish from the internal network Twenty stays on); a server's compose is unchanged.
- feat(runner,spaces,daemon): lending a computer works end to end between two machines. A member's own session for a Space runs on their computer instead of the server (the agent by name, found on the lender: `VYRE_CLAUDE_BIN` or PATH; the Space's definition is `lentSpec` or the member's own agent with the provider as the only network), the work sits in an encrypted workspace (gocryptfs, key from the Space's lease, memory only), every turn is checkpointed to the Space's home, and when the grant ends (an Offer withdrawn, the member removed or left) the home tells that computer down the connection it holds (`wink.lent.revoked`, `runner.revoke`): the sessions stop and the whole workspace is deleted within about two seconds while the home keeps everything. Also fixed: the home names the computer calling (`lent.whoami`, from what the transport proved) and the Offers are made under that id (the identity entry id never matched what the home sees, so a lent computer was never allowed); the home's challenge for an offer call carried no op or payload (WIRE_TO_PROOF), so no device could sign it; `spaces.devices.lend` answers a server's challenge with this computer's key on a development build; an owner or admin can stop a member's computer from the Space's own home (`member`, the id the Space gives it); a revoked runner is made again after a new grant. Not wired: reinstating a computer whose lease was revoked is an admin act on the home's sealing process with no tool on the wire, so a computer removed from a Space cannot be lent to it again until that is done.

- feat(wink): storage works on the built-in network, no Tailscale. (1) The Wink module runs on a person's computer that belongs to a server (machine "device"), as the client side: it pairs a server, reaches the Spaces hosted there, lends itself, and holds a connection for the storage drives it can reach; a computer on its own (solo) stays out. (2) A drive paired with `wink.storage.pair` or `pick` now joins the Space's pool: the kernel hands the Wink module the pool, `backendFor` and `createBridge` (kernel/index.js), and the module attaches every paired offer as a pool node (before, a paired drive was recorded and nothing was ever placed on it). Storage grants stay in the module's own table: `storage.hold` is not a kernel action, so the kernel refused every pairing ("a grant needs a subject in this Space"). (3) A computer keeps one connection to its server (`serverlink.hold`, `holdDrive`); the home gets each admitted device's session through the peer door (`winkHolds`) and calls back down it. `wink.storage.discover` on the home also lists what the held devices see from where they sit (`wink.storage.bridge.scan`), `pick` of such a drive hands it to that device at once (the sealed secret, then the device serves it), and a device serves its drives again after a restart (`wink_meta served:<offer>`, `resumeServing`). `wink.storageRoots` in the config adds folders drives may be mounted under. Proof on testbox6 with the real relay and directory: a bucket paired on a server took a cold chunk; a folder on a second computer, paired to the server over the relay, listed itself, was picked and took a chunk.

- fix(daemon): the home serves the lent-computer wire. A Space's home now registers the `lent` service (core/runner/lent-home.js, built by core/daemon/lent-service.js) on its remote server, so a member's computer can start a lent session, checkpoint it and resume it over the peer wire; until now only tests built it and every `lent.*` call answered no_such_call. The Space's definition of a session comes from the daemon option `lentSpec`; with none the home answers not_found rather than inventing a program. Boundaries: `core/daemon -> core/runner` gains lent-home.js.

- feat(stores/twenty,spaces): every image of a Space's Twenty and of the home unit is pinned by tag and digest (twenty v2.44.0, postgres 16.4-alpine, redis 7.4-alpine, headscale v0.23.0); the Space compose and an upgrade take a full `name:tag@sha256:...` reference (`TWENTY_IMAGE_REF`), never a bare tag. Only vyred's own image stays on its release tag.
- feat(sessions): Vyre owns the context window of every session it runs (core/switchboard/rollover.js, team/0.2.5/memory-context.md section 3c). After a turn, when the window is 60% full (`sessions.rollover_at`, per project; `sessions.rollover` turns it off) and nothing is running, Vyre ends the agent's session and starts a fresh one in the same folder; the thread, its folder and its event log do not change and the transcript says once "Continued in a fresh session". For Claude the fresh window runs under a new session id (`threads_rolls`, migration; a session id names one transcript), resumes under it, and `threads.origin`, `threads.own-transcript` and `threads.bind` know it for its thread; another agent (Codex, Grok, any ACP agent) just starts a new session. The person's next message carries a seed in front of it (held in the thread's saved options until it goes out, so a restart in between loses nothing): the person's own decisions for the project, the plan as the agent last left it, an index of pointers into every earlier window (the person's requests with turn numbers, files touched, commits made) and the last turns word for word (up to 48,000 characters), one cut for the tail and the pointers (`recall.pointers`, which indexes the windows first). Every dropped turn stays one `memory_turn` away; the seed itself is not a turn in Recall (`lib/seed.js`). The window is the agent's own report (Claude's request usage and result window; Codex's usage_update; Grok's last request) or, with none, the characters said counted at four to a token, rolled at the earlier 50%. It waits up to 3 turns for a running tool, subagent or background job, rolls at 75% whatever is running, never rolls twice within 10 turns, refuses a seed over 30% of the window, and a message sent during a roll waits for it. A named agent's fresh window starts through `agents.resume` with its own credentials and scope. `threads.roll` (now, a person's surface only) and `threads.rolls`; event `thread.rolled`. A thread another provider runs is kept word for word under `<home>/mirror` in Claude Code's own layout, which Recall indexes when its turn finishes, so its windows are retrievable as Claude's are.
- feat(cli): `vyre roll` continues a long Claude Code session in the person's own terminal: it builds the same seed (`threads.roll-session`), starts `claude --session-id <fresh>` in the folder with the seed as its first message (a seed too long for an argument goes in a file under `<home>/rolls`, `--file`, and the message names it), and records the window it came out of so a second roll reaches back through the first. `--print` prints the seed, `--no-start` writes it and starts nothing, `--session` names a session, `--thread` asks a Vyre-run session to roll now. A person's own terminal session is told once when its window passes the line (`harness.enrich` reads the session's transcript, only inside a transcript folder, and the hook prints it as a systemMessage); a session Vyre runs and an agent's are never told.

- feat(memory): turn links and `memory_turn`. The indexer now records what each turn touched in `recall_links (session, seq, kind, ref)` (migration 3): files changed (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit), files read, commits (named in a turn's words or printed by a `git commit` result) and urls, found without a model by core/transcripts/links.js (a tool call links to the next assistant turn of its exchange, else the one before). Sessions indexed before the table existed are linked once on the next pass. New tools `recall.turn` (a span of a session word for word, by seq with before/after or from/to/span, each turn with its pointer `session:seq`, time and links; a turn the index cut at 4,000 characters is read whole from the transcript when the file still says the same words) and `recall.links` (turns that touched a file by path or bare name, a commit by short or full hash, or a url), scoped exactly as recall.thread is and offered to agents as `memory_turn`; `memory_search` takes `file` and `commit` to narrow to turns that touched them. No new dependency.
- feat(wink): the built-in network runs for real. `core/wink/netd.js` is started by the wink module on a server home: a supervised Headscale (loopback only), the gate in front of it, the Wink node (wink-forwarder) joined to it, and the node host's door answering peers as `device:<eid>` through the peer door's new `serve` (core/daemon/peer-door.js: the relay row is read on every call, the kernel's chain records the path as "wink"). Deny-by-default policy from control/policy.js: the home is the hub, every other node reaches the door port and nothing else. It never blocks the module's start; a failed piece is retried every 30 s and the relay carries everything meanwhile. State is plain: `off`, `no-binary`, `starting`, `up`, `failed` (with a reason), read by `wink.network.status` through the node host; `wink.controlUrl` in the config names a public control address (the gate then listens on every interface and a pairing is handed a one-time join key), `wink.network: false` or `VYRE_WINK_NET=0` turns it off. The box image carries Headscale (pinned v0.29.4, sha256 per architecture) and wink-forwarder (built from `wink/forwarder` in a digest-pinned Go stage); no Tailscale product. Tests: `core/wink/netd.test.js` (fake engines), `test/box-wink-net.test.js`, and the real-binary `core/wink/netd.real.test.js` under `VYRE_WINK_REAL=1` on a test server.
- refactor(wink): one Headscale path. A space's home unit (lib/spaces/home-unit.js) no longer carries a Headscale service, volume or port (it was an opt-in, pinned to v0.23.0, started by nothing); the Wink network is the box's own, `core/wink/netd.js`, on Headscale 0.29.4 pinned by sha256 in box/Dockerfile. `spaces.create` no longer takes `headscale`. The join policy is tied to the paired device row: a one-time key is for one device and its node joins as `nodeNameFor(device)` (carried in the pairing hand-over as `hostname`); a node reaches the door only while that device has a live row, a node bound to no row is deleted once no key is outstanding, and removing the row (or pairing one) re-syncs the policy at once instead of waiting for a poll. The peer-channel listener now ends connections a dead path left half-open when it closes, so a removed device cannot hang a shutdown. Real-binary test (VYRE_WINK_REAL=1) covers row removal.
- feat(relay): a self-hosted relay and name directory as one container. `relay/Dockerfile` (base pinned by digest, non-root, healthcheck, `/data` volume for the directory's one state file), `relay/compose.yml` (loopback ports, read-only root, caps dropped), `relay/README.md` (TLS in front), `relay/node/main.js` and `relay/node/directory.js` (names/worker's real code, no DNS published), `scripts/relay-roundtrip.mjs` (box registers a sealed pairing ticket, a device resolves it once). test/box-init.test.js now checks relay/Dockerfile's pin too.
- feat(wink): `core/wink/reach.js`, a reachability fallback for a home server behind NAT. The relay stays the first working path; in the background it tries a global IPv6 address, UPnP (SSDP and SOAP, lease, delete on stop) and NAT-PMP, refuses a router behind carrier-grade NAT, and calls the state "direct" only after an outside check reached the port. `relay/node/server.js` gains `POST /v1/reach/check` (dials only the caller's own public address, ports from 1024, rate limited) and `relayVerifier` calls it. Not yet called by the daemon (netd), and the hosted Cloudflare relay has no such endpoint.

- fix(wink): wink.share (Share a computer) now does what the runner reads. A relay `app` row is a phone as well as a computer, so it also checks the Wink device row (only your own computer is shared; a phone, server or storage device is refused), switches the computer's compute offer on and records the member's side, so computeAllowed answers yes for your personal space (the old call only wrote a node.host grant nothing read). test/wink.test.js asserts it.
- fix(storage): discover finds an attached cloud volume or any real disk mounted anywhere (reads /proc/self/mountinfo, skipping the system's own partitions, loop and tmpfs mounts), not only folders under /Volumes, /media and /mnt. So a droplet with a volume attached shows it as a candidate.
- fix(files): files.drive.* no longer answers `no_tailscale` or names Tailscale; folders-as-a-disk sharing says plainly it is not available on this device yet (code `unavailable`), and the Space's own Drive does not depend on it.

- fix(spaces): the home unit pins Twenty by tag and digest (v2.44.0, the release stores/twenty's live suite runs against) instead of the placeholder.
- refactor(wink): the Wink code's renderer (`vyrecode2.js`, which draws the rings) and `identity.js` (the colours and skin tones the marks share) moved from deck/vendor/vyrecode to `lib/wink-code/` beside the decoder, so drawing and reading live in one place. The Deck, the app (drawn code source, marks), the other vendored mark files, the daemon's served libs, sw.js, shell-hashes and the tests import from there. The app's Metro config now watches lib/wink-code (the earlier decoder move needed it too: the phone bundle could not otherwise resolve lib/wink-code/payload.js). The camera page no longer paints a raw colour (`color.bg`).
- feat(mac): the app window's streams work. A custom URL scheme cannot carry a WebSocket, so the chat and terminal streams the page opens on vyred's ticketed /v1/streams/<module>/<name> never connected in the Mac window. The page's WebSocket is now replaced (VyreAppWindow.wsShimSource, only when the window has a vyred) by one that asks the app to open the stream: `Host/BoxSocket.swift` speaks WebSocket (RFC 6455: the upgrade, masked client frames, ping and close, fragments) over vyred's unix socket as the capsule caller, only for stream routes (`isStreamPath`), and hands each text or binary message back through `window.__vyreWS`. Addresses other than vyreapp://box (or ws://box) keep the real WebSocket. Tests: Tests/BoxSocketTests.swift (the RFC's accept key and frame examples, fragments, long lengths, broken streams, the path rule, the shim's pieces). Typechecked, not run: CI runs the suite; a stream in the real window is unseen.
- feat(app): Android feel. A row press on Android is the system ripple (`PressableScale` rippleColor, `pressFeel` in ui/motion/logic.js, tested): no scale spring and no pressed fill there, as Material rows have; other platforms are unchanged. `android.predictiveBackGestureEnabled` is on in app.json, so Android 13 and later show the system's predictive back animation (a no-op on the Note 10+'s Android 12). The tab-bar indicator pill (64 x 32) and the first row's 8 pt under the status bar were already in Shell.tsx. Not device-checked.
- refactor(wink): the Vyre code's decoder moved out of deck/ to `lib/wink-code/` (decode-core2.js and its test, payload.js, rs.js, geometry.js), so the phone's camera reader, the Deck, the Wink page and the renderer import one copy while deck/ is deleted. The Deck's imports follow (scan-worker, avatars, the renderer's geometry, the browser scan test and the decode harness), the daemon serves the four files at /lib/wink-code/ (DECK_LIBS), sw.js and shell-hashes.mjs list them there, and the app's page build and drawn-code source read them from lib. app-design's vendored copies of payload.js and rs.js in deck/vendor/vyrecode are separate and untouched.
- fix(app): three phone copy leaks (SPEC-AUDIT-ui-apps section 5): Add a device no longer lists "A server" ("Another computer", "One that stays on, to take heavy work."), the add-by-code card no longer says "Run the installer on the server" ("It shows a code when it is ready. Scan it, or paste the long code.") or "Asking the server" ("Asking your Vyre."), and the empty Devices list says "No devices paired yet."
- feat(app): the Wink camera reader for the phone, groundwork (the camera stays off, CAMERA_SCAN is false, until the box side is confirmed). `src/native/WinkScan.native.tsx` runs the Deck's own decoder (deck/vyrecode: geometry, Reed-Solomon, payload, decode-core2) in the system WebView on a generated page (`scripts/build-wink-scan.mjs` makes `wink-scan-page.generated.js`; the test fails when it is out of date): the page opens the back camera, grabs a square frame every 350 ms, a worker runs the rotation, scale and perspective search, and a frame that decodes posts the 8-byte ticket to the app once. In a WebView because an attempt is 1 to 2 s of JIT work, ten times that in Hermes; one decoder for phones and browsers. `wink-scan-model.ts` reads the page's four messages (only a ticket of exactly eight bytes) and holds the plain words for a refused camera and a slow read. react-native-webview was already a dependency.
- fix(app): the app's version now follows the release bump. scripts/bump-version.mjs moves package.json, the lockfile and the plugin manifest but not apps/app/app.json, so an app built after a bump would still say the old version. `app.config.js` now reads the repo's package.json: the iOS short version is the dotted number (no `-rc.1`), the Android name is the full version, and the iOS build number and Android versionCode are one integer that rises with the release and puts a release candidate below its release (apps/app/scripts/app-version.cjs, tested). app.json's version is a placeholder.
- chore(app): the phone app's version is 0.2.9 (apps/app/app.json), so the sideload builds report it.
- fix(app): the Vault's Held-fields reveal asks the box for `records.reveal` through the app's own call (the passkey, or the phone's yes), as the vault reveal does, instead of passing the Deck's simulated proof, which never worked on a real box.
- feat(app): Find takes the arrow keys on the web (Down and Up move through the rows, Enter opens the highlighted one, Up from the first goes back to the box) and adds `mentions.search` as sections after memory: vault names, Drive, artifacts and GitHub, names only, with a note for a provider that was late.
- feat(app): Find on every device (parity row 13), at /u/search and as a Cmd-K command bar (`FindHost`, `openFind()` in screens/find, for the shell to mount): one box over chats (names, then what Recall found in them), projects, people (assistants and Contact records), other records, Go-to places, files (files.search, with a preview) and memory (memory.relevant), the p, t and u prefixes, and Enter runs the line the way the Deck's Find does (`@agent` asks it, `tell <chat> to ...` types into it and watches it, `watch <chat>` watches it, anything else asks the assistant and opens the thread). A sealed field is never searched. The grammar, prefixes and session merge are the Deck's own modules. Logic tests in screens/find (12 pass on testbox2). No arrow-key row selection yet.
- feat(app): Glass in the web app (parity row 8; web only for 0.2.9, phone and Mac in 0.3.1), at /u/glass/<agent> (and /u/glass/box for files): watch an agent's computer live, take over the keyboard or sign in privately, hand back with a note, and a Files tab (list, preview, download, upload with progress, new folder, rename or move, trash). The picture is the Deck's vendored noVNC in an iframe page (src/glass/frame.js, copied with it to public/glass/ by `scripts/glass-assets.mjs`, run by `export:web`), with the Deck's rules: view only unless this surface holds the keyboard, fewer frames over a relay or a slow link, reconnect at 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s, pause while the tab is hidden and keep the last frame. The Glass mini card opens it on the web. On a phone or the Mac app the route says Glass is in the web app. Logic tests in screens/glass (11 pass on testbox2). Not yet seen in a real browser: no browser on the test box.
- feat(app): Connections follows connectors-029's connect answers: a token step carries the vendor's guide (steps and https links), and the OAuth-client step carries its guide, redirect and the two fields, so the app can be typed in directly (`connectors.connect { app }`) or picked from the vault (`client`). Removes the unused `clearClipboard` source call from Vault.
- feat(app): Connections in the app (parity row 5), at Settings, Connections (/u/connections): Add (the connector catalog with who can use it, the vendor sign-in with a paste box for another browser, token and OAuth-client steps; the one Google sign-in for Gmail and Calendar is the catalog's own `google-api` preset, so it needs no special case), MCP servers (add, test, restart, remove, per-tool Read, Held or Off), Google accounts (Sign in with Google, service account, refresh-token item, scope test), GitHub (device code or a pasted token, a shared repo picker `RepoPicker` for Projects to use) and Access (which surfaces may use each connection, Agents grants asking for the person). A typed token goes to the box once and any echo of it is masked. Nothing polls except while a sign-in is open. Logic tests in screens/connections (13 pass on testbox2).
- feat(app): Vault in the app has the Deck's other pages (parity row 6). - feat(names): the old 72-hour recovery rebind is removed (0.2.9, gap A10); instant recovery (the identity's own chain) is the only path. - feat(records,kernel,app): objects layer, items 10 to 13 of the 0.2.9 platform gaps. (10) A field takes `visible_if` and `required_if`, Expressions over the record's other stored fields: the language (`defineField.*({ visible_if, required_if })`, checked and printed back), the gateway (`field_not_shown` when a value is written to a field the record does not show, `field_required` when a visible required_if field is left empty; a create is judged whole, an update only where it touches the field or what its condition reads) and the record page (hidden fields are not listed, a required empty one shows a Required chip and cannot be saved empty). (11) A type stores its `views` (list, board, calendar, columns, grouping, sort, filter), validated by `records.define`; `viewDefOf` lays the first stored view of each kind over deck/ui/view-defs.js, which stays as the default for a type that stores none; a Kit's views are folded into the type they show when the Kit is installed (the Kit's own list stays for the install card); list, board and calendar apply a view's filter. (12) A `base` Kit in the library: Contact, Lead, Appointment, Client, Subscriber, Project; Lead, Client and Subscriber are roles linked to the one Contact; practice area is a choice. (13) A stage takes `enter_if` and a type takes `stage_sets` (`defineStage([...], { sets: [{ name, when, stages }] })`): the first set whose `when` holds gives that record's stages, the default stages otherwise. The gateway refuses a stage outside the record's set (`stage_not_in_set`) and an entry whose condition fails (`stage_entry_refused`); kernel/flows/stages.js advances along the record's own set and holds a record whose next stage cannot yet be entered. One new module, kernel/expr/conditions.js, is the single judge for the gateway, the stage module and the app. No new permission, log, table or runner.

- feat(wink): the built-in network runs for real. `core/wink/netd.js` is started by the wink module on a server home: a supervised Headscale (loopback only), the gate in front of it, the Wink node (wink-forwarder) joined to it, and the node host's door answering peers as `device:<eid>` through the peer door's new `serve` (core/daemon/peer-door.js: the relay row is read on every call, the kernel's chain records the path as "wink"). Deny-by-default policy from control/policy.js: the home is the hub, every other node reaches the door port and nothing else. It never blocks the module's start; a failed piece is retried every 30 s and the relay carries everything meanwhile. State is plain: `off`, `no-binary`, `starting`, `up`, `failed` (with a reason), read by `wink.network.status` through the node host; `wink.controlUrl` in the config names a public control address (the gate then listens on every interface and a pairing is handed a one-time join key), `wink.network: false` or `VYRE_WINK_NET=0` turns it off. The box image carries Headscale (pinned v0.29.4, sha256 per architecture) and wink-forwarder (built from `wink/forwarder` in a digest-pinned Go stage); no Tailscale product. Tests: `core/wink/netd.test.js` (fake engines), `test/box-wink-net.test.js`, and the real-binary `core/wink/netd.real.test.js` under `VYRE_WINK_REAL=1` on a test server.
- feat(relay): a self-hosted relay and name directory as one container. `relay/Dockerfile` (base pinned by digest, non-root, healthcheck, `/data` volume for the directory's one state file), `relay/compose.yml` (loopback ports, read-only root, caps dropped), `relay/README.md` (TLS in front), `relay/node/main.js` and `relay/node/directory.js` (names/worker's real code, no DNS published), `scripts/relay-roundtrip.mjs` (box registers a sealed pairing ticket, a device resolves it once). test/box-init.test.js now checks relay/Dockerfile's pin too.
- feat(wink): `core/wink/reach.js`, a reachability fallback for a home server behind NAT. The relay stays the first working path; in the background it tries a global IPv6 address, UPnP (SSDP and SOAP, lease, delete on stop) and NAT-PMP, refuses a router behind carrier-grade NAT, and calls the state "direct" only after an outside check reached the port. `relay/node/server.js` gains `POST /v1/reach/check` (dials only the caller's own public address, ports from 1024, rate limited) and `relayVerifier` calls it. Not yet called by the daemon (netd), and the hosted Cloudflare relay has no such endpoint.
