- fix(app): no fixed "5 minutes" about a code: the Mac's type-the-code help says the server shows how long it has left, and "Add your device" counts down from the box's own `code_expires`. The line to run on a server (Install, Add a device) is the release candidate's own `install-box.sh` line only when the bridge gives a version with a hyphen (`window.__vyreShell.version`, "0.3.0-rc.1"); a plain "0.3.0", no version, or anything that is not a version gets the stable `curl -fsSL vyre.run/i | sh` (first-run.js installLine).

- feat(app): the Mac window's boxless "On a server" (rows 4e and 4f of the prototype). When the bridge says `boxless` (`window.__vyreShell.boxless`, native-core), setup goes name > "Type the code your server shows" > "Type this on your server" (the ack, typing it there is the yes) > "Connected to your server" > "Add your phone". Three wrong tries end the code; an expired code and an unreachable server have their own sentences (screens/install/MacServer.tsx, copy and rules in first-run.js, over `joinWithCode`).

- feat(app): the browser's start screen has "Type the code" again, over `joinWithCode` (relay/client/join.js): the browser types the code the phone's Devices, Add a device screen shows, shows the ack to type on the phone, and keeps the pairing it gets. Adding this device to a name reads the identity's own Vyre name from the pairing (`identity.vyre`), not the box's name; the rules of it are tested with stubs (src/identity/add-device-core.js: the name is kept only when the list holds the key; a wrong ack, a timeout and an enrolment failure keep nothing).

- feat(app): adding this device to a name from another device now works (it was a not_built stub). src/identity/add-device.ts makes this device's key, redeems the QR, long code or typed code over the relay (relay/client/phonepair.js addThisDevice), shows the three words for a long code or the ack for a typed one, and keeps the name only once the names directory's list holds this device's key; the pairing is kept too, so Now has a box. The "Add this phone from another device" step has the paste/scan entry and a "Type the code" field. Not yet run end to end: the showing device's wink.phone.open needs a proof the awbox stand-in does not give.

- fix(app): a device with no box of its own types an invite code through the client library, not a box tool (platform-3's ruling): Join a space calls `redeemInviteCode` (relay/client/join.js) at the relay (EXPO_PUBLIC_VYRE_RELAY, else wss://relay.vyre.run), shows the ack to type on the inviting device, and carries on with the link it returns. The browser start screen no longer has a typed field: adding a browser or phone to an identity by typed code waits on wiring `addThisDevice` (relay/client/phonepair.js), which the app still stubs as not built.

- feat(app): typing a short Wink code. parseWinkCode accepts WINK-NNPP-PPPP (any case, dashes optional) as a typed code. A "Type the code" field (screens/devices/TypeCode.tsx) on the browser's start screen and on Join a space calls wink.code.redeem, shows the code to type back on the other device, polls wink.pair.status, and carries on when it says done (an invitation's link is accepted as a pasted one is). The showing screens (Add your device, an invitation) show the typed code under the Wink code with a countdown, and an "enter the code the other device shows" field that calls wink.code.ack. The typed line and the fields appear only when the box returns a code.

- feat(flows): the `extract` AI step. It reads named fields (`fields: [{ name, kind: text|number|date|boolean, description? }]`, 1 to 20) out of a message or document through the same model door as classify (sealed values placeholders, no tools, the per-run and per-Space AI budget), asks the model for one JSON object, and returns exactly the declared fields in their kinds (`steps.<id>.fields.<name>`), null where the text did not say or the value is not that kind, plus `found` and `raw_ok`. It is a model step on the approval card and in the canvas and SDK.
- fix(flows): SW-1, a 503 on a write whose connector takes no idempotency key is never sent again (it may have been done): the run stops with `outcome_unknown` and the owner gets a card; a 429, a read, and a write with a key still wait out the Retry-After and go again.
- feat(work): how much of the record's world an agent is shown is a setting of each Space (kept with that Space's Flows, set by an owner or admin with `flows.budget { context_tokens }`, default 1,200, 200 to 8,000; the AI daily budget is per Space too), and a call or a task (`form.context_tokens`) can ask for more, within the ceiling.
- feat(work): an agent doing a task gets the record's world (item 14). `work.situation` with `context: true`, or with a `task` (the task names the record), adds the records the record links to, the records that link to it, recent communications on it and with the contacts on it (through the participant records), and what happened to it lately (core/work/native/context.js), in its own 1,200-token budget so the 400-token situation is unchanged. Everything is read under the agent's own chain: a sealed field is its placeholder, a message's text is only in the quoted data block, and a shared room never gets it.
- feat(flows): best-suited doer (item 15). An `assign` or `agent` step may name `pool:<name>` as well as a role, and `skills: [...]`. The runner chooses (kernel/flows/assign.js): candidates with every skill asked, then the most tasks already given on this record, then the lightest open load, then the order given; the choice and its reason are on the task (`form.chosen`), the step's output (`chosen`) and a `step.assigned` event. A pool is the team members whose `role` is its name; a team member has a new `skills` field. A role keeps its other holders as helpers. Nobody fitting is a plain `nobody` failure.
- fix(flows): FS-1, a Code step's memory is capped as a whole: on Linux the sandboxed command runs under `ulimit -v` (1.5 GB of address space) as well as the heap flag, so a step allocating 1 GB of Buffers fails with `failed` and the next step still runs.
- feat(flows): AI steps are metered (FS-2). A classify step passes `max_tokens`, is cut to 16,000 characters, and counts what it spent against a per-run allowance (20,000 tokens), and a Space's daily allowance (200,000 by default; an owner or admin sets it with the tool `flows.budget { tokens_per_day }`, 0 turns AI steps off; stored in the Flow schedule records, no new table). Past either the step fails with code `ai_budget` and "This space's AI budget for today is used up".
- fix(kernel): `fn.run` and `model.call` are a Flow run's alone (authorize answers `runner_only` to any chain without a run's automation hop, owner included); a run needs only `flows.run` of its approver. Members hold `flows.run` and `ask.request`; admins and owners also `service.read` and `service.call`.
- feat(flows): the service step reads the connector declaration as the Connectors work defines it (`ops` with `outward`, `read`, `idempotent`, `readback { method, path, vars, compare }`; `idempotency { header }`; `rate`): outward comes from the matching operation's own flag (a draft operation that writes is not outward), the vault adds the provider's idempotency header from the run's key, a `rate_limited` answer with `retryAfter` puts the run to sleep and it sends again with the same key, and a draft sends `{ [wrap]: body }` when the connector's draft says `wrap`. The runner has no limiter of its own.
- feat(flows): safe outside writes, built into the step runner (kernel/flows/runner.js `#service`, kernel/flows/safe-write.js), not into any Kit. From the connector's declaration (`ops`, `rate` on the catalog entry; a connector that declares neither behaves as before): a write carries an opaque, stable provider idempotency key in the header or parameter the operation names, and the ledger holds the key, the attempt and `sent_at` before the call; an operation that pairs a read-back reads the record again and compares the paired fields, and a mismatch fails the run with `readback_mismatch`, pauses the Flow and puts a card in front of the owner; a per-connector `rate.per_min` makes the run sleep (suspended in the ledger, woken by the clock, surviving a restart) instead of calling; a 429 or 503 with Retry-After is waited out and sent again with the same key. After a crash the ledger decides: a finished write is never sent again (only its read-back is made); a write that may have gone out is sent again with the same key where the provider takes one, and otherwise is not sent, fails with `outcome_unknown` and tells the owner, and a person's retry of the run says go.
- feat(flows): a Code step runs in a real vyred. The daemon passes Flows a sandbox port (kernel/flows/code-sandbox.js): one OS-sandboxed process per call built from the module sandbox's own command line (no network, no files, no child process, no environment), declared inputs and outputs, a wall-clock limit that kills it and a heap cap, refused unless the supervisor's self-test proved the sandbox on this machine. A declared `needs` power is refused, never granted. Proven in a real daemon: a date computed from record fields; a loop that never ends is stopped and the run fails with code `timeout`.
- feat(flows): a classify step uses the kernel's model door (`gateway.model`) in a real vyred, so sealed values reach the model only as placeholders and the step offers no tools; with no door the run fails with "this home has no model door". A port's own failure (sandbox timeout, a door refusal) now keeps its code on the run instead of `error`.
- fix(kernel): `flows.run`, `ask.request`, `fn.run` and `model.call` were registered only by the Flow test harness, so in a real daemon a manual start and every ask, Code and classify step answered `unknown_action`, and no role held `service.read` or `service.call`. They are now registered with the other grant actions; a member holds the four Flow ones, an admin and an owner also the two service ones (roles-enforced updated).
- fix(flows): the watcher bridge never fired in a real daemon. The module bus hands a listener the whole event, and the bridge read `name` and `items` off it, so `watcher.fired` was ignored (the fake-port tests hid it). The module now hands the bridge the payload. Proven with a real watcher process, a real daemon and one run per item (test/flows-gaps-daemon.test.js).
- fix(calendar): the held card for a calendar write says everything that will be sent (title, start and end, who is invited, place, a digest of the body) and the task records the bind of the exact request; an event edited while its change waits is asked about again, so an old yes cannot send a new body (reviewer-3 CC-1). fix(vault): a connector's idempotency header may not be Authorization, Cookie, Host, X-Api-Key, proxy-*, Content-Type or If-Match (CC-2).
- feat(calendar): the Space's calendar sync runs for real and by default (core/daemon/calendar-sync.js, started for every Space with the Flows host): every five minutes it finds a calendar connector in the vault by its declared ops, pulls outside changes into Event records and pushes Vyre's own, on the connector declaration (records/calendar/sync.js now speaks events.list, events.insert, events.patch). A write to the outside calendar is outward: the kernel asks, a task goes to the owner, nothing is sent until they say yes, and then it goes out once with that approval and its bind; a Space rule that refuses is a refusal; a no is final for that change. The owner's decision is acted on at once: the decided task's event starts a look, so an approved change goes out right away. A new event carries an id derived from its record so a repeat after a crash reads the event that is there. Every Space now defines the core types (contact, organization, communication, event ...).
- feat(connectors): one Google sign-in covers Gmail and Calendar. A credential may name several hosts and each service route says which host it is on (vault `service.allow[].host`); declarations that sign in the same way merge into one credential (`mergedCredentialConfig`), and the catalog offers one `google-api` preset with both sets of scopes, saying "Vyre can write drafts; sending asks you first". `connectors.declare` takes `also` to share one credential.
- feat(connectors): `connectors.declared` lists the shipped declarations (ops with their outward flags, polls, whether a credential is installed); `connectors.declare` (a person's own, never a model) makes the vault credential from one with a key, a service account (subject and key item) or an OAuth app; `connectors.logging` returns the recipe for logging one mailbox or calendar (the watcher input for `watchers.preset` and the stored Flow for `flows.define`) and writes nothing. Each OAuth declaration also appears in the catalog as an api preset (`gmail-api`, `google-calendar-api`) whose sign-in makes a credential carrying the declaration's endpoint classes, rate and service rules, so it is a connector for Flows and watchers. `watchers.preset` takes `kind: "connector"`.
- feat(connectors): a connector is a declaration (records/connectors/format.js): base url, auth, rate with retry-after, an idempotency header, and ops with input and output shapes, a kind (read, draft, change, send, spend, delete) that alone decides "outward", a read-back pairing, polls and an inbound webhook. `toCredentialConfig` makes the vault's api-credential from it and `buildRequest`, `parseResponse`, `readbackRequest` and `compareReadback` check one op. Stripe moves onto it (its webhook events come from the declaration); Gmail (drafts are not outward, send is) and Google Calendar ship as declarations beside it. The vault's connector `service` block now carries draft, idempotency, rate and ops to the Flow step runner, and an outward call through a connector that declares an idempotency header sends one derived from the call's idem key (platform gaps item 5).
- feat(watchers): a `connector` preset polls any declaration's read op with one generic loop and no per-service code (item 7): list since the last look, read each item's record when the poll says to, map it, file it once by its own id. Items carry the mapped fields (comm_kind, source_key, people ...) so a Flow reads them as trigger.item. `watcher.json` takes `memory: false` to file items without teaching them to Memory.
- feat(records): the default "Log communications" Flow (records/comms/log-flow.js), one per mailbox or calendar, in native steps: one Communication per item keyed on its source key, one Participant per person linked to the contact by main email, then by a further address, else kept bare (a switch makes the contact; another skips colleagues' domain). Our own sync through the vault, not Twenty's (item 6).
- feat(records): `records.roles` (what a contact or organization is to the Space) and `records.holders` (who holds a role, optionally at one stage) are tools over the gateway's calls of the same name, under the caller's own chain; listed as open reads in agent-reach, allow.json and the tool reference (platform gaps item 8).
- feat(kernel): the kernel is ON by default (KERNEL-default-on, branch work/kernel-default-on, not merged until the walk passes kernel-on). `VYRE_KERNEL=0` turns it off in a development build only; a packaged build ignores it, says so (one log line at start and a line in `vyre status`: "VYRE_KERNEL=0 is ignored: this build always runs with the kernel on") and keeps the kernel on (MA-5; a stray variable must not take a server down). package.json `files` gains `kernel` and `names/worker/chain.js` so a release ships them. The tripwire test core/memory/legacy-labels.test.js is deleted; the `SHIM(legacy labels)` branches stay for their owners to remove (assistant: core/memory; windows: core/spaces), because a call with no chain still reads its label there.
- test(wink): the owner's-phone card test asks its outward card for mail.send, a tool marked `outward: true`, in place of the made-up email.send that only the old verb pattern accepted.
- test(walk): the walk's paired-device helper builds its device row the way the daemon does (the relay's row plus the person Wink's record names), so a signed-in paired app device reaches bridges.merge.links as the person. Not a bridges bug: the check reads the call's kernel chain, and a paired device's chain is one person (core/daemon callerFacts); the test's row had no person, so no chain was built. publish.whoIs uses the same chain check and needs no change.
- feat(gateway-door): a refusal "not from a signed-in person" now logs why (the first hop the kernel built, whether person facts were proved, and, for a device, a hint to check its enrolment in the Space); the caller still gets the plain words. test/wink-paired.test.js adds the HTTP-over-relay case: the paired session's bearer and signed proof reach records.me and records.define as the person.

- fix(spaces): the home Space is its owner's by definition. `spaces.devices.enrolled` and the list a device is first enrolled with (`kernelSpacesOf`) no longer depend on the kernel's membership table naming the owner: a home whose table did not (awbox: the kernel owner was an identity the Space's grants never adopted) wrote an empty enrolment list for every new device, so the kernel gave a confirmed paired device no person chain and records.* answered "not from a signed-in person". Found by running app-wire's walk against a copy of awbox's home.

- test(wink): a typed-paired, acked device defines a record type (a real DefineDiff) over its own paired session and through the daemon's device facts (callerFacts), on the kernel; records.me answers the owner. Guards the one rule (a confirmed paired device is the person; a change of types needs no extra proof from it).

- feat(cli): `vyre phone` and `vyre relay pair` say, after a pairing by the relay's offer, "This device can't sign in as you until you confirm it from Devices." (that way of pairing has no owner confirmation; the typed code confirms the device itself). 0.3.1 moves them to the typed code and removes the offer path (team/BACKLOG.md).

- feat(app): New chat. Chats has a New chat button (header, and the empty state's action) that opens /new-chat: pick an agent (your assistant is the default), optionally a first message, Start chat. It calls threads.start as you, naming the agent, its kind and your default AI account (src/state/new-chat-model.js), and opens the new session. Codes: under the drawn Wink code the app shows the typed code large with "Type this code on your other device" when the box answers one (`code` on wink.phone.open and spaces.invites.create; neither returns it yet), and otherwise says to copy the link or paste the long code. It never says the drawing can be scanned.

- test(app): scripts/app-walk-firstrun.mjs walks the first-run screens in headless Chromium against a real vyred (browser start, welcome, Who it is for, the Wink codes, the empty states); the two proofs a headless page cannot give (wink.phone.open, and an invitation to a this-computer space) are answered by named stand-ins beside their steps. fix(app): the long code under the Add your device code wraps.
- fix(spaces): the home Space is its owner's by definition. `spaces.devices.enrolled` and the list a device is first enrolled with (`kernelSpacesOf`) no longer depend on the kernel's membership table naming the owner: a home whose table did not (awbox: the kernel owner was an identity the Space's grants never adopted) wrote an empty enrolment list for every new device, so the kernel gave a confirmed paired device no person chain and records.* answered "not from a signed-in person". Found by running app-wire's walk against a copy of awbox's home.

- test(wink): a typed-paired, acked device defines a record type (a real DefineDiff) over its own paired session and through the daemon's device facts (callerFacts), on the kernel; records.me answers the owner. Guards the one rule (a confirmed paired device is the person; a change of types needs no extra proof from it).

- feat(cli): `vyre phone` and `vyre relay pair` say, after a pairing by the relay's offer, "This device can't sign in as you until you confirm it from Devices." (that way of pairing has no owner confirmation; the typed code confirms the device itself). 0.3.1 moves them to the typed code and removes the offer path (team/BACKLOG.md).

- feat(wink): a device paired by the typed code can open a person session. `wink.code.ack` is a pair yes moment (it takes the owner's software yes on a development build, like wink.phone.open), the owner's typed-back ack is the confirmation the paired session is granted on (the record is confirmed by the owner, with a key id `ack:<offer>`), and `addThisDevice({ ..., presenceKey })` reports the device's P-256 presence key at pairing: that key, never the Ed25519 identity key, signs presence.person.start-paired. test/wink-paired.test.js covers typed pair, signed ack, start-paired and a person-session call.

- feat(wink): `wink.phone.wait` answers `identity: { id, vyre? }` once the yes is done, and `addThisDevice` returns it, so a device that joined an identity reads its list by the identity's own name; `name` stays the other device's (box) name.

- feat(wink): a browser with no box pairs to a server by the code the phone's Devices screen shows, with the existing `joinWithCode({ relay, input, name, onState, pairOptions: { crypto, keyStore, about: { kind: "web" } } })` (relay/client/join.js); a test covers it. wink.code.ack no longer says "Development only" (reviewer-3 TY-2).

- feat(wink): a device with no box of its own uses the typed code through the client library, with no tool to call. `addThisDevice({ code, relay, key, onAck })` (relay/client/phonepair.js) adds this device to an identity from the code the other device shows, and `redeemInviteCode({ relay, input, onAck })` (relay/client/join.js) takes an invitation's code out to its link for the join page or spaces.invites.accept. Both run the code's PAKE over the relay and show the ack to type back. A phone that came in by the typed code is confirmed by the code itself: the ticket is gated like the QR's, the ack typed back on the computer is the yes (no three words), and the identity list takes the key through the same wink.phone.wait step. The tool `wink.code.redeem for: "phone"` follows the same path through this app's own box.

- feat(wink): the typed WINK-NNPP-PPPP code works on a release build (RC1, user ruling 5 Oct 2026). A code lasts 10 minutes (the relay's rendezvous too), is single use, and closes after 3 wrong tries (a fresh one replaces it); the ack typed back stays one try and a yes moment. `wink.phone.open` returns `code`, `code_expires`, `code_offer` beside the QR (either one ends the other), and `spaces.invites.create` returns the same three for its link through the new internal `wink.code.carry`: the link rides the ticket's sealed record after the ack, and `wink.code.redeem` (typing side, `for: invite` by default, or phone, server, storage) shows the ack and `wink.pair.status` ends `done` with `invite.link` for the usual `spaces.invites.accept`. The old development flag only decides whether the install flow shows a typed code in place of the QR; `wink.typedCode: false` (or VYRE_WINK_TYPED_CODE=0) is the kill switch. The cryptography is still unreviewed outside: copy must say CPace from the IETF draft on audited primitives, not audited. The live relay needs the 10 minute rendezvous deployed (until then a code lasts 5 minutes).
- feat(one-yes): relay.enable, relay.pair.start and wink.phone.open take a proof signed over the call itself, through yes() (lib/one-yes.js), instead of widening the development stand-in. `x-vyre-presence: yes proof=<base64url>` carries the owner key's proof for the act and fields signOf gives the call, checked in the home owner's chain by the sealing process; a software key stands on a development build only, a release build answers software_key and nothing runs; a proof is single use and covers exactly that tool and input. The three tools are in MOMENT_OPS.pair. `node scripts/dev-sign-proof.mjs --home <dir> --yes pair --tool wink.phone.open --input '{}' --header` signs one for a test or a headless walk. test/one-yes-tool-proof.test.js covers both builds.
- test(wink): the owner's-phone card test asks its outward card for mail.send, a tool marked `outward: true`, in place of the made-up email.send that only the old verb pattern accepted.

- test(one-yes): an `outward: true` tool on reach hook or modules is held for a hook caller, a module with no person behind it and a module acting for an agent, and never runs; a module acting for you runs it (reviewer-3 OW-5).
- chore(app): the sideload iPhone build is kept at apps/app/dist-ios/Vyre.app (gitignored) after install, so a locked phone does not cost a rebuild.
- feat(app): a phone's connect step offers `TypeCode kind="phone"` (app-wire's typed-code field, the box side is platform-3's wink.code.redeem) under the pasted code, above "I don't have Vyre running yet". A finished typing goes to the spaces step.
- test(app): `src/identity/restore-store.test.js`: recovery asks the store it was handed (a phone-store stand-in refuses a second name before any directory call), and the root layout wires `./store` (the platform file), not `./store.ts`. Run with restore.test.js on the full repo on testbox3.
- test(app): the phone's connect screen has tests (screens/install/phone-novyre.test.js): no camera view in RC1 (`CAMERA_SCAN` is now in first-run.js and guards PairEntry's permission request, camera and permission line), "I don't have Vyre running yet" only on a phone (`offersNoVyre`), the share text is the setup link with no install command, and the step shares it through the system share sheet with "Not now" keeping the skip flag then opening the landing.
- fix(app): recovering a name on a phone now reads and writes the phone's identity store. restore.ts named the web store (IndexedDB) explicitly so its Node test could load it, so on a phone the recovery never touched the Keychain. It now holds a swappable store (`useIdentityStore`), and `src/identity/restore-wire.ts`, imported by the root layout, hands it the platform's `./store` (store.native.ts on a phone).
- feat(app): the phone's "I don't have Vyre running yet" (step `novyre`, copy NO_VYRE): "Send me the setup link" opens the share sheet, "Not now" keeps a `vyre.setup.skipped` flag and opens the not-connected landing (/u/now). The setup gate lets an unpaired phone with that flag see only /u routes, and still gates everything else. The scan step offers it on phones. RC1 pairing by camera is off (the drawn Wink avatar cannot be read yet, RC2): `PairEntry` shows no camera view, a code is typed or pasted. Still open: the typed short code (WINK-...) is refused by `parseWinkCode` until the box accepts it.
- fix(app): the Android build died at setup with "Cannot find native module 'ExpoCamera'". Metro tries the extensions in order and, for each, the platform file before the plain one, so `scan.ts` was found before `scan.android.tsx` and pulled in expo-camera (excluded from the Android build). `scan.android.tsx` is now `scan.android.ts`, and a test fails when a platform file uses a later extension than the plain file beside it.
- fix(app): a fresh install no longer opens an empty shell. `SetupGate` (src/shell, rules in setup-gate.js, tested) sends a phone with no pairing and no configured box address to the install flow (/u/install) from every route except setup, a pairing link and a join link, and re-reads the pairing on each route change so the shell opens once setup saves it. Now, Chats and Agents say one plain line with one action (Connecting to your server; Nothing needs you / Open Chats; No chats yet / Start with an agent; No agents yet / Open Chats) instead of blank. `ListRow` has an explicit full width: Places drew three chevrons and no rows on Android. The tan bar at the left edge in the phone screenshots is Samsung's Edge panel handle, not Vyre.
- fix(app): the same wrong-file import as the Android launch crash, in `src/pwa/pwa.web.ts` (fromB64url from "../auth/person" is person.web.ts on the web) and `src/auth/paired-key.native.ts` (derToP1363 and fromB64url from "./person" is person.native.ts on the phone): both name person.ts. `store.native.ts` gains `hadIdentity`. New test `src/platform-exports.test.js` fails when a file imports a name from a platform-split module (x.native.ts or x.web.ts beside it) that a variant does not export. Known and left: `src/identity/restore.ts` imports "./store.ts" explicitly (for its Node test), so on the phone the recover path reads the web store, not store.native.ts.

- fix(app): the Android RC1 release crashed on launch (`undefined is not a function` in nativeRandom). webcrypto.native.ts and relay.native.ts imported `fromB64url` from "../auth/person", which Metro resolves to person.native.ts on the phone, and that file exports no such function. Both now import the real source (presence-proof.js, person.ts). The webcrypto install is also wrapped so a broken random source logs and fails the identity calls instead of killing the app at launch.
- fix(daemon): the member hello refuses a device under 24 hours on the identity's list unless it founded the list (MB-2). fix(wink): a released server still reports owned and names its owner, and a different identity is refused with the owner's name and how to reset. feat(kernel): `seal.reveal` is held by the owner and the admin by role.

- fix(daemon): an open member stream re-checks the device's identity entry and the membership on every call and by a watcher, so a removed device or member is refused and its stream closed.

- feat(kernel/remote,records): `seal.reveal` crosses to the home with the person's proof for the home's challenge, so a device on a server-hosted space can reveal with a yes (needs a wired inference door and a reveal grant). fix(wink): a pairing that does not finish says why in the server's log; the home logs the reason of every non-presence refusal.

- feat(spaces): a call with no space named acts in the one space the person made; with two or more it answers `needs_space` and lists them. A member's stream reconnects with no error after the invitee channel's life (tested).

- feat(spaces,daemon,kernel): a person who joined a space on a server lists it and reaches it through a member stream to its home (the peer door admits a member only when the space's kernel says so); a sealed value from a device on a server-hosted space goes to the home's sealing process (`seal.put` over the wire). fix(spaces): creating a space on this computer asks for the person's yes first and makes nothing until it has it.

- fix(relay): a refused pairing says its reason in the log every time (the first five repeats in a minute as "refused again"), so a retry is no longer silent.

- feat(spaces): on a development build an invitee's accept is signed by the computer's own software key and enrols it on the server in the same call. fix(wink): a server removed and paired again no longer reuses the old relay connection (`forget`).
- feat(app): typing a short Wink code. parseWinkCode accepts WINK-NNPP-PPPP (any case, dashes optional) as a typed code. A "Type the code" field (screens/devices/TypeCode.tsx) on the browser's start screen and on Join a space calls wink.code.redeem, shows the code to type back on the other device, polls wink.pair.status, and carries on when it says done (an invitation's link is accepted as a pasted one is). The showing screens (Add your device, an invitation) show the typed code under the Wink code with a countdown, and an "enter the code the other device shows" field that calls wink.code.ack. The typed line and the fields appear only when the box returns a code.

- test(app): a stand-in phone for the walks. scripts/standin-phone.mjs lists approvals.pending as a second caller and answers yes (a software-key proof over the card's own `sign`, scripts/dev-sign-proof.mjs), no, or not at all; it is test-only and refuses on a release-kind build, and nothing in the app or daemon knows it. scripts/app-walk-approval.mjs runs the app's own ask code (heldAsk, askYes) against a real vyred with it: yes, no and (with --timeout) a card nobody answers. The enrolment recipe is in scripts/app-walk.README.md.

- feat(app): New chat. Chats has a New chat button (header, and the empty state's action) that opens /new-chat: pick an agent (your assistant is the default), optionally a first message, Start chat. It calls threads.start as you, naming the agent, its kind and your default AI account (src/state/new-chat-model.js), and opens the new session. Codes: under the drawn Wink code the app shows the typed code large with "Type this code on your other device" when the box answers one (`code` on wink.phone.open and spaces.invites.create; neither returns it yet), and otherwise says to copy the link or paste the long code. It never says the drawing can be scanned.

- test(app): scripts/app-walk-firstrun.mjs walks the first-run screens in headless Chromium against a real vyred (browser start, welcome, Who it is for, the Wink codes, the empty states); the two proofs a headless page cannot give (wink.phone.open, and an invitation to a this-computer space) are answered by named stand-ins beside their steps. fix(app): the long code under the Add your device code wraps.
- test(team): core/team/team.test.js (about 118 s alone, the 300 s per-file limit on a loaded box) is split into four files by topic (team, team-roles, team-worktree, team-merge) over one shared team-fixture.js. All 60 tests and every assertion are unchanged; the longest part runs in about 30 s.

- test(one-yes): an `outward: true` tool on reach hook or modules is held for a hook caller, a module with no person behind it and a module acting for an agent, and never runs; a module acting for you runs it (reviewer-3 OW-5).
- feat(wink): the typed WINK-NNPP-PPPP code works on a release build (RC1, user ruling 5 Oct 2026). A code lasts 10 minutes (the relay's rendezvous too), is single use, and closes after 3 wrong tries (a fresh one replaces it); the ack typed back stays one try and a yes moment. `wink.phone.open` returns `code`, `code_expires`, `code_offer` beside the QR (either one ends the other), and `spaces.invites.create` returns the same three for its link through the new internal `wink.code.carry`: the link rides the ticket's sealed record after the ack, and `wink.code.redeem` (typing side, `for: invite` by default, or phone, server, storage) shows the ack and `wink.pair.status` ends `done` with `invite.link` for the usual `spaces.invites.accept`. The old development flag only decides whether the install flow shows a typed code in place of the QR; `wink.typedCode: false` (or VYRE_WINK_TYPED_CODE=0) is the kill switch. The cryptography is still unreviewed outside: copy must say CPace from the IETF draft on audited primitives, not audited. The live relay needs the 10 minute rendezvous deployed (until then a code lasts 5 minutes).

- feat(one-yes): a non-person call to a tool marked `outward: true` is held as a card in the approvals queue (`approvals.hold`, registry only) and runs only when it is retried with the card the person's phone answered, bound to the asker and a digest of the exact input. A tool that already holds agents through its own ask flow says `asks: true` and test/outward-flags.test.js names the test that proves it; for RC1 these keep their flow: publish approve, publish, rollback and secret grant, github PR open, merge and review, google send and calendar writes, apps.send, the vault forward and send tools. More tools marked outward: artifacts.public.set, files.drive.url and offer, files.deliver, bridges.kit.export, hooks.open, github.session.pr, vault.pass.create, spaces.invites.create, spaces.members.add. The module SDK reads `asks`.

- refactor(one-yes): lib/one-yes.js has no verb pattern for the outward moment: momentOf and opFitsMoment take the registry's `isOutward` (the module.json flag), so the card queue, the registry floor and the moment code share one source.

- feat(one-yes): every outward tool says so with `outward: true` in its module.json (mail, Drive share and upload, PR merge and review, git push, publish, vault forward and send, invites and transfers, apps.send). The outward moment (the phone card in core/presence) is now any tool the registry marks outward, in place of a verb pattern; `ctx.modules.isOutward(tool)` is the one read. The plain mark is valid in the SDK schema and manifest check for any reach. The registry's fail-closed hold still applies to the older kind words only, so a marked tool keeps its own held flow for agents. test/outward-flags.test.js fails on any tool with an outward verb that is neither marked nor listed with a reason.
- feat(app): the phone's "I don't have Vyre running yet" (step `novyre`, copy NO_VYRE): "Send me the setup link" opens the share sheet, "Not now" keeps a `vyre.setup.skipped` flag and opens the not-connected landing (/u/now). The setup gate lets an unpaired phone with that flag see only /u routes, and still gates everything else. The scan step offers it on phones. RC1 pairing by camera is off (the drawn Wink avatar cannot be read yet, RC2): `PairEntry` shows no camera view, a code is typed or pasted. Still open: the typed short code (WINK-...) is refused by `parseWinkCode` until the box accepts it.
- fix(app): the Android build died at setup with "Cannot find native module 'ExpoCamera'". Metro tries the extensions in order and, for each, the platform file before the plain one, so `scan.ts` was found before `scan.android.tsx` and pulled in expo-camera (excluded from the Android build). `scan.android.tsx` is now `scan.android.ts`, and a test fails when a platform file uses a later extension than the plain file beside it.
- fix(app): a fresh install no longer opens an empty shell. `SetupGate` (src/shell, rules in setup-gate.js, tested) sends a phone with no pairing and no configured box address to the install flow (/u/install) from every route except setup, a pairing link and a join link, and re-reads the pairing on each route change so the shell opens once setup saves it. Now, Chats and Agents say one plain line with one action (Connecting to your server; Nothing needs you / Open Chats; No chats yet / Start with an agent; No agents yet / Open Chats) instead of blank. `ListRow` has an explicit full width: Places drew three chevrons and no rows on Android. The tan bar at the left edge in the phone screenshots is Samsung's Edge panel handle, not Vyre.
- fix(app): the same wrong-file import as the Android launch crash, in `src/pwa/pwa.web.ts` (fromB64url from "../auth/person" is person.web.ts on the web) and `src/auth/paired-key.native.ts` (derToP1363 and fromB64url from "./person" is person.native.ts on the phone): both name person.ts. `store.native.ts` gains `hadIdentity`. New test `src/platform-exports.test.js` fails when a file imports a name from a platform-split module (x.native.ts or x.web.ts beside it) that a variant does not export. Known and left: `src/identity/restore.ts` imports "./store.ts" explicitly (for its Node test), so on the phone the recover path reads the web store, not store.native.ts.

- fix(app): the Android RC1 release crashed on launch (`undefined is not a function` in nativeRandom). webcrypto.native.ts and relay.native.ts imported `fromB64url` from "../auth/person", which Metro resolves to person.native.ts on the phone, and that file exports no such function. Both now import the real source (presence-proof.js, person.ts). The webcrypto install is also wrapped so a broken random source logs and fails the identity calls instead of killing the app at launch.
- feat(app): no plain QR anywhere (ADR 0043). An invitation and the Mac's "Add your phone" show a Wink code (src/ui/WinkCode.tsx: the drawn avatar with its ring from the Deck's own renderer, unique per code, under its kind's words "Join <space>" or "Add your device"); a test fails if any screen imports a generic QR component. The browser screen reads "On your phone, open Vyre, then Devices, then Add a device, and scan or paste its code here." Invites keep "Copy link", and "Email it" opens the person's own mail app (a mailto on the web, the share sheet on a phone) with the link in it. Vyre sends nothing itself.

- feat(app): no blank landing screens. Now, Chats and Agents each say one thing and give one action when empty (src/ui/EmptyHere.tsx, copy in screens/install/first-run.js): what is missing on this device comes first (a phone or browser with no Vyre: "Not connected" with Scan the code; a Mac with no phone paired: "Nothing can approve yet" with Add your phone), then a box that has not answered ("Your Vyre has not answered yet", Try again), then the screen's own line. The Places sheet leads with the same row when something is missing. `Empty` (src/ui/Screen.tsx) takes a second line and an action.

- feat(app): first run per platform (team/0.3/DESIGN-first-run-per-platform.md). A phone or a Mac opens on a Welcome (one line, "Get started" or "I already have Vyre"); a browser opens on "Open Vyre on your phone" (scan or paste) with "Set up Vyre on a computer or server first" and an Open vyre.run button, no command. A Mac chooses "On this Mac" or "On a server" before it names the space, then "Add your phone" shows the phone's QR (drawn as a Wink code, see below) with Skip. A phone or browser never asks where a space lives: it makes it on the Vyre it is connected to. Creating a space asks "Who it is for" (a team, a client or just me); a space for one person skips the members step, and the answer rides in `spaces.setup.save` picks (core/spaces keeps `picks.who`). Pairing errors on a phone or browser no longer say "server" or "install line" (screens/install/first-run.js PHONE_SAY). New routes /u/install/phone and /u/install/connect are the actions of the empty states.
- fix(relay): a refused pairing says its reason in the log every time (the first five repeats in a minute as "refused again"), so a retry is no longer silent.

- feat(spaces): on a development build an invitee's accept is signed by the computer's own software key and enrols it on the server in the same call. fix(wink): a server removed and paired again no longer reuses the old relay connection (`forget`).

- feat(kernel,spaces,wink): pairing a computer as a server's owner enrols its presence key in the home's sealing process in the same call as the owner adoption (software keys only on a development build; a failure leaves the pairing as it was and says why). The owner's computer can then prove its own invites.

- feat(spaces): inviting to a space on a server is answered on the owner's computer with the person's own key. The home's one-use challenge is signed as a kernel proof carrying `home` and `challenge`: by a hardware signer a surface sets, or by a software key on a development build only (a release-kind build hands the call back as a request to sign). fix(kernel/remote): the challenge for `grants.invites.create` and `confirm` now says what to sign.

- fix(permissions): the unattended answer stays the ordinary `presence_required` (not `held`), to match what the apps are built to.
- fix(permissions): MO-1 each moment covers an explicit list of tools (`MOMENT_OPS` in lib/one-yes.js: pair: presence.enroll, link.pair.approve, wink.phone.pair.answer, wink.server.pair.answer, wink.pair.server; vault: reveal, copy, totp, inject, resolve, render; outward: the send/post/pay/publish/reply/forward verbs until the flagged list lands), never a prefix; a card, and an approval at the floor, exist only for those, and the phone's line is written from the op itself (`lineOfOp`), so a destructive tool is never shown under a harmless sentence. The sealer's `unattested` strength (a sideloaded iPhone, an Android phone) counts as real, never software. `approval` is reserved as the envelope key: a test fails if a new tool declares an input of that name (vault.service.forward and vault.device.join already do and are left alone by the registry). The registry's presence floor for the moments still falls back to the old proof check for an on-the-spot proof: legacy method proofs are not kernel proofs.
- feat(permissions): the retry of a moment tool. A device's call to a floor-bearing moment tool with neither a proof nor an approval is stopped by the ordinary `presence_required` (the apps' trigger to ask for a card with approvals.ask; the error `detail` now travels over the peer wire); the retry carries `approval: <id>` as an input field (or the header x-vyre-approval), spent once for the asking device. A "no" on a card counts only from the server's own screen or a device session of a real key; a software browser's no is ignored. test/reach-module-calls allowlists serverlink's approvals.ask / approvals.status (the device's own peer-wire session).
- feat(permissions): the three moments take an approval. The registry's presence floor accepts `approval` (a card id from core/approvals, carried by the header `x-vyre-approval` or beside a peer-door call, never in a tool's input) for a floor-bearing tool that is one of the moments (`momentOf`: vault.*, wink.*/presence.* for pairing, outward send/post/pay/publish): the call's plain input is the request, the asking device comes from the verified caller (mandatory: a redeem with no device spends nothing), the approval is spent once, and the old proof check is the fallback. `signOf` uses fixed keys with the request's fields nested (`{ what: op, fields }`), so no field can override the op, with a test; each moment is tested end to end on a real sealer (pair, vault, outward). The old per-tool presence floors remain as the other route.
- refactor(permissions): one card queue for every yes (design note 6e03707). The presence.person.session-ask / session-status / session-pending / session-answer tools are removed; a browser asks for a yes-moment through the existing approvals queue: `approvals.ask { moment, request }` (validated per moment, written by the server, with `sign` = exactly what the phone signs, space included), the phone's `approvals.answer` proof is verified and spent by yes() when it answers (no dry needed, no proof ever travels to the asker), `approvals.status` says approved with the approval id, and the asker's act spends the approval once (`yes(moment, request, { card })`). A device cannot answer its own card; a no counts only from a signed-in person session and holds the device ten minutes. The legacy approvals flow for grants and task decisions is unchanged. `lib/one-yes.js` is the shared helper (core/presence re-exports isYou, yes, configureYes, signOf). serverlink: askApproval / approvalStatus. The vault reveal, device pairing and outward-send sites do not read an approval yet, and the server does not run a held act itself.
- feat(permissions): the gate wiring. The daemon calls `configureYes` at kernel boot with the kernel's own presence verifier (the sealing process; the kernel handle now exposes `presence`): `yes(moment, request, proof)` checks a real-key proof over the act the sealer takes (`signOf`: pair, vault, outward map to `grant.pair_device`, `task.vault_use`, `task.outward_act` with the card's op and fields), once; a replay, another request and an unknown key are refused. A card the owner's phone approved is spent once by the asking device's act (`yes(..., { card })`): the phone's proof is verified and spent when it answers, `session-status` hands the browser the card id, never the proof, so nothing is replayed at the moment. Cards list `sign` (exactly what the phone signs). The gate keeps the kernel's `isExactlyPerson` (`isYou` on a chain is the same test, covered by a test). The existing per-tool presence floors for vault, pairing and outward sends are not rewired here.
- fix(presence): a paired device answers a card (yes or no) only from a session of a real key; a software session lists but cannot answer, so a compromised browser cannot hold the asker for ten minutes with a no.
- fix(presence): CD-2. A card's answer is checked when it is given: `session-answer` verifies its proof with `yes(..., { dry: true })` over the card's op and fields, so junk from any device is refused with the yes() reason and nothing is approved; `dry` tells the verifier to check without spending (the proof is spent where the act uses it).
- fix(presence): CD-1, the card always reaches the phone and only a real key can say yes. `presence.person.session-pending` is listed by any of the owner's paired sessions (the strength floor is gone); `presence.person.session-answer` counts only when its `proof` stands for `yes()` over the exact request the server wrote on the card (the kernel presence proof shape): a software key is refused `software_key` on a release build, a yes over another request is refused, and a refused answer approves nothing. Until the daemon calls `configureYes` with the sealing process's check, no answer stands.
- fix(presence): reviewer-3 OY-1 to OY-4, YY-1 to YY-3, reviewer-2 CD-1. A phone card shows this server's own name for the device and a line the server writes from a validated request (the asker's label is no longer accepted); the request must fit the moment (pair, vault, outward: op shape and plain fields); a second different card while one waits is refused `conflict`, the same card returns the same id; `session-answer` has no extra presence floor (the phone's signed yes on the card is the one prompt), needs the proof, and the asking device cannot answer its own card; a hardware-registered phone can list the cards. `yes()`: only `null` from the verifier means the proof stands, a result with no strength counts as software, and `isYou(meta)` is false when the call carries an agent or thread. test/reach-anyone.json: reasons for session-ask and session-status.
- refactor(presence): the strength words are two, `software` and `real` (core/presence/strengths.js; rows written with `enclave`, `enclave, unattested` or `passkey` read as real). The paths nothing calls any more are gone: the door's session port (`sessionOf` in kernel/remote/wink.js), the pairing-time proof strength record, the 12-hour cap parameters on sessions and grants (the unused cap_ms column stays).
- feat(presence): the one place permission is asked (DESIGN-one-yes). `core/presence` exports `isYou(subject)` (a chain of exactly one person, or lib/caller's verified person check on a call) and `yes(moment, request, proof)` (moment: pair | vault | outward; { ok } or a reason: no_proof, expired, replayed, wrong_request, software_key, unknown_key; software keys count only where the build takes them; nothing configured is refused), with `configureYes({ verify, softwareOk })` as the daemon's one wiring. core/presence/one-yes.js and its test.
- feat(permissions): one rule (ruling c328cd1, DESIGN-one-yes). A person caller (a chain of exactly one person: a paired device, the terminal, the Capsule, the app) does admin acts with no presence: kernel/core/authorize.js asks the session only of a chain with an agent or assistant in it. The peer door says "this is you" for a paired device and no longer consults session strength for admin acts (the SW-1 gating and the 12 h approval cap are removed). The sign-in ask path is now the card for the owner's phone, used only for the three moments (pair, vault, outward): `presence.person.session-ask { moment, request }`, `session-answer { id, yes, proof }`, the signed yes comes back once through `session-status`; it upgrades no session. Tests converted: kernel authorize policy, gateway define, drive restore, grants unlend, SERVER-HOSTED space, the paired-session and card tests.
- fix(runner,box): reviewer-3 LS-1/LS-2 on the transcript share and the probe. The probe skips Docker's embedded resolver only when ROOT owns the socket (a session's own process listening there is reported); `recover` in place checks, right before writing, that the folder is the pinned one, the file's real path is its own path, and the file's owner is its folder's owner, or writes nothing. Tests: ownserver.test.js, confine.test.js.
- feat(mac): capsule-mac also uploads Vyre.dmg (artifact Vyre-dmg-<sha>): `scripts/make-dmg.sh` puts Vyre.app beside an Applications shortcut with hdiutil, the same script a Mac runs locally. Self-signed only (no Developer ID, no notarization); the README install line says to right-click, then Open, the first time.

- fix(runner): after a kill a session in the packaged box did not resume ("No conversation found with session ID"): `recover` replaced the account's transcript with a renamed file owned by vyred, which the session's uid could neither read nor append to. A transcript owned by another uid is now rewritten IN PLACE (same file, truncated to the checkpoint); the spawner's `share` makes it group-readable AND group-writable (g+rw, that one file) so vyred can. Test: core/runner/ownserver.test.js (same inode, same content, no temp left). Hosted dev-owned run: turns 1 and 2 are sealed as the account uid; resume was the failing block.

- fix(relay,wink): a server that is owned:false but still held a paired device row refused a new pairing silently (walker). Every refused hello is now logged with its reason (`relay: refused a hello (...)`), and `wink.server.code` on an unowned server lets go of devices left by a pairing that never completed ownership (`relay.devices.clear-leftover`, Wink module only). Once owned, the first owner still wins. The relay tool asks `wink.server.owned` for itself and answers `owned` on an owned server, and refused-hello log lines collapse to one per reason per minute with a count of the repeats.
- feat(box): own-server sealing reads an account's transcript. Claude writes it 0600 in the account uid's HOME, so vyred (in the account's group) could not read it and no turn was sealed (hosted packaged-boot). New spawner op `share` (core/spawner/server.js, client `shareTranscript`): as that uid, `chmod g+r` on ONE file that is a .jsonl under the account's own <HOME>/.claude/projects, not a link, owned by the uid; never the folder, never world-readable, any other path or account refused. The daemon's ownserver-host asks for it before each seal; if it cannot, that turn is not sealed and the log says why. Test: core/spawner/spawner.test.js.

- fix(runner): the box confinement self-test also reports UDP listeners and abstract unix sockets (a session shares the box's network namespace; no file mode protects an abstract name) and now REFUSES any listener (TCP, UDP or abstract) that is not vyred's own, naming the port (reviewer-3 CF-5, CF-6): vyred's own are taken from its own socket descriptors (`ownListeners`), so a normal box never refuses. CI: the unit job installs bubblewrap (and lifts the Ubuntu user-namespace restriction) so the sandbox tests run instead of failing. test/boundaries: the daemon to spawner edge is frozen with its reason.

- fix(runner,sessions): own-server sealing found no transcript for a session in the packaged box: it ran as an account's uid and wrote its transcript in that account's HOME (<accounts home>/<uid>/.claude/projects), which `threads.own-transcript` never looked in, so no turn was sealed (found by the hosted packaged-boot run). Under the docker supervisor it now also looks in each account uid's folder by name (the accounts folder is entered, never listed).

- fix(box): the box agent's home belongs to the agent's own group (1001), not the /work group (1002): an account's session working under /work joined 1002 and could read it (found by the confinement self-test on the hosted box); vyred reads it through group 1001 (spawner groups), and the spawner moves an older volume.
- fix(runner): the box confinement self-test, reviewer-3 CF-1 to CF-4: a protected folder the session's uid can ENTER now counts as reached (the probe only tried read, write and list); the box's secrets folder, the spawner's folder and the key file are protected; the accounts folder is made 711 by the spawner and checked as "not listable"; EVERY project folder of the session is checked, not the first; and any TCP port something listens on in the box is reported (the session shares the box's network; the hosted run found one loopback listener that closes every connection and nobody has named yet), refused only where the box asks (`refuseListen`). "The wall" in the ruling is not probed (no firewall rule applies to session uids): it stays the container, the uid and the file modes. Tests: core/spawner/confine.test.js.
