- refactor(presence): the strength words are two, `software` and `real` (core/presence/strengths.js; rows written with `enclave`, `enclave, unattested` or `passkey` read as real). The paths nothing calls any more are gone: the door's session port (`sessionOf` in kernel/remote/wink.js), the pairing-time proof strength record, the 12-hour cap parameters on sessions and grants (the unused cap_ms column stays).
- feat(presence): the one place permission is asked (DESIGN-one-yes). `core/presence` exports `isYou(subject)` (a chain of exactly one person, or lib/caller's verified person check on a call) and `yes(moment, request, proof)` (moment: pair | vault | outward; { ok } or a reason: no_proof, expired, replayed, wrong_request, software_key, unknown_key; software keys count only where the build takes them; nothing configured is refused), with `configureYes({ verify, softwareOk })` as the daemon's one wiring. core/presence/one-yes.js and its test.
- feat(permissions): one rule (ruling c328cd1, DESIGN-one-yes). A person caller (a chain of exactly one person: a paired device, the terminal, the Capsule, the app) does admin acts with no presence: kernel/core/authorize.js asks the session only of a chain with an agent or assistant in it. The peer door says "this is you" for a paired device and no longer consults session strength for admin acts (the SW-1 gating and the 12 h approval cap are removed). The sign-in ask path is now the card for the owner's phone, used only for the three moments (pair, vault, outward): `presence.person.session-ask { moment, request }`, `session-answer { id, yes, proof }`, the signed yes comes back once through `session-status`; it upgrades no session. Tests converted: kernel authorize policy, gateway define, drive restore, grants unlend, SERVER-HOSTED space, the paired-session and card tests.
- fix(presence, wink): the enclave strength needs the entry to still stand. At a paired device's sign-in, wink (`wink.device.enclave-live`, presence module only) reads the identity's list from the directory (by the Vyre name recorded at pairing) and checks that the entry that held the device's enclave key still holds it; cached for 10 minutes. Entry gone, revoked or another key: the sign-in is software, the device is marked `needs_repair` and `wink.device-needs-repair` is emitted; a directory that cannot be reached is software for that sign-in only. Appended migrations: wink_devices.enclave_eid, vyre_name, needs_repair.
- fix(presence): the phone-approved sign-in (reviewer-3 SA-1 to SA-4). `presence.person.session-pending` is readable only by the owner's non-software session (or a person surface on the server); a device the owner declined cannot ask again for 10 minutes (`rate_limited`); ending a device's sessions clears its asks; the strength a phone approval gives lasts for that session, at most 12 hours (`presence_pair_grants.cap_ms`, appended migration), then the next sign-in asks again.
- fix(presence, wink): the strength is proven at each sign-in. `presence.person.start-paired` takes an optional `esig`, the `paired-start` message signed by the identity entry's enclave key (the point wink verified and recorded at pairing, `wink_devices.enclave_key`); when it verifies the session is `enclave, unattested`, otherwise the grant's strength stands (software, or what the owner's phone approved). A device key copied off a phone can no longer open an enclave-strength session. serverlink `startPaired` signs with `signEnclave` when the app provides it.
- fix(presence, wink): ST-1, a paired session's strength comes only from what the server verified. Wink records the strength of the owner proof that paired the device (`wink_devices.proof_strength`: "enclave, unattested" when the identity entry's enclave key signed it, else "software"); the app's own keyStorage claim decides nothing. The pairing grant carries that into the session's `strength` (the column memory-access added; one list of words in core/presence/strengths.js). A phone-approved sign-in takes the approving proof's strength ("passkey" or "enclave, unattested").
- feat(presence): the paired session carries its strength (`strength` column on presence_people and presence_pair_grants, an appended migration; "software", "enclave, unattested" or "passkey"; old rows read as software). A device that reported hardware key storage now opens a non-software session (the wink record reads `keyStorage`; setConfirmed's hardware flag no longer decides), and the sessions list shows the strength. New tool `presence.person.session-pending` lists the waiting sign-in asks for the owner's phone.
- feat(presence, wink): a paired session's strength comes from the key the device reported at pairing: an enclave or keystore key (`hardware`, accepted unattested for RC1) opens a session that is not software and counts as presence over the peer door on a release server; a software key opens a software one. A browser can ask the owner's phone to let it sign in: `presence.person.session-ask` / `session-status` from the browser (serverlink `askSignIn`, `signInStatus`), `presence.person.session-answer` from the owner's device with its presence proof; the next sign-in's session takes the approving proof's strength, once. The door logs the strength every time it passes a session.
- fix(wink): SW-1, a software-marked paired session is presence over the peer door only where the presence module takes software proofs (a development build behind VYRE_SEAL_SOFTWARE); on a release build it is refused needs_presence. The door passes `software: true` with the session so the chain shows it.
- fix(kernel, wink): a paired device's live presence session now reaches the kernel on the remote path, so admin acts such as records.define on a server-hosted space can pass from a paired device. The peer door asks the home on every call whether the device holds a live paired person session (`sessionOf` in kernel/remote/wink.js withKernelCall) and passes `session` in the peer only then; no session, or one revoked or expired, gives none. Nothing else loosens.
- refactor(presence,pluginagent): one strength vocabulary, core/presence/strengths.js (software, enclave, "enclave, unattested", passkey; isNotSoftware), used by presence.person.strength and pluginagent's phone revoke (reviewer-3 ST-2); `hardware` and `keystore` are gone (an attested key is `enclave`). The strength a row records must come from what the server verified, never an app's keyStorage claim (ST-1, wink-2's recording, gated by reviewer-3).
- fix(presence): a paired session made before strength was recorded fails closed (reviewer-3 PR-6): a new last migration adds presence_people.strength and marks every existing paired row software; strength() answers the recorded strength, else software for a paired row and the flag for any other; startPaired records its opening proof's strength (software or hardware from the grant today; wink-2 passes `enclave, unattested` or `passkey`). Such a device opens a fresh session to prove its key. Tests in core/presence/presence.test.js (the migration marks old paired rows; recorded strengths answer as recorded; an unrecorded paired row is software).
- fix(pluginagent,presence): a phone's revoke passes for every non-software session strength: hardware (attested), `enclave, unattested` (a sideloaded iPhone's enclave key or an Android keystore key, hardware on release per ruling 6410c6a), keystore, passkey (core/pluginagent PHONE_STRENGTHS); only software or an unknown session is refused up front. presence.person.strength answers a row's recorded `strength` when it has one (startPaired's, wink-2) and the older `software` flag otherwise. Note: today's paired sessions only carry that flag, and wink never sets it to hardware (nothing attests yet), so until startPaired records the strength a phone's revoke is refused as software. Also merged work/devbox and restored core/memory/plugin-agent-daemon.test.js (devbox removed it because the trunk lacks the held recall restriction this branch carries).
- test(reach): test/reach-module-calls fails if any file other than core/modules/index.js writes a `relayedBy` mark (reviewer-3's lint; nothing writes one now, the strength rule replaced it).
- fix(pluginagent,presence,agents): agents.delete is not widened (`device` is out of its callers again, and no relay mark): pluginagent.revoke from a paired phone relays the delete as the person's own surface ("local") only when the phone's session key was attested (new internal presence.person.strength, asked by pluginagent alone; hardware strength, the door's rule). A software-strength or unknown device is refused up front with `software_key` and a plain line, before the key is turned off, so the key stays on and the agent stands. Revoke deletes by the agent's id (agents rows carry `id`, agents.delete takes an optional one). Note: agents.delete's `deck` caller already admits an owner's device with a person session (not changed here).
- fix(agents): revoke deletes by the agent's id (reviewer-3 PR-4): agents rows carry `id` (agents.list shows it), agents.delete takes an optional `id` and answers not_found when the name now belongs to a different agent; pluginagent keeps the id it was given at grant (new appended migration). Tests core/pluginagent/revoke-relay.test.js.
- fix(relay-client): test/wink.test.js no longer outlives its tests (the hang the integrator saw). The 15 s answer timers in `addThisDevice` and `pairServer` are cleared when the call answers, and a Connection's pause between tries no longer keeps a Node process alive by itself (an open socket still does).
- fix(runner): the box confinement self-test, reviewer-3 CF-1 to CF-4: a protected folder the session's uid can ENTER now counts as reached (the probe only tried read, write and list); the box's secrets folder, the spawner's folder and the key file are protected; the accounts folder is made 711 by the spawner and checked as "not listable"; EVERY project folder of the session is checked, not the first; and any TCP port something listens on in the box is refused (the session shares the box's network), unless the box says it expects it. "The wall" in the ruling is not probed (no firewall rule applies to session uids): it stays the container, the uid and the file modes. Tests: core/spawner/confine.test.js.

- fix(runner): the real dev-box failure "bwrap: execvp <node under the person's folder>: No such file" (reproduced on the test box with node under ~/node24/bin): with the egress proxy the sandbox runs Vyre's shim with THIS process's node, and only the shim file was bound, so a node outside /usr was missing inside. Its folder (real path) is now bound read-only whenever the proxy is on. Test: core/runner/homesandbox.test.js (plan binds the node folder), and a throwaway prepareSandbox run with a node-script agent (`env node`) on the test box: prepared and spawned.

- fix(relay): IV-5 (reviewer-3, outsider-exploitable): invitee channels were admitted for anyone who knew the route and never closed, so 32 idle ones filled the relay's per-route slots and the owner's paired phone got "too many connections". They now have a pool of 8 per box (the rest are refused at once, paired devices' slots are never theirs), close after 30 s with no stream, as soon as the stream they opened ends (accept or refusal) and after 5 minutes whatever they do. A stream with no call either way for 30 s is closed too (2 minutes while the home waits for the invitee's presence answer).
- fix(daemon,relay): found by the first real-daemon join (two daemons, a server-hosted space): the invitee door could never admit anyone on a real server. (1) It read this box's id with `relay.route.id` as the daemon, which that tool refused (`module:vyred` is now allowed on that one read), so every hello ended `cannot_check`; (2) the remote server it served an invite from had no `attest`, so the invitee's preview always ended "This server could not prove that it holds this space" (the door now signs the invitee's nonce through the server's `spaces.attest`); (3) accepting did not end the stream at once (a call inside the close was still served), and the home asking the invitee for presence ended the stream before the signed retry could use it. A refused hello now says why in the daemon log (`peer door: invitee <id> refused (<reason>)`).
- fix(daemon): the invitee door (reviewer-3 IV-1 to IV-4). A rate limit counts only a hello whose signature verified (naming a person no longer spends their allowance); a channel's own allowance is its own key's; the directory is asked inside a box-wide cap (`perBox`, 120 a minute) and an entry it just said it did not know is remembered for a minute; the nonce store drops the oldest nonces first instead of forgetting all of them; the signed hello (`vyre-invitee-hello-v2`) names the channel's own key id (`channel`), which must be the id the relay gave the channel.
- feat(relay-client,wink): `connect({ invitee: true })` puts `invitee: true` in every hello (the dial ignored it). An invitee link now uses a throwaway channel key of its own, and `inviteeSessionFor(channel, helloFor, { invite })` takes a function of the channel's key id that signs a fresh hello for every stream.
- feat(relay-client,wink): "Add this device from another device", the joining side. `relay/client/phonepair.js` (`addThisDevice`, Buffer-free, for a phone or a browser) redeems the existing device's code, shows the three words and, on the person's yes there, hands over this device's identity key; `wink.phone.wait` takes `entry` once and `wink.phone.pair.answer` puts the key on the identity's list through `spaces.identity.enrol`.
- feat(relay,daemon): the invitee door (DESIGN-spaces-first.md, "How a second person reaches a space to join it"). A channel whose hello says `invitee: true` makes no device row and has one door: a peer stream `{ peer: "wink", space: "home", invitee: { space, invite, identity, entry, name?, ts, nonce, sig } }`. The home admits it only with a fresh hello (2 minutes, one-time nonce) signed over this box's id, the space, the invite, the identity, the entry, the time and the nonce by a key on the identity's own list (read from the names directory like at pairing), and only when the space's kernel shows the invite pending (unexpired, unused, addressed to nobody or to this identity). The stream then carries `grants.invites.get` and `grants.invites.accept` for that one invite and nothing else; accepting ends it; a bad hello or invite closes it. Rates per invite, per identity and per channel. A key that is a waiting or paired device is not admitted as an invitee. The label `invitee:` is not a socket label.
- names, spaces, wink: the newcomer rule on record updates now covers a person's record too (same signer may continue). The space key's role is written down: it attests the server and confers no authority (a token signed by it for an invite the kernel never issued is refused; the kernel's own invite record is the only authority), with a test. A relay link whose box key is not the one the record names never opens a channel, so no hello is sent (test, with a control), and the refusal is plain.

- spaces, names: a server proves it holds a space. `spaces.host-here` makes the space's key ON THE SERVER (spaces/<id>/root.key) and answers its public half as `rootPublic`; the owner-signed directory record carries it, and the invite fingerprint words derive from it. A joiner's preview asks the server to sign a fresh nonce (`grants.invites.get` with a trailing `{ attest }`, answered by `spaces.attest` through the peer door's remote server); a server whose proof does not match the record's `rootPublic` is refused with `server_not_proven` before the card is shown. `claimServerSpace` takes the key from host-here and holds none; a server that gives none is refused (`server_too_old`). The directory Worker refuses an update of a SPACE's record by an owner device under 24 hours old unless that device signed the record's current version (`newcomer`), so a stolen newly added device cannot repoint a space.

- fix(wink, spaces, daemon): first owner wins on pairing. A home whose kernel already has a claimed owner takes no pairing from a different identity: `wink.server.adopt` refuses `owned_by_other` before any ask, ticket use or relay device, and adopt never changes the owner of an owned server (any other owner, with or without presence, is refused; handing a server over is a separate act). The same identity's second device (a computer after a phone) pairs: its identity proof is checked, the person at the server picks the words, and nothing about the owner changes. The kernel decides the owner before the device has a session or an enrolment, and a refusal fails the pairing and takes back the owner record and the device row. A paired device is the owner's person only as the person its own record names, and only while that person is the home's owner (`callerFacts`, `device.person`). New internal tool `spaces.owner.claimed`. The identity entry's enclave key shows as `owner_proof: enclave, unattested` (never "hardware" without a verified attestation).
- fix(stream, wink): PS-A, a stream over the peer wire no longer keeps the access it was opened with. `stream.open-peer` asks access again (the same read the open used, with the call's own chain) before any frame leaves, once per queued batch rather than once per frame: a person taken out of the chat, a revoked membership or a changed role takes effect at the next frame, the stream ends with `access_ended`, and the roles a viewer is drawn with are the ones just read. A reset frame (a `from` below the log floor) is now sent before the stream closes (it was dropped). Tests: core/stream/peer-open.test.js (removed from the chat, membership revoked, two viewers with a sealed field, reset), test/wink.test.js (a web device with a software session opens a chat but a presence call is refused; the ninth open on one device is refused).
- fix(wink): a computer that pairs a server sends `owner.pin` (the head and length of the identity chain it last verified) like a phone does, so a release server's PI-2 check no longer refuses it for a missing pin. `spaces.identity.self` carries the pin; Wink reads it through the `identityPin` seam.
- records, wink: `records.types` and `records.define` reach a space hosted on a paired server: the remote gateway has `definitions` (wire call `records.definitions`), and the person's proof for the call rides over the gateway door to answer the home's presence challenge (nothing is loosened: no proof, no change).
- spaces, wink: the invitee hello is v2 and signs the channel's own key id (reviewer IV-4); the link asks for it per stream (`inviteeSessionFor(channel, helloFor, { invite })`). `spaces.identity.self` also answers the identity's pin.

- spaces, cli: `vyre space add-agent <space> <agent>` (tool `spaces.members.add-agent`) adds an agent as an actor of a space through the kernel's own actor membership, under the person's proof; refused plainly without it.
- names: a key that was removed and put back is a newcomer again for the record rule (its age starts when it was last added), so an old key cannot come back and repoint a record it once signed. The forged-token test now carries a real, well formed person proof.

- spaces: a space asked for on a server is never made on this computer instead (`server_not_paired`, `server_unreachable`, nothing made); a read of a server-hosted space's members gives up after 4 s so a silent server cannot hold up lists and pairing; `invites.create` and `members.set-role` say `no_identity` on a home with no claimed identity.
- records, cli (#84): every `records.*` answer carries `acted_in: { id, label }`, the space it acted in ("home" for the home's own); with no `space` calls still act in the home's space. `vyre space use <name>` remembers a space, `vyre call --space <name>` overrides it, and tools that take a `space` get the remembered one; `vyre status` shows it.

- test(sweep): every write or outward tool a plain model session (bare `mcp` or `harness`) can reach is found mechanically on a real daemon (a probe input no tool declares answers `bad_input` past every gate and runs nothing) and must be refused, held for the person, the session's own work, or a hook, each with a reason in test/plain-session-writes.json; a new reachable tool fails the test. A second look hands the refused ones the input they ask for, and a second test proves a plain session cannot stop, send to, archive, delete, fork or switch a thread that is not its own. 5 tools wait for an owner (vault.generate, vault.request, vault.ssh.generate, files.fetch, github.project.local-init).
- fix(pluginagent,test): pluginagent.revoke's agents.delete was refused for a module and swallowed, so the revoked agent stayed registered. It now runs as the revoking person (ctx.call as: meta.caller; CALL_AS gives pluginagent person labels and the per-call check allows agents.delete only), so agents.delete's person-only rule decides and a failure is reported, not swallowed; agents.delete is unchanged (person-only; this is a PERSON_PROXY entry in test/reach-module-calls). test/model-is-never-person.json: core/recall/index.js drops from 2 frozen helpers to 0 (a28ba2c5d replaced recall's label helpers with lib/caller's isPerson/modelKey), so its entry is removed.
- feat(pluginagent): the plugin agent is given exactly memory and recall reads, projects reads, the sessions reads (threads.list/get/history/lineage) and memory.remember (a pending suggestion); every other tool, read or write, and every other route is refused `not_in_grant`, decided in core/pluginagent (`pluginagent.allows`, asked by the daemon's tool door for each call and each listing), so the tool listing holds only what it is given (reviewer-3 PG-1). `pluginagent.decline` and a revoke mean no until `pluginagent.on`; an unanswered ask expires at 24 h and the next waits 7 days; one pending ask at a time; the computer is named by the daemon (PG-5), not the asker; an expired ask cannot be granted, `expired` (PG-4). Real-daemon test core/pluginagent/pluginagent-grant.test.js.
- fix(daemon): the home's assistant's session is opened as the Space's assistant actor ("assistant") by name. lib/kernel-session now gives a session started for no agent and no chat the hop "session" (nobody's assistant), and the daemon had left the assistant to the old default, so an assistant's own kernel calls (tasks.move, tasks.submit, tasks.list) answered not_found "no such record" (walk step 10, rounds 35 to 37; each side passed alone, the merge of flows and devbox 96c8fca57 broke it; found by bisect with test/assistant-golden-path.test.js).
- feat(plugin): the plugin's server tells Claude, when recall or memory finds nothing beyond this session's project and more was expected, that Claude Code reads only this session's project until the person allows it once in Vyre; the line it says is "Claude Code can read only this session's project until you allow it in Vyre." (no screen named), also what pluginagent.status returns. Real-daemon test core/pluginagent/pluginagent-scope.test.js: not granted reads only its own session's project and no personal memory; another OS user's plugin or a copied label gets nothing, and the key file and socket are mode 0600. Copy now reads "the sessions of your projects".
- fix(planner,projects,assistant,files): who a call is from is meta.thread and meta.agent as the daemon vouched them, never the `:thread:<id>` or `:agent:<name>` text of a label (RC-1). projects.reach takes `thread` and `claim` from the asking module (files and the module door forward them); the label is read only when no verified meta came with the call.
- test(hooks,undo): core/hooks' "acts as you outside" red: the registry now answers a model's, an agent's or a module's outward act with `held_unavailable` (held at the Gate, not wired yet) before any callers list, so the tests expect that code for hooks.open and hooks.close (a guest and a module still get `denied`); core/undo's isPerson is lib/caller's and its test calls as a paired device label, a bare `mobile` is no one (platform-3's one list of person surfaces).
- feat(agents,recall,memory): "Claude Code on <this computer>" (lead's ruling) as a named agent granted ONCE the person's personal memory and every project's sessions to read. agents gets a `personal` flag (a new last migration step; agents.create/update by the person's surfaces and modules only, never a model; agents.list and agents.scope show it). A kernel token whose chain is [owner, that agent] with projects "*" and personal: core/recall reads every project (all:true), core/memory's gate reads it as the person's own session does (agent null, ownSession, plugin: name) with writes still pending and no correction or whole-graph pin. It is never the person. The registration and handing the plugin its token (and the approval that asks once) is platform's; this is the side that consumes it. Real-daemon test core/memory/plugin-agent-daemon.test.js.
- fix(recall): RC-1 and the token route. reach() no longer reads a thread out of the caller LABEL (a model sends any label it likes): it uses `meta.thread`, which the daemon vouches, and the kernel session token's chain (`meta.token`): [owner] or [owner, assistant] is the person (every project), [owner, named agent] is that agent (its granted projects), anything else is not. An unnamed model with a vouched thread reads its own project (a Vyre thread's project, or for a bound terminal session the project its own transcript's folder is in); with no token and no thread it reads nothing. Real-daemon test core/recall/model-token.test.js (the person's token reads across projects, kit's token only northwind, no token or a claimed `mcp:thread:<id>` label nothing, a bound session its own project).
- test(cli): the home's Agents section lists the built-in Engineer on a fresh home (agents.list always has it), so core/cli/commands/home.test.js and test/projects-cli.test.js expect `engineer` instead of "none yet".
- test(migrations): a module's migration list is append-only. test/migrations.released.json records a hash of every module's released steps in order (47 modules, 206 steps; `node scripts/record-migrations.mjs` at a release); test/migrations-append-only.test.js fails if a released step is moved, edited or removed or a step is inserted anywhere but the end. core/store logs `migration <module> v<n>: column already present, treated as applied` each time the duplicate-column repair fires (launch's update proof must fail on that line for a box upgraded from a released version). Memory's MS-1 helper admits a signed-in owner device.
- fix: the who-is-the-person sweep (platform-3). The MS-1 guard helper no longer counts as a module-local person helper (renamed mayRebuild: it reads the kernel's Who, or with the kernel off the surface labels), harness enrich's HD-4b flag is named typedBy and asks lib/caller (modelKey/agentName), and test/model-is-never-person.json is lowered for core/harness. Memory's label-side helpers go with the default-on flip on work/memory-shim-removal (counts there: 0 in core/memory); recall and projects keep an unnamed mcp as the user's own session until the lead rules (reading, ADR 0030).
- feat(pluginagent): Claude Code on this computer is an agent the person grants ONCE (ruling 4 Oct). The plugin's MCP server files `pluginagent.ask` the first time it runs here; the person approves with presence (`pluginagent.grant`, a surface of theirs): vyred registers a personal agent for every project, adds it to the Space and writes `plugin-agent.json` (mode 0600) in the home. From then on the server calls as that agent with its key; the daemon checks it (`pluginagent.vouch`), makes the call a model's own `mcp` and stamps that agent's kernel token itself (never the client's). Never the person. `pluginagent.revoke` ends it at once. Real-daemon test with the plugin's actual server: core/pluginagent/pluginagent.test.js. Carries assistant's a28ba2c5d (the `personal` flag).
- fix(daemon): RC-1, a model caller's label is built by vyred from what it verified and never passed through as a client sent it. A client-sent `mcp:thread:<id>` or `harness:thread:<id>` (any thread, any tail) arrives as bare `mcp` or `harness`; with a verified thread (a session's key, a bound thread socket) the label is `mcp:thread:<that thread>`, with a verified agent `mcp:agent:<name>`. One builder, `modelLabel` in lib/caller.js, used by socketCaller (which also covers the event stream upgrade) and route. test/model-label-rc1.test.js drives the real socket; test/thread-label-hygiene.test.js fails on a module that parses a thread out of a label.
- names, spaces, wink: the newcomer rule on record updates now covers a person's record too (same signer may continue). The space key's role is written down: it attests the server and confers no authority (a token signed by it for an invite the kernel never issued is refused; the kernel's own invite record is the only authority), with a test. A relay link whose box key is not the one the record names never opens a channel, so no hello is sent (test, with a control), and the refusal is plain.

- spaces, names: a server proves it holds a space. `spaces.host-here` makes the space's key ON THE SERVER (spaces/<id>/root.key) and answers its public half as `rootPublic`; the owner-signed directory record carries it, and the invite fingerprint words derive from it. A joiner's preview asks the server to sign a fresh nonce (`grants.invites.get` with a trailing `{ attest }`, answered by `spaces.attest` through the peer door's remote server); a server whose proof does not match the record's `rootPublic` is refused with `server_not_proven` before the card is shown. `claimServerSpace` takes the key from host-here and holds none; a server that gives none is refused (`server_too_old`). The directory Worker refuses an update of a SPACE's record by an owner device under 24 hours old unless that device signed the record's current version (`newcomer`), so a stolen newly added device cannot repoint a space.

- fix(stream, wink): PS-A, a stream over the peer wire no longer keeps the access it was opened with. `stream.open-peer` asks access again (the same read the open used, with the call's own chain) before any frame leaves, once per queued batch rather than once per frame: a person taken out of the chat, a revoked membership or a changed role takes effect at the next frame, the stream ends with `access_ended`, and the roles a viewer is drawn with are the ones just read. A reset frame (a `from` below the log floor) is now sent before the stream closes (it was dropped). Tests: core/stream/peer-open.test.js (removed from the chat, membership revoked, two viewers with a sealed field, reset), test/wink.test.js (a web device with a software session opens a chat but a presence call is refused; the ninth open on one device is refused).
- fix(wink): a computer that pairs a server sends `owner.pin` (the head and length of the identity chain it last verified) like a phone does, so a release server's PI-2 check no longer refuses it for a missing pin. `spaces.identity.self` carries the pin; Wink reads it through the `identityPin` seam.
- fix(sessions): the Switchboard emitted `thread.sandbox` (a partly sandboxed session, and now `confined_by` on every confined one) without declaring it under watches.emits, so the kernel refused the emit and failed the start ("threads emitted thread.sandbox, which its manifest does not declare"; found by the hosted packaged-boot run). Declared; core/switchboard/emits-declared.test.js keeps every literal emit name declared.

- feat(runner,sessions): a session in the packaged box is confined by the container, its own uid (an account's, or the box's one agent; never vyred's, never root) and the wall, and proves it before every start (ruling 4 Oct "b"; there is no bubblewrap in the box and no user namespaces). core/spawner/confine-probe.sh (a fixed program the spawner is allowed to start) runs AS THE SESSION'S UID and reports who it is, whether it can use its project, and whether it can reach Vyre's home, the keys and vault, the daemon's socket, the spawner's socket or another agent's home; core/spawner/confine.js turns that into failures, and lib/agent-sandbox.js refuses the start with `sandbox_failed: <the check>`. Only under VYRE_SUPERVISOR=docker with a spawner; everywhere else a missing bwrap still refuses. The record of a session says `confined_by` (`uid`, `bwrap` or `seatbelt`) and its log has a `thread.sandbox` line. Tests: core/spawner/confine.test.js (every refusal, a hung probe, the real probe as the test's user).
- perf(runner): the home-sandbox self-test tried the machine's own addresses one by one, each dropped connect costing its 1.5 s timeout: 35 s per session start on a box with a dozen bridges (the 13 s on the dev box). They are tried together now: 2.4 s. A kill during the self-test waits until bwrap has set its parent-death signal (a kill in that window left the inner process running), and an exited child ends the wait without its pipes closing.
- fix(runner,sessions): a script agent starts in the sandbox. An npm-installed Claude Code is a node script (a link into its package, shebang `env node`): the self-test and the real spawn bound only the link's folder, so `bwrap: execvp .../node: No such file` (dev box). lib/agent-sandbox.js `programDirs` now gives the program's folder, its link target and package folder, and its interpreter's folder (shebang, through `env`, found on PATH), read-only and nothing wider; on Linux they are first on the session's PATH (`pathDirs`). The self-test also honors sessions' abort `signal` (kills the probe and the agent check) and an early-exiting agent check no longer raises EPIPE. core/runner/person-chain.test.js: the stub context has `events.on` (the module subscribes to turns). Tests: core/runner/homesandbox.test.js (programDirs, npm-style script agent and native control, abort).
- fix(runner): on a packaged box (no bubblewrap in the image) the first session start ended vyred: the self-test probe was spawned with no "error" handler, so ENOENT was an uncaught exception (found by the hosted packaged-boot run, "spawn bwrap ENOENT", exit 70). The probe now records the error as the start's failure, and the daemon asks `unavailable()` once when it builds the session sandbox and refuses every start with "Vyre did not start this session because its sandbox cannot run here: <reason>". Test: core/runner/homesandbox.test.js (no bwrap on PATH: ok false, no uncaught exception).
- fix(box): the host's `vyre <command>` (call, status, modules, ...) runs inside the container as the vyre user, with a terminal when there is one. As root it carried an ancestry the daemon could not read as a person at the terminal (`caller_unknown`; on a kernel-on box `memory.me` said "no kernel chain" in the rc-update proof). packaged-boot checks it.
- fix(runner): the sandbox agent check listens for errors on the child's stdin before it ends it (test/stdin-hygiene).
- box: each session's temp folder lives in its own volume `vyre-sessions` at `/home/vyre/.vyre.sessions` (the default path of lib/session-temp.js), labelled run.vyre so `vyre uninstall` lists and removes it, made 0700 for vyre in the image. It is out of the home volume and its backups.
- fix(runner): a session start can no longer hang. The sandbox's agent check closes the program's stdin (a program that waits on stdin made `--version` hang for the whole 20 s and the start fail), the probe run is killed after 45 s, and the whole self-test is bounded at 90 s in `prepareSandbox` with a plain reason ("its safety check did not finish in time"). Found with the fake claude on testbox3: a real-daemon start with the sandbox on took 29 s and failed; it now starts.
- fix(runner,sessions): one bad session start no longer ends vyred (RC1 dev box: "the sandbox runs an absolute program path" was an unhandled rejection from the self-test's agent check, exit 70). The agent check catches everything it throws and reports "the agent does not start" as that session's result; the agent's program is resolved once against PATH outside the sandbox (`resolveAgentCommand` in lib/agent-sandbox.js; a name or relative path that cannot be found fails that session plainly: "the assistant's program was not found on this computer ... install it"), and every process the session launches uses its absolute path. Real-daemon test: test/session-bad-agent.test.js (missing, relative and not executable: the thread fails, no unhandled rejection, the daemon answers system.echo).
- feat(agents,recall,memory): "Claude Code on <this computer>" (lead's ruling) as a named agent granted ONCE the person's personal memory and every project's sessions to read. agents gets a `personal` flag (a new last migration step; agents.create/update by the person's surfaces and modules only, never a model; agents.list and agents.scope show it). A kernel token whose chain is [owner, that agent] with projects "*" and personal: core/recall reads every project (all:true), core/memory's gate reads it as the person's own session does (agent null, ownSession, plugin: name) with writes still pending and no correction or whole-graph pin. It is never the person. The registration and handing the plugin its token (and the approval that asks once) is platform's; this is the side that consumes it. Real-daemon test core/memory/plugin-agent-daemon.test.js.
- fix(recall): RC-1 and the token route. reach() no longer reads a thread out of the caller LABEL (a model sends any label it likes): it uses `meta.thread`, which the daemon vouches, and the kernel session token's chain (`meta.token`): [owner] or [owner, assistant] is the person (every project), [owner, named agent] is that agent (its granted projects), anything else is not. An unnamed model with a vouched thread reads its own project (a Vyre thread's project, or for a bound terminal session the project its own transcript's folder is in); with no token and no thread it reads nothing. Real-daemon test core/recall/model-token.test.js (the person's token reads across projects, kit's token only northwind, no token or a claimed `mcp:thread:<id>` label nothing, a bound session its own project).
- test(cli): the home's Agents section lists the built-in Engineer on a fresh home (agents.list always has it), so core/cli/commands/home.test.js and test/projects-cli.test.js expect `engineer` instead of "none yet".
- fix(recall): an unnamed model session (`mcp`, `mcp:thread:<id>`) is never the person (reviewer-2): it no longer reads every session. It reads its own thread's project (a thread label names it; the project's folders as for a named agent with one project); a bare `mcp` with no thread has no project and reads nothing. The person's surfaces, modules and named granted agents are as before. Recall's person helpers ask lib/caller (isPerson, modelKey) and core/recall leaves the frozen list. Test in core/recall/scope.test.js. NOTE: a terminal Claude Code session through the plugin is a bare `mcp` today, so its recall tools read nothing until the kernel's session token carries its project.
- test(migrations): a module's migration list is append-only. test/migrations.released.json records a hash of every module's released steps in order (47 modules, 206 steps; `node scripts/record-migrations.mjs` at a release); test/migrations-append-only.test.js fails if a released step is moved, edited or removed or a step is inserted anywhere but the end. core/store logs `migration <module> v<n>: column already present, treated as applied` each time the duplicate-column repair fires (launch's update proof must fail on that line for a box upgraded from a released version). Memory's MS-1 helper admits a signed-in owner device.
- fix: the who-is-the-person sweep (platform-3). The MS-1 guard helper no longer counts as a module-local person helper (renamed mayRebuild: it reads the kernel's Who, or with the kernel off the surface labels), harness enrich's HD-4b flag is named typedBy and asks lib/caller (modelKey/agentName), and test/model-is-never-person.json is lowered for core/harness. Memory's label-side helpers go with the default-on flip on work/memory-shim-removal (counts there: 0 in core/memory); recall and projects keep an unnamed mcp as the user's own session until the lead rules (reading, ADR 0030).
- fix(0.3, release): a 0.2.x server updated to 0.3 by its OLD updater no longer comes up with 0 modules. The release's signed module list and app record ride inside shell.json as exact text (scripts/shell-hashes.mjs, built by build-site.sh, checked by check-release-dist), the one file every updater since 0.2 fetches, verifies and publishes. lib/release-shell.js takes them only from a shell.json whose signature chain verifies (the signed SHA256SUMS lists that shell.json and each text); the kernel's list reader and the app gate use it when the package root has no modules.json or appbuild.json, place-release.sh rebuilds both at a container's start, and a packaged kernel-on daemon with no list yet says "Finishing the update" in `vyre status`, waits up to two minutes for the published files and restarts once by itself (core/daemon/release-watch.js); if they never arrive it says so and stays. found by scripts/rc-update-proof.sh.
- gateway door: records, tasks, rules and files tools now reach a Space hosted on a paired server through the remote kernel. `lib/gateway-door.js` no longer asks the local kernel for a chain in a Space it does not host (that answered "no such space"); for a remote handle it checks the call is from this home's signed-in person and lets the server mint the chain from the device it proved.

The recovery screen spreads `await recoveryKeyOptions()` (keys/index: enclave plus requireEnclave on an iPhone, no_biometrics without Face ID, nothing on web) into recoverIdentity; a retry on a kept identity throws `unreachable` when the directory cannot be read or does not take the op (RX-2a); the re-read that decides `landed` is verifyChain'd (RX-2b); replaceRecoveryCode saves first, publishes, returns the code only after both, and puts the old list back when the publish is refused or unknown (RC-1). Tests in restore.test.js: 8 of 8 on testbox (42 of 42 with the install tests). A device under 24 hours old is refused by the list (code `newcomer`), so the offer opens a day after the recovery; a lost publish answer is checked by reading the chain again; the code is returned once and never kept. Test on testbox: 5 of 5 in restore.test.js.
- feat(0.3, app, peer stream, 4 Oct): a peer-paired device follows a chat over the peer wire: src/real/peer.ts peerDuplex (stream.follow through peer.openStream, resumed by `from`) is the duplex box-stream.ts hands the resumable stream client when the device is peer-routed; relay/client/peerclient.js from work/wink-session d9c278a66. - feat(0.3, app identity, 4 Oct): recoverIdentity (apps/app/src/identity/restore.ts), box-less: resolve the name's chain at the directory, check the recovery code's key (codeSigner in recovery.js) is on it, make this device's key (the phone's Keychain key or a fresh WebCrypto one), sign an `add` op with the code's key, keep the identity, then publish; refusal codes not_found, not_a_person, wrong_code, unreachable, rate_limited, newcomer, rolled_back (the pin), exists. A wrong code changes nothing, a second recovery on a device is idempotent, and a failed publish forgets the kept key. hadIdentity (store.ts) is the marker that a device once held a name. addThisDevice is a stub (not_built) until tailnet's phone-side client. Events and streams are not routed yet.

- spaces: `spaces.host-here` on a server too small for the larger store no longer fails with the kernel's invite wording ("The person who invited you has not confirmed...", the store's `needs_confirmation` code run through the invite word table). It refuses with code `needs_store_confirmation` and the kernel's own text, hosts nothing, and hosts when asked again with `acceptBuiltinStore: true`. `spaces.create` for a server home returns the same `needs_confirmation` step a local creation does, answered by `storeChoice`.

- app, spaces: `claimServerSpace` (apps/app/src/identity/claim-space.js), the creator's half of making a space on a paired server from a device with no box (phone, web): ask the server to host (`spaces.host-here` over the peer session), make the root key, sign the space's chain and the sealed record (id, label, root key, owner name, home route) with the device key through the identity's list, claim it in the directory; a failed claim takes the hosted space back. `spaces.person.learn` (the door records an invitee's Vyre name after the directory confirms it), `spaces.owner.adopt` takes the owner's name, space records carry `ownerName`, and the identity op time check no longer rejects an op made a moment before it is applied.

- spaces, wink: a second person can join a space that lives on a server. The space's directory record carries its home's route (relay, route, box id; read from Wink's paired record by the new internal tool `wink.server.channel`) and is republished when the space is made on a server. An invitee's device opens a peer stream to that route with a hello signed by its own identity (`vyre-invitee-hello-v1` over box, space, invite, identity, entry, time and nonce; the stream head gains `invitee`), reads the card and accepts through the home's kernel with its own presence. The row `invitee-route/<space>` is kept from the first preview until accept. New: `inviteeSessionFor` in `core/wink/serverlink.js`, the `winkInviteeSessionFor` hand-up in `core/modules/index.js`. The home's door admitting the hello is tailnet's.

Move it to your server first.", code `this_computer`). An invitee who cannot reach a space is told "This space lives on <owner>'s computer and cannot be reached from here. Ask them to move it to their server." (code `unreachable`, no more "yet"). `spaces.resume` takes `meta` (lint).

- fix(kernel): the lender's network cap (reviewer-2 CAP-1 to CAP-3, ruled by the lead). CAP-1: `offers.lend` binds `network_cap` into the hashed input (`null` when none is stated, a signed value), so a proof made for one cap is refused for another or for none; an invalid cap is bad_input; kernel/remote/proof.js builds the same input. CAP-2: `capOf` answers the tightest cap across every live acceptance for that computer (provider is tighter than internet; an acceptance that states none never loosens one that does). CAP-3: lending a computer that is already lent with a different cap is refused with a plain message (stop lending it, then lend it again), never silently kept at the old one. Tests: reviewer-2's rv2-lender-cap.test.js unchanged in core/runner, and a test per finding in kernel/grants/grants.test.js.
- ci(runner): the real sandbox is tested where every merge is checked. New workflow runner-linux.yml installs bubblewrap and gocryptfs on a hosted Ubuntu 24.04 machine, allows unprivileged user namespaces, and runs the runner's tests with `VYRE_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`: a test file that imports core/runner/testing/require-sandbox.js (runner.test.js, lent-wire.test.js) then fails loudly instead of skipping when the sandbox or the encrypted workspace is missing, and prints the reason when it does skip on another machine.
- fix(sessions): `threads.send` threw "meta is not defined" for every caller on the trunk: its handler used `meta` (for the Mac-forwarding check, person-labels a11fb3b7d) without taking it as a parameter. Found by the own-server daemon test timing out at turn 2.
- fix(runner): the runner's session stdin listens for errors (test/stdin-hygiene), and the lent-wire test that needs a real sandbox and workspace is skipped where the machine has none (the hosted runner has no bubblewrap), like the runner's other tests.
- feat(kernel): the lender's network cap is part of the Offer. A member's own acceptance (`offers.offer` or `offers.lend`, side member_accepts) may carry `network_cap: "provider" | "internet"`; any other value, or the Space's side carrying one, is refused; `offers.capOf({ member, device })` reads it. The lent home limits the session's definition by it (the Space can never hand a session more than the lender allowed), `lent.status` reports it, and the lender host applies the same cap locally; the old `lenderCap` option stays as an override.
- fix(records): forgetting a live record (sqlite `persist.destroy`) takes it out of the kept stage counts, deletes its attribute row (`kernel_attrs`) and its cache entry, in one savepoint with the row and its log entries; a rolled-back forget changes nothing. Tests: raw bytes of the file and write-ahead log, counts equal a scan after forget, restart and a rollback.
- feat(records): `records.forget` is the person's own act with their presence (the kernel gate: `records.define` is an admin act, a presence session or a signed proof, never inherited by a chain that holds an agent); the registry classifies it person-only. `records.forget.propose` is what an assistant uses: it makes a task for the person and forgets nothing. The answer says what happened: tasks and events emptied, sealed values destroyed in the sealing process (and any it could not drop), linked files that stay in Files, how many sessions mention the record, and "Sessions that quoted this record are not searched. Forget them in Memory."
- fix(relay): the grace before a waiting pairing whose app is gone is dropped is 30 s (was 15 s), so a phone on a poor network can reconnect; the abandoned-pairing test waits on the `pairing.abandoned` event and no longer sleeps. Tests: the web-kind session is stopped by the presence floor (`presence_required`) and passes it with a fresh proof; a long garbage `sig` on an Ed25519 entry is refused, two valid passkey signatures over one op give one head and cannot change what it says.
- fix(presence): `presence.remove` lists its callers like `presence.enroll`, so the relay can take a device's presence key away when the device goes or a setup session ends (the registry's origin check on a defaulted tool had refused it, leaving the key enrolled; core/relay/setup.test.js was right). Wink: the pairing-time identity proof follows wink-2's rule (no fallback to the three words). Tests: relay.status refuses a bare model, link.macs.call writes refuse a model or a module acting alone. 0.3 is the first release with the esig rule, so there are no earlier identities to migrate.
- fix(identity): NE-1, one op has one hash. An `esig` is accepted only as exactly 64 bytes r||s with s in the low half (DER and the high-s twin are refused), and the hash a next op names as `prev` leaves out a WebAuthn assertion's `sig` (its high-s twin is valid and anyone can make it), so neither form can fork the chain head. chain.js re-pinned.
- feat(wink): `wink.server.probe { device }` (read-only, the person's surfaces): a system.info over the channel this device paired a server on, answering `{ reachable }` or `{ reachable: false, code }`, kept after wink.remove so a removed device's refusal can be shown. fix: link.macs.call writes need the person past a module hop; relay owner() refuses a bare model session.
- feat(identity): NK-2, a phone's list change also needs its Face ID signature (kernel/identity/chain.js, re-pinned). A device entry may carry `enclave` (the raw uncompressed P-256 point of its Secure Enclave key, part of the signed entry) and `attest` (an opaque App Attest assertion for the enrolment verifier). Every add, remove, replace-code or space-owner change signed by an entry with `enclave` must carry `esig`, that key's ECDSA P-256 signature (SHA-256, 64 bytes r||s or DER, base64url) over the same op message, or it is refused `needs_enclave` at every home and the directory Worker. `makeOp` takes `esign`. Entries with neither `enclave` nor `held` (a Mac or a server) still sign alone.
- fix(wink): SP-1 exact owner ids in production (`per_` plus 26 base32; `spc_` plus 12 or 26); `createWink({ looseOwnerIds })` is for tests only. `pairServer` maps a refused owner to `bad_owner`. A waiting pairing whose app closed and did not come back within 15 s is dropped by the relay (`pairing.abandoned`) and wink clears its ask at once, so the server no longer answers "busy" until restart. test/mobile-tailnet.test.js mints its enrolment code from presence directly (a module hop without an origin is refused by the registry now).
- feat(wink): device-first pairing grants the session. When a box-less app adopts a server and says what it is (`deviceKind` phone, computer or web, `deviceName`, `keyStorage`), the pick of the three words at the server is the owner's confirmation: the device is recorded as the owner's with that kind and its paired session is granted in the same act, so it goes straight to pair-challenge and start-paired. `web` is a new device kind (a session and nothing more); presence accepts it for pair-grant. New internal `wink.device.paired { device, identity }` (any kind, modules only). fix(presence): `presence.enroll` states its callers (the person's surfaces and modules) so the relay's pairing-time enrolment of a device's presence key is no longer refused as no_such_tool by the module-hop default.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2 gate of e620c0429. KR-1: a protected type is created and read only by an owner or admin (as themselves, or through a service acting for them), and only rows made by a service or by an owner or admin are shown (a row planted behind the gateway, or by a member before the rule, is never returned by get, query, count or search); update and remove keep the maker-or-admin rule. CT-1: a kept count is used only while its flag is on disk, so a first count built inside a transaction that rolls back is built again. SC-1: `tasks.scrubTexts` compares on a normalised form (NFKC, case-folded, without spaces, punctuation or zero-width marks, with the leaves of a form joined so a value split over two fields matches) and takes `records` (every task about one of them loses its text); late sealing passes the records it moved and reports `task_texts_cleared`.
- fix(onboard): the assistant check is event-driven, no timer. It runs once at start (3 s, agents module up) and on owner.adopted (the daemon now emits it from the kernel's onOwnerAdopted), owner.seen, owner.changed, onboard.claude-changed (new: connect and disconnect) and account.changed (sessions to announce other providers' sign-ins). An assistant whose account is disconnected later stays and onboard.assistantState says "Your assistant has no AI account connected"; reconnecting clears it. providers.list always reports the machine's own Claude login (account "default") as signed in, so that row does not count as a connection; any other signed-in account or onboard's own Claude connection does. Daemon tests for made, waiting and disconnected.
- spaces: `spaces.invites.create` refuses a space that lives on this computer ("This space lives on this computer, so other people cannot join it. Move it to your server first.", code `this_computer`). An invitee who cannot reach a space is told "This space lives on <owner>'s computer and cannot be reached from here. Ask them to move it to their server." (code `unreachable`, no more "yet"). `spaces.resume` takes `meta` (lint).

- fix(kits): installed Kits and the proposals waiting for a yes are now records on a real vyred (the host passed no kit store, so a Kit proposal was lost at a restart); written and removed by the Flows service's own chain, which the kernel's protected `kit-proposal` and `kit-install` rows require. kits.apply takes the kernel's `begin` for every Kit, with or without types, and `resume` for a resumed install, covering only the types still missing.
- fix(callers): one answer for who is the person (MH-1, MS-1). lib/caller.js exports isPerson (a person's own surface or device) and modelKey (the agent a named model claims, `caller:<kind>` for one that names no one, null only for the person); chrome's agentOf and hands' grantKey use it (chrome keeps a standalone copy, checked against lib/caller.js by local/hands-chrome-mac/caller.test.js). A bare `mcp` inside vyred now gets "This assistant has no permission to use this computer yet. Add it in Access." from chrome and hands. The standalone Chrome runtime keeps its exemption (the person's own install is the grant), meta.standalone is stripped from every registry call, and the runtime refuses to start while a vyred runs. test/model-is-never-person.test.js finds a module-local helper that maps a label to the person or an owner (proved on the three helpers as they were before the fixes) and freezes today's remaining 23 files in test/model-is-never-person.json as the sweep list.
- fix(team): an upgraded box lost the whole team module ("migration team v11 failed: duplicate column name: title"). My team_charter_drafts migration had been inserted in the MIDDLE of the list, shifting every later number, so an existing box re-ran ADD COLUMN title. It is now the last step, with a note never to insert above it, and core/store's migrate treats a step's "duplicate column name" as already applied (retries statement by statement; any other error still fails). core/team/migrations.test.js runs the chain twice, from a box that already has each later column, and from the list as released before the drafts table; core/store test for the tolerance.
- fix(memory): MS-1 (reviewer-2, HIGH). `reach` reads an unnamed model session (`mcp`, `mcp:thread:<id>`) as every project, and `guard` with whole:true skipped the owner check, so such a session could pin and mute the main graph or a project it was not granted and run memory.curate on the whole graph. Steering and curating the whole graph now need the person at one of their own surfaces (the kernel's Who, or the surface labels with the kernel off) or a named agent held to its own project; a module and an unnamed model are refused. reviewer-2's repro is core/memory/rv2-memory-steer.test.js, unchanged. An unnamed model still reads the rooms it names.
- feat(onboard): the assistant exists once the server has an owner and an AI account is connected, with no first-run page (0.3: the owner arrives by pairing, nothing named it, so a fresh home had none). core/onboard/assistant-ready.js runs 4 s after start and every minute: an owner (a claimed identity or the named person) plus a signed-in provider account (or the machine's own Claude sign-in) makes the assistant (Juno unless named); an owner and no account sets onboard.assistantState to "Connect an AI account to start your assistant". Real-daemon test test/assistant-ready-daemon.test.js.
- feat(kernel): `kits.resume` is repeatable (lead's ruling): one approval, as many resumes as it takes, within a day, by the approver's own chain, for a Kit that still hashes to the approval's `kit_hash`. Each resume defines only the types still missing from the live catalog and writes `kit.resumed` with an attempt number first; `kit.installed` is written once, when nothing is missing (the last spent type, or a Kit with no types at begin); a resume with nothing missing defines nothing and answers `{ already_installed: true }`; an update is never resumed; a changed Kit is refused. Test: kernel/tasks/kit-apply.test.js.
- feat(0.3, stream e2e, 4 Oct): e2e-step8.test.js, step 8 inside a real chat turn on a real vyred: the harness seeds a contact with a sealed ssn; the assistant (fake provider) runs `vyre-sock work.call {tool: contacts.find}` on its own thread socket, so vyred adds the thread's kernel session, and its stored thread events hold `{sealed: "US SSN", present: true, valid_format: true}`, never the value and never a sealed reference. e2e-step7, sigterm, asker and step8 4 of 4 on testbox.
- perf(kernel): count by stage from kept counts. The built-in store keeps `kernel_counts` (type, field, value, n) for a type's stage and select fields, built from the table the first time a plain count by that field is asked for and maintained inside every write's transaction (an upsert per write, two when the value changes); a changed definition drops it. A rolled-back write leaves it untouched, a restart keeps it. Test: kernel/store/sqlite.test.js (kept counts equal the scan through creates, edits, removes, restores, a restart, a rollback and a redefinition). Late sealing now calls `tasks.scrubTexts` unguarded and the raw-bytes test restarts the kernel.
- feat(onboard): the assistant exists once the server has an owner and an AI account is connected, with no first-run page (0.3: the owner arrives by pairing, nothing named it, so a fresh home had none). core/onboard/assistant-ready.js runs 4 s after start and every minute: an owner (a claimed identity or the named person) plus a signed-in provider account (or the machine's own Claude sign-in) makes the assistant (Juno unless named); an owner and no account sets onboard.assistantState to "Connect an AI account to start your assistant". Real-daemon test test/assistant-ready-daemon.test.js.
- fix: the known-red files on the trunk. core/recall: stop() used `within` from lib/within.js but the folder helper of the same name shadowed it inside the module (the original stop() TypeError), renamed to `inFolders`. core/harness: `harness.learn` declares `prompt_id` and `agent` (the hook sends both and the registry now refuses undeclared keys, so failed and fixed signals never reached Learning), test/harness.test.js calls as the hook and gives the interactive-yes test a transcript line (its failures left daemons running: the hang). Test stubs declare their reads (agents job, context, goals, assistant); personal/answer follows HD-8.
- fix(tests): `--test-force-exit` is gone from `npm test`, `test:windows` and the workflows (redteam, runner-perf, sessions-sdk, vault-mac): it ended a file's process mid-run and still exited green, so tests silently never ran (windows saw lib/spaces/homes.test.js run fewer than its 44 in about half its runs). `npm test` is now `scripts/test-counts.mjs run`, which counts the tests each file really ran (scripts/test-count-reporter.mjs) and fails when a file ran fewer than it declares or fewer than the last recorded count in test/test-counts.json; pull requests also fail when a recorded count falls and the diff deletes no test( or it( line (`npm run test:counts -- diff <base>`).
- feat(kernel): Kit path, reviewer-2 KW-A, KW-B, KT-4 and the protected rows. (1) A define under a Kit waiver spends its types only after the define succeeds (`kitApply.spend`), so a refused define strands nothing. (2) The waiver binds the whole chain as `chainHash` does (every hop with its surface, device and session) and its job, so another chain of the same person is refused. (3) `gateway.kits.resume({ chain, task, kit })`: once per task, only for a task whose `kit.applying` is in the log, by the approver's own chain, for the approved Kit, only for the types not yet defined (an update is never resumed); writes `kit.resumed` first. (4) Protected types: `kit-proposal`, `kit-install` and any type with `protected: true`: a row is changed or removed only by whoever made it (`created_by`) or an owner or admin acting as themselves; reading and creating are unchanged. Tests: kernel/tasks/kit-apply.test.js, kernel/gateway/protected-types.test.js.
- test(kernel): late sealing clears the task texts that quote the sealed values (gateway `sealField` calls platform's `tasks.scrubTexts({ values })` before the store scrub, whose VACUUM then leaves no copy in the file): kernel/store/late-seal-texts.test.js searches the raw bytes of the database and its write-ahead log.
- perf(kernel): a restricted caller whose access is attribute equalities (project, owner, sensitivity, created_by; one person, no rule on reading, no temp, grants whole-type with no condition) is counted and listed natively. `authorizer.rowPredicate` says the access as `{ any: [ { attr: value, ... }, ... ] }`; the gateway passes it as `attr_filter` to a store that declares `features().attr_filter` (the built-in store, from `kernel_attrs`, with new indexes on project and owner) when no module supplies an owner or project for the type and the home has no attribute function; otherwise, and for anything it cannot say, the rows are asked about one by one as before. A list page still asks about each row it returns. Member by project, testbox3 at load 5, p50 / p95 ms: 20,000 records count 14 / 75, page 16 / 63 (row by row 1,872 / 2,425 and 330 / 366); 100,000 records count 120 / 205, page 133 / 213 (row by row: `unsupported` after 3.6 s, page 5.3 s). Tests: kernel/gateway/attr-filter.test.js (pushed equals row by row over five grant shapes, every page, plus the safe-use checks); reviewer-2's KQ repros unchanged and passing.

- feat(0.3, onboard): `onboard.claude {mode:"disconnect"}` removes the AI sign-in from the vault (the person's own, with presence; a model is refused), and `onboard.status` answers `owned` (boolean) so an app can show "pair first" before a tap.
- fix(0.3, package): scripts/admin-wipe.mjs and scripts/admin-anchor-reset.mjs are in package.json "files", so `vyre admin wipe` and `anchor-reset` have their script in every packaged image; test/package-files.test.js derives the list from the scripts box/vyre runs in the image.
- feat(0.3, box): a server has no first-run page. onboard.link refuses (`not_available`, pair from your app), the kept link is not reopened at start, the compose no longer publishes the onboarding port nor sets VYRE_ONBOARD_HOST, and packaged-boot checks nothing listens on 7300 or 7301 inside the box and nothing is published on the host.
- feat(learn,memory,team): the three items left by platform-3. `/vyre lesson` (learn.add, now open to a session) makes a PROPOSED lesson when the caller is a model (the chain with the kernel on, the `mcp`/`harness` labels only as SHIM(legacy labels) with it off), active only from the person; the person accepts with learn.accept. memory.pin, mute and curate admit a model's own session and the body's guard decides what it may steer (a project agent only its own project). team.charter.draft by a session is PENDING (table team_charter_drafts, shown by team.charter.get) until the person accepts it with the new team.charter.accept; a person's surface still writes outright. Tests in learn.test.js, remember-poison.test.js, team.test.js.
- feat(0.3, app, peer, 4 Oct): a device paired to its server over the relay (device-first install) calls it over the peer wire: src/real/peer.ts opens relay/client/peerclient.js (wink-2, copied identical) from the saved pairing, src/real/box.ts tool() routes through it when the pairing marked the device (usePeer), and the server runs each call as this device with its paired session. Pairing sets the mark after the yes, then opens the paired session (pair-challenge, start-paired).
- fix(hands): chrome.open refuses a non-public address for a model (loopback, the daemon's ports, LAN and private ranges, link-local, the cloud metadata address, tailnet and the box's own addresses, a name that resolves to any of them) and checks where the page landed after a redirect; the person's own call is not held to it. The address guard moved to lib/netguard.js (core/runner/netguard.js re-exports it). HD-6c: only input roles (entry, textbox, searchbox, combobox, slider) are believed from the page, never to make a click observable.
- feat(flows, kits): a Kit installs on a real kernel after the owner's approval. kits.propose writes `form.kit_hash` (hash of the Kit id, version, content hash and its type definitions); kits.apply takes the kernel's approved-Kit waiver (`gateway.kits.begin`, kernel/tasks/kit-apply.js) for the Kit's types only, once, and ends it. The Flows host defines the record types a Kit's templates, roles and views are stored in (template, def-role, def-view) with its own, and `#ensureDefType` awaited the async catalog (it read `types` of a promise). Real-daemon test: the Engineer proposes a library Kit, the owner's signed approval installs it (test/engineer-daemon.test.js "RC1 walk").
- feat(sessions): own-server sessions are sealed per turn (core/daemon/ownserver-host.js, threads.own-transcript), with a daemon-level recover test.
- fix(hands): the click guard matches the whole name and vetoes grant, accept, send and leave words anywhere in it (HD-6b); a page's own role no longer makes a control observable, and a native submit or a consent, checkout or deletion link is consequential. presence.enroll and agents.rollover list `module` so the relay's pairing-time enrol and the assistant's daily roll reach them with no person as original caller.

- feat(wink, daemon, 4 Oct; wink-2): device-first pairing leaves the device usable. The pick of the three words at a fresh server records the pairing device as its owner's (phone, computer or web, with its key and where the key lives), enrols its own key (`presence.device.enroll-paired`), makes its paired-session grant and enrols it in the home space; the device then signs in (start-paired) and calls the server's tools and kernel over a Wink peer session (`wink.sessionFor`, `wink.remoteKernel`). The daemon composes the relay's peer door (core/daemon/peer-door.js).
