The assistant stubs declare their tools as reads.
- feat(kernel): an approved Kit install is the presence for that install and nothing else. `gateway.kits.begin({ chain, task, kit })` (kernel/tasks/kit-apply.js) checks the task (a person approved it, within a day, not applied before), that the form names the Kit (`form.kit_hash === sha256(canonical(kit))`, the form being in the body the approval proof covers), that the chain is the approver's own and carries no assistant; writes `kit.applying` to the log first (which spends the approval for good, across restarts); and returns a waiver only it can make. `records.define(chain, diff, { waiver })` accepts it as the admin presence, only for a diff made of exactly the Kit's listed types, byte for byte, each once, for the same chain, for two minutes. Rules are not covered yet (rules.set needs a person chain). Tests: kernel/tasks/kit-apply.test.js.
- feat(0.3, app, pairing, 4 Oct; reviewer-3 PD-B/PD-D, vault's paired session): the box-less server pairing sends the identity proof in the FIRST adopt call (signIdentity), strips control and bidi characters from the owner name, and never takes the direct path when a box pairing is saved; after the yes the browser runs presence.person.pair-challenge then start-paired over the channel (src/auth/paired.ts, signed with this browser's P-256 key, ES256 raw 64 bytes) and keeps the token where webPerson reads it; box.web.ts then signs every request, relay too, when a token is kept. Node tests: src/auth/paired.test.js. Needs the server to make the pair-grant for the pairing device (tailnet).
- feat(wink): device-first pairing grants the session. When a box-less app adopts a server and says what it is (`deviceKind` phone, computer or web, `deviceName`, `keyStorage`), the pick of the three words at the server is the owner's confirmation: the device is recorded as the owner's with that kind and its paired session is granted in the same act, so it goes straight to pair-challenge and start-paired. `web` is a new device kind (a session and nothing more); presence accepts it for pair-grant. New internal `wink.device.paired { device, identity }` (any kind, modules only). fix(presence): `presence.enroll` states its callers (the person's surfaces and modules) so the relay's pairing-time enrolment of a device's presence key is no longer refused as no_such_tool by the module-hop default.
- fix(0.3, stream e2e, 4 Oct): the step 7 harness (core/stream/e2e-step7-vyred.js) switches the spaces module off for its temp home, because a device that is not enrolled in the Space gets no kernel chain and the harness has no claimed identity to enrol carol's paired device with (e2e-step7, e2e-sigterm, e2e-asker 3 of 3 on testbox).
- feat(kernel): `scripts/admin-anchor-reset.mjs`, what `sudo vyre admin anchor-reset` runs (AN-1). Offline, sealing process only: it prints one request line, takes the owner's presence proof for `anchor.reset` on stdin (made after the request: the sealing process takes no proof issued before it started), has the sealing process forget the anchor, and appends one `anchor.reset` event naming the person to the home's log (BL2-1). Test kernel/seal/anchor-reset.test.js runs it against the real sealing process (needs work/sealing's anchor.reset; skips without it).
- feat(kernel): BL-2, the log anchor. The sealing process keeps the newest (seq, head) it was shown outside the database, forward only. Each signed checkpoint first verifies the log up to its head, advances the anchor to that head, and only then is written into the log (a broken log signs nothing; a log the anchor says is behind writes no checkpoint). A restart compares the log with the anchor (`kernel/audit` `anchorCheck`): a log shorter than the anchor, or with another event at its position, reports `boot.why` `anchor_rolled_back` or `anchor_history_differs` (an unreadable anchor fails the check); no anchor boots and the first checkpoint writes it. A packaged home refuses to start on any failed boot check and names the owner's `anchor.reset` as the way out; a development build says so and starts. The home now gets the Space's checkpoint key from the sealing process (`checkpoints: true`) and signs a checkpoint every 1,000 events or 10 minutes. The anchor defends against the database alone being put back, not against a whole-home restore or someone holding the sealing folder. A checkpoint public key given as base64 DER (what the sealing process returns) now verifies.
- fix(hands): the click guard is an allow-list (group D HD-6). A control is observable only when it is passive (an entry, a tab, a row) or named for moving, showing or selecting; Authorize, Allow, Accept, Save, Continue, Grant, Enable, Apply, Order, Log in and every unreadable name are consequential, so an agent cannot approve an OAuth screen by clicking. test: modules/hands-chrome/consequence.test.js.
- test: reads are reads (test/reads-are-reads.test.js). Every tool that declares `effect: "read"` is called twice as the person with no input and must change no row, emit no event and call no write tool; six known writers are listed to be redeclared by their owners.
- fix: undeclared input keys. The Deck and the app sent keys their tools never read and the registry now refuses (agents.ask model, team.ask surface, threads.mode surface, threads.list project, threads.unqueue uuid, vault.reveal purpose, watchers.list agent): dropped at the call sites. wink.server.adopt lists `proof` (the pairing app sends it).
- fix(vault): vault.relay is the person's; audit, uses, emergency.list, pass.list, vaults.list, device.list and people are the person's and modules'; vault.agent.grants shows a model its own agent's logins only.
- fix(harness): the six hook tools list their callers (mcp, harness, the person's surfaces, modules). Without a list the registry's write default limited them to the person's surfaces and a real hook call from the `harness` label was refused (core/harness tests 7 to 15 failed on the trunk). The tests call as the hook and declare their stub modules' tools as reads.
- fix(memory): the read-by-meaning tools (memory.prompt, brief, today, relevant, retrieve, context, card) are declared reads, so the registry's write default no longer refuses the Switchboard's module hop that hands a teammate its memory. Real-daemon tests use the LB-2 definite-outside ancestry.
- fix(daemon): a socket peer read that comes back empty (a busy box) is retried three times, short and bounded, while the connection is open, before the call is demoted; a call whose peer still could not be read and whose label was cli or local is refused with "Vyre could not tell who is calling; try again" (code caller_unknown), not "not a signed-in person". The "ancestry: unknown" log line is written once per connection, not on every call (ND-1). test/ancestry-production.test.js: a real vyred in its own process, 50 concurrent real CLI calls on a busy box through the production peer read, all classified alike.
- fix(daemon): SI-1b the dev stand-in widens only for a ROOT-owned login server (sshd, login), carried as server.uid from peer.js; a user-owned tmux, screen, terminal app or process named sshd (all of which a model can start daemonized) uses the real `vyre signin`. `signin.dev` refuses a node that already holds a real session.
- fix(daemon): restore `const crossOrigin` and `let person` in route(), which the removal of the duplicate signin daemon half (ed2e9ca15) dropped: every socket call answered "crossOrigin is not defined".
- fix(daemon): only `cli` and `local` get person facts from a socket label; `deck` and `mobile` reach a daemon through their own listeners, so on the socket they are claims and never the person, whatever the ancestry says (a bare deck label gave different answers by host and by run). A socket call whose ancestry measurement is not definite is logged once ("not a person, asked again next call"). test/ancestry-determinism.test.js: 50 concurrent CLI calls on a busy box, all classified alike.
- fix(daemon): SI-1 the development stand-in (surfaceAncestry) widens only for a named login server on a short system list (sshd, tmux, screen, login, the terminal apps) run from a system folder, never for any unknown: a setsid'd model whose parent is init stays no person. asTaken keeps the server it found.
- feat(signin): `signin.dev`, development builds only: with the stand-in file and a caller the daemon already counts as the owner, an ordinary cookie person session for the walk's browser node, marked "stand-in". Release builds refuse it.
- feat(signin): `vyre signin` and `vyre signout`. After LB-2 a CLI over ssh, in tmux or through `docker exec` is no person by label, so it signs in: `signin.ask` (from a terminal login the daemon measured), the phone signs `grant.cli_signin` (kernel `cliSigninPayload`/`cliSigninCheck`, the same sealing check as the rollback approval), and on a yes that terminal login holds a person session (new `cli` kind in presence_people, migration rebuilds the table; carried as the bearer header, signed by no key, pinned to node `cli:<login key>`, 30 days sliding). The credential is a 0600 file (`lib/cli-session.js`) the daemon client sends on cli calls. A model's shell (under a claude or a thread) has no login key, is relabelled `mcp` first, and can neither ask, read the status nor use a copied secret. Person-only refusals now say "Sign in with `vyre signin` (approve on your phone)". New module core/signin; module-sdk enum lists the daemon needs the loader hands out.
- fix(registry): every tool declares its `effect` (935 non-internal tools; the hygiene count of undeclared tools went from 906 to 4, the test's own) and a state-changing tool open to anyone declares `callers` where its body shows who calls it (one commit per module, branch work/kernel-declare). Group D fixes inside: onboard actions are personOnly (HD-1), threads.start takes an allow-list of keys from a model (HD-2), link.call refuses a module hop made for a model (HD-3), harness.enrich takes `interactive` from the hook's label only (HD-4), hands resolve a named agent from any label (HD-5), session push, undo and redo are the model's own session (HD-7), agents.ask stays inside the session's project (HD-9), team.charter.draft and revert are the person's (HD-10), memory.retrieve ignores a model's knobs. import.start sent `mode` and `plan` to sync.consent, which read neither: it now sends `planHash`.
- feat(0.3, app, install, 4 Oct): the install page's server step runs the real pairing for a device with no box (PairServer: starts the watch session, shows the three words, waits for the yes at the server); pair-direct sends the identity proof only when the server asks for it (core/wink adoptInput does not list `proof`, so a server set up for one identity can not be completed yet: tailnet); scripts/app-walk-claim.mjs walks claim then pair against a throwaway server (--code-cmd, --answer-cmd).
- feat(0.3, app, pairing, 4 Oct): a device that has only claimed an identity pairs a fresh server itself (serverSession uses relay/client/serverpair.js, tailnet's pairServer, when no box answers): the long code's 16-byte seed is redeemed at the relay, wink.server.adopt is called over the paired channel with this identity as owner, a proof signed by its key over box and device, and the three words from a commit-then-reveal; on the person's yes at the server the pairing is kept. Tests: test/wink.test.js "a device with no box pairs a fresh server" (tailnet).
- feat(0.3, walk, 4 Oct): scripts/app-walk-claim.mjs, the browser claims a name against a stand-in names directory in headless Chromium (4 of 4 on testbox, test build with rc.ts browserClaim flipped on a test copy). The two EXPO_PUBLIC flags read in InstallScreen and install.ts are now plain `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_...` reads: an optional-chained read is not inlined by the bundler and was always off in a browser.

- fix(0.3, app identity, 4 Oct; reviewer-3 identity-port): KP-3 the device key is kept and read back BEFORE the name is claimed (claimIdentity takes `beforeClaim`; a failed keep claims nothing; a failed claim takes the key back out, an unreachable directory leaves it). KP-1 (passkey for list changes) is waiting on the chain rule for web-class keys.

- fix(0.3, stream, 4 Oct): core/stream tests green on the trunk without force exit (issue #88). access.test.js: a person-reach call over the tailnet carries the person session the router sets. group-ks-live.test.js: stream.send and threads.start refuse keys they do not take (chat, asker), and a module hop names the origin. group.js: a delivery after a restart runs in no call, so it names its row's surface as the origin (ctx.events.withOrigin); before, juno's held words were refused as `threads.start is not available to module callers` and never delivered after a restart (group-live.test.js).
- perf(kernel): the event log's window read at open (the newest 2,000 events) used the subject index and sorted every event of the Space (0.5 to 1.3 s at 1.4 million events); it now walks the table from its end (`NOT INDEXED`). A restart over 1,403,744 events: 1,459 ms before, 726 ms after (testbox2, warm cache, load 1.8). Test: kernel/store/boot-perf.test.js asserts the plan.
- perf(kernel): a list or a search by a caller whose answer is the same for every row (`rowUniform`: the owner and admin on a type with no rule, room or privileged record) is one store call per page: no row is asked about and no second page is read to look ahead; the store's own cursor is the answer. A restricted caller is unchanged. Test: kernel/gateway/lookahead.test.js.
- feat(kernel): one transaction per record write. On the built-in store the record's change and its event commit together (one fsync instead of two) or not at all: `createUnit` (kernel/boot.js) gives writers turns at a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` held only across steps that wait on the microtask queue, the store's own commit is a SAVEPOINT that joins it, and the gateway commits after the event (and the record's kernel attributes). An event the database refuses rolls the record back with it and takes it out of memory (`store.undo`, also its unique-value index and change count); a failed commit does the same and says `unavailable`. The rollback wrappers stay as the safety net. Tests: kernel/store/unit-of-work.test.js (a SIGKILL between the two former commits leaves neither the record, its change entry nor its event; refused update, remove and create leave memory and disk in agreement; 60 concurrent writers), which fail on the two-commit code. write-bench (kernel/store/bench/write-bench.mjs), WAL and synchronous FULL, one writer: testbox4 about 290 to 450 writes a second before, 420 to 520 after; testbox3 120 to 170 before, 200 to 300 after. At 20 writers flat out the rate is set by CPU per write (about 2.5 ms), not by the fsync, and did not change.
- feat(kernel): the SQLite store scrubs a field sealed in place (`persist.scrub(type, fields)`, and `store.scrub` where the memory store has none): the field's keys leave `before` and `after` of every change-log entry of the type, the search index is rebuilt without them, and a VACUUM with `secure_delete` and a truncated write-ahead log leave no copy of the old values in the file. Test: kernel/store/sqlite.test.js (40 records with two versions each, bytes of the file and the log searched afterwards, another type's own copy untouched).
- test(kernel): a restart over 100,000 events must read by type prefix from the index and boot within 1,800 ms (kernel/store/boot-perf.test.js; the LIKE scan took 2,450 ms there, the range about 500 ms), and a prefix range must not match a neighbouring type (`grant-x.`, `grant_x.`, `grant0.`, `grants.`, `grantz.` are not under `grant.`).
- feat(kernel): PR-2. The form a Flow sends with a task (a proposal's diff, a Kit card) is bound into what the checker's presence proof covers: when a task has a `form`, `form_hash` (hash of the canonical form) is part of the body that `payload_hash` is taken over, for guarded decision tasks and outward sends alike. Tasks without a form hash as before. Test: kernel/tasks PR-2.
- fix(kernel): WF-2. The real send of an approved task runs before its event is written; if the event is refused the task goes back to waiting, and a second approval no longer sends again (the send is made once per task and payload, and the release is given the same `idem` key). Test: kernel/tasks WF-1 test now asserts one send.
- fix(kernel): RT-2 (per DESIGN-spaces-first: an admin sets policies short of ownership). Owner AND admin change standing rules with presence (`rules.set`, `.enable`, `.disable`, `.remove`, `.accept`, `.dismiss`); the store now accepts an admin where it refused all but the owner. Only an owner makes a rule that binds members over `grants.*`, `drive.restore` or `kits.*` (it could lock an owner out); an admin is refused that before a proof is spent, and a manager or member is refused every change at the gate. A rule switch no longer carries `switched_by`/`switched_at` (a rebuild from the log could not reproduce them). Tests: RT-2 and RT-1 in kernel/rules.test.js.
- fix(kernel): `ruleEnable` and `ruleDisable` join the grants store's one-at-a-time, restore-on-failure wrapper, so a switch whose event cannot be written leaves the rule as it was (test: R4 on rules.enable and rules.disable).
- feat(kernel): `rules.get`, `rules.test`, `rules.enable` and `rules.disable` on the rule store, and the app's `rules` module (core/rules-tools: `rules.list`, `.get`, `.define`, `.test`, `.enable`, `.disable`, `.remove`, `.propose`, `.accept`, `.dismiss`, one tool each under the caller's own chain). A rule can be switched off (status `disabled`, still listed, binds nothing, an event in the log) and on again by an owner with presence; `rules.test` says what the rules would do to an act (`outcome` never, always_ask, draft_only or none) for an assistant, a member or an assistant acting for a member, for one stored rule or a rule not yet made, and writes nothing. Time-window rules are 0.3.1.
- fix(daemon): a stop that arrives while vyred is still starting no longer exits at once and leaves a half-started daemon (socket, pid file); it waits for start to settle and then drains (core/daemon/main.js). main.js tells a supervisor or test that has an IPC channel when its stop handlers are on, and the SIGTERM-while-starting test counts from that message instead of a sleep, so a loaded box cannot kill the daemon before its handlers exist.
- fix(kernel): restart time. A read of the event log by type prefix (`grant.*`, `member.*`, ... which every store reads at boot) was `type LIKE ? ESCAPE`, which SQLite cannot serve from the type index, so each read scanned every event and parsed its JSON (about 13 s of a 100,000-event boot). It is now a range on the type index. Boot at 103,111 events: 4,064 ms before, 528 ms after (testbox4, node 22, one run each). Test: kernel/store/bounded.test.js.
- feat(kernel): the built-in store answers at 100,000 records. A query's equality and range comparisons are left bare where NULL and false agree, so a field index serves find by email and list by stage (they were wrapped in COALESCE and scanned the type); an unfiltered grouping has its own covering index; search has a trigram full-text index (sealed fields never indexed, built in slices on an older database) and ranks in SQL; a ranked search with one common word beside rare ones ("Client 4521") never reads the common word's postings. Every path is proven equal to the reference store on random queries and pages. BL-1: the event log's filter columns are generated from the event JSON. BL-3: a record's kernel attributes ride in its create event and the log wins over `kernel_attrs`.

- feat(kernel): the real registry has `kits.propose` (write), `kits.install` and `kits.remove` (admin) on `vyre://<space>/kit/<id>`; owner and admin hold them. An assistant acting for an owner or admin may propose; installing and removing are a person's act. Before this every Kit proposal failed `unknown_action`. Test: test/roles-enforced.test.js (kits).
- fix(sessions, review): HD-2 threads.start from a model's call takes declared fields only; HD-7 a model call pushes, undoes and redoes its own session's branch only (the assistant included); HD-9 agents.ask refuses a wider agent; HD-10 charter draft and revert are the person's; flows.start by an assistant's chain runs tainted; PR-1/3/4/5 proposals: admin non-doer checker, card recomputed from the stored draft, one application per task, no removals; ENG-2 the engineer name is reserved; the Flows service loses events.read; Recall counts a person's app-started thread as human whatever the driver.
- feat(sessions): adoption-safe person ids. The Switchboard reads a queued turn's asker, compares the running turn's asker, and accepts a new turn's asker through the kernel's `canonicalPerson` (module handle), and the daemon opens a kernel session for a stored or queued person id as the identity that replaced it. Test: core/switchboard/adopt.test.js (a thread started before adoption is still listed after a restart, a session for the old id opens).
- fix(daemon): `callerFacts`'s caller measurement was a `const ancestry` that shadowed the imported function used earlier in the same handler (a dead-zone error: `threads.bind` answered internal). Renamed.
- fix(test): the fake `claude` in sessions.test.js used `require` in a file node reads as a module; it now uses `process.getBuiltinModule`.
- fix(flows): pausing or resuming a Flow that was never defined stores nothing.
- feat(work): the work module registers the owner attribute for the `session` type (`needs.kernel.attrs`; `owner` and, for lines under a project, `project`, nothing else), so the kernel's owner-scoped session reads (work/kernel-reg, KW-1) answer the owner on this module's own sessions. Merged work/kernel-reg. `projects.of` declares effect read: under the registry's write default a module hop with no person behind it was refused, so Recall could not name the session's project.
- fix(work): reviewer-2's KW-1 to KW-4. A session's lines are the owner's: reading, windowing and searching them needs the owner role in the chain's first hop as well as `records.read` on the record (a member, manager or admin who is not the owner gets nothing; lines are withheld in a room of more than one person). KW-3: a shared suggestion shows only to someone who may read every source it cites. KW-2: a fact that needs a task, proposed under the read-only viewer chain, is kept as a private suggestion instead of throwing. KW-4: `work.know.capture` and `.forget` need the registry's `firstParty` flag. reviewer-2's repro is core/work/memory/rv2-know-lines.test.js.
- feat(work,recall): capture takes the session's project. Recall resolves the session's folder with `projects.of` and passes `project` to `work.know.capture`; the work module keeps the lines under `vyre://<space>/project/<slug>`, so a teammate granted the project reads its sessions (know-daemon test now grants the project, not a session). A bad project name falls back to the session's own address.
- fix(harness): HD-4b, `interactive` needs the person behind the call (with the kernel on, the call's chain: one person, no agent, viewer or delegated hop; the `harness` label only as SHIM(legacy labels) with the kernel off) AND the session transcript's last user line equal to the prompt, so a model in a person's terminal cannot answer its own lesson. reviewer-2's repro is core/harness/rv2-hd4b.test.js.
- fix(recall): `stop()` threw a TypeError (it called the folder helper `within` with a promise), so the embedder's child process was never closed and the daemon, and every test that started one, never exited. This is why full-suite runs and core/recall/embed-install.test.js hung. The embedder is now closed in a `finally`; embed-install asserts no process is left.
- feat(work): Space memory runs on a real daemon with the kernel on (the work port from work/kernel-work-handle, Recall's capture from work/flows). A call whose chain names no chat is one to one (no audience lookup). Real-daemon test core/work/know-daemon.test.js: a session is indexed, a teammate recalls its decision in a later session with the line address, another project's teammate gets nothing, the SSN is nowhere.
- fix(memory): the gate asks the kernel's `canonicalPerson` before the membership check, so a session token minted before owner adoption is still the owner's. Memory and Recall key nothing by person id, so their data survives adoption unchanged. Seed, adopt, still-recalled test in core/memory/adopt-recall.test.js.
- fix(harness): HD-4, `harness.enrich` takes `interactive` only from the hook's own `harness` label with no Vyre thread behind the call and a session that is not headless, so a session can no longer accept its own lesson with `interactive:true, prompt:"yes"`. Attack test in core/harness/enrich-interactive.test.js.
- fix(memory): HD-8, `memory.remember` from a session or agent is an untrusted, attributed write in the `you` room (pending), never a told claim at 0.95, so it stays out of the profile, brief and prompt lines. Attack test in core/memory/remember-poison.test.js.
- feat(memory): SD-3, `memory.sealscan {ledger: true}` asks the sealing process about candidate values in memory's held text, one candidate per call, a few at a time, and reports table and column and row counts only. `ctx.kernel.sealDetect(chain, value)` is the kernel's side (a module that declares `needs.kernel.sealDetect`; the module name is the registry's, a record the chain may not read counts for nothing, one owner-visible `seal.detect` event per answer without the candidate). Tested on the real sealing process (kernel/seal-detect.real.test.js) and a real daemon (core/memory/sealscan-daemon.test.js). The daemon takes `opts.kernelSealer` for tests.
- fix(team): `recheckParent` now says `parent_narrowed` when the owner narrowed the adder's grant so it no longer contains the teammate's grant; the kernel already refused such a child, the teammate looked active. New role-cap tests on the real kernel (core/work/team/role-cap.test.js).
- test(memory): a teammate's new session is given the decision the person typed in an earlier one, on a real vyred (core/memory/teammate-recall-daemon.test.js).
- feat(recall): sealed-class shapes (SSN, card, bank, IBAN, EIN and the rest) never stay in the transcript index. New turns, titles and names are scrubbed on the way in (only the matched span becomes a placeholder, so a later pass still compares equal). `recall.sealscan` reports table, column, rows and class for what is stored, plus how many vectors were made from those turns, never a value. `recall.sealscrub` (the person's surfaces only, with presence) rewrites only the matched spans, drops the vectors of a changed turn, tells the dense index to rebuild, merges the full-text segments and keeps one log row of counts and classes. No new migration, no stored row outside a match changes.
- feat(0.3, sessions): the Engineer, built in. `agents.list` shows `engineer` (`builtin`, `proposes_only`, its `tools`); it cannot be deleted, renamed, given projects, credentials or a computer. Its session reaches a short list of tools and no others: `agents.scope` hands vyred an `only` list from the stored row, vyred puts it on the call's meta as `agentOnly`, and the registry refuses anything else. It drafts (`flows.define` stores an unapproved version) and proposes: new tool `flows.propose { what: "flow", id, version }` or `{ what: "types", diff }` makes ONE task in Now (`form.kind: "proposal"`) with the approver as checker and the Flows service as doer; only after the kernel has the approver's yes does the change apply, as the approver (kernel/flows/proposals.js). `flows.kit.propose` now accepts a person's assistant (the person is the approver); `flows.approve`, `flows.kit.remove`, pause and resume stay a person's own.
- fix(flows): the flows module declared `needs.kernel.actions: []`, which reinstalled the service grant the Flows host made with no actions, so every Flow write on a real vyred was refused (`no such record`). The module now declares the same actions as the host, plus `tasks.work` (the Flows service starts and completes the tasks it asks). The host gains `forDoer`.
- fix(switchboard): BR-2 for the Switchboard. The keyboard holder, an owner device's right to answer a Mac's ask, and the person's own surface come from the call's kernel chain (`ctx.kernel.chain(meta)`), never from a `tailnet:`/`device:` label; a build with no kernel keeps the label rule, marked SHIM(legacy labels). FROZEN count for core/switchboard/index.js is gone.
- feat(recall): the capture port. After Recall indexes a batch of a session's turns (already scrubbed) it hands the same lines once to `work.know.capture` (chunks of 2000), `work.know.forget` first when a transcript was rewritten, and when a session is deleted (`thread.deleted`) or forgotten. No work module, or a refusal, never fails an index pass.
- fix(0.3, onboard): HD-1 again, as a guard in the tools: onboard.claude, .name (not check or status), .tailscale (not status), .history start and .finish refuse a model client and any other module, and need the person's presence once the box has an owner (core/onboard/owner-write.test.js). The module.json reach change is reverted: the loopback onboarding page's caller ("onboard") is not a reach-person caller.
- feat(0.3, box): rollback approval through the owner's phone (modules.list.reset.ask, then status polled every 2 s; refused, none or no answer changes nothing). `vyre admin anchor-reset` runs kernel-2's script with the request line and the pasted proof on the terminal. The daemon serves /.well-known/apple-app-site-association and assetlinks.json when VYRE_APPLE_TEAM_ID and VYRE_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256 are set. scripts/install/i.sh --from uses the checkout's own installer. ci: rc-dry-run (release-dist, packaged-boot, update-refusals, cosign-refusals as one dispatch).
- fix(0.3, box): PF-1 each publish-fill container step has a time limit and a fixed name (removed on timeout, the queue moves on); PF-2 the claimed folder is deleted, never moved back through the daemon's path. MW-5: sw.js and manifest.webmanifest are listed in the signed appbuild.json (made at package time from the same inputs) and the daemon serves them only when they match. The pairing line names the device when the app sends `deviceName` in wink.server.adopt.
- fix(0.3, onboard): HD-1 onboard.claude, .name, .tailscale, .finish and .history are reach person (no presence: setup runs before any owner exists). system.build is reach person.
- feat(0.3, box): `sudo vyre admin anchor-reset` (AN-1), offline, with a consequence line; the wrapper half. It runs scripts/admin-anchor-reset.mjs from kernel and vault and refuses plainly while that script is not in the image. A container whose config says machine device or solo now stops with a plain error (box-only units were silently off); packaged-boot checks it.
- fix(0.3, build): DP-1 the release stamp cannot fail open. `scripts/stamp-build-kind.mjs` (run by build-site.sh) stops the build unless lib/build-kind.js says release afterwards; kernel/devbuild.js and the stamp share the two lines in lib/build-kind-text.js; packaged-boot checks the packed tree and the running image say release and honour no developer switch. ci: node runs in five shards; heavy workflows run only on main, work/v0.3, work/launch-* and their owners' branches or by dispatch.
- fix(0.3, cli): `vyre up` on a box waits (up to a minute) for `onboard.link` when the daemon answers before its modules have all started, instead of ending the install with "no tool onboard.link" (update-refusals J2b hit it on the full signed module list).
- fix(0.3, box): `vyre uninstall` removes the Space helper's units (path, service and the watcher) and keeps the wrapper until they are gone; found on a real box, where the watcher kept running after the wrapper was deleted.
- feat(0.3, box): the Space helper's `publish-fill` verb (reviewer-3's conditions): `publish-fill <space id> <site folder> <deployment>`, three tokens each from its own anchored pattern, never a path or a volume name. Root claims the daemon's site folder by rename into its own folder, walks it (plain files and folders only, no second hard link, a size cap, a link swapped in after the check is a link and refused), copies it with a throwaway container (no network, the folder read-only, two capabilities, the vyre image by id) into a volume whose name it rebuilds, runs a fixed check on the volume (a volume that fails is removed), and puts the folder back.
- fix(0.3, box): SH-4 the firewall marker names this start of the vyre container (`<id> <start time>`) and is removed when it dies or stops; SH-5 the entry fails closed when the helper is installed and its subnet list is missing, and an `up` is refused when the container does not mount the helper's state folder.
- fix(0.3, release): the installer and `vyre update` fetch `appbuild.json` with the other signed files, so a packaged box can serve the web app (it answered 503 app_build_unsigned). appbuild.json now carries the release counter and a tree hash; the daemon's `system.build` tool returns it with SHA256SUMS and its signature for the Mac window's check (MW-5).
- feat(0.3, wink): `wink.server.pairing` answers `{ asking: false, paired: true, owner }` once the server has an owner (a name in words), and the installer's closing line names the space.
- fix(sessions, review): HD-2 threads.start from a model's call takes declared fields only; HD-7 a model call pushes, undoes and redoes its own session's branch only (the assistant included); HD-9 agents.ask refuses a wider agent; HD-10 charter draft and revert are the person's; flows.start by an assistant's chain runs tainted; PR-1/3/4/5 proposals: admin non-doer checker, card recomputed from the stored draft, one application per task, no removals; ENG-2 the engineer name is reserved; the Flows service loses events.read; Recall counts a person's app-started thread as human whatever the driver.
- feat(sessions): adoption-safe person ids. The Switchboard reads a queued turn's asker, compares the running turn's asker, and accepts a new turn's asker through the kernel's `canonicalPerson` (module handle), and the daemon opens a kernel session for a stored or queued person id as the identity that replaced it. Test: core/switchboard/adopt.test.js (a thread started before adoption is still listed after a restart, a session for the old id opens).
- fix(daemon): `callerFacts`'s caller measurement was a `const ancestry` that shadowed the imported function used earlier in the same handler (a dead-zone error: `threads.bind` answered internal). Renamed.
- fix(test): the fake `claude` in sessions.test.js used `require` in a file node reads as a module; it now uses `process.getBuiltinModule`.
- fix(flows): pausing or resuming a Flow that was never defined stores nothing.
- feat(0.3, sessions): the Engineer, built in. `agents.list` shows `engineer` (`builtin`, `proposes_only`, its `tools`); it cannot be deleted, renamed, given projects, credentials or a computer. Its session reaches a short list of tools and no others: `agents.scope` hands vyred an `only` list from the stored row, vyred puts it on the call's meta as `agentOnly`, and the registry refuses anything else. It drafts (`flows.define` stores an unapproved version) and proposes: new tool `flows.propose { what: "flow", id, version }` or `{ what: "types", diff }` makes ONE task in Now (`form.kind: "proposal"`) with the approver as checker and the Flows service as doer; only after the kernel has the approver's yes does the change apply, as the approver (kernel/flows/proposals.js). `flows.kit.propose` now accepts a person's assistant (the person is the approver); `flows.approve`, `flows.kit.remove`, pause and resume stay a person's own.
- fix(flows): the flows module declared `needs.kernel.actions: []`, which reinstalled the service grant the Flows host made with no actions, so every Flow write on a real vyred was refused (`no such record`). The module now declares the same actions as the host, plus `tasks.work` (the Flows service starts and completes the tasks it asks). The host gains `forDoer`.
- fix(switchboard): BR-2 for the Switchboard. The keyboard holder, an owner device's right to answer a Mac's ask, and the person's own surface come from the call's kernel chain (`ctx.kernel.chain(meta)`), never from a `tailnet:`/`device:` label; a build with no kernel keeps the label rule, marked SHIM(legacy labels). FROZEN count for core/switchboard/index.js is gone.
- feat(recall): the capture port. After Recall indexes a batch of a session's turns (already scrubbed) it hands the same lines once to `work.know.capture` (chunks of 2000), `work.know.forget` first when a transcript was rewritten, and when a session is deleted (`thread.deleted`) or forgotten. No work module, or a refusal, never fails an index pass.
- feat(0.3, box): the Space helper, the root side of a Space's Twenty store. A root path unit on a spool vyred can only add `req-<id>` files to; five fixed verbs (up, stop, down, firewall-add, firewall-del) parsed whole from a claimed copy; secrets made and kept by root; the compose regenerated in the recorded image and linted; the vyre container joined to the Space's network and the agent firewall rule put into its own namespace BEFORE the store starts, then proved with an agent-uid refusal and a daemon-uid control, and re-applied after every update. `purge` and `fscrypt-enable` are `sudo vyre admin` only, with a typed word. box/vyre, scripts/install-box.sh, box/compose.yml, docs/work/space-helper.md, test/space-helper.test.js.
- fix(0.3, release): `vyre update` checks every module the signed list names by name after the new container is up (running or off; failed or missing rolls the update back).
- 0.3 install (launch): the box has no Tailscale sidecar. compose.yml is vyred and the docker-api proxy; vyred owns its network and publishes the onboarding page on host loopback; the image ships the pinned Wink core binaries at /opt/vyre-wink/bin (VYRE_WINK_CORE_BIN, VYRE_WINK_CLI_BIN) and the compose sets VYRE_SEAL_PROFILE=server. install-box.sh drops the TUN check, adds a memory and disk preflight (how many spaces fit the larger store, from the one constant that matches stores/twenty REQUIRE.memoryMb), and writes VYRE_KERNEL=1 and VYRE_STORE=auto into vyre.env once. The wrapper no longer starts or mentions Tailscale. compose.egress.yml is untouched (platform's row).
- feat(wink): the asker at the server reads `Alex (alex.vyre.run)` (display name and the directory-verified Vyre name, `createWink({ vyreName })`); no Vyre name known: `Alex (id aaaaaa)`; a look-alike display name is dropped; never a raw `per_` id. New internal `wink.server.paired { device, identity }` (modules only): is that device a server still paired to this identity.
- feat(wink): a device with no box of its own pairs a fresh server (`relay/client/serverpair.js`, `pairServer`): it redeems the server's wink/2 code over the relay, shows the three words, and on the person's pick at the server the claimed identity and its name become the owner. A server owned by an identity says that identity's name (not "Personal", "You" or "your space").
- feat(records): `TypeDefinition.kind` ("project"), carried by define, the SDK, the compiler and both stores; `contact_point` core type (one unique record per further address) with `addContactPoint` and a `findContact` fallback; Twenty's timeline is switched off (`isAuditLogged: false`) on every Vyre object when the Twenty offers it; `records.linked` (the reverse of a link across types, permission-checked, capped); `records/kits/library.js` lists and loads the Kits this build ships (`kitLibrary`, `kitFromLibrary`); native group-by accepts money sub-field measures.
- feat(records): contacts, roles and field switches. Core types `contact` (main email and phone unique, other addresses in lists), `organization`, `communication` (one per connector item, `source_key` unique) and `participant` in every Space; a Kit may add fields to a core type (the estate Kit's contact now carries only its own fields: `name` replaces `full_name`). A type is a role with `role: { link, ended }`; gateway `roles(holder)`, `holders({ role, stage })`, `merge`/`unmerge` (join, relink, one `records.merged` event, undo) and `records/comms/log.js` (`logCommunication`, `findContact`, `timelineOf`). Field switches: `hidden` (removed softly, data kept), `hidden_from` roles, `computed` (an Expression or a total over linked records; `days_since` and `round` added to the Expression language), and `migrate.sealField` (plain values move through `seal.put`, the plain field goes, the old values are scrubbed from the change log, snapshots, Twenty's timeline and the event log). Search no longer finds a record through a field outside the caller's limit.
- feat(records): conformance revision 5 and no row cap on totals: the gateway's aggregate and the Twenty store fold page by page (`createAggregator`), so the 20,000-row refusal is gone. Real Twenty v2.44.0: 32 of 32. Fixed live: Twenty's unique index keeps soft-deleted rows, so a removed record kept its value; the store now holds a removed record's unique values aside and gives them back on restore. A real vyred on a real Twenty sealed a field end to end (team/0.3/E2E-RUN.md step 6).
- feat(spaces): `spaces.devices.lend` is the one switch for sharing a computer: on makes the kernel's compute offers in that Space (the space's side when the person is an owner or admin, and the member's own side bound to the computer) under the person's chain in that Space; off withdraws them; the stored record (first_grant_at, allowed_by) is the one fact. `spaces.compute.*` stays as the module-local pair. Test on the real kernel (test/one-registry.test.js).
- fix(kernel): the development presence stand-in threw `ReferenceError: isChain is not defined` (not imported), so every stand-in proof failed closed; fixed. It now also works where the kernel has no verifier of its own (a hosted Space on a file key), and a hosted Space's kernel receives the home's stand-in (`bootOptions`).
- fix(kernel): restart time. A read of the event log by type prefix (`grant.*`, `member.*`, ... which every store reads at boot) was `type LIKE ? ESCAPE`, which SQLite cannot serve from the type index, so each read scanned every event and parsed its JSON (about 13 s of a 100,000-event boot). It is now a range on the type index. Boot at 103,111 events: 4,064 ms before, 528 ms after (testbox4, node 22, one run each). Test: kernel/store/bounded.test.js.
- feat(kernel): the built-in store answers at 100,000 records. A query's equality and range comparisons are left bare where NULL and false agree, so a field index serves find by email and list by stage (they were wrapped in COALESCE and scanned the type); an unfiltered grouping has its own covering index; search has a trigram full-text index (sealed fields never indexed, built in slices on an older database) and ranks in SQL; a ranked search with one common word beside rare ones ("Client 4521") never reads the common word's postings. Every path is proven equal to the reference store on random queries and pages. BL-1: the event log's filter columns are generated from the event JSON. BL-3: a record's kernel attributes ride in its create event and the log wins over `kernel_attrs`.

- feat(kernel): the real registry has `kits.propose` (write), `kits.install` and `kits.remove` (admin) on `vyre://<space>/kit/<id>`; owner and admin hold them. An assistant acting for an owner or admin may propose; installing and removing are a person's act. Before this every Kit proposal failed `unknown_action`. Test: test/roles-enforced.test.js (kits).
- fix(kernel): WF-1 on `records.define`: a type definition whose `types.defined` event the log refuses is put back (a new type removed, a changed type restored), so a defined type never stands without its line in the log. Test: kernel/gateway/define-wf1.test.js on both stores.
- fix(kernel): WF-1 on tasks. A task changed in memory before its event was written, so an event the log refused left an approval (or a start, or a new task) live while the caller was told it failed. A task now goes back to what it was when its event cannot be written (`pending` in kernel/tasks/tasks.js; the approval record and the body are set or dropped only after the event). The grants store already restores on a failed write (R4); the sweep of the other stores found nothing else that sets state before a refused write: room writes the event first, records use an intent journal with recovery, the rest are best-effort audit notes.
- feat(spaces): `spaces.devices.list` (the Device screen's list: enrolled and lent per space), `spaces.devices.lend { space, device, on }` and `spaces.devices.lend.status`. Lending a computer is a record on the home (the module's own table, kept across restarts), not a screen setting. The person's presence (Face ID) is asked only for the first grant for a device in a space; stopping never asks, and turning it on again after a first grant does not. Only the person whose device it is may lend it (it is on their identity list); an owner of the space may stop a lent device. Event `space.device-lent`.
- fix(spaces): the claimed identity is adopted as the home kernel's owner right after the claiming call and at module start (single-flight, slot cleared after the promise is stored), not only at the next spaces call; Spaces are hosted for the identity id. Proven on testbox3 on a fresh home and on an existing home that claimed before the kernel ran.
- feat(names): CORS for the browser app. `GET /v1/ids/resolve` answers any origin (read-only, no credentials); `POST /v1/ids/claim`, `/append` and `/update` (self-proving) also accept the origins in `APP_ORIGINS` (default https://app.vyre.run) and answer that exact origin; every other state-changing route still refuses a foreign Origin; the per-IP claim limit applies. `scripts/standin-directory.mjs --app-origins` sets them for the test server's stand-in. The live names directory is NOT redeployed by this change (lead's go needed).
- fix(kernel): a manager no longer holds `records.define`. Changing the Space's types is Customize (admin and owner, ROLE_BUNDLES `customize.definitions`); the role table gave it to managers. `test/roles-enforced.test.js` holds each role's grants to its bundle on the real kernel (who holds which action, who may make whom, temp scope, and a temp's end at the expiry with no sweep, extension, no self-extension).
- feat(publish): the box end of the Publish tunnel. `lib/publish/tunnel.js`: `createTunnelEnd` carries each stream the relay transport hands it to Caddy's loopback port (fixed, never named by the relay), reads only the first TLS record to find the SNI and refuses a name that is not the Space's (own domains from the directory's verified list), with limits per stream (idle, lifetime, bytes, hello wait) and per edge (open streams); TLS stays end to end. `edgeCompose(..., { tunnel: true })` publishes Caddy's 443 on `127.0.0.1:18443` only; `caddyfile(..., { tunnel: true })` drops the redirect listener. TCP only, no HTTP/3 through the tunnel.
- refactor(spaces): `kperson` removed; platform's `adoptOwner` makes the kernel's owner the claimed identity.
- fix(publish): SW-1 (reviewer-3). The site-folder sweep never touches a folder younger than an hour: a preview writes its folder before its record exists, so a second preview at the same time used to take it. Test: four previews at once keep four folders.
- feat(spaces,kernel): one space id, the kernel's (`spc_` plus 12 base32). `spaces.create` hosts the Space in the kernel's Spaces registry first (the kernel handle gains `spaces: { storePlan, host }` for a module that declares `needs.kernel.spaces`), takes its id, and fails the step if the kernel or the store attach fails; the kernel's first owner is the person it knows (`owner`), so records and tasks work in the new Space under the caller's chain in that Space (`chainIn`). `membership` answers for any Space this home hosts. Publish's `SPACE_RE` is exactly `/^spc_[a-z2-7]{12}$/`. A device with no enrolment list is enrolled in a Space this module has no row for. Test: test/one-registry.test.js on a real daemon (create, records.types/create/list, tasks.list, records.me).
- fix(publish): FF-1 and FS-2 (reviewer-3). A deployment record keeps only the NAME of its site folder; `publish.edge` rebuilds the path under the space's own sites folder and uses it only if the name is `site-XXXXXX` and the folder is a real directory (not a link), ours, mode 0700, and `volumeFill` takes only such a folder directly under that root, so an edited record cannot point the copy at /etc or the secrets folder. Site folders no live deployment names (retired, superseded, left by a refused build) are removed on each new build and each edge write, and the total is capped at 50.
- feat(publish): the product call for the site volume (PW-3). When a static build previews, its checked files are written by `writeSiteFiles` into a private folder under the space's publish folder (the deployment records it), and `publish.edge` returns `fills`: for each live static site, the docker call (`volumeFill`) that copies that folder into the site's volume; the box runs it. A hand-off with a link is refused (`bad_output`) and writes nothing; module-level test.
- fix(publish): EG-1 and the volume writer (reviewer-3). `egress` must be absent or false (any other value, "yes" included, refuses the workload), every workload setting is type-checked, a deployment description refuses any key it does not define, and the generated compose is refused if a workload joins the egress bridge. The site volume is filled only by `lib/publish/site-write.js`: the checked file list is written into a fresh folder one file at a time with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` (nothing a builder made as a directory is copied or extracted), then copied into the empty volume by a throwaway no-network container (`volumeFill`); a file and a folder of one name, and case or Unicode twins, are refused. Replaces the tar of the previous commit.

Real Twenty v2.44.0: 32 of 32. - fix(kernel): WF-1 on `records.define`: a type definition whose `types.defined` event the log refuses is put back (a new type removed, a changed type restored), so a defined type never stands without its line in the log. Test: kernel/gateway/define-wf1.test.js on both stores.

A task now goes back to what it was when its event cannot be written (`pending` in kernel/tasks/tasks.js; the approval record and the body are set or dropped only after the event). - fix(wink): `wink.server.adopt` declares `proof` (the registry refuses undeclared input, which broke every server pairing on the dev box). reviewer-3 SP-1: an owner id must have an id's shape (`per_` or `spc_` and base32), and a proof offered with no --pair-to is checked against the claimed identity; `pairServer` takes `signIdentity` to make that proof. SP-2: the owner name is reduced to letters, digits and `. _ @ : -` when stored as well as when shown, and the installer strips control bytes from the line it prints. `wink.server.code` with no typed code says "cannot reach its relay" at once (6 s at most) instead of hanging. test/declared-inputs.test.js checks that every input a wink, relay, link or network tool reads in its own body is declared.
- feat(wink): the asker at the server reads `Alex (alex.vyre.run)` (display name and the directory-verified Vyre name, `createWink({ vyreName })`); no Vyre name known: `Alex (id aaaaaa)`; a look-alike display name is dropped; never a raw `per_` id. New internal `wink.server.paired { device, identity }` (modules only): is that device a server still paired to this identity.
- feat(wink): a device with no box of its own pairs a fresh server (`relay/client/serverpair.js`, `pairServer`): it redeems the server's wink/2 code over the relay, shows the three words, and on the person's pick at the server the claimed identity and its name become the owner. A server owned by an identity says that identity's name (not "Personal", "You" or "your space").
- fix(link): HD-3, `link.call` declares `callers` (the person's surfaces and modules), so a model or an agent can no longer forward a box tool as the owner's device.
- feat(relay): the relay half of the Publish tunnel (relay/node/tunnel.js, `createRelay({ tunnel: { resolve } })`, `relay.listenTunnel()`). Public TLS on 443 is read for one SNI name (16 KB, 5 s, no IP literal, no split hello), looked up in the directory (cached 60 s, re-asked every 30 s and a stream whose name stops resolving to its route is closed), and piped to the box over a data socket the box opens, announced by a `tunnel` control message that carries the name and the visitor's address (never in the bytes). Port 80 is a fixed redirect and never reaches a box. Per-address, per-route and total caps; slots are freed however a stream ends. The box's link (core/relay/link.js) hands a stream to `ctx.tunnelEnd.accept(stream, { host, ip, port })` (a new `needs.daemon` name, `tunnelEnd`, for the daemon to provide). Not live: nothing starts the listeners yet, and the directory's name-to-route answer is not built.
- feat(identity): KP-1, the web-key rule in the identity chain (kernel/identity/chain.js, re-pinned). An entry with `held: "web"` (a key a script on a web origin can reach) may sign its own genesis and nothing else about the list: no add, remove, replace-code or space-owner change, whatever its age. A new entry kind, a passkey (`alg: "webauthn-es256"`, a P-256 key and its `rp`), signs each op with a WebAuthn assertion that must carry user presence and verification, name that op (the challenge is SHA-256 of the op's message), and come from its own rp and https origin. The directory Worker and every home run the same file. Needs reviewer-3's gate before the pin stands.
- fix(relay,wink,daemon): reviewer-3 round. Only a browser's offered passkey is enrolled at pairing (a phone keeps its device key); a browser (`web:`) reads its own row of `relay.devices.list` only (PA-4); `setup:`, `web:`, `space:` and the bare class words are not socket labels (LB-1b); the setup page's sign-in is asked by its channel, never a person (LB-2); a reset counts a hosted Space's events as data (DS-1); the question at the server carries the first characters of the identity id beside the claimed name (PA-2); the installer says "Connected to <space>. Finish setting up on your <device>." once the server is owned and warns that a printed code can reach a screen share or a log (PA-3).
- fix(modules): the pairing steps a device takes before it has any person session (`wink.server.adopt`, `wink.server.release`, `wink.phone.wait`, `relay.setup.claim`, `relay.devices.path`, `presence.person.status`) are exempt from the `reach: person` session rule that landed with the kernel merge; each checks its own caller.
- fix(relay): BR-2, the relay listener's caller label is the trust claim. `device:<id>` goes only to a live device of kind app; a browser is `web:<id>` and a setup page `setup:<id>`; any other kind gets no channel. A `web:` caller is none of the person's classes: a tool that lists callers (every `person` tool) does not exist for it unless it names `web` (`relay.devices.ask-trust`, `relay.devices.list`, `relay.web.release` do); tools open to anyone stay open. A trusted browser therefore reaches no person tool until a web reach class is designed (the relay limits lift, nothing more). The setup page keeps its own name list (the relay's setup gate), and names and tailscale accept `setup:` where they accepted its old device label.
- fix(wink): one identity. Wink's owner id is read live from the spaces module (`spaces.identity.self`, internal), the identity claimed through the names directory; a box with none falls back to the route-derived id. `wink.pair.targets` and `spaces.identity.status` report the same id (test/identity-one.test.js, real daemon and stand-in directory).
- feat(relay): `relay.devices.list` carries `storage` (hardware | software | unknown, the app's own report) for the Devices line. `wink.server.status` tells the installer who owns the server and which device paired it.
- fix(wink): removal of a device and a reset await `presence.person.end-paired` and fail when it cannot, leaving the owner and the device in place. `network.wink.status` and `.whois` name their callers (the person's surfaces, devices, modules), so a model session cannot call them.
- fix(wink): a reset where presence is missing (`no_such_tool`) now fails closed like any other failure to end the paired sessions, never "nothing to end".
- fix(presence): `presence.person.start-paired`, `pair-challenge` and `rotate` declare `callers: ["tailnet", "relay", "device"]` (a paired phone's relay or tailnet channel), so no model, guest or MCP caller reaches them (platform's golden refresh).
- fix(wink, presence): end paths of a paired person session. A recovery reset now AWAITS `presence.person.end-paired` for every device before it forgets anything, and fails (`unavailable`, nothing reset, the code still good) if presence cannot end them; a box with no presence module has none to end. Removing a presence key also deletes the pending pair grants it confirmed (PS-4). `presence.person.sessions` called by a paired session lists only that session. Tests: core/wink/reset.test.js, core/presence/presence.test.js, test/wink.test.js (revoke, sign-out-everywhere, owner-key removal with a really enrolled key, sessions scope).
- test(wink): two more end paths of a paired person session on a real vyred and kernel (test/wink.test.js): a revoked session id is gone at once, and sign-out-everywhere (`presence.person.end-paired` with no device, module:wink only) ends it while any other caller is refused. Shared setup `pairedOnKernel`.
- feat(daemon): on a development build whose home holds the hand-made `dev-presence-stand-in` file, a surface label (cli, local, deck, mobile) that is not inside a model counts as the signed-in owner (surfaceAncestry), so a CLI at a terminal over ssh can seed and walk a dev box after LB-2; a release-kind build ignores the file, and a model's shell is still relabelled `mcp`.
- fix(daemon): LB-2 a person's-surface label on the socket becomes a person chain only when the ancestry was read to the top and is definitely outside (`outside` from asTaken, passed to callerFacts). A named server above the caller (tmux, ssh), an unreadable process table, a `docker exec` and a platform that cannot read peers (Windows) give no person facts: such a call is a person only with a person session. test/label-ancestry.test.js covers each; it is on the Windows list.
- fix(kernel): WF-1 on `records.define`: a type definition whose `types.defined` event the log refuses is put back (a new type removed, a changed type restored), so a defined type never stands without its line in the log. Test: kernel/gateway/define-wf1.test.js on both stores.
- fix(kernel): WF-1 on tasks. A task changed in memory before its event was written, so an event the log refused left an approval (or a start, or a new task) live while the caller was told it failed. A task now goes back to what it was when its event cannot be written (`pending` in kernel/tasks/tasks.js; the approval record and the body are set or dropped only after the event). The grants store already restores on a failed write (R4); the sweep of the other stores found nothing else that sets state before a refused write: room writes the event first, records use an intent journal with recovery, the rest are best-effort audit notes.
- feat(spaces): `spaces.devices.lend` is the one switch for sharing a computer: on makes the kernel's compute offers in that Space (the space's side when the person is an owner or admin, and the member's own side bound to the computer) under the person's chain in that Space; off withdraws them; the stored record (first_grant_at, allowed_by) is the one fact. `spaces.compute.*` stays as the module-local pair. Test on the real kernel (test/one-registry.test.js).
- fix(kernel): the development presence stand-in threw `ReferenceError: isChain is not defined` (not imported), so every stand-in proof failed closed; fixed. It now also works where the kernel has no verifier of its own (a hosted Space on a file key), and a hosted Space's kernel receives the home's stand-in (`bootOptions`).
- feat(kernel): the work port. A first-party module that declares `needs.kernel.work` (core/work) gets `chainFor` (the call's own person chain, never the service chain), `chainForPerson` (a member's viewer chain plus the module's service hop, read only), `serviceChain`, `ask`, `definitions`, `actions`, `members` and `tasks.list/forRecord`, from the kernel's own pieces. Fix: `appendService` now keeps the `viewer` flag, so a service hop after a viewer chain no longer lifts its read-only limit.
- fix(kernel): restart time. A read of the event log by type prefix (`grant.*`, `member.*`, ... which every store reads at boot) was `type LIKE ? ESCAPE`, which SQLite cannot serve from the type index, so each read scanned every event and parsed its JSON (about 13 s of a 100,000-event boot). It is now a range on the type index. Boot at 103,111 events: 4,064 ms before, 528 ms after (testbox4, node 22, one run each). Test: kernel/store/bounded.test.js.
- feat(kernel): the built-in store answers at 100,000 records. A query's equality and range comparisons are left bare where NULL and false agree, so a field index serves find by email and list by stage (they were wrapped in COALESCE and scanned the type); an unfiltered grouping has its own covering index; search has a trigram full-text index (sealed fields never indexed, built in slices on an older database) and ranks in SQL; a ranked search with one common word beside rare ones ("Client 4521") never reads the common word's postings. Every path is proven equal to the reference store on random queries and pages. BL-1: the event log's filter columns are generated from the event JSON. BL-3: a record's kernel attributes ride in its create event and the log wins over `kernel_attrs`.

- feat(kernel): the real registry has `kits.propose` (write), `kits.install` and `kits.remove` (admin) on `vyre://<space>/kit/<id>`; owner and admin hold them. An assistant acting for an owner or admin may propose; installing and removing are a person's act. Before this every Kit proposal failed `unknown_action`. Test: test/roles-enforced.test.js (kits).
