It now also works where the kernel has no verifier of its own (a hosted Space on a file key), and a hosted Space's kernel receives the home's stand-in (`bootOptions`).
- feat(spaces): `spaces.devices.list` (the Device screen's list: enrolled and lent per space), `spaces.devices.lend { space, device, on }` and `spaces.devices.lend.status`. Lending a computer is a record on the home (the module's own table, kept across restarts), not a screen setting. The person's presence (Face ID) is asked only for the first grant for a device in a space; stopping never asks, and turning it on again after a first grant does not. Only the person whose device it is may lend it (it is on their identity list); an owner of the space may stop a lent device. Event `space.device-lent`.
- fix(spaces): the claimed identity is adopted as the home kernel's owner right after the claiming call and at module start (single-flight, slot cleared after the promise is stored), not only at the next spaces call; Spaces are hosted for the identity id. Proven on testbox3 on a fresh home and on an existing home that claimed before the kernel ran.
- feat(names): CORS for the browser app. `GET /v1/ids/resolve` answers any origin (read-only, no credentials); `POST /v1/ids/claim`, `/append` and `/update` (self-proving) also accept the origins in `APP_ORIGINS` (default https://app.vyre.run) and answer that exact origin; every other state-changing route still refuses a foreign Origin; the per-IP claim limit applies. `scripts/standin-directory.mjs --app-origins` sets them for the test server's stand-in. The live names directory is NOT redeployed by this change (lead's go needed).
- fix(kernel): a manager no longer holds `records.define`. Changing the Space's types is Customize (admin and owner, ROLE_BUNDLES `customize.definitions`); the role table gave it to managers. `test/roles-enforced.test.js` holds each role's grants to its bundle on the real kernel (who holds which action, who may make whom, temp scope, and a temp's end at the expiry with no sweep, extension, no self-extension).
- feat(publish): the box end of the Publish tunnel. `lib/publish/tunnel.js`: `createTunnelEnd` carries each stream the relay transport hands it to Caddy's loopback port (fixed, never named by the relay), reads only the first TLS record to find the SNI and refuses a name that is not the Space's (own domains from the directory's verified list), with limits per stream (idle, lifetime, bytes, hello wait) and per edge (open streams); TLS stays end to end. `edgeCompose(..., { tunnel: true })` publishes Caddy's 443 on `127.0.0.1:18443` only; `caddyfile(..., { tunnel: true })` drops the redirect listener. TCP only, no HTTP/3 through the tunnel.
- refactor(spaces): `kperson` removed; platform's `adoptOwner` makes the kernel's owner the claimed identity.
- fix(publish): SW-1 (reviewer-3). The site-folder sweep never touches a folder younger than an hour: a preview writes its folder before its record exists, so a second preview at the same time used to take it. Test: four previews at once keep four folders.
- feat(spaces,kernel): one space id, the kernel's (`spc_` plus 12 base32). `spaces.create` hosts the Space in the kernel's Spaces registry first (the kernel handle gains `spaces: { storePlan, host }` for a module that declares `needs.kernel.spaces`), takes its id, and fails the step if the kernel or the store attach fails; the kernel's first owner is the person it knows (`owner`), so records and tasks work in the new Space under the caller's chain in that Space (`chainIn`). `membership` answers for any Space this home hosts. Publish's `SPACE_RE` is exactly `/^spc_[a-z2-7]{12}$/`. A device with no enrolment list is enrolled in a Space this module has no row for. Test: test/one-registry.test.js on a real daemon (create, records.types/create/list, tasks.list, records.me).
- fix(publish): FF-1 and FS-2 (reviewer-3). A deployment record keeps only the NAME of its site folder; `publish.edge` rebuilds the path under the space's own sites folder and uses it only if the name is `site-XXXXXX` and the folder is a real directory (not a link), ours, mode 0700, and `volumeFill` takes only such a folder directly under that root, so an edited record cannot point the copy at /etc or the secrets folder. Site folders no live deployment names (retired, superseded, left by a refused build) are removed on each new build and each edge write, and the total is capped at 50.
- feat(publish): the product call for the site volume (PW-3). When a static build previews, its checked files are written by `writeSiteFiles` into a private folder under the space's publish folder (the deployment records it), and `publish.edge` returns `fills`: for each live static site, the docker call (`volumeFill`) that copies that folder into the site's volume; the box runs it. A hand-off with a link is refused (`bad_output`) and writes nothing; module-level test.
- fix(publish): EG-1 and the volume writer (reviewer-3). `egress` must be absent or false (any other value, "yes" included, refuses the workload), every workload setting is type-checked, a deployment description refuses any key it does not define, and the generated compose is refused if a workload joins the egress bridge. The site volume is filled only by `lib/publish/site-write.js`: the checked file list is written into a fresh folder one file at a time with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` (nothing a builder made as a directory is copied or extracted), then copied into the empty volume by a throwaway no-network container (`volumeFill`); a file and a folder of one name, and case or Unicode twins, are refused. Replaces the tar of the previous commit.
- fix(kernel): `ruleEnable` and `ruleDisable` join the grants store's one-at-a-time, restore-on-failure wrapper, so a switch whose event cannot be written leaves the rule as it was (test: R4 on rules.enable and rules.disable).
- feat(kernel): `rules.get`, `rules.test`, `rules.enable` and `rules.disable` on the rule store, and the app's `rules` module (core/rules-tools: `rules.list`, `.get`, `.define`, `.test`, `.enable`, `.disable`, `.remove`, `.propose`, `.accept`, `.dismiss`, one tool each under the caller's own chain). A rule can be switched off (status `disabled`, still listed, binds nothing, an event in the log) and on again by an owner with presence; `rules.test` says what the rules would do to an act (`outcome` never, always_ask, draft_only or none) for an assistant, a member or an assistant acting for a member, for one stored rule or a rule not yet made, and writes nothing. Time-window rules are 0.3.1.
- feat(records): `TypeDefinition.kind` ("project"), carried by define, the SDK, the compiler and both stores; `contact_point` core type (one unique record per further address) with `addContactPoint` and a `findContact` fallback; Twenty's timeline is switched off (`isAuditLogged: false`) on every Vyre object when the Twenty offers it; `records.linked` (the reverse of a link across types, permission-checked, capped); `records/kits/library.js` lists and loads the Kits this build ships (`kitLibrary`, `kitFromLibrary`); native group-by accepts money sub-field measures.
- feat(records): contacts, roles and field switches. Core types `contact` (main email and phone unique, other addresses in lists), `organization`, `communication` (one per connector item, `source_key` unique) and `participant` in every Space; a Kit may add fields to a core type (the estate Kit's contact now carries only its own fields: `name` replaces `full_name`). A type is a role with `role: { link, ended }`; gateway `roles(holder)`, `holders({ role, stage })`, `merge`/`unmerge` (join, relink, one `records.merged` event, undo) and `records/comms/log.js` (`logCommunication`, `findContact`, `timelineOf`). Field switches: `hidden` (removed softly, data kept), `hidden_from` roles, `computed` (an Expression or a total over linked records; `days_since` and `round` added to the Expression language), and `migrate.sealField` (plain values move through `seal.put`, the plain field goes, the old values are scrubbed from the change log, snapshots, Twenty's timeline and the event log). Search no longer finds a record through a field outside the caller's limit.
- feat(records): conformance revision 5 and no row cap on totals: the gateway's aggregate and the Twenty store fold page by page (`createAggregator`), so the 20,000-row refusal is gone. Real Twenty v2.44.0: 32 of 32. Fixed live: Twenty's unique index keeps soft-deleted rows, so a removed record kept its value; the store now holds a removed record's unique values aside and gives them back on restore. A real vyred on a real Twenty sealed a field end to end (team/0.3/E2E-RUN.md step 6).
- fix(kernel): `ruleEnable` and `ruleDisable` join the grants store's one-at-a-time, restore-on-failure wrapper, so a switch whose event cannot be written leaves the rule as it was (test: R4 on rules.enable and rules.disable).
- feat(kernel): `rules.get`, `rules.test`, `rules.enable` and `rules.disable` on the rule store, and the app's `rules` module (core/rules-tools: `rules.list`, `.get`, `.define`, `.test`, `.enable`, `.disable`, `.remove`, `.propose`, `.accept`, `.dismiss`, one tool each under the caller's own chain). A rule can be switched off (status `disabled`, still listed, binds nothing, an event in the log) and on again by an owner with presence; `rules.test` says what the rules would do to an act (`outcome` never, always_ask, draft_only or none) for an assistant, a member or an assistant acting for a member, for one stored rule or a rule not yet made, and writes nothing. Time-window rules are 0.3.1.
- feat(kernel): ONE registry and ONE person. `spaces.create` makes the Space in the kernel's Spaces registry (the kernel handle gives the spaces module `ctx.kernel.spaces`: host, storePlan, list, hosts; `needs.kernel.spaces`), so the kernel's id (`spc_` and 12 base32 characters) is the Space's id everywhere and its built-in store is attached at that moment; `records.*` and `tasks.*` answer in it. The home's owner id becomes the claimed identity's id: `adoptOwner` (kernel, once, logged; the spaces module hands it the identity's id on the first call after a claim or at a start that finds one) replaces the old owner in the grants log (member.removed, member.set, grant.revoked, grant.created: a rebuild from the log reaches the same state), rewrites `kernel/space.json`, and every reader of the owner reads it live (chains, gateway, approver, `kernel.id.owner`, Flows). The spaces module takes the caller's chain IN the Space it asks about (`kctxOf(meta, space)` over `chainIn`), not the home's chain. Test: test/one-registry.test.js (records.me, spaces.identity.status, spaces.list, spaces.get and the pairing's identity target agree after a claim; a Space made by spaces.create takes records.create and tasks.list).
- feat(presence): the development stand-in reaches the kernel too: with the owner's hand-made `dev-presence-stand-in` in a development build, a one-person chain counts as having a presence session and a proof with method "stand-in" is taken, each use a `presence.stand-in` event. `records.dev-seed` (only while it is on) seeds the walk's types, records and tasks.
- feat(records): `records.types` leaves the kernel's own bookkeeping types out (`system: true` when asked for with `system: true`) and returns a type's `kind` (`project`), which `records.define` stores as given.
- feat(presence): a DEVELOPMENT-ONLY presence stand-in for the automated walk. A proof with `method: "stand-in"` is taken only when the daemon says so: a development build (not packaged) whose home holds `dev-presence-stand-in`, a file the owner makes by hand outside the daemon (never config, never a tool). Every `presence.proved` event carries method "stand-in", so a walk is never mistaken for a real proof; a packaged build ignores it, logs one line and refuses. The `fromClaude` and every real-method path are untouched.
- fix(kernel): devices enrol per Space. A call's chain from a `device` fact (`ctx.kernel.chain(meta)`, `chainIn`) is built only if the spaces module (`spaces.devices.enrolled`, the daemon's `deviceEnrolled` port) says the device is still enrolled in THAT Space; a removed device gets no person chain there (the module's service chain, so the call is refused) and keeps its chains in the Spaces it is still in. An error from the port is a no; a build without the spaces module has no list. Also: the box's chrome and the Mac's chrome share a name for different machines (module-names test allows disjoint roles); core/settings decides the person by the kernel's chain for the call, not its label.
- feat(records): `records.seal-put` (the value goes straight to the sealing process; the record keeps only the reference), `records.reveal` (human-only: needs the person's presence proof), `records.sees-as` (the person's view, or the assistant's through the kernel's Surfaces door for one 30-second look: sealed fields only as placeholders) and `records.events` (the log as the caller may read it, for a record, a task or all).
- feat(tasks): the app's task calls. A `tasks` module (core/tasks-tools): `tasks.list`, `.get`, `.request`, `.decide` (the person's own act, presence proof beside the request), `.move` (start, stuck, skip, fix: the kernel's own acts and gates), `.submit` (the kernel's output check, the Deck's `{ note: { text, sources } }` taken in the kernel's shape), each under the caller's own chain in the Space it names. The kernel's task store gains `list(chain, { record, doer, checker, state })`, every task through the same `tasks.read` gate `get` uses.
- fix(publish): JP-1 (reviewer-3). The edge's access log keeps `/join/redacted`, never a join token. And a site is filled from a tar built by Publish (`lib/publish/site-tar.js`) out of the checked file list: regular files and their directories only, owned by the site's user, read-only, so a link or a path outside the site cannot exist in what is extracted. `scripts/publish-e2e.mjs` fills its site this way and shows each link (to .env, .git/config, /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, /run/secrets/NAME) refused.
- fix(publish): PB-1 (reviewer-3). A build may hand over only regular files by plain relative paths (`lib/publish/outputs.js`): a link of any kind, a device, a pipe, `..`, an absolute or repeated path refuses the whole build, so a symlink in a static site can no longer serve `.env`, `/etc/passwd` or a granted secret past the dotfile rule. A static site takes no environment and no runtime secrets (build use only), and no site gets outbound network until the box has the rule that keeps the publish bridges off the host and private ranges.
- feat(publish): the page behind a join link. The edge serves https://<space>.vyre.run/join/<token> from one static page (lib/publish/join.js, a read-only compose config, no server behind it): "Open in Vyre" hands the whole link to the app as `vyre://join?link=<link>`, "Copy link", no outside request, no referrer, no storage, a strict Content-Security-Policy, `no-store`; the rest of that host answers 404. The shared Referrer-Policy header is now a default (`?`) so a page can set its own. Verified on a real box (`scripts/publish-e2e.mjs`).
- fix(bridges,publish,spaces): BR-2. The person a bridges or publish call is for comes only from the call's own kernel chain (`ctx.kernel.chain(meta)`); no caller label or `isPerson` check remains in core/spaces, core/bridges or core/publish. No chain, a service chain or a viewer chain is nobody. `spaces.self` takes the kernel's person and answers only for the home's own (the kernel handle gains `owner`).
- feat(spaces): setup in progress (`spaces.setup.save` and `claim`, `setup` on `spaces.get` and `spaces.list`); a space is listed only once it has its home; one identity per person (`spaces.identity.id`, read by pairing); members show the name they chose; devices enrol per space (`spaces.devices.set`, `enrol`, `remove`, `restore`, `enrolled`, `spaces`); `spaces.label` answers for the home's own Space; presence recovery carried to the sealing process (`spaces.presence.begin`, `recover`, `sync`); invite revoke and list on a kernel-hosted space.
- fix(publish): the edge's Caddy runs from a derived image (`caddyDockerfile`, built once on the box: the official binary cannot exec under cap_drop ALL because of its file capability, and its /data and /config were root-owned so a non-root Caddy could not keep certificates); a static site answers 404 for dotfiles and dot folders (the file server served `.env` and `.git`), `/.well-known/` excepted; `publish.edge` also writes `caddy.Dockerfile` and returns the image to build. Found by running the real project (`scripts/publish-e2e.mjs`, needs Docker).
- fix(relay): BR-2, the relay listener's caller label is the trust claim. `device:<id>` goes only to a live device of kind app; a browser is `web:<id>` and a setup page `setup:<id>`; any other kind gets no channel. A `web:` caller is none of the person's classes: a tool that lists callers (every `person` tool) does not exist for it unless it names `web` (`relay.devices.ask-trust`, `relay.devices.list`, `relay.web.release` do); tools open to anyone stay open. A trusted browser therefore reaches no person tool until a web reach class is designed (the relay limits lift, nothing more). The setup page keeps its own name list (the relay's setup gate), and names and tailscale accept `setup:` where they accepted its old device label.
- fix(wink): one identity. Wink's owner id is read live from the spaces module (`spaces.identity.self`, internal), the identity claimed through the names directory; a box with none falls back to the route-derived id. `wink.pair.targets` and `spaces.identity.status` report the same id (test/identity-one.test.js, real daemon and stand-in directory).
- feat(relay): `relay.devices.list` carries `storage` (hardware | software | unknown, the app's own report) for the Devices line. `wink.server.status` tells the installer who owns the server and which device paired it.
- fix(wink): removal of a device and a reset await `presence.person.end-paired` and fail when it cannot, leaving the owner and the device in place. `network.wink.status` and `.whois` name their callers (the person's surfaces, devices, modules), so a model session cannot call them.
- fix(wink): a reset where presence is missing (`no_such_tool`) now fails closed like any other failure to end the paired sessions, never "nothing to end".
- fix(presence): `presence.person.start-paired`, `pair-challenge` and `rotate` declare `callers: ["tailnet", "relay", "device"]` (a paired phone's relay or tailnet channel), so no model, guest or MCP caller reaches them (platform's golden refresh).
- fix(wink, presence): end paths of a paired person session. A recovery reset now AWAITS `presence.person.end-paired` for every device before it forgets anything, and fails (`unavailable`, nothing reset, the code still good) if presence cannot end them; a box with no presence module has none to end. Removing a presence key also deletes the pending pair grants it confirmed (PS-4). `presence.person.sessions` called by a paired session lists only that session. Tests: core/wink/reset.test.js, core/presence/presence.test.js, test/wink.test.js (revoke, sign-out-everywhere, owner-key removal with a really enrolled key, sessions scope).
- test(wink): two more end paths of a paired person session on a real vyred and kernel (test/wink.test.js): a revoked session id is gone at once, and sign-out-everywhere (`presence.person.end-paired` with no device, module:wink only) ends it while any other caller is refused. Shared setup `pairedOnKernel`.
- fix(vault, files): VL-1: `vault.connections.list` and `.revoke` use the signed-in person check (chain person AND a person session), so an owner device with no session gets no person surface (daemon test, unsigned case). A Drive path segment with leading or trailing whitespace is refused with the other path tricks (`safePath`).
- feat(files): the Space's own Drive for the app, three tools in the files module (core/files/space-drive.js): `files.drive.upload { space?, path, base64, base? }` (a new version, at most 8 MB per call, a second writer makes a conflict version), `files.drive.versions { space?, path }`, `files.drive.restore { space?, path, version }` (a new version, the person's own act with their presence proof). Each runs under the caller's own chain in the Space it names (lib/gateway-door.js); the kernel's drive.write, drive.read and drive.restore grants decide; paths are checked in one form and sizes at the entry; a Space with no Drive wired answers `unavailable`. Not the box's shared folders (files.drive.list and read).
- fix(vault, presence, files): the person comes from the kernel's chain, never a caller label, in the four sites the vault team owned. The gate's presence check asks `presence.personOf` (set by the daemon from the kernel's chain for the call, the registry now passes `meta` to `presence.verify`) before a session proves a vault tool; vault connections take the person from the chain (`core/vault/person.js`) and a device or tailnet label with no proven person gets no surface; Drive share, unshare and access require the paired Mac's peer id AND the kernel's chain saying person; the sync namespace check is a vault-id helper (`isDeviceGroupId`), not a caller label. Only a build with no kernel keeps the old label rule in presence, marked SHIM(legacy labels) (FROZEN count 1 stays for core/presence/index.js; drive, vault connections and vault index lowered to 0). test/vault-labels-daemon.test.js on a real kernel-on daemon: a confirmed owner device signed in is the person; web, setup, removed, never-paired devices and tailnet labels with no proven facts get nothing.
- fix(kernel): devices enrol per Space. A call's chain from a `device` fact (`ctx.kernel.chain(meta)`, `chainIn`) is built only if the spaces module (`spaces.devices.enrolled`, the daemon's `deviceEnrolled` port) says the device is still enrolled in THAT Space; a removed device gets no person chain there (the module's service chain, so the call is refused) and keeps its chains in the Spaces it is still in. An error from the port is a no; a build without the spaces module has no list. Also: the box's chrome and the Mac's chrome share a name for different machines (module-names test allows disjoint roles); core/settings decides the person by the kernel's chain for the call, not its label.
- feat(records): `records.seal-put` (the value goes straight to the sealing process; the record keeps only the reference), `records.reveal` (human-only: needs the person's presence proof), `records.sees-as` (the person's view, or the assistant's through the kernel's Surfaces door for one 30-second look: sealed fields only as placeholders) and `records.events` (the log as the caller may read it, for a record, a task or all).
- feat(tasks): the app's task calls. A `tasks` module (core/tasks-tools): `tasks.list`, `.get`, `.request`, `.decide` (the person's own act, presence proof beside the request), `.move` (start, stuck, skip, fix: the kernel's own acts and gates), `.submit` (the kernel's output check, the Deck's `{ note: { text, sources } }` taken in the kernel's shape), each under the caller's own chain in the Space it names. The kernel's task store gains `list(chain, { record, doer, checker, state })`, every task through the same `tasks.read` gate `get` uses.
- feat(records): the app's way into a Space's records. A `records` module (core/records-tools) registers `records.me`, `.actors`, `.types`, `.define`, `.list`, `.get`, `.create`, `.update` and the internal `records.workspace.create` and `.delete` (what `spaces.create` calls; every Space has its built-in store, so it answers at once), each under the CALLER's own chain in the Space it names (`lib/gateway-door.js`, `ctx.kernel.chainIn(space, meta)`: a session token's or the person's proved facts under that Space's own key; never the body, never the module's service chain). Person surfaces and `device` only; a model, guest, anonymous or a call that proved no person is refused. The kernel decides each answer.
- feat(kernel): the kernel's `dataStores` list (lib/data-stores.js), handed to Wink as `ctx.dataStores` (`needs.daemon`): the vault (its own read when this build has lib/vault-wipe.js, else holds), the Space's records and events, the modules' own tables and activity events, and the files in the home. Default is "holds data": anything unknown, unanswered or not known to be bookkeeping counts, so a store added later is protected until the list says it is empty. No entry can wipe. `vyre wink reset` on an owned box refuses while any holds data.
- feat(kernel): `seal.put` is in the member, manager, admin and owner role bundles (writing a value into a sealed field is part of writing the record). A temp member holds it only where a grant of theirs names it; an assistant has none of its own and the sealing process refuses a chain with a model in it. Homes whose role grants were made earlier get it when the role is next set.
- fix(kernel): SG-5-3. On a packaged build whose signed release files (modules.json, SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.sig) are missing, unreadable or badly signed, NO first-party list is in force; the last accepted list is never a fallback. The boot log says why and the daemon still starts; the accepted names stay reserved. A development build keeps the old behaviour. The names `vault` and `leases` are reserved whatever list is in force (the vault's service forward trusts `module:leases`); an added module under either is refused.
- feat(0.3, app identity, 4 Oct): a device with no box claims its Vyre name itself (apps/app/src/identity). The Ed25519 device key is made on the device, non-extractable where WebCrypto has Ed25519 (the noble software key where not), the recovery code and its Argon2id key (@noble/hashes, byte-identical to kernel/identity/stretch.js with the real work factor), the genesis chain (kernel/identity/chain.js itself) and the sealed record (WebCrypto AES-GCM, byte-identical to lib/identity/directory.js) go to the names directory. Tests open each side's output with the other and claim against the real directory code (scripts/standin-directory.mjs). The install name check asks the directory, not a box. New kernel/identity/chain.d.ts and names/worker/id-messages.d.ts are types only; the pinned chain.js is untouched. No new dependency (noble was already one).

Once the server is paired (or "On this computer" is chosen, which has no server step) setup moves on by itself to look, members, connectors and the first Kit, with no refresh and no second sign-in; the server's terminal says "Connected to <space>. Finish setting up on your <device>." and asks nothing more. Closing and reopening resumes at the same step (src/state/setup-progress.ts keeps the step and what was typed, never a code or key; a pairing in progress resumes at the code).
