The create step now only names and claims the space; its look moved after pairing. Pairing copy follows tailnet's words card: "Pick one of the three choices, or type all three words."

- fix(0.3, app, 4 Oct): the font ruling. The app uses the platform font everywhere (San Francisco on Apple, Roboto on Android, the system font on Windows, Linux and the web); no text font is bundled (assets/fonts, the expo-font plugin and the web @font-face are gone), the word-spacing patch is gone, negative tracking is not applied on iOS, and the font setting is System and Serif ("sans" reads as System). Instrument Sans stays for the wordmark and web pages. Pairing confirm is a pick of one of three word sets or all three words typed (`PairingSession.choices` and `answer`); a wrong answer rejects for good. Six icons from the family (Contacts, Spaces and members, Assistants, Flows, About), the space switcher only on the tab bar's own places on a phone, Spaces: one plus menu and Extend in the end slot, the record page (desktop page title and 40 mark, empty fields behind one line, no Stage row, menu on hover or long press, Add a field icon on a phone), and a device row says "This device keeps its key in software" when `software` is true.

- feat(0.3, wink pairing in the app): every typed-code screen is gone. Install ("Pair to:", the server step, the other-device scan) and Devices, Add a device both run scan or paste the long code (`src/api/wink-code.ts`, one parser: a long code or an offer reads, a short `WINK-XXXX-XXXX` is refused in plain words), then confirm the same three words with Confirm or "These are not the same" (`screens/devices/PairParts.tsx`, shared). The three words come from `PairingSession` (`src/api/pairing-session.ts`); `openPairing` is the one place it is opened and returns the mock until the app is wired to the Wink module (wink.phone.scan, wink.pair.server). The terminal copy shows the long code, then who is asking, the words and "Waiting for yes." Removed: the 47/12/85 number pick, `canFallback`, `pick`, `pickNumber`, `SERVER_CODE`.

- feat(chat): task W1, the stream no longer holds, retries or queues (lead ruling, sessions' queue). core/stream/group.js: the per-person turn queue and the busy retry are removed; a person's words are written to the chat at once and the stream calls `threads.send` once with `{ chat, asker }` (asker = the bare `per_...` id, converted from the kernel-verified author at the stream's boundary). The outbox row completes on the Switchboard's `queued` answer or its normal answer; on `queued` the message frame shows state `queued` with the Switchboard's `queued_id`, and `thread.sent` via "turn" for that id (the queued turn starting) switches the replies to that asker and answer id and shows the message `picked-up`. core/stream/module.json declares `needs: { daemon: ["kernelThreads"] }` and group.js reads `ctx.kernelThreads`; core/daemon/index.js and core/modules/index.js are platform's (work/kernel 7dcd110fc). Merged origin/work/kernel, work/flows and work/v0.3.
- feat(chat): task V, a second person's message mid-turn is its own turn under that person (chat 0.3, reviewer SS-1 and SS-2). core/stream/group.js holds an outbox row whose asker differs from the running turn's until the thread leaves `working` (one event, no timer), then sends it under its own asker; two people's waiting messages are two turns in arrival order; a `busy` refusal from the Switchboard is held and retried once at the turn's end; the queue is the group's outbox, so a restart keeps it; a stopped stream sends nothing more. With the kernel on `stream.send` refuses a call without a kernel-verified person. The stream no longer calls beginTurn (the kernel-session open does, once per turn). core/stream/access.js no longer needs a session token to build the caller's chain: a person's Deck call carries the daemon's facts chain, so `stream.send` works on a real vyred (it answered `chain_not_person`). core/stream/module.json requires threads (outbox rows at start need the Switchboard). The step 7 harness has no test-only option of `start()` left: it seeds the home with a real signed presence proof and calls tools with daemon-style facts. Tests: group-ks-live V1 to V4.

- feat(kernel): `modules.list.reset`, the owner's presence-gated reset of the accepted first-party module list (core/modulelist, over `resetModulesList` in kernel/home.js), so `vyre update --rollback` to an older release can proceed. Person surfaces only, `{}` input, one `kernel.modules-list-reset` event; a delegated, viewer or room chain, a model, a guest and a call with no proof are refused with a non-zero exit.
- feat(wink): the identity ports are wired. `core/wink/identity-ports.js` gives Wink `identityEntry` and `signIdentity` (so a `--pair-to` can be proved and answered, Q-3) and the network's `identity` port (`entry`, `self`) for `vyre doctor`, all by the spaces module's own internal tools read live; `spaces.identity.sign` now also signs `vyre-wink-pair-to-v1` (and nothing else new). With no spaces module they answer null and a pairing is refused plainly. The node host and relay clock ports stay absent (the doctor says unknown) until the daemon composes the node host.
- fix(kernel): SG-5-1 and SG-5-2. The kernel and lib tree check runs at EVERY boot, not only when the counter advances, and a mismatch leaves no first-party list at all (not even the last accepted one); only a module with its own signature is first party, and the boot log says why.
- fix(kernel): RF-2 and RF-3. The held answer to a model carries no `resolved` or `slots` (one refusal for every unreadable-placeholder reason); they reach the approver through the registry's `held` hook (the held card), with a hash of the exact values resolved (`bound`). `checkBound` re-resolves before the send and refuses a record changed since approval (`changed_since_approval`). A malformed `{{field:` is refused, not sent as text.
- fix(daemon): RF-1, a `{{field:...}}` placeholder in an outward action resolves under the turn token's own chain (its agent and its grants, the chat left out: `surfaces.chainFor(token, { noChat: true })`), not a full person chain for the device `vyred`, so an agent granted one project cannot have a field of another substituted into an action; a field its chain cannot read refuses the whole action (`placeholder_unreadable`). Also the Switchboard's `probe` (is this person in this chat?) no longer opens a session or begins a turn.
- feat(kernel): two modules may share a name for different machines (disjoint `roles`); the signed list carries one entry per folder (`also`), and a build with two folders of one name and overlapping roles fails.
- fix(vault): reviewer-2's SV-2a/b/c, Drive and WP findings. `vault.service.forward` claims an approval atomically in the vault's own database (spent for good, 24 h, survives a restart) and keeps the in-flight call under the idem key, so two truly concurrent calls send once and both get the one answer; the approval bind now also covers headers, upload sources and saveTo; Drive paths also refuse a colon, a leading `~` and bidi or zero-width marks. `wipeHome` reads where the vault's key lives from the home's own config and refuses an argument that disagrees (`keystore_mismatch`); a symlinked backup is never followed blindly (a target inside the home is destroyed with the link, one outside is refused by name) and every listed path is verified gone before success. New scripts/admin-wipe.mjs, the entry `sudo vyre admin wipe` runs: --home, --seal-dir, --backup, exit 0 wiped, 2 refused, 64 bad arguments.
- fix(vault): wipe WP-1 and WP-2. `keystore` has no default: a missing or unknown value refuses (`keystore_unknown`), and `homeKeystore(home)` reads it from the home's config.json. `backups: [paths]` (the update's previous release and source, a database snapshot) are overwritten and removed, or named in `backup_survives` with no success reported; the result carries `notices` (an exported vault backup string is yours and still opens with its own passphrase; provider sign-in tokens stay valid at the provider). test/vault-wipe.test.js.
- fix(vault): SV-2 and Drive paths for a Flow's service call. An approval releases one request: the held decision carries `bind` (`requestBind` in kernel/seal/uses.js: connector, method, canonical path, query, body hash), the retry passes it back, `vault.service.forward` recomputes it from what it will send and refuses a mismatch or a missing bind, and an approval id is spent once (the same idem replays the first answer). `upload.drive.path`, multipart part paths and `saveTo` get the same one-form refusal as request paths (`safePath`) before the Drive is touched. The kernel's task payload should also carry `bind` so an approval cannot be minted for another request (platform). core/vault/service.test.js.
- feat(seal): the log anchor for BL-2: sealing-process ops `anchor.advance { seq, head }` and `anchor.read` (client `anchor.advance`, `anchor.read`, kernel channel only, never a model's chain), per Space, sealed in the process's own store, moving only forward (`anchor_behind`, `anchor_split`), kept over a restart. The kernel side (checkpoint call, boot check) is kernel-2's. Test: kernel/seal/seal.test.js.
- fix(seal): `seal.detect` is scoped to what the person may read (SD-2): the sealing process finds the records holding the candidate and the client's `detectValue` requires a `canRead(record)` from the kernel's grants, so a value sealed only in records the person cannot read answers no; the records never leave the kernel. The per-day counts are sealed on disk and survive a restart (SD-1). The tool's contract: `first_party` and the module name come from the module registry, never from input (SD-3).
- feat(vault): `vaultHolds({ home })` in lib/vault-wipe.js, a read for `vyre wink reset`: exactly `false` when the home holds no vault item, shared record, SSH key, emergency bundle or sealed value; unreadable counts as holding.
- fix(vault): SV-1, a connector's route rules matched the raw path while the request went out on the URL parser's rewrite (a backslash became a slash, tabs vanished), so a probe got past a deny on `/v4/users/*`. One canonical form now, `canonicalPath` in kernel/seal/uses.js, used by the Flow connector rules (`vault.service.forward`), the lent-session route rule (`routeAllows`) and both kernel/gateway/leases.js paths: a backslash, space, control character or NUL, an encoded slash, backslash, dot or NUL, an empty segment, dot segments before or after decoding, a double-encoded percent and a query are refused (identical `not_found`), percent-encoding is decoded exactly once, and rules match and the request is sent in that one form. Tests: core/vault/service.test.js (the probe plus 30 more spellings), 56 of 56 with forward, forward-file, uses, leases, compile and boundaries.
- feat(vault): reset with wipe, host CLI only (`sudo vyre admin wipe`, daemon stopped). `wipeHome({ home, vaultDir?, sealDir?, db?, destroyKeychain? })` in lib/vault-wipe.js takes the home's lock (refuses with `daemon_running` while vyred runs), then destroys the vault key files and the sealing master first, then empties every vault_ table and both folders; counts only. No tool, no sealer op; it also refuses (`sealer_running`) while a sealing process serves the folder, and refuses by name (`keystore_survives`) when a key lives in the OS keychain and no `destroyKeychain` is given or the sealing master is not a file; it checks no key file survives before reporting success. test/vault-wipe.test.js scans that nothing but the host CLI imports it. kernel/seal/wipe.js holds the sealing half.
- feat(vault): a Flow's "Call a service" reaches the vault. An api-credential may carry `service: { allow, deny }` (rules `{ method?, path }`; `*` one segment, trailing `/*` the rest, deny wins, default no); a credential with it is a connector. Two internal tools for the kernel's lease module only: `vault.service.catalog` (the rules, no host or secret) and `vault.service.forward` (route check, host from the credential, key added, response or `{ saved }` or `{ held }`; an approved outward call runs once per `idem`, the approval named in the audit row). The daemon's `forwardCredential` and the Flows catalog use them. core/vault/service.js, core/vault/service.test.js.
- feat(seal): `seal.detect` for first-party modules, a yes or no on one candidate against the Space's sealed values (process op `match`, client `detectValue`); rate limited per module and Space, a chain with a model in it refused, never returns a value; event `seal.detect {module, count}`.
- fix(wink): a reset where presence is missing (`no_such_tool`) now fails closed like any other failure to end the paired sessions, never "nothing to end".
- fix(presence): `presence.person.start-paired`, `pair-challenge` and `rotate` declare `callers: ["tailnet", "relay", "device"]` (a paired phone's relay or tailnet channel), so no model, guest or MCP caller reaches them (platform's golden refresh).
- fix(wink, presence): end paths of a paired person session. A recovery reset now AWAITS `presence.person.end-paired` for every device before it forgets anything, and fails (`unavailable`, nothing reset, the code still good) if presence cannot end them; a box with no presence module has none to end. Removing a presence key also deletes the pending pair grants it confirmed (PS-4). `presence.person.sessions` called by a paired session lists only that session. Tests: core/wink/reset.test.js, core/presence/presence.test.js, test/wink.test.js (revoke, sign-out-everywhere, owner-key removal with a really enrolled key, sessions scope).
- test(wink): two more end paths of a paired person session on a real vyred and kernel (test/wink.test.js): a revoked session id is gone at once, and sign-out-everywhere (`presence.person.end-paired` with no device, module:wink only) ends it while any other caller is refused. Shared setup `pairedOnKernel`.
- test(wink): a real daemon with the kernel on: a phone pairs, the owner picks, the device signs `start-paired`, and `memory.graph` answers as the owner with the session id that call gave, with no prompt; without the session it gets the sign-in hint; after removal it is denied.
- fix(wink): the software-key line comes from the app's own report, not a default. The hello's `presenceKey.storage` (hardware | software, from the platform's key API) is recorded as `key_storage` at the owner's pick and shown on the Devices row (`software: true`) only when it says software; unknown or hardware shows nothing. It is display only: the paired session still treats every key as unattested, so the optional software-key cap applies to all until real attestation (0.3.1).
- fix(relay): one pairing path (lead ruling, 4 Oct 2026). The setup page's one `relay.pair.ticket` is refused: a device that redeemed it was paired at the relay (row of kind app, presence key) with no three-word confirm, and no owner existed to give one. The first device pairs with the code the installer prints, confirmed with three words. The setup page's phone step (site/setup flow.js) now gets a 403 and needs the installer flow instead (launch).
- feat(wink): reset on a box that holds data refuses, with the reason, and points to `sudo vyre admin wipe` (lead ruling: no daemon tool destroys data; that command stops the daemon, runs the vault's wipeHome, makes a fresh Space identity offline, then starts the daemon unowned). Lost devices: identity recovery. A box with no data resets with the console code alone. The list of data stores is the kernel's (`createWink({ dataStores })`, each `{ name, holds() }`); a missing list, or a store that does not answer `false`, counts as holding data.
- feat(wink): vault's paired-session contract (ADR 0032 2d), wink side. The owner's pick for a phone records who confirmed, with which presence key, and the device's own request-signing key (the public key it offered in its hello; the relay's `relay.pair.pending.confirm` now answers it and takes `trusted`); `wink.device.record` (module:presence only) answers that record; the pick then calls `presence.person.pair-grant`. The relay marks the device trusted at the same moment. Removal of a device and a reset call `presence.person.end-paired`. A device that keeps its key in software shows `software: true` on its Devices row. The device gets its challenge with `presence.person.pair-challenge` over its own channel.
- fix(daemon): the test-host guard reads the machine's platform once at import, so a test that fakes `process.platform = "darwin"` (relay's Mac refusals) no longer makes it think it runs on a Mac. "a Mac box never mints, before vyre-core" passed only where VYRE_TEST_HOST=testbox was set.
- chore(wink): three dead reset cards (`resetOnServer`, `resetFingerprint`, `resetNeedsYou`) are deleted; the fingerprint they named is gone.
- fix(relay): R-2, a ring ticket (`relay.pair.ticket`) is always a gated ticket: its redeemer is a waiting pairing with no row, no presence key and no person chain until the three words are confirmed, with or without the Wink module and with or without a QR open. `relay.pair.gate` is deleted (it was a switch the module set late); the test switch `VYRE_TEST_UNGATED_RING` is honoured by an unpackaged daemon only.
- fix(wink): WP-1, the answer to the three words is a pick of 1 of 3 or all three words typed; the typed first word is gone (it was 2^-11, not 2^-33). Decoys never share their first three letters with the real word in the same place. The box forgets a ticket's secret at the first ask and on every failure.
- memory: the Capsule exception is gone. A Capsule call is the owner only with the daemon's pinned-binary proof and then has a chain like any surface; the bare label is refused. A real-daemon test covers the device rows (owner device signed in and unsigned, web, setup, removed, never paired).
- fix(daemon): PH-1, a `device:<id>` is the owner's only if the home holds its own row for it. `callerFacts` takes the home's `relay.device.info` row and builds person facts only for a paired, not removed, `app` device; a web browser (trusted or not), a setup page, a removed device and an id never paired get none, whatever the relay says. A device with no person session carries no session fact (no presence session). Tests: an arbitrary id, no row, removed, web, trusted web, setup, no person session, and a real daemon with the relay table.
- feat(daemon): the Capsule's own chain. A call on the socket labelled `capsule` builds the owner's chain only when `verifiedCapsule` proves the peer is the pinned Capsule binary (cdhash pinned by the person, checked per connection and bound to the pid's start time); a bare label builds none. `callerFacts` takes the proof as an argument; tests cover the proof, the label alone, and a listener identity.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2 SG-5, LF-1, LF-3, FL-1. A release's `modules.json` lists the `kernel` and `lib` trees and the boot checks them (a build whose kernel or lib differs uses no first-party list from itself). `leases.forward` counts rate, budget and once through `enforce` once all decisions allow (a refused request counts nothing); `leases.bind` keeps the whole route record (deny wins, size cap, content types, Drive lists, header names) and `forward` carries it to `vault.forward` and `vault.forward.file`, with `gateway.drive.files(chain)` as the Drive door under the caller's chain (handed in-process as meta; the vault takes it only from the lease module). `forFlow` refuses a viewer, delegated or room chain as approver.
- feat(daemon): the stream gets its view of the kernel sessions by DECLARATION (`needs.daemon: ["kernelThreads"]` gives `ctx.kernelThreads`: `forThread`, `reopenPending`; no token, no opener), and the restart reopening runs once the modules are up when no stream asked. `start({ kernelPresence })` is a test seam for a presence verifier. `callerFacts` is exported and a real-daemon test covers the phone (relay `device:<id>`, tailnet owner node, `mobile` on the socket) and what builds no chain (guest, agent node, unknown listener). golden re-recorded after the spaces, sealing and teammates tools (56 newly open tools named in allow.json, six of them open to guests by their modules' design, for reviewer-2 to confirm); `memory.sealscan` is person only.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2 SG-1 to SG-3 on the signed module list. The list decides for every name it holds (an old `module.sig` is no longer an OR with it; a name the list does not hold still goes by its own signature). Names in the list stay reserved (`reservedName`, `deps.reservedName` in the Module host): a folder that fails the list is refused, never loaded as an added module. The counter is written to the log only after every module folder of the build verifies against the list (`verifyTrees`). `kernel.modules-list` events count only when the home wrote them. The owner can reset the counter for a deliberate downgrade (`resetModulesList(chain, proof)`, presence `grant.modules_list_reset`, one `kernel.modules-list-reset` event).
- feat(presence): PS-3. A paired device whose key is not attested as hardware is recorded as a software key with no prompt (the sessions list says so), and a space's standing rule (config presence.softwareKeyCap) gives it the 90-day cap back; the default is no cap.
- fix(presence): the paired-session tools are named pair-grant, start-paired, pair-challenge and end-paired (a tool name is lowercase; the camel-case names made the whole presence module invalid in d8e851159). A start now signs a challenge the box made for the grant, so a signed start from an earlier grant is worthless (reviewer-2 PS-2), and a paired session past 30 days plus 3 without a rotation answers only presence.person.rotate (PS-1). Real-vyred test in test/person.test.js.
- feat(presence): an owner-paired device opens its person session at pairing, with no second sign-in (ADR 0032 section 2d). `presence.person.pair-grant` (wink only, reads the pair record, key id from the verified proof), `presence.person.start-paired` (the device proves the confirmed key, one refusal for every failure, three tries), `presence.person.rotate` (30-day secret rotation signed by the device key) and `presence.person.end-paired` (device removal, reset, sign-out everywhere). A paired session slides 30 days idle with no 90-day cap; migration adds presence_pair_grants and presence_people.paired. Needs tailnet's `wink.device.record` and the calls in the pair answer.
- fix(connectors): an api sign-in whose token store fails now takes back the credential it just made (`removeCredential`, as the person who started it), so none is left tokenless; a re-connect keeps its old credential. test(vault): a live-pass and a sign-in-token move into a real shared vault are refused with nothing written.
- test(vault): a completed `vault.move` by a member, a refused move for a read-only member, role refusals and a rotate, on the existing two-member shared-vault rig in core/vault/shared.test.js. docs/work/vault.md corrected: the rig existed.
- fix(vault): `members.invite` builds the invite and the key wrap before the member is added, so a failure there no longer leaves a member with no invite. The rest of the shared-vault member paths, the .env rewrite and the connectors writes were swept and are listed in team/0.2/CHAT.md.
- fix(vault): a provider sign-in token is never put or moved into a shared vault (`vault.put` to `<vault>/claude-setup-token`, `vault.move`): both are refused and recorded as `vault.refused` (reviewer-2 low).
- feat(vault): a refused attempt is a record of its own. `Vault.refuse(action, name, who, why)` writes one audit row (ok false, "refused: ...") and emits one `vault.refused` event (who, which item, why; never a value), used when a put or a grant tries to attach a module grant to a provider sign-in token, an invalid grant is put, a move meets a live pass, or an edit rename would strand grants. Also: a Drive write that cannot be recorded (the pool step fails) takes its version back out and removes the stored object, leaving no orphan.
- fix(vault): the lead's rulings on VP-5 and VP-6. A refused `vault.put` (an invalid grant, or a grant on a provider sign-in token) writes nothing and leaves exactly one audit row saying it was refused. The write-then-refuse order was checked in every other vault write: `vault.pass.create` pinned a person's card before it checked hosts, methods, paths and items (now checked first), `vault.move` wrote the shared copy before remove refused an item in a live pass (now checked first), and a `vault.edit` rename to a provider sign-in item carried grants after the old item was gone (now refused up front). A packaged build that is told `vault.launcherOnly: false` ignores it and logs one line saying so.
- fix(vault): reviewer-2 VP-5 and VP-6. VP-5: every grant on a put is validated (a short list of valid module names) before the item is written, so a refused grant leaves no new item and no changed value or audit row (it used to write, then fail). VP-6: `vault.launcherOnly: false` is honoured only in a development build (lib/build-kind.js); a packaged release always has it on, whatever config.json says (`buildKind` is a code-only constructor option, not read from config).
- feat(vault): VP-1 closed: `vault.launcherOnly` is on by default. The two provider sign-in items (claude-setup-token, anthropic-api-key) take no module grant and no module can release or inject them, so only the session launcher reads them, through the credentials port. core/onboard stores the token without `grants`; a put that carries grants for those items is refused before anything is written (it used to write, then fail). `vault.launcherOnly: false` turns it off. sessions' core/switchboard/launcher-only.test.js now reads the port from the registry (the vault provides it).
- fix(vault,daemon): the vault clears `credentialsPort` when it stops (`ctx.provide(name, null)`), and the daemon's sandbox then says the vault is not running instead of reading a stopped instance (reviewer-2 note on VP-4).
- 0.3 install (launch): the box has no Tailscale sidecar. compose.yml is vyred and the docker-api proxy; vyred owns its network and publishes the onboarding page on host loopback; the image ships the pinned Wink core binaries at /opt/vyre-wink/bin (VYRE_WINK_CORE_BIN, VYRE_WINK_CLI_BIN) and the compose sets VYRE_SEAL_PROFILE=server. install-box.sh drops the TUN check, adds a memory and disk preflight (how many spaces fit the larger store, from the one constant that matches stores/twenty REQUIRE.memoryMb), and writes VYRE_KERNEL=1 and VYRE_STORE=auto into vyre.env once. The wrapper no longer starts or mentions Tailscale. compose.egress.yml is untouched (platform's row).
- fix(runner): the runner module no longer fails to start on a real kernel (walk step 11: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'deviceId')"). `ctx.kernel.runnerPorts` needs the host's answers (the person's chain, this computer's device id and key, sync and spec), which the module called without; building them now answers "not connected yet" through `runner.status` instead of throwing. The host supplies them as `ctx.kernel.runnerHost()`; until that exists the runner reports that it is not connected.
- fix(runner): macOS home profile, reviewer-2's three gaps. The network is closed except one loopback port, the per-session egress proxy in internet mode (core/runner/homeproxy.js: public addresses only, the same refusals as Linux: loopback, LAN, link-local, the cloud metadata address, carrier-grade NAT including tailnet, this machine's own address, mail ports); the daemon now starts one per session on macOS and Linux and `release` stops it with the session. launchd (`launchctl` and its Mach services) and the preferences daemon are denied, and the per-user temp (`/private/var/folders`) and `/private/tmp` are unreadable except the session's own folders. The self-test now PROVES each from inside before every session on a Mac: a launchd job started from the session must not run outside, `defaults read` of another app must fail, a file in the per-user temp must be unreadable, and a direct connection to a public address must fail. Tests: home-network.test.js and reviewer-2's rv2-seatbelt.test.js in the hosted Mac job.
- fix(runner): RN-3b (reviewer-2). The transcript is opened with O_NOFOLLOW and the descriptor's device and inode are compared with what the path check saw, so a link swapped in between is never read; the project folder is rechecked (device and inode, not a link) before recover's temp file and rename. The checkpoint store refuses an assistant acting for the person (an agent hop with no session of its own).
- fix(sessions): on Windows an agent session gets no shell tool, or does not start (reviewer-2 ENG-1; lead's ruling until a Windows sandbox exists). `spawnSession` passes Claude `--disallowedTools Bash,BashOutput,KillShell,KillBash,PowerShell`, and refuses an agent it cannot start without a shell (codex, grok, gemini and others) with one plain reason; other systems and non-agent commands are untouched (`windowsShellGuard` in lib/agent-sandbox.js). Hosted Windows test: core/sessions/windows-no-shell.test.js in `test:windows`.
- fix(runner): reviewer-2's gate of the own-server seal (RN-1 to RN-5). RN-5: the two checkpoint actions are now registered in the kernel (`checkpoint.write`, `checkpoint.read`, kernel/gateway/checkpoints.js; two segments because the grant syntax allows no more) and only the owner role holds them, so the owner can mint a per-session grant to that session's own chain; before this every store call was not_found. RN-2: with the kernel on, start, stop, lock and move accept only the home's owner (`ctx.kernel.owner`), not any member's person chain. RN-3: `createTurnSeal` takes the provider's projects folder as `root` and refuses any file that is not the plain file `<root>/<project>/<session>.jsonl` (other path, `..`, link, another session's file, link as project folder), for seal and recover alike. RN-4: a checkpoint's turn can be at most one past the last, and the owner's seal numbers its own turns. RN-1: the store keeps a line count, a sparse offset index and the last line instead of every line; lines are read from disk by offset (`getTranscript` takes an optional `limit`), a replaced tail truncates the file; seal reads only the new bytes in 4 MB slices and `recover` writes in pages. A second finished event for a sealed turn returns the same checkpoint. Tests: ownserver, checkpoint-store, person-chain, and checkpoint-kernel (real kernel authorizer).
- fix(runner): the Mac sandbox suite is green on a hosted macOS runner (run 37168094398: 103 tests, 97 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped Linux-only).
- fix(runner): the macOS home profile could not write into the folders it allows back (project, temp): on a hosted Mac the blanket `(deny file-write*)` was not overridden by a later `(allow file* (subpath ...))`, so every session write failed with EPERM. Each writable folder now also gets its write operations named, which the hosted diagnosis (run 37167578152) showed works. The Mac workflow no longer uses `--test-force-exit` and the measure step has 25 minutes (3 reps).
- feat(runner): own-server sessions are sealed at every turn like lent ones. core/runner/ownserver.js: at a turn's end only the complete lines of the provider's transcript are taken (a torn tail waits), the file is fsynced, the lines go to the checkpoint store and the checkpoint is written last; `recover` puts the file back to exactly the last whole turn (temp, fsync, rename) so `claude --resume` starts from a complete history. A provider that rewrote its file is refused as a continuation (`rewritten`). The module seals on `thread.finished` when the sessions side supplies `ports.ownServer.resolve`; new events `runner.sealed` and `runner.seal-failed`.
- fix(runner): who is "the person" for start, stop, lock and move comes only from `ctx.kernel.chain(meta)` with the kernel on (a chain of person hops only, no viewer, agent or service hop); a web, setup or unknown device or tailnet label gets no chain and is refused. The old label refusal stays only as a legacy-label shim for a kernel-off daemon.
- test(runner): a hosted-Mac test loads the real home and lent seatbelt profiles with sandbox-exec and fails the job when seatbelt rejects either, or a command does not run in it, so a profile that cannot load can never pass silently again.

- test(runner): the macOS Mach probes (clipboard, keychain, Apple events) first run a command that must work in the same sandbox (so a profile error cannot pass them) and compare with the same command outside (a marker on the clipboard, the keychains listed), then require the sandboxed one not to see it (reviewer-3, HS-4).
- fix(runner): the macOS home sandbox profile no longer lists one deny rule per LAN address: seatbelt accepts only `*` or `localhost` as the host of a network address, so the profile was invalid and no home session could start on a Mac (found by the hosted run 37162622014, 7 home-sandbox tests failed with "host must be * or localhost"). The daemon ports are still denied on every address by port.
- fix(runner): checkpoint I/O. The transcript is fsynced before the space is told a checkpoint exists, and the local checkpoint file is written by temp file, fsync, rename and folder fsync (it was a plain write, so a power cut could leave it empty). A full disk (ENOSPC, quota) refuses the line with `disk_full` and cuts the file back (no half line, no gap in the numbers), leaves no temp file, and shows as `reason: "disk_full"` on the `runner.checkpoint` event; the checkpoint the space already holds still stands. A torn last transcript line (a kill in the middle of an append) is cut off at the next start instead of dropping the whole outbox, and a temp file left by a killed process is removed. Restore writes through the same atomic path and leaves no temp file when the disk fills. New core/runner/checkpoint-io.test.js and scripts/runner-ckpt-bench.mjs (20 sessions at once, throttled disk, SIGKILL rounds).

- feat(0.3, memory): the surface-chain fallback in core/memory's kernel gate is deleted. With the kernel on, a memory call with no kernel chain is refused whatever caller label it wears; the CLI, local and Deck get the owner's chain from the daemon's proven facts. Two named exceptions: a first-party module's own call (registry flag) and the Capsule, with a test that runs a real daemon and fails when the Capsule no longer needs it.

- feat: the `{{field:<urn>#<name>}}` resolver (kernel-2's shape). `kernel/core/fields.js` resolveFields; the registry resolves placeholders in an OUTWARD tool's input before the call is held (core/modules/index.js), from the record under the person the session's turn is for (their own grants, not the room's view; the daemon hands in `resolveFields`). A value they cannot read, a missing record, no session or too many placeholders refuses the whole action with `placeholder_unreadable` and nothing is held or sent; otherwise the held answer names which fields will be filled in (`resolved`, names only) and which sealed ones the sealing door merges at the send (`slots`); a sealed field is never substituted. Tests: kernel/core/fields.test.js, test/threadsock.test.js.
- feat: a person's own surface call carries a kernel chain in a module (CUTOVER.md G). The daemon proves facts about the connection (`callerFacts`: a person's cli, local, deck or mobile call on the 0600 socket; a paired or signed-in owner device on a listener) and the registry passes them as `meta.kernelFacts`, set only by the daemon; `ctx.kernel.chain(meta)` builds the owner's chain from them with the kernel's builder (refuses a uid that is not the owner's), after a session token's chain and before the module's service chain. The Capsule is not wired yet.
- feat(core): the caller sweep, part A (TAILSCALE-removal step 2, additive). `device`, `space` and `agent` stand next to `tailnet` in every caller list and in PERSON_CALLERS; approval, vault-reveal and vault-forward tools get `device` only. `callerAllowed` admits `device:<id>` for a `device` entry and never lets a bare `tailnet`, `device`, `space` or `agent` pass as a caller; `space` and `agent` entries admit nothing yet. `lib/caller.js` gains `isDevice` and `isSpaceMember`, with tests for `Device:`, `device :x`, `device:` and zero-width look-alikes. The kernel golden set gains two caller columns (`space:alex@harlow`, `agent:kit`); no existing cell moves. Nothing is deleted.
- feat(kernel): a task's answer reaches whoever asked. When a doer completes a task with output kind decision, fields or note and it goes to done, the task row keeps `answer` (plain frozen data, at most 8 KB) and `task.completed` carries it; an approved needs-check task of those kinds keeps the doer's evidence as `answer` with `outcome: "approved"` and `task.approved` carries it. This is how a Flow's ask and agent steps read the answer back. Merged kernel-2's standing rules 37399f23d and containment 8bcdd51ea.
- feat(chat): task U, chat and asker on every assistant turn, and step 7 on a real vyred process (chat 0.3). core/stream/group.js passes `{ chat, asker }` on every threads.start and threads.send of an assistant turn (seam path); the Switchboard opens the asker's kernel session before any word reaches the session. The live rig lost its ks.open stand-in and now covers carol's turn stamped with carol's session, an outsider getting no session, and ignored chat/asker inputs. core/switchboard/index.js: a send to a dormant thread resumes it with the turn's chat and asker (it opened the owner's session and refused the reply). New core/stream/e2e-step7.test.js and e2e-step7-vyred.js (skipped unless VYRE_E2E=1): a real vyred process, a real WebSocket, kill -9 mid-turn and restart. start() gains two test-only options, `kernelPresence` and `kernelForWrap`, that vyred's main.js never passes.
- test(chat): task T, the group stream's live rig runs on the real Switchboard (chat 0.3). core/stream/group-ks-live.test.js loads core/switchboard and core/sessions and drives the fake claude; the stand-in threads module and scripted thread events are gone. The only stand-in left is opening the thread's kernel session from the person's send (threads.start/send carry no chat or asker yet). Found: the Registry hands kernelSession and sandbox to a module named "switchboard", whose manifest is "threads".
- feat(chat): task S, the stream uses the kernel-session seam on the daemon path (chat 0.3). An assistant's kernel session is vyred's: the stream asks `ks.forThread(thread)` for beginTurn (first, once per turn; `unsupported` falls back, any other failure is a refused turn) and appendOpen, and never opens a session for an assistant. A restart goes through `ks.reopenPending({ timeoutMs: stream.resumeWaitSeconds * 1000, onGiveUp })`; a given-up turn shows "couldn't resume, ask again" and its pending reply is dropped. Daemon: `deps.kernelThreads` (`forThread`, `reopenPending`) reaches the stream module alone as `ctx.kernelSession`; the daemon reopens at start only when no stream does. Tests: group-ks, group-ks-live (real kernel and sessions, rig for threads), group-ks-daemon.
- feat(chat): Highlight to assistant. A "Highlight to assistant" action under a finished message and in a terminal block's footer pins the message, the selected part of it or the terminal's output as a chip above the composer (one tap removes it); it is quoted into the person's own next message when they send. Nothing is sent by highlighting. apps/app/src/chat/highlight.js.
- merge: work/flows, work/kernel and work/kernel-chats-2 into work/chat-03; stores/twenty `storeFor(space, meta)` kept with the kernel's per-Space `stageFactory`.
- test(chat): task R, an assistant reads what its person reads (chat 0.3). The access test no longer asserts a blanket denial of an assistant on the person's own chat (that was the old reach rule); a real-kernel test in core/stream/kernel.test.js drives the daemon-shaped call (`cli:agent:<name>` plus the session token): alex's assistant opens a chat alex is in, gets `not_found` on a chat between others, `as` names nobody else, an unlisted assistant and another person's assistant are refused. Merged origin/work/kernel a49848b4c (stream tools are already OPEN in core/modules/agent-reach.js; no code change).
- feat(chat): task Q, nothing reaches a group chat except through the reply handle (chat 0.3). Reasoning, tool progress, tool and terminal blocks, asks and files are written to the kernel's reply handle and shown with its `rid`/`ver` through the same per-viewer check and field-value rule as the reply text; a turn of thinking only writes nothing (the old release at a status was dead code: status frames are not shown, so the buffer never emptied; a status now ends the turn). The wait for an assistant session after a restart ends after `stream.resumeWaitSeconds` (60): the reply is dropped, the room gets `status failed, note "couldn't resume, ask again"` and the app says "Couldn't resume. Ask again.". A terminal, diff or files block in a chat of more than one person carries `note: "visible to everyone in this chat"`, drawn as a quiet line under the block. ADR 0052 gains the honest limits. Tests in core/stream and apps/app/src/chat.
- feat(chat): task O, group replies stream per viewer (chat 0.3). With the kernel on, an assistant's reply opens at its first delta (`chats.appendOpen`, stamped with the room's membership version) and each delta is written as it comes; a viewer receives a frame only if `chats.mayReceive(viewerChain, rid)` says they were in the room at that version and still are, so someone who joins mid-reply gets none of it and gets the next reply; the whole-message hold is gone and `room_changed` is not used. The filter is the viewer's `may(frame)`; frames a viewer may not have become cursor-only `session.hidden` frames. A new participant sees the chat from their join (`viewer.floor`; earlier messages one `hidden` span, earlier joins marked `quiet`); apps/app draws one quiet "Chris joined" line. Merged origin/work/kernel-chats-2 (25dd88c19). core/stream/reply-port.js, fake-reply-port.js, group-stream.test.js (x100 seeded with random link kills and a mid-stream join, both ports).
- feat(flows): standing rules for a space, the two behaviours authorize calls on. Draft only: a `service` step uses the connector's draft operation (`draft: { method, path }`), a `call` step its `draft_as` action, and nothing is sent even after an approval; no way to draft means the step fails with the rule's words. Always ask: the held task is answered by the named person or role, carries the rule and cannot be waived. Never: the step fails with the rule's label. feat(sessions): the sandbox takes the session's token variable from the existing auth resolution (the vault items claude-setup-token and anthropic-api-key); `forThread` gains `beginTurn`.
- feat(kernel): `service.read` (read) and `service.call` (outward.send, asks first) are registered actions on `vyre://<space>/service/<connector>`, for the Flow step "Call a service" (sessions) and vault's forward; cherry-picked records' unique-field lines (`unique_violation` is a refusal, `FieldDefinition.unique`). Merged work/flows 9a64b1e75.
- fix(core): reviewer-2's R-1 and the lead's E-2. An assistant claim is PROVEN only when the daemon bound the call to a session (`meta.thread`: a session's own socket or a vouched key); an unproven `thread:` or `agent:` label on the person's own socket reaches no person-reach tool, open or ask-first (label walk test on the person's socket, and a proven session socket gets open tools and a held ask-first tool); the retrofit gates carry the thread through the legacy chain. The golden matrix gains two proven caller columns (appended); unproven agent cells go back to denied (1,950 cells, none to allow). A sandbox that cannot be built on macOS or Linux refuses the session with the reason (only a development build can opt out, VYRE_SESSION_SANDBOX_OFF). `threads.mode` and `files.drive.access` are person-only (an assistant must not change its own mode; widening a share); `glass.take` stays open on purpose (the user's hands-free screen rule; the person's stop stays person-only). The default assistant has an off switch: `grants.defaultAssistant.remove(chain, { presence })` and `.add`. `spaces.invites.confirm` is classified. Sessions' sockets in a private folder are 0600.
- feat(daemon): stages for hosted Spaces (a `stageFactory` in the Spaces registry builds the stages module over each Space's own kernel); `personChainFor` (a device chain of this home, never session facts) and a durable `turns` table for the Switchboard's kernel sessions (reopened after a restart); the session opener is a device chain so kernel-2's CH-7 rule does not refuse it. Merged work/flows d6bf63d47 and work/records 17bff60cb.
- feat(sessions): Grok runs. A provider that cannot move its settings folder (`relocatable: false`) starts sandboxed with its own real folder allowed back and nothing else; the session is marked partly sandboxed (`thread.sandbox` partial, one notice per machine). Needs runner's planHome to accept it (asked in CHAT.md); the real-sandbox test skips until then. chore: the stale core/daemon -> core/sessions boundary entry is removed (kernel-session lives in lib).
- feat(flows): the trigger registry (kernel/flows/triggers.js): five kinds, one entry each. New `watcher` trigger and `runner.watcherItem` with a bridge from the watchers module (kernel/flows/watcher-bridge.js, ports only). Schedules read cron in the Space's time zone (DST gap and overlap rules in kernel/flows/zone.js), survive a restart and catch up once. Every run records which trigger fired and with what (`source`, capped and scrubbed `input`, `caught_up`, `missed`); `paintRun` answers why a run ran.
- feat(flows): the `service` step (Call a service) replaces `http`. A Flow names a connector (a vault credential and its route), a method, a path and optional query, headers, body and Drive references; it never holds a URL or a credential. Reads (GET, HEAD) run at once (`service.read`); anything else is `service.call`, outward, held for the ask-first task and run once with that approval. The compiler refuses an unknown connector or a path the route does not allow and lists connector, method, path and Drive files in the effects. The runner calls a `ports.service` (the vault's forward); responses are capped, credential headers dropped, the run tainted.
- feat(sessions): the sandbox launcher is proven on a real sandbox (lib/agent-sandbox.e2e.test.js: bubblewrap on testbox, scripted session over its own socket, self-test passing and refusing, real claude and codex starting from a relocated config folder). The provider table now carries `private` (config-folder relocation: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME; Grok has none and refuses to start sandboxed). The launcher refuses a workdir that is or contains the home, passes an environment allow-list and refuses a credential in argv. Windows starts unsandboxed with one notice and `thread.sandbox` on the log. kernel-session: `forThread` (calls, never the token) and `reopenPending` (restart). fix(switchboard): a resume no longer ends a pending one-turn ask on another provider (resumeQueued), and the return waits for its own switch.
- feat(sessions): a chat turn's kernel session. `threads.start` and `threads.send` take `chat` and `asker` from the first-party stream only; the Switchboard opens that turn's session for the asker through the daemon (the kernel checks they are in the chat), the thread's socket stamps the current turn's token, and the previous turn's ends. fix(modules): the kernel-session and sandbox deps went to a module named `switchboard`, which does not exist (it is `threads`), so neither ever reached the Switchboard.
- fix(sessions): the provider sign-in token comes from the daemon's one-shot credentials port (`ctx.credentials(provider)` for the threads and agents modules), not from a module grant on the vault items, so `vault.launcherOnly` can be switched on: a session still signs in and a module asking for the token is refused.
- feat(sessions): a chat turn's kernel session. `threads.start` and `threads.send` take `chat` and `asker` from the first-party stream only; the Switchboard opens that turn's session for the asker through the daemon (the kernel checks they are in the chat), the thread's socket stamps the current turn's token, and the previous turn's ends. fix(modules): the kernel-session and sandbox deps went to a module named `switchboard`, which does not exist (it is `threads`), so neither ever reached the Switchboard.
- fix(vault,daemon): VP-4. The vault may provide `credentialsPort` again after a restart and the new port replaces the old (no more "already provided" failing the vault's start); the daemon's sandbox asks the registry's current port at each call instead of holding the first. Nobody but the vault can provide it.
- fix(vault): the forward's never-passed header families also cover `x-access-token*`, `x-oauth*`, `x-session*` and `x-goog-api-key` (reviewer-2 low).
- fix(wink): sixth-run pairing gate (X-1, X-2, Q-2, Q-3, D-1b) and the words check. A phone's or server's QR (and the ring, `relay.pair.ticket`, once the Wink module is up) is a gated ticket: redeeming it makes a waiting pairing in the relay's memory, with no device row, no presence key and no bridge session, and a channel that reaches only `wink.phone.wait` (phone, ring) or `wink.server.adopt` (server); `relay.pair.pending.confirm` (module:wink) enrols the device only after the person picks the right words, and a no, a timeout or `relay.devices.drop` leaves nothing and keeps the ticket spent. `device.paired` carries `via` and `gate`; new event `pairing.pending`; new internal tools `relay.pair.pending.confirm` and `relay.pair.gate`. The server's pairing question is seen and answered only by cli, local, deck and capsule (an allow list). `--pair-to` is set from the server's own command line and needs a signature by a key on that identity's list (`identityEntry` and `signIdentity` ports), never a claim. A storage device may call exactly `wink.storage.bridge` and `wink.storage.bridge.accept`. A bare yes is refused on the server console and the phone question: the person picks the right three words among two decoys (`pick`) or types the first word (`first`); `scripts/install/i.sh` asks for 1, 2 or 3.
- fix(wink): fifth-run pairing fixes. The three confirm words come from the ticket secret, both keys and two fresh nonces with commit-then-reveal (`pairing.commit/reveal/tag/cancel` on `wink.server.adopt`, the same on `wink.phone.wait`), so two pairings of one app and box differ and a relay between two sessions shows different words per leg; every end of an ask (expired, no, wrong pair-to, cancelled, error) drops the app's relay device; a second scanner cannot end the first one's ask and an app whose QR ticket was taken is told at once; a phone is named by the name it sent ("A phone" as fallback); `wink.phone.scan {code}` says `typed_code_off`; a ring-paired phone is held for the same words and registers nothing before them.
- feat: the `{{field:<urn>#<name>}}` resolver (kernel-2's shape). `kernel/core/fields.js` resolveFields; the registry resolves placeholders in an OUTWARD tool's input before the call is held (core/modules/index.js), from the record under the person the session's turn is for (their own grants, not the room's view; the daemon hands in `resolveFields`). A value they cannot read, a missing record, no session or too many placeholders refuses the whole action with `placeholder_unreadable` and nothing is held or sent; otherwise the held answer names which fields will be filled in (`resolved`, names only) and which sealed ones the sealing door merges at the send (`slots`); a sealed field is never substituted. Tests: kernel/core/fields.test.js, test/threadsock.test.js.
- feat: a person's own surface call carries a kernel chain in a module (CUTOVER.md G). The daemon proves facts about the connection (`callerFacts`: a person's cli, local, deck or mobile call on the 0600 socket; a paired or signed-in owner device on a listener) and the registry passes them as `meta.kernelFacts`, set only by the daemon; `ctx.kernel.chain(meta)` builds the owner's chain from them with the kernel's builder (refuses a uid that is not the owner's), after a session token's chain and before the module's service chain. The Capsule is not wired yet.
- feat(kernel): a task's answer reaches whoever asked. When a doer completes a task with output kind decision, fields or note and it goes to done, the task row keeps `answer` (plain frozen data, at most 8 KB) and `task.completed` carries it; an approved needs-check task of those kinds keeps the doer's evidence as `answer` with `outcome: "approved"` and `task.approved` carries it. This is how a Flow's ask and agent steps read the answer back. Merged kernel-2's standing rules 37399f23d and containment 8bcdd51ea.
- feat(kernel): first-party signing for a packaged box. The release ships `modules.json` (every shipped module's version and tree hash, plus a counter) as one more line of the SHA256SUMS that the release key already signs; the kernel (kernel/modules/release-list.js, kernel/home.js) verifies SHA256SUMS.sig against the release key, checks modules.json's sha256 against its line, and treats a module as first party when the list names it, its folder hashes to the listed tree and its version matches (a changed file, an added file, a different version or an unlisted module gets one plain log line naming it and why). The highest counter accepted, with the signed material that carried it, is kept in the sealed log and re-verified at boot, so a rollback, a missing file or a forged log event never relaxes it. `scripts/modules-manifest.mjs <unpacked package root> --counter N --release X.Y.Z` writes the list for the release job. Per-module `module.sig` stays valid next to it. Tests in kernel/modules/release-list.test.js (tamper, add, version, unlisted, no signature, another key, edited list, rollback, missing, forged event).
- chore: new person-reach tools from wink and vault classified (pairing and provider changes person-only, provider status open).
- feat(kernel): `gateway.leases.forward(chain, { session|connector, method, path, query?, headers?, body?, upload?, saveTo?, idem?, approval? })`: a credentialed request run at the home by the vault's forward. Authorized HERE for the caller's chain (a person's or a Flow run's) against the route before the vault is asked: `service.read` for GET and HEAD, `service.call` (outward) otherwise, which comes back `{ held }` and sends nothing; the credential comes from the Space's own session definition (`leases.bind` routes, now with an optional `connector` name), never from the caller; a Drive file it reads or saves needs the caller's own `drive.read` or `drive.write` (reviewer-2 FW-2, FW-3). The daemon passes `forwardCredential`, which calls the vault's internal `vault.forward` as `module:leases`; the Flows host's "Call a service" port goes through it. A connector with no session definition needs the vault's route table, which is not exposed yet (says so).
- feat(test): `absent` in test/helpers.js, a presence verifier that finds no person, for tests that a denied proof stops a presence-guarded tool.
- feat: Flows run in the real daemon. `core/daemon/flows-host.js` assembles `createFlows` per Space (the home's own and every hosted one) over that Space's kernel: the records-backed run store (record types are defined if missing, so an existing home gains `flow_schedule`), the Kit store, stages made of tasks, the log subscription, a timer and recovery, and the `service` port (kernel decides `service.read` or `service.call`, then the vault's forward). The first-party module `core/flows` registers the `flows.*` and `flows.kit.*` tools, each under the caller's own chain (a person on their own surface acts as the Space owner, an assistant only through a daemon-bound session token); approve, pause, resume and remove-a-Kit are person-only. A Flow run's automation hop is a job label under its approving person in authorize. Record type names and event types may contain underscores (the gateway refused `def_flow`, so the records-backed store had never run on the real gateway). Proof: test/flows-daemon.test.js, a real daemon with a Flow defined through the tool, approved, run by a record event and a schedule, and still there after a restart.
- fix(core): a module receives what only the daemon can hand it by DECLARATION (`needs.daemon`: kernelSession, sandbox, flowsHost; built-in modules only), not by a name: the Switchboard's real manifest name is `threads`, so the earlier name match handed it neither and every real session started with no kernel session and no sandbox. A missing sandbox on macOS or Linux with the kernel on is a refusal; the self-test probes are real (a unix socket and a loopback listener, made per self-test and torn down). Test against a real daemon boot in test/threadsock.test.js.

- fix(vault,daemon): the credentials port no longer needs `core/daemon -> core/vault`. The vault provides it to the registry once at its own start (`ctx.provide("credentialsPort", ...)`, `provideOnce` in core/modules/index.js: only the vault, only that name, only once); the daemon reads `registry.deps.credentialsPort` and sets `sandbox.credentials`; `takeCredentialsPort` and the daemon import are gone.
- fix(vault,seal): reviewer-2's forward gate (FW-1 to FW-3) and provider-token gates (VP-2, VP-3). FW-1: request headers from a lent program are now an allow-list, not a pattern: a safe default (accept, accept-language, content-type, content-language, if-match, if-none-match) plus exactly the names the route's own record lists (`headers` on a route, passed as `allow_headers` by the home); every other header is dropped, and the method-override, rewrite, forwarding, proxy, `sec-` and credential-carrying families (x-http-method*, x-method-override, x-original-url, x-rewrite-url, x-forwarded-*, x-real-ip, x-host, authorization, cookie, host, x-goog-iam-*, x-amz-security-token, x-ms-authorization-*) are dropped even when a route names them. FW-2: the Drive is reached as the lent member: `deps.filesFor({ session })` is the kernel's Drive door under that session's member chain (a held file request records its session and is sent through the same door), so the route's Drive lists only narrow it; `deps.files` stays for a rig with no kernel. FW-3: a test shows the route, credential, limits, Drive lists and header names come only from the home's record and anything the program adds is ignored. VP-3: `Object.hasOwn` on the provider tables (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString` no longer pass). VP-2: the daemon takes the credentials port once, right after the vault starts (core/daemon/index.js), and hands it to the sandbox the Switchboard reads per session; the port answers a string, the shape sessions reads (`credentials("claude")` is the setup token, `credentials("anthropic")` the API key, null for nothing); a test fails if the port is not the daemon's.
- fix(seal): found by moving the sealing and door tests onto the kernel's real chains. A member on a paired device could not reveal a sealed value: the kernel's device chain carries `via.device` and no `via.surface`, and the process accepted only deck, capsule and mobile surfaces. `chainCtx` now reports `device`, and reveal accepts a person on a paired device (the hardware-signed proof is what proves them); a daemon speaking for a person in a session (no passkey) still cannot. Tests: kernel/seal/testing.js builds person, agent and module chains with the real chain builder (SHIM(chain-shapes) for the shapes no door builds); the forward and file tests use the real sealing process and a real kernel chain (SHIM(gateway-forward), SHIM(authorize)); kernel/gateway/leases.real.test.js runs the kernel's lease wiring against the real process, with a real hardware proof for reinstating (SHIM(presence) for the kernel's own grants acts).
- feat(seal): the master key for 0.3 (the lead's rulings). A server uses profile "server" (a file master owned by the sealing process's own uid, an agent's uid refused); a desktop home, the default profile, now uses a 0600 file master inside the Vyre home, so no development switch is needed anywhere (it was refused until an OS keystore existed, which is a 0.3.1 item). `health` reports `custody { master, profile, platform, note }` and `custodyNote` says in plain words where the key lives: on a server root or a stolen disk can read it; on a desktop Vyre's own sessions are sandboxed away from it and the disk's encryption protects it at rest; on Windows sealed data is only as protected as the PC's own account. Tests: both profiles boot with no development variable (sealer and a real kernel boot); `kernel/seal/custody.test.js` checks that the macOS profile denies the whole Vyre home and nothing allowed back reaches the kernel folder, that the Linux profile gives an empty home with no bind into it, that on the box image the agent uids (1001, 2000 to 2063) are refused, and the Windows notice.
- feat(vault): two additions a practice-management connector needs (from the Clio research note). An OAuth credential may leave `scopes` out, and its refresh request then carries no `scope` at all (a provider that takes none). A credential may set `rate: { per_minute }` (1 to 6000, default none): the vault holds every caller of that credential (Flows, sessions, forwarded programs) to one shared allowance, waits for it up to 30 s and beyond that refuses with `rate_limited` and `retryAfter`; the same limit counts forwarded file calls. A provider's own 429 is waited out by its `Retry-After` (seconds or a date, up to 30 s, at most two retries, safe for any method because the provider did not act), the cooldown is shared by every caller of the credential, and a longer Retry-After is handed back to the caller untouched.
- feat(0.3, memory): the one Ask door. `memory.ask` is unchanged for the person; one to one, the Space's memory (core/work's engine) is one more source the existing answer pipeline retrieves from; in a chat with more than one person it is answered from the Space's memory alone, narrowed to the room, and never reaches Recall or personal facts. `work.know.capture` and `work.know.forget` are the capture port sessions calls once so the Space's memory knows what was said.

- feat(0.3, memory): the 0.3 minimum for core/memory. Every memory tool is gated by the kernel before the 0.2 rules: a call from a chat with more than one person is refused (the room is the running turn's own), and when the kernel built a chain with a person in it, that person must be the home's owner with only their own assistants beside them. Free text is scrubbed with the kernel's sealed-class detectors on every way in; `memory.sealscan` reports what memory already holds, by table and class, and changes nothing. Tests on a real kernel; a test refuses any migration that drops the person's corrections, pins, taught facts, writes or site rows.

- feat(wink): Add a phone by scan or paste, confirmed by three words (DESIGN-wink section 4, ruling of 4 Oct). `wink.phone.open` shows a QR and a long code (a 128 bit secret, one phone, 5 minutes; `typed: true` only behind the development flag); `wink.phone.scan` takes the QR or the pasted text and then shows the same three words the computer shows (`wink.pair.status` state `confirm`); the computer asks "Add Alex's iPhone to your identity? Words: ..." (`wink.phone.pairing`) and `wink.phone.pair.answer` adds the phone only on a yes with matching words. A no, wrong words or 5 minutes without an answer add nothing and drop the phone's relay device; a second scanner is refused by the single-use ticket. New: `wink.phone.pairing`, `wink.phone.pair.answer`, `wink.phone.wait`. `wink.code.ack` is refused unless the development flag is on. Phone QR is `vyre://wink/2?...&k=phone`; a server QR is not taken for it. Copy: cards.js phone lines, `apps/app/screens/devices/wink.js` fallback wording. Tests: core/wink/pairing.test.js, test/wink.test.js (real daemon, flag off).

- fix(wink): reviewer-3's H-1, S-1, P-1, Z-1, D-1 and the user's rulings Q-1 and typed code OFF, with `composeWinkHome`. H-1: `wink.server.handover` answers only `module:wink` (an empty or any other caller is refused); the Wink module's own code reads it in-process (`wink.ownHandover()`). S-1: a removed device's signing key is cleared and a re-added row starts with none. P-1: no recurring timer under 60 s: the 20 s liveness probe (host.js) and the held-connection ping (hold.js) are on demand (a link silent for 20 s is pinged before the next call), the 5 s call-level race stays, and holdDrive's 2 s check is one shot. Z-1: `acceptDrive` resolves real paths for the roots and every folder (`realOf`, `rootedDir`), opens with O_NOFOLLOW and O_DIRECTORY, compares device and inode, and re-checks before every frame. D-1: a storage entry (`kind` or `deviceKind` "storage") may call only `wink.storage.*` on the direct and the relay door (`toolAllowed`). Q-1: the first adoption of an unowned server by a paired device is a question at the server (`wink.server.pairing`, `wink.server.pair.answer`): who asks and three words made from both keys (`relay/client/pairwords.js`); no answer in 5 minutes pairs nothing, a second scanner is refused, the app shows the same words (`wink.pair.status` state `confirm`); `i.sh` shows the question and takes y or n, and `--pair-to <identity id or name>` makes an unattended install take only that identity. Typed code OFF: `wink.code.open`, `wink.server.code {typed}` and `wink.pair.server {code}` are refused unless `VYRE_WINK_TYPED_CODE=1` (or config `wink.typedCode`); `i.sh` and the cards say scan or paste. `wink.peer.shared`, the claim path and `peers.serve` are deleted. An unowned box refuses a non-device caller's `release`; a release the server never confirmed is given up after 30 days with a card. `composeWinkHome({ ctx, host, kernel, wink, space, serve, identity, handoverSource })` (core/wink/compose.js) sets `ctx.peerDoor`, wraps with `withKernelCall` using `host.pathOf`, and returns `{ peerDoor, handover, holdsOnSession, pathOf, serve, serveHome, own, stop }`.

- test(0.3, work): the memory engine, the group-audience rule, @Engineer, the native situation, teammates (context, delegation, doing line, stuck watch) and the Estate end to end run on the real kernel (`test/kernel-rig.js`, `createKernel`); the fake kernel is gone. Fixes it forced: notes and proposal tasks now match what the kernel accepts, auto-accept is the kernel's own rule, the Engineer reads definitions and `types.defined` and checks narrowing with `authorize`, `delegateGrants` carries the adder's presence proof, the stuck watch reports through `ask.stuck` as the doer.
- feat(kernel): the built-in store answers at 100,000 records. A query's equality and range comparisons are left bare where NULL and false agree, so a field index serves find by email and list by stage (they were wrapped in COALESCE and scanned the type); an unfiltered grouping has its own covering index; search has a trigram full-text index (sealed fields never indexed, built in slices on an older database) and ranks in SQL; a ranked search with one common word beside rare ones ("Client 4521") never reads the common word's postings. Every path is proven equal to the reference store on random queries and pages. BL-1: the event log's filter columns are generated from the event JSON. BL-3: a record's kernel attributes ride in its create event and the log wins over `kernel_attrs`.

- fix(kernel): DL-1, containment on every dimension of a grant. `contains` (delegation) and the new `containsDims` (also used when a grant is narrowed in place) compare actions, the resource prefix, row predicates, the field list, where (surfaces, nodes, residency), when (start, expiry, schedule), how (presence order none < session < fresh, the same approver, once), budget (same meter, limit not larger), rate (count not larger, window not shorter), once, audience and delegation depth: equal passes, tighter passes, looser refuses. A dimension or key it does not know (in the parent or the child) refuses, so a field added to grants later fails closed until it is taught. A grant that carries a `schedule` is never met silently (authorize makes it an ask: it stores a schedule but does not evaluate one). At every start the grants store checks each stored delegated grant against its parent and cuts one that is wider to its parent's limits (`clampTo`), writing a `grant.narrowed` event that says why, and revokes one that cannot be cut down.

- feat(kernel): standing rules for a Space (DESIGN-flows-joints 5a). An owner sets a rule with a fresh presence proof (`gateway.grants.rules.set`, `remove`, `accept`, `dismiss`; `list` for a manager and above; `propose` for a Kit or anyone holding `rules.propose`, with no effect until an owner accepts). A rule is `{ kind: never | draft_only | always_ask, binds: [assistants, members], covers: { actions, resource? }, approver? (always_ask), label }`, an event in the sealed log that survives a rebuild. `authorize` asks the rules BEFORE grants and a rule only tightens: `never` denies (`rule_never`), `always_ask` makes the act wait for the named person or role whatever any grant says (the approving held act is checked against the approver in `tasks.approvedAct`, once), `draft_only` allows only a draft (obligation `draft_only`, kept even after an approval; `seal.deliver` refuses it). Every decision under a rule carries `rule: { id, kind, label }`. A rule binds an owner's own assistant, and may not cover the rules calls. Presence for a rule act is signed as `grant.rule_<verb>` (the sealing process accepts only task and grant acts).

- feat(kernel): `chats.beginTurn(token)` (CH-10 as ruled): the session's turn fixes the room's membership version before its first read; everything the turn reads and the reply it opens belong to that version or an older one, so the kernel does not depend on the stream's call order (reads still lower the version, so a stream that never calls it is covered). A test walks every `read` action in the gateway's table under a group token. `core/sessions/kernel-session.test.js` no longer expects the removed `size`.

- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's gate of 0c095c487. X-1: only a chain made from a session TOKEN is `delegated` (`fromFacts` takes `from_token`, set only by the Surfaces door's `chainFor`), so the daemon's own owner chain (`session_person` built in process) opens sessions as before. CH-8b: the room rule now covers every gated read, not only records: a read action is allowed to a group session only when every person in the room is allowed it (`roomedAuthorizer` in kernel/core/room.js, wired once in the gateway), so tasks, drive, listings (grants, members) and event reads give the room's view; `tasks.needsYou` keeps only tasks everyone may read; an event is seen only if every person in the room may see it. CH-10: a reply belongs to the OLDEST room version any read since the last reply was made under, so a reply built before someone joined never reaches them, however late it is opened. R4-b: a failed state-changing call restores the store from the log, and if the log cannot be read either, from a copy of the state the call started from (`rebuild` also swaps back on failure), never an empty store.

- fix(kernel): a streaming reply stops when the assistant, as well as the person it acts for, is removed from the chat: each `write` and `close` checks the token, the person and the listed assistant; what was already written stays and the log records `message.ended` with the bytes, the hash so far and the reason, and the handle is then `closed`. feat(kernel): `ctx.kernel.chats.roomFor(token)` for event-driven code: the same live room as `audienceFor` (same rules, same rate limit) from a token that verifies and names a chat, only for a module whose manifest declares `needs.kernel.room: true`.

- feat(kernel): a reply belongs to the room version it was written for (team-lead's ruling, replacing `room_changed`). `chats.appendOpen(token, { kind?, chat? })` opens a reply stamped with the chat's membership version and returns `{ id, chat, ver, write(delta), close(final?) }`; every write checks the token is still good and the person still in the chat, and a handle is dead after close. `chats.append(token, message)` is the same in one step (a person's own message is stamped the same way). `chats.mayReceive(viewerChain, messageId)` is the one answer to "may this person receive it": true only if they were in the room at the message's version and are in it now, for the asking person only. Each chat keeps who was in it at each version (`chat.changed` events carry `ver`, `joined`, `left`); `room_changed` and the read-version tracking are removed; reads still see the live room.

- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's chat findings CH-7, CH-8, R3, R4 and the room handle. CH-7: every chain made from a session token is `delegated` (and carries the chat its token names); `chats.create`, `chats.change`, `surfaces.open` and `surfaces.revoke(session, chain)` refuse a delegated chain, so only a person acting directly, in the chat, changes who is in it. CH-8: a session whose token names a chat of more than one person reads the room's view at the gateway itself (records get, query, aggregate, search and event views): a field is a value only when every person in the live room may read it and it is not sealed, else the placeholder `{{field:<urn>#<name>}}`; a record any one of them cannot read is not in the view; filters, sorts and groups only on fields the whole room may read. R3: the room is the chat's live participants at every question (no snapshot), each chat carries a version, and `chats.append` refuses a reply written under an older version once the room has grown (`room_changed`). The handle is `{ group, read, canRead }` (no `size`), `read` and `canRead` are rate limited per session, and `canRead` applies row predicates. R4: every state-changing call in the grants store (create, revoke, narrow, setRole, transferOwner, removeMember, addActor, offer, unoffer, the invite calls, sweep, installModule, chat create and change) runs one at a time and, when it fails while writing its sealed event, restores the store from the log and tells the caller it failed; a revoke can no longer undo itself at the next rebuild.

- fix(wink): reviewer gate W-4, W-5, W-7, the node-key hijack and the signed relay instruction. `wink.server.adopt` records the adopter for every caller kind (a cli adoption too); once an owner exists any change is refused unless the target space's admin claim holds (the kernel directory port's admin check, until the signed claim exists) or the owner's presence is shown on the new `wink.server.retarget`. `wink_compute` is dropped (a migration); compute offers live only in the kernel's `gateway.grants.offers`, called through the `offers` port of `createWink` (a fake in tests). `devices.add` is an upsert that refuses a change of identity, kind or owner, and adopt's own row has `devices.setSelf`. `peers.shared(device, nodeKey, stableId)` never binds: only the node key the host reports as proven for a call (the fourth argument of `peers.serve`) binds, and unproven notes expire after a minute; `host.serveHome` takes `{ peers, serve }` and uses them; `peers.ownSecret()` is the server's `shared` for `joinPeer`; `createPeerAllowCache` gives the bridge a sync `allow(deviceId)` over `wink.peer.allow`. `homeServe(peers, inner)` is the home's peer door dispatcher for `withKernelCall`. `wink.relay.apply` takes an instruction signed by an owner device's registered key (`wink.device.key`, presence) so a headless box changes its relay without a presence path.

- feat(seal): service credentials, sealed instead of in a 0600 file (the Space's Twenty API key, for records). `sealer.service.put({ name, value })` (also how a rotation lands, in place), `get({ name })` at the point of use, `delete`, `list()` (names only) and `adopt({ name, file })` (moves an existing file in once and shreds it). A name is `<module>.<space>.<what>`. Held in the sealing process's own folder, encrypted under its master, on no other disk; a call that says a model started it is refused; nothing else ever returns a value. 64 of 64 seal tests.
- feat(vault): provider sign-in tokens on the items Vyre already has (reconciled with sessions; supersedes the `provider-token` kind, which is gone). The items stay `claude-setup-token` and `anthropic-api-key` (made by core/onboard, chosen per session by `sessions.auth`; `LAUNCHER_ITEMS` in core/vault/vault.js). What is added: `vault.provider.set`, `vault.provider.remove` (presence; only you, or the setup page for you, add, replace or remove them: a module, agent, watcher or hook is refused, also through `vault.put` and `vault.delete`) and `vault.provider.status` (which are stored and when, never a value); and `takeCredentialsPort()` (core/vault/index.js), a frozen `{ credentials(provider) }` the daemon takes ONCE and hands to the session launcher (`claude` or `anthropic`: the token or null, one audit row per use without the value). - feat(vault,storage): files through the forward (the lead's addition; JCS needs a retainer sent for signature and documents filed). BUILT: Drive references both ways. The lent computer sends a Drive path and version, never bytes: the home reads the file as a stream and sends it as a plain body or a multipart form (text fields plus Drive files, exact length known), and a download is saved straight into the Drive (`saveTo`) with a reference coming back; a response can also come back as a stream for an in-process caller. NOT BUILT: a file streamed up from the device inside the request, because an outward call must wait for a person and a stream cannot; the device syncs the file to the Drive first. `vault.forward.file` (core/vault/forward-file.js) enforces per-route `maxBytes` (default 25 MB up and down, refused before sending or stopped mid-stream with nothing left behind), `contentTypes` (request body, parts and response; default JSON, form and text) and `drive: { read, write }` path lists (default none, dot segments refused). An outward send is held with the files named and pinned to their Drive versions and content hashes; after approval it is rebuilt from the held record, must match the hash, and sends exactly those bytes even if the file has changed since. A credential value split across chunks of a response is caught and the save abandoned; error answers are scrubbed. Nothing is held whole in memory: `Pool.putStream` and `getStream`, `Drive.putStream`, `stat`, `stream` and `driveFiles` move a chunk at a time. Routes take `maxBytes`, `contentTypes` and `drive` (`normalizeRoute`), and `leasedForward` takes a `forwardFile`.
