- feat(vault,seal): credentialed calls from a lent computer run at the home (the lead's ruling: one mechanism, no header value, key or token ever reaches the device). `vault.forward` (internal tool, callable only as `kernel:leases`, `ApiRequests.forward` in core/vault/request.js) runs one forwarded request through `vault.request`'s own checks (hosts, SSRF guard, read or outward) and returns `{ status, headers, body }` as bytes or `{ held }` for an outward call held for the ask-first task. The three kinds a real firm needs all work through it (a plain key, an OAuth sign-in that refreshes with the rotation sealed, a Google service account with delegation whose subject and scopes are the credential's). `kernel/seal/uses.js`: `normalizeRoute` and `routeAllows` (per-route allow and deny lists of method and path pairs, deny wins, the default is no, the kernel's path rules), and `leasedForward` (a live lease, the session's route, then forward, then one `vault.used` event). Limits: request bodies are text, JSON or form up to 1 MB (a binary or multipart upload is refused with a clear error); a response is returned as bytes up to 2 MB and refused beyond it, never cut; no streaming. Text responses are scrubbed of every credential value, bytes that carry one are withheld. `leasedUse` (which returned a secret) is superseded and goes when platform's `leases.use` moves to `leasedForward`.

- feat(kernel): the default assistant is a delegate. It holds no grants; alone it can do nothing, and acting for a person (a chain of that person and `assistant`) authorize treats its hop as a pass-through, so it can do what that person can: not a role or grant change (model chain), not chat membership, not an admin act without the person's presence, and a send raises a task. Named assistants are not delegates. A Space made before it existed gets the actor only by an owner's approval with presence (`grants.defaultAssistant.present()`, `addActor`).

- fix(chat): the reviewer's gate on chat 0.3 (C-1 to C-6). `stream.open` authorizes per session before it makes a ticket or a log (a chat's readers are its participants; a thread is read with threads.get as the caller; the kernel's `session.read` is asked too when it can speak for the caller), tickets are bound to the caller and device, last 15 s and are used once, unknown ids are refused. `term.open {session}` resolves the session as the caller, `cwd` must be the session's folder, `term.attach` re-checks it, a typed command is recorded with its typist (author, via, surface), and a terminal is documented as a full shell, not a sandbox. The stream draws every frame for its viewer on the server before it is sent (sealed and hidden fields are placeholders, a record the viewer may not see is an empty `hidden` frame with its cursor) and `thread.shell` output is redacted. `ws.js` and `sanitize.js` moved to `lib/` and the stream and term boundary exceptions are gone. `threads.edit-retry` and `threads.retry` check the keyboard before they rewind, messages record their author and only the author (or the owner's own surface) edits one. - feat(chat): the real group send path and door streaming (chat 0.3 task I, ADR 0052). core/stream/group.js: tools `stream.send`, `stream.react`, `stream.pin`, `stream.keep`, `stream.mark-read` (reach person). `stream.send` appends the caller's message (author from the caller), routes it with whoAnswers (an @mention, the default assistant when no person talks to a person, or `to`), and hands the words to each answering assistant's own switchboard thread (threads.start first, threads.send after, one uuid per message and assistant); each thread's frames are projected into the group's log with the assistant as author and the asker as acts_for. Two or more answers make a fan-out set; `stream.keep` marks one. Deliveries sit in an outbox until the switchboard takes them and every thread's last projected event is stored, so a stop and start loses and repeats nothing. Read markers are stored per person and heard by that person's other open connections only (`also` option on serve). core/stream/door-adapter.js maps door.stream events (text, tool_call, cut, done) to frames with the asker's chain as author and acts_for. apps/app: Frame typedef gains author, acts_for, message; join notices show display names; box-stream gains sendGroup, keep, react, pin, markRead through the outbox. threads.send takes `uuid` from first-party modules only. - feat(kernel): the grants store (kernel/grants). Grants and memberships are kernel records with one event per change (grant.created, grant.revoked, grant.narrowed, member.set, actor.added) and `rebuild()` from the log. `grants.create`, `revoke`, `narrow`, `list`, `setRole` and `addActor` are risk-`grant` acts: a fresh presence proof by the granting person bound to the exact input (verified by the one verifier, `grant.*` ops), never from a chain holding a model (`model_chain`). Widening is a new grant; narrowing is in place and only smaller; a delegated grant is contained in its parent and made by its holder; revoking a parent revokes its children. The five roles instantiate their bundles (kernel/grants/roles.js); temp carries a scope and an expiry; a Space keeps an owner. `authorize` reads grants and members from the store (the retrofit path stays when no store is given). Selectors take an optional `fields` allow-list: the gateway omits other fields on read, refuses writes to them (`field_not_allowed`) and refuses filters, sorts and groups on them; `human`-level seals hide a field from members outside the reveal roles. Stage gates are not built yet.
- feat(kernel): the tool surface (kernel/tools, built by the assistant team, landed here once) and the kernel facade it reads: `Store.types()` (suite revision 3), `gateway.definitions(chain)` through authorize, `actions()`, `members.roleOf` and `isAdmin`, `serviceChain(name)`, `tasks.list`, `ask` and `model.call` when tasks and a door are wired. - fix(kernel): reviewer-2's K4 gate items 1 to 8 and 11. A task is decided once at a time, the kernel's skip proposal has no doer and its card says skip, the card's recipients and slot classes are resolved by the kernel (`resolve`), the approved body is `{ action, resource, payload, facts }` as a frozen copy and a send must name an outward action, `seal.deliver` is unblocked by an approval for exactly its sink and recipients, `use` and `deliver` belong to the task's doer and expire after a day, a sealed slot must be on the task's record, `revise` goes through the table, and `reveal` is refused when no door is wired.

The tasks' own verifier is deleted. A proof is used up when checked.

A standing service reads only what it declared, a presence session never stands for an assistant on admin or grant, an unknown condition makes the effect ask and `rate` is an obligation, stored job chains expire, a poison event is retried then set aside, `audit.verify` checks commitments, the gateway owns kernel attributes (a record it did not write matches no predicate), a store that alters a field or returns a stale version is caught (`store.disagreed`), no cursor when only unreadable rows remain, and a generated-caller differential test proves the gates match the registry beyond the golden matrix.
- feat(kernel): K4, tasks with approval (kernel/tasks): the transition table as data, human-only `decide` from a chain that is exactly one person with a hardware-signer proof bound to the payload hash, decision and chain (single use), the kernel-built approval card, kernel output checks, stuck detection. An approved task is an approval: `createApprovals` hands the sealing wiring the approver chain, the template version, the record and the sealed slots from the canonical body the person approved, so `seal.use` and `seal.deliver` open only for an approved task. - feat(kernel): kernel/contracts/identity.d.ts: Identity (id plus kind: user, space, device, agent, project, session, task) as the base type, devices owned by a user or space identity and never members of a space, DeviceKind and offers, Node, Offer and Use (a member's computer runs a space's work only with both grants, for that member's own sessions). Constants IDENTITY_KINDS, DEVICE_KINDS, OFFER_KINDS, DEVICE_OFFERS.

- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's K1 and K2 gate items. Wildcards cover only read and write actions and need an action-set version, unknown trust or class labels are refused, a delegated grant dies with its adder's membership, a predicate on a missing attribute never matches, URN segments refuse dot, encoded and control forms, a model chain cannot filter, sort or group on a sealed field (new `Store.describe`), the retrofit's presence and asked gates fail closed, `fromLegacy` moved to a legacy-Space-only builder, `recover` completes only on an exact match, `gateway.events` goes through authorize, type and id are validated on every call. Field kind `ref` is now `link`, and the old `link` is `url`. Sealing is vault's: the kernel's own seal and door code is gone, work/sealing is merged and `kernel/gateway/sealing.js` wires it.
- feat(kernel): K3, sealing and the inference door (kernel/seal, kernel/model). The sealing process (serve.js: a line protocol on stdin and stdout, run under the Node permission model with no child processes, no workers and no files outside its own and the vault and egress folders) holds sealed values encrypted under the Space's vault key and is the only place plaintext lives; `put` returns metadata only, `use` merges into a template's body at a declared slot and hands the output to the egress boundary (a verified contact point or a document of the same record only; from a model's plan always an Ask), `reveal` needs a kernel ticket bound to the exact call plus, on the kernel side, a chain that is exactly one person and a signer's proof over that reveal, used once. The class registry (SSN, ITIN, EIN, card, bank account, routing, IBAN, passport, tax id, medical, free), one normaliser (full-width, digit words, separators), best-effort detectors, a per-session seal ledger of keyed hashes, and `model.call`, the one door: it refuses a service that is not a declared sink, a provider the Space does not allow and any prompt containing a value the session resolved, and sends only detector-sanitised text. The gateway returns placeholders to declared sinks as well as to a model in the chain. The shared `gate` moved to kernel/core/gate.js. 18 tests.
- feat(kernel): K2b, the retrofit. `Registry.call` can now take `deps.gates` (kernel/retrofit/gates.js): the static permission gates (module reach, outward, visibility, callers, guest, person session), the presence requirement and the asked requirement are then decided by `authorize` over grants compiled from today's rules, and the inline rules run only when no gates are given (the default, so nothing changes in a shipped build yet). The golden set proves the two paths give the same answer for every tool, caller shape and world (120k cells on the box and local roles); seven deliberately broken gates were each caught. Schema checks, projectArg, the rules hook, proof verification, the asked-match and running stay in the registry.
- feat(kernel): K2a: the gateway's record calls (kernel/gateway: authorize first, an intent before the store call and one event after, rows filtered by the gateway itself so a store cannot leak, ids minted by the gateway and kept, version hashes verified on read with `modified_outside`, sealed values as placeholders for a model, recovery of intents a crash left open), the in-memory reference store (kernel/store) and the conformance suite that defines "a store" (kernel/conformance, 14 rules plus 5 broken stores the suite must catch). Retrofit against the golden set is K2b.
- feat(kernel): K1 (kernel/core): `authorize` (contract 6.3: space check, candidates and an effective grant per hop, structural narrowing with the parent rechecked and its obligations carried, policy by risk class, taint, sealed placeholders; deny by default and fail closed), the kernel-built chain (`createChainBuilder`: only SurfaceFacts in, a model's call is never the person, unvouched agent claims have no chain, a stored job chain is sealed with a key), time-prefixed ids, canonical JSON and one hash, and the event envelope with a hash-chained, salted-commitment in-memory log (erasure keeps the chain verifiable, at-least-once consumers with durable cursors). 31 tests. Presence signatures and approvals are K4; durable storage is K2.
- feat(kernel): K3, the sealing door. `kernel/seal`: a separate sealing process (stdio, bare environment, its own 0700 folder, AES-GCM bound to ref, Space, record and field) that holds sealed values: `put`, `use` (sealed slots merged into a sealed derivative, only to the record's own verified contact point or a document for it, else a presence proof), `deliver` (to an egress sink socket, only a status returns), human-only `reveal` (a hardware-signed proof over the exact payload, one use), `detect` (placeholders), `lookup`. `kernel/door`: the inference door and seal ledger, and a CI check that no file outside the sink registry names a model provider. Vault and Drive actions, events and the "used for Gmail 3 times today" summary in `kernel/seal/uses.js`. Tests: canary-corpus and no-plaintext properties.
- feat(kernel): kernel/contracts/roles.d.ts: the five fixed roles (owner, admin, manager, member, temp) as grant bundles (`ROLE_BUNDLES`), `Membership` (temp needs a scope and an expiry), `VyreName`, `SpaceIdentity` (a Space is an identity with a vyre.run name and a root key) and the optional person name on `Actor`. Types and frozen tables only.
- feat(kernel): a reply belongs to the room version it was written for (team-lead's ruling, replacing `room_changed`). `chats.appendOpen(token, { kind?, chat? })` opens a reply stamped with the chat's membership version and returns `{ id, chat, ver, write(delta), close(final?) }`; every write checks the token is still good and the person still in the chat, and a handle is dead after close. `chats.append(token, message)` is the same in one step (a person's own message is stamped the same way). `chats.mayReceive(viewerChain, messageId)` is the one answer to "may this person receive it": true only if they were in the room at the message's version and are in it now, for the asking person only. Each chat keeps who was in it at each version (`chat.changed` events carry `ver`, `joined`, `left`); `room_changed` and the read-version tracking are removed; reads still see the live room.

- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's chat findings CH-7, CH-8, R3, R4 and the room handle. CH-7: every chain made from a session token is `delegated` (and carries the chat its token names); `chats.create`, `chats.change`, `surfaces.open` and `surfaces.revoke(session, chain)` refuse a delegated chain, so only a person acting directly, in the chat, changes who is in it. CH-8: a session whose token names a chat of more than one person reads the room's view at the gateway itself (records get, query, aggregate, search and event views): a field is a value only when every person in the live room may read it and it is not sealed, else the placeholder `{{field:<urn>#<name>}}`; a record any one of them cannot read is not in the view; filters, sorts and groups only on fields the whole room may read. R3: the room is the chat's live participants at every question (no snapshot), each chat carries a version, and `chats.append` refuses a reply written under an older version once the room has grown (`room_changed`). The handle is `{ group, read, canRead }` (no `size`), `read` and `canRead` are rate limited per session, and `canRead` applies row predicates. R4: every state-changing call in the grants store (create, revoke, narrow, setRole, transferOwner, removeMember, addActor, offer, unoffer, the invite calls, sweep, installModule, chat create and change) runs one at a time and, when it fails while writing its sealed event, restores the store from the log and tells the caller it failed; a revoke can no longer undo itself at the next rebuild.

- fix(kernel): the offers port takes the member for the member's own side from the proven caller's chain, never from an argument (reviewer-2, low): a call naming another member is refused.
- fix(kernel): the room's `canRead` judges a task by both `records.read` and `tasks.read` (the narrower of the two), and team members, playbooks and records by `records.read` on their urn, for every person in the room; a test covers all four kinds and that the handle names no one.

- feat(kernel): merged kernel-spaces 4156c6cbf (`grants.transferOwner` on the gateway and the remote table, `kernel/remote/person-of.js`). New narrow service read: a first-party module that declares `needs.kernel.membership: true` gets `ctx.kernel.membership(person)`, which answers `{ member, role }` for one named person in this Space and nothing else, and every answered call is an owner-visible `membership.read` event naming the module and the person. Listing members stays under the calling person's own chain (`grants.members.list(chain)`).
- feat(kernel): the chat is in the session from birth (reviewer-2 CH-1 to CH-5, V-1, V-2; team-lead ruling in DESIGN-chat.md). `surfaces.open(chain, { chat })` writes the chat into the signed token after checking the opener is in it; `chats.bind` is gone. `ctx.kernel.audienceFor()` takes the room from the turn the registry is running (the token of that call, held in `core/modules/index.js` `currentCall`, never one a module passes) and returns `{ group: false }` or an opaque handle `{ group, size, read(resource, fields?), canRead(resource) }`: a field is a value only when everyone may read it and holds the same value, a sealed field is always restricted, a record anyone cannot read is null, and no chain or per-person answer leaves the kernel. An opener who left the chat gets `no_audience`. `ctx.kernel.chats.append(token, { kind?, body, chat? })` is the only write path: the destination is the token's chat, an assistant must be listed, the log records who wrote where with a hash, never the text. Viewer chains are internal to the room, are not "exactly one person" and are refused by create, change and read. `ctx.kernel.canRead` and the chains from `audienceFor` are removed. Kernel code: kernel/core/room.js.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's V-1 and V-2 on the chats. A viewer chain is not "exactly one person" (`isExactlyPerson` false, `chainCtx().one_person` false), so it cannot open a session, hold a lease, decide a task, change a chat or reach the sealing process as the person; probe and test in kernel/chats.test.js. `ctx.kernel.canRead(chain, resource, action?)` lets the harness answer from what each person in the room may read.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's re-gate of e8b2806ac. M-1b: a `kernel.minimums` event now carries the release-signed document itself and is re-verified against the release key at every boot; the counter and minimums come from the verified document, an event that does not verify is ignored and named in the log, and the highest verified counter wins (forged-event probe in kernel/minimums-home.test.js). M-3b: "packaged" is decided at build time: `lib/build-kind.js` says "development" in a checkout and `scripts/build-site.sh` stamps "release" into the package it signs; anything but the exact word "development", a missing file included, means packaged and ignores the developer switches. The golden recorder's `--write` now refuses a refresh in which an existing cell moves from refused to run unless `kernel/golden/allow.json` names it with a reason (`weakened` in kernel/golden/index.js).
- feat(kernel): chats the kernel owns. `gateway.grants.chats` (`create`, `change`, `read`, `bind`) keeps each chat's people and assistants in the sealed grants log (rebuild and snapshot carry them). `read` is the stream's read decision: participants only; an owner or admin outside the chat is refused; an assistant reads only a chat the person it acts for is in and that lists it. `bind(chain, session, chat)` ties a session to its chat once, by the asker, and never moves it. `ctx.kernel.audienceFor(extra)` (extra.token, the call's session) returns `{ group, chains }` of read-only viewer chain (new `viewer` facts; authorize refuses every act above read for it) for every person in that session's chat, asker first; the room is never an argument and it throws `no_audience` for a session in no known chat. `ctx.kernel.chats` is the same API for the stream module.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's gate of a148d874e. F-1: `leases.use` no longer takes a credential from the runner. The Space holds the mapping, set when a session is bound (`leases.bind(session, lease, { routes: [{ route, ref, methods?, paths? }] })`); a use names only the session and the request (host, method, path), and the credential is looked up from that definition; anything not mapped is absent, a path is checked like a Drive path, and a GET or HEAD is `vault.read` while any other method is the outward `vault.call` and asks. The runner's `vault.credential` forwards `{ session, route, method, path }` only. F-2: `drive.restore` and `drive.restoreBackup` are their own admin action (`drive.restore`, owners and admins, needs presence), a version must be a positive integer and a put is size-capped. M-1: the accepted minimum versions and their counter are `kernel.minimums` events in the sealed log; a missing, unreadable, unsigned or older `minimums.json` never relaxes them (the counter file is gone). M-3: `VYRE_KERNEL_FILE_KEY` and `VYRE_KERNEL_PATH_RULE` count only in a development tree (`kernel/devbuild.js`: a tree carrying `SHA256SUMS` is packaged and ignores them, loudly).
- feat(kernel): Wink's `offers` port over `grants.offers` (W-5). `ctx.kernel.offersPort()` (kernel/remote/offers-port.js) gives `get(space, device, { member, device_key })` and `set(space, device, side, on, { member, device_key, meta })`; the wink module uses it when no `inject.offers` is given, so wink_compute is never touched on a kernel home. `set` runs under the caller's chain (`ctx.kernel.chain(meta)`) with the proof from `meta.kernel_proof`, finds the offer to withdraw with the new `grants.offers.find({ side, member, device })`, and is a no-op when the offer is already as asked. `core/wink/pairing.js` passes the member (the device's identity), its node key and the call's meta. The golden set is refreshed for runner.start (runner's merged change).
- chore(repo): `.github/CODEOWNERS` names the repository owner's GitHub login as the required reviewer for `/kernel/` (identity, seal and door included) and `/.github/workflows/`. It takes effect once "Require review from Code Owners" is switched on in branch protection.
- feat(kernel): the daemon opens the Spaces registry at boot (`bootHomeKernel` builds `createSpaceKernels` over the home's sealing process and awaits `spaces.start()`, one kernel per hosted Space, each in its own sealing namespace, no key file; a file key only in development). `ctx.kernel.storageIndex` for the pool's own module (`wink-storage`): `record(head)` writes vault's `storage.index { seq, hash, copies, at_risk }` into the log so the checkpoint owners' devices hold covers it, and `head(checkpoint)` is the head a new home should expect on `restoreIndex` (the latest at or before that checkpoint; unverified when there is none). The golden set is refreshed to the merged registry.
- fix(storage): reviewer-3 notes folded into the index backup work. Scrub rate scales with the pool to a full cycle in two weeks (never under 5 chunks a tick) and the controller skips a tick when the machine is loaded (`loaded`, `scrubCycleMs`). When no copy of a chunk opens (a wrong key, a failing store) scrub and `fetch` keep every pointer and raise an alert (`storage.alert`) instead of deleting; a copy dropped beside a good one is kept on the chunk's `dropped` list for a cycle. The bridge refuses a frame signed before it started, so a restart does not reopen the replay window. (Supersedes the 50-chunk scrub entry.)
- fix(storage): the controller scrubs 50 chunks a tick (reviewer-3 note: 5 was months per terabyte; about 70 GB a day at one-megabyte chunks), `scrubChunks` to change it.
- feat(storage): the encrypted index backup and restore (`kernel/storage/indexbackup.js`). The pool's index and the Drive's paths and versions are written, encrypted under the owner's key with the sequence authenticated, to every node that may hold a backup (never only the home) as `i/<seq>` and `i/latest`: hourly, after 32 MB of change, and at once for the first change (controller option `backup`, event `storage.index { seq, hash }`). `restoreIndex` rebuilds a new home from the nodes alone, takes the highest sequence it can open, drops locations on lost nodes and refuses (`rollback`) anything older than or different from the head the owner's devices recorded (`expected`); without a head it says `unverified`. Run across two boxes: the home wiped, both files read back from the office drive alone, heal remade the copies. Merged work/v0.3.
- fix(storage): reviewer-3 gate on the pool, bridge and Drive (S-1 to S-11). Drive: a turn per path, so two writers at once get two versions and a conflict. Pool: a failed drain leaves the node as it was and a drain checks room by class (the home is never drained); a scrub (a few chunks a controller tick) reads and opens every copy and drops one that is missing or does not open, `fetch` drops a bad copy it meets, and deletes a node missed are kept and retried; one writer per chunk so a node is never counted twice. Bridge: frames carry a nonce accepted once (a captured frame cannot be replayed), a NaN or missing time is refused, `serveBridge` checks the headers and the declared size before reading a body, caps put bodies and in-flight puts, answers a bad escape with 400, and reserves capacity before the write; replies are capped at 8 MB on the home side. S-11: `sealer.poolKey({ owner })` derives the pool key from the home's master for that purpose, per owner. Frame change for tailnet: add `nonce` (see CHAT.md).
- feat(runner) L-1 (platform's per-session socket, reviewer-2 D-1 to D-3): core/runner/homesandbox.js, the sandbox for a session Vyre starts on the person's own computer. Every unix socket and loopback connection refused except the session's own, the whole Vyre home and the person's secret folders unreadable (macOS seatbelt allow-default plus later denies; Linux bubblewrap with a private network namespace, a tmpfs over the home and only the session's socket bound in at /run/vyre-session.sock, VYRE_SOCKET set to it), and selfTest() runs the proof from inside the sandbox before the session starts (person's socket, another session's socket, the daemon's loopback ports, a key file and the Vyre home must fail; the session's own socket must work). Windows is refused with a plain reason until the AppContainer pipe rule exists. Tested on a Mac and on Linux.
- fix(runner): sleep detection compares wall time with the monotonic clock, so a long blocking call is not mistaken for a sleep.
- fix(runner) S-1: the checkpoint reads the workspace from inside the session's own sandbox (reader.js, run by readerhost.js with the same confinement and no network), never from the runner with the member's rights, so a planted link or a racing helper cannot reach a host file: 0 host reads in 10,000 tries on Linux (bubblewrap) and macOS (seatbelt); the Windows reader is the same AppContainer path, untested yet.
- fix(runner) reviewer-2 gate: sync never follows a symlink the session plants (safefs.js: lstat on every folder, O_NOFOLLOW, regular files only, rename into place, the session is paused while the runner reads); the runner's state moved out of the sandbox's view (mnt/state beside mnt/work); a watchdog process closes the workspace when the runner dies, a start-up reconcile closes any workspace nobody holds a lease for, and locked or deleted is said only once verified (lock-pending and delete-pending are chased); the lease is enforced by the wall clock every 30 s and locks after a sleep; a credentialed route lists its methods and paths, the vault is told method and path, and anything else is refused; no home folder, no folder holding a secret folder, and no program outside a granted tool folder is ever bound; seatbelt drops the blanket sysctl-read and the resolver; bubblewrap drops capabilities and nested user namespaces; resume carries the trust label and routes; runner.start takes only a space and a session (the program, routes and credentials come from the space's definition), and runner.revoke is no longer a tool (the kernel's withdrawn-offer callback does it).
- feat(kernel): `personOfChains` (kernel/remote/person-of.js), the product `personOf` for the Wink adapter: a proven device id is a device entry on a member's identity chain, read live on every call, so a removed device maps to nobody at its next call (tested with the real chain and the real server). fix(kernel): `transferOwner` checks every argument before its first step (a `temp` demotion no longer fails after the new owner is made).

- feat(kernel): `grants.transferOwner(chain, { to, demote_to }, { presence })`, ownership handed on under one proof (the new owner is made first, then the caller steps down; a failure between leaves two owners and a repeat finishes it, the store restored from the log). fix(kernel): reviewer-2's W-1 and W-2 on the Wink adapter: `withKernelCall` requires `pathOf` (no default; anything but "wink" is recorded as the relay), the two-machine run passes it on each leg, and a removed device maps to nobody at its next call.

- feat(kernel): `acceptProofRequest` (what an invitee signs from the join card) and `proofChainHash` on ctx.kernel, and kernel/remote/run/real.mjs, the hand-run proof of the remote call between two machines (home on one, device on the other, direct and through a relay; see the kernel-remote-run review).

- feat(kernel): the remote kernel call over Wink's peer wire (`kernel/remote/wink.js`). `winkTransport({ sessionFor })` is the device's transport; `withKernelCall(serve, { serverFor, personOf })` wraps the peer door's dispatcher so the `kernel.call` tool reaches the Space's remote server with the proven device as peer, mapped to a person by the identity chain. Verified against the real `peerSession` of work/wink over an in-memory pipe.

- feat(kernel): the remote kernel call over Wink's peer wire (`kernel/remote/wink.js`). `winkTransport({ sessionFor })` is the device's transport; `withKernelCall(serve, { serverFor, personOf })` wraps the peer door's dispatcher so the `kernel.call` tool reaches the Space's remote server with the proven device as peer, mapped to a person by the identity chain. Verified against the real `peerSession` of work/wink over an in-memory pipe.

- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's gate on kernel-spaces (KS-1 to KS-7). The remote server shares one answer between a call id sent twice at once (the in-flight promise is stored first), rate-limits per device (members 300 a minute, non-members 30), bounds the stored answers (8 MB, oldest first) and caps a non-member's answer; remote `surfaces.revoke` takes the chain and is held to the session's opener or an admin, and `surfaces.open` may name only an assistant the Space has; `peer.session` is read only from the transport's peer; invite ids are 128 random bits; a hosted Space's kernel key is the home's sealing process namespaced per Space (`kernel/spaces/namespace.js`), no key file unless `fileKey` (development).

- feat(kernel): the spaces side of the kernel (kernel-2). Reads on the grants store, each through `authorize`: `grants.members.list` and `members.get` (a manager and above sees everyone, anyone else only themselves), `grants.invites.get` (the join card: role, scope, expiry, invitee, status and the Space's label, no hash or secret; read by the issuer, a manager, or the person it is for), and `grants.list` filtered the same way. An ownership change also writes a separate `owner.changed` event carrying only `owner_change { op, person, by, role_was, role_is, space }`, visible to the Space (member.set and member.removed stay owner-visible), for the spaces module to append the owner op to the identity chain. `kernel/remote/proof.js`: `proofRequest(space, call, ...args)` (what a surface signs) and `proofFrom(meta)` (the `{ presence }` option from `meta.kernel_proof`), on `ctx.kernel`. `kernel/spaces` (one kernel per Space on a home, `for(spaceId)`) and `kernel/remote` (client, server, wire, in-memory transport): a Space this home does not host is called over the transport port with the same gateway API; the home mints the chain from the peer the transport verified.
- feat(kernel): the daemon's HTTP edge carries `x-vyre-kernel-proof` (base64url JSON, at most 4 KB, malformed is absent) to the tool as `meta.kernel_proof`; the legacy `x-vyre-presence` proof is never one. kernel/identity is windows' final (W-1 fixed, reviewer-2 passed), one identical copy and one pin for work/kernel, work/sealing and work/spaces.
- feat(kernel): K-3, the kernel key never leaves the sealing process. `kernel/core/seal.js` is the one sealing handle: `kernel.mac` and `kernel.verify` of the sealing process (or, for a development kernel, a local key behind the same interface). Only the chain builder (stored job chains, session tokens) and the grants store (its events) hold it. The grants store numbers its own events (`gseq`, `gprev`) so a replay is skipped, verifies them in pipelined batches at rebuild, and a migration pass reads events an older key sealed (position-bound) once, writes one `grants.snapshot` under the new seal and the daemon then deletes `kernel.key`. `createKernel`, `bootKernel`, the grants store's `bootstrap/rebuild/sweep/installModule/snapshot` and the Surfaces door's `open/chainFor` are async; `chains.serialize/restore` return a Promise when the seal is the sealing process (`await` them; a development key answers at once). Measured on the test box: a MAC is 0.4 ms sequential, a verify 0.09 ms pipelined (0.34 ms sequential), so a grants change costs 0.4 ms more and rebuilding 10,000 events about a second. Only a module that declares `needs.kernel` is made a service of the Space.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's K-2, K-3 and A-4, and the wiring asks. K-3: the kernel key is derived inside the sealing process (`kernel.mac`, per Space) and held in the daemon's memory, never written to disk; where the sealing process cannot run safely the kernel does not start (`key_custody`) unless a developer opts into a file key; a key file from before only verifies what it sealed. K-2: first party is a signature by the compiled release key (lib/release-sig.js) with no path-rule fallback and no pin file (a developer path rule is loud and opt-in), and the minimum versions carry a signed counter (`acceptMinimums`) so an older document is refused. A-4: an approval is spent atomically by the decision that uses it, wherever `authorize` is called, within 24 hours of its approval. `surfaces.model.stream` is the door's streaming call under the session's chain. `ctx.kernel.runnerPorts` and `.leases`: the runner's ports from the kernel's pieces, with `allowed` computed by the kernel. `gateway.drive`: VyreDrive behind authorize (drive.* actions, the chain's actor as author, hidden entries absent, no bytes in events). Merged vault's L-5 (member from the chain), recovery and streaming; refreshed the golden set.
- feat(kernel): goals move onto the kernel. With `ctx.kernel` (first-party module, daemon with the kernel on) new goals are kernel records of type `goal` (declared under `needs.kernel` in module.json: actions, prefixes and the type, which the kernel defines at install); goals made before stay in `goals_items`, are read and written where they are and list beside the new ones; with the kernel off nothing changes. `createKernel().kernelFor` is now the one place `ctx.kernel` is built (the daemon and tests share it).
- fix(seal,door): reviewer-2 notes V-3 and S-2. A presence key from before the first pin that is never bound stops proving a day after the pin (`needs_bind`; a sync with its bind brings it back). A streamed tool input is capped at 256 KB and 64 open tools, past which the stream is cut.
- feat(storage): the bridged network drive (`kernel/storage/bridge.js`). A drive that only another device on its network can reach is offered by that device (the bridge) and used by the space's home over the Wink connection: `createBridge` (the handler on the device with local access: HMAC-signed frames, 60 s window, bounded size and capacity, idempotent, a folder underneath), `bridgeBackend` (the pool backend, `send` is the Wink call), `serveBridge` and `httpSend` (a plain HTTP form for tests), and `backendFor` takes a `bridge` for a drive with no local mount. Chunks are ciphertext before they leave the home, so the bridge and the wire carry nothing readable. Run across two test boxes (a directory exported on one, a space whose home is the other): 11 MB in 1.4 s, 12 of 12 chunks on the drive, and a read from the drive alone. `dirBackend.ping` creates its folder.
- feat(seal): the kernel's MAC key (reviewer-2 K-3) lives in the sealing process: `kernel.mac` and `kernel.verify` (client `sealer.kernel.mac/verify`) with a purpose to keep uses apart. The key is derived from the home's master, never returned by any op, and falls under the master's custody rule (a server runs the process under its own uid, a desktop needs the OS keystore, refused otherwise).
- feat(storage): VyreDrive on the pool (`kernel/storage/drive.js`): files by path with every version kept (the newest is working data, older ones cold, unchanged chunks free), two writers give two versions and a conflict flag instead of a merge, a delete is a version that can be undone, `prune` and `pruneBackups` let old things go (never the last backup), backups as class backup (a copy off the home). `Pool.reclass`, a per-device `classes` list (a cold-and-backup device never takes working data) and `kernel/storage/devices.js` `backendFor`, the `makeBackend` for the Wink storage adapter (S3 and cloud volumes through SigV4, a plugged-in disk or a mounted network drive as a folder).
- fix(seal): reviewer-2 follow-ups. V-1: a pinned person's `presence.enrol` brings the current chain (`ops`, else `needs_chain`), which is synced first, so a device removed since the last sync is gone with its keys before its bind is looked at. V-2: `presence.sync` drops keys only on chain evidence (a key whose device left the list, or an unbound key when the chain removed a device the last pin had), so a bare sync cannot force a recovery. L-5: a key lease is keyed by (Space, member, device): another member naming the same device shares no key and cannot revoke it; the member is the chain's own person, a lease id is useless to anyone else, and `lease.revoke` and `lease.reinstate` name the member explicitly (owner or admin acts, decided by the kernel).
- feat(door): streaming through the inference door, `door.stream(input)` (kernel/door/stream.js). The request passes the same checks as `call`; the reply is scanned as it arrives with a hold-back just long enough that a value split across chunks is seen whole before any part leaves (none with no number near and an empty ledger; from the first digit when a number is forming; the longest ledgered form otherwise). A hit stops the upstream and ends the stream with `cut` and a `model.cut` event. A tool call is delivered only after its whole input is scanned. Fix: tool-call inputs in `call` are now judged (a sealed-looking shape or a ledgered value is refused) instead of sanitised and discarded. Measured on testbox2: 0.5 ms per chunk and first text in about 5 ms for plain text, about 5 ms per chunk with a ledger.
- feat(kernel): what windows needed. Invites: `grants.invites.create` (an admin's presence-proved act, bound to the exact role, scope, expiry and invitee; stores a pending single-use approval), `confirm` (the inviter confirms the invitee's fingerprint words; admin and owner invites stay pending until then) and `accept` (under the invitee's own `invitee` chain and their own proof; the kernel applies the membership from the stored approval, with no admin present; refused if expired, used, for another invitee or if what was shown differs from what was approved). Expiry: `grants.sweep()` is the kernel's own act that revokes expired grants and removes expired temp members (and withdraws their offers), reducing power only. `ctx.kernel` for first-party modules (daemon with the kernel on): records, events, grants, tasks, audit, authorize, limits, model, `serviceChain()` and `chain(meta)`; a module is given exactly what its manifest declares under `needs.kernel` (`grants.installModule`, kernel-only, source `install:<module>`); a module from outside gets none.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's L-5, K5-1, K-1 and D-1. L-5: a lease slot, its key and its revoked set are keyed by (space, member, device) (kernel/seal/leases.js, process, client), a refused issue revokes nothing, and `gateway.leases.revoke` lets only that member or an admin revoke (another member naming the same device id cannot). K5-1: kernel/audit/key.js uses windows' kernel/identity/chain.js (position-based validity: the endorsement or revocation names the position of the owner's list it relied on and the device must still be on it), so a removed owner's device cannot endorse or revoke with a backdated time. K-1: first party is judged by signature at every load, with release-signed minimum versions (`signMinimums`, `verifyMinimums`); the registry takes `deps.firstPartyCheck`, which the daemon sets from a pinned `<home>/kernel/release.pub`. D-1: a provider that reports no usage is charged what was reserved.
- feat(kernel): the daemon boots the kernel behind `VYRE_KERNEL=1` (or `start({ kernel: true })`; off by default, nothing changes when off). `bootHomeKernel` (kernel/home.js): a Space id and first owner made once for the home, the kernel key (0600), the durable log and store in the home's SQLite, the module supervisor (self-test at start) and host; `registry.deps.moduleHost` is set so modules from outside Vyre run only under the supervisor. The handle exposes `kernel`.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's G-4, T-1 and T-2. An acceptance (`member_accepts`) names the computer's key and `offers.active` answers yes only for the device that presents that key (leases pass it through), so a second machine cannot claim the first one's offer. The tool surface drops a duplicate tool name (a type tool is never shadowed) and shows only the field names the chain's grant allows.
- feat(kernel): what sessions needed from the gateway. A required task with no checker completes on the kernel's output check (`required` only makes a skip a proposal); `continue_in_space` is a task source only from a service chain; `flow` and `form` travel on a task as opaque, capped data; idempotency keys on `records.create/update/remove/restore` and `tasks.request` (`{ idem }`: a repeat returns the first result, other input is `idem_conflict`); events under a job chain carry `corr` = the run id; `record.stage-entered` is written when a record enters a stage; `chains.forFlow` and `chains.forModule`; an approved held-act task passed as `approval` to `authorize` satisfies the outward ask for exactly that act by its doer, once. The Surfaces door for daemons (`kernel/core/surfaces.js`, `createKernel().surfaces`): the person opens a session and gets a token, the daemon presents it, the kernel mints the chain for that session's person and assistant (never a presence session), and `surfaces.model.call/stream` is the door's call under that chain.
- fix(kernel): G-1b, the grants store's event MAC binds the event's position (its seq and the hash before it), so a genuine `grant.created` or `member.set` appended again later does not verify and a revoked grant or removed member cannot be replayed back; a second `grant.created` for an id is ignored. Taken from sessions (3ebbc0903) with a test: `limits.doorBudget().release` and the door giving back a reservation when a call fails before the provider answers (a call the provider answered and a scan refused is charged its reported usage).
- feat(kernel): key leases wired to the kernel (kernel/gateway/leases.js, over vault's sealing-process leases). `allowed` is computed by the kernel from the two Offers on every issue and renew; withdrawing either Offer, a role change or removing the member revokes the lease at once through the person whose act it was; reinstating a revoked computer is admin-only with the admin's presence proof; a credential is used by route from a session that holds a live lease, per request, with one `vault.used` event that carries no value. Merged work/sealing (leases, presence sync and recovery).
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's K5 and K6 gate. K6: the egress fetch pins the checked address and re-checks the connected socket (DNS rebinding), `privateAddress` parses to bytes and covers every IPv6 form that embeds an IPv4, the self-test proves 13 attempts, the macOS profile is deny-default, `needs.egress` is shown on an install card and approved, shared-suffix wildcards are refused, an entry cannot leave its folder, first party is a signed-manifest check (`kernel/modules/firstparty.js`). K5: a delegated checkpoint key endorsed by an owner and revocable by any owner, a staleness rule on devices, `latest()` verifies.
- refactor(sessions): core/space-sessions keeps only the session engine (one Space per session, checkpoint state with taint and permissions, resume, continue in another space, budgets); the working copy, sync, lease and placement code is gone, because core/runner and the vault own them. fix(sessions): continue.edit sanitizes under the caller's chain. Estate e2e uses the Kit's own payment Flow.
#### ui: real marks, one icon family, no "How this page is made" (native-core, 3 Oct 2026)

- Avatars are marks, never letters. `apps/app/ui/marks/source.js` (pure, tested) draws every mark from the Deck's own generators (`deck/vendor/vyrecode`: creature, agent, teammate character, project and space emblem) plus the person face v2 ported from the prototype and the device drawings of `team/0.3/assets`; the seed is the entity's own seed, else its id (a record with no seed gets its emblem from the id bytes, a contact with no photo a face from its id), else the name's slug. `Avatar` is now `<Avatar of={{ kind, id, name, seed? }} size space onPress />`: `space` draws the 16 pt space emblem badge with a 2 pt ring (it replaces the text chip), `onPress` makes it a button with the nod. `AvatarStack`, `SpaceMark`, `IconTile` (a kind of thing, not a who). One parse per (kind, seed, size band, scheme), cached. Metro now watches `deck/vendor/vyrecode` and `lib/avatar-seed`.
- Icons: `src/ui/icons.source.json` is the 24-grid family of `team/0.3/assets/icons` (stroke 1.6); `scripts/gen-ui-icons.mjs` writes the typed `IconName` union and the element data into `src/ui/icons.generated.ts`. Every earlier name still works through an alias table (`chev-r` is `chevron`, `faceid` is `face`, `box` is `kits`). The glyph characters used as arrows and triangles (Back, stage folds, month navigation, select caret, sort) are real icons now. `gen-icons.mjs` (the 16-grid icons.txt reader) is retired.
- "How this page is made" is gone from the list, board, calendar and record pages (component, `describeDef` and its test).
- Card, type, depth, buttons (ui-system.md, ui-review Global 4, 5, 6, 8, 12). Tokens: `v2.radius` card 16 on a phone and 14 wider, `cardHero` 20 and 16, paper elevation as v3; `v2.type.platform` has the iOS, Android and web role tables and the new `headline` and `secondary` roles. `Card` is surface-2 with level-1 depth and no coloured edge; `hero` steps to surface-3, level 2, padding 20. `Text` gains `headline` and `secondary`, a `medium` weight (500) and the tracking of the big roles; the font is the platform's own by default (SF, Roboto, and Inter bundled as woff2 with its OFL file for the web, precached with the other hashed assets). `Button`: 44 tall on a phone and 36 wider, label 15 medium, secondary is ghost on desktop and a surface-3 fill on a phone. `Chip`: 24 high (26 on a phone), caption 500, and `AskCard` shows at most two. `AskCard` is the hero card, stacks its actions on a phone and no longer draws a "Needs you" chip. New `SectionLabel` (11 mono, uppercase, 0.08em), `SpaceSwitcherTitle` (28 space emblem, name, chevron, no border) and a `Segmented` control of 36 (40 on a phone) with the chosen segment on surface-3.
- Sheet fix: `@rn-primitives` drops `className` on the web for its Overlay and Content (they are not compiled by NativeWind), so the exported web Sheet had no scrim, background or padding. The Sheet, Menu, Switch and Tabs now set real style props from the theme. `scripts/check-sheet.mjs` opens the gallery's Sheet in Chromium at 390 and 1280 and reads the computed style (optional in CI).

#### ui: motion, haptics and phone chrome (native-core, 3 Oct 2026)

- Motion kit, `apps/app/ui/motion/`: springs derived from `tokens.v2.motion` (the token damping is a ratio, so the coefficient is 2 * ratio * sqrt(stiffness) at mass 1; spatial springs may overshoot, effects springs never do), `useReducedMotion` (the person's Appearance setting OR the system's, either is enough), `PressableScale` (spring press feedback; Button, IconButton, Row, board cards and the AskCard title use it), `Appear` and `Stagger` (fade and rise with the token stagger: 24 ms a step, none past the eighth), `Skeleton`, `SkeletonRows`, `SkeletonPage` (shine stops under reduced motion) and `Pulse`. Loading is skeletons, never spinners: Button's loading state breathes in place instead of showing an ActivityIndicator, and Now, Projects, Records and the record page show skeleton rows instead of a blank "Loading". Pure logic in `logic.js`, tested in `motion.test.js`.
- New dependency `expo-haptics`: the only way to give the phone a tap for an approval, a stage move, a selection and a held press (no other module does it on iOS and Android). `haptic.approve / stage / selection / warn`, a no-op on the web. Fired on Send with Face ID, Approve, Mark done, a stage move (board drag or menu, and a record that advances after its last task), a Switch change, a swipe drawer opening, and a hold button completing.
- Phone chrome: `LargeTitleScreen` (the page's large title scrolls away and a small title springs into a bar; Android gets the same component as a medium-bar look with the small title left; wide screens keep the title in the page), pull to refresh on Now, Projects and the records pages (`useStoreQuery().reload` now returns a promise), swipe actions (`SwipeActions` on `Row` and `AskCard`: right is Mark done, left is Reassign and Open; each is a real button, rows also expose them to a screen reader, and a task card keeps its own visible buttons), a native `Sheet` built on reanimated and gesture-handler (token springs, drag the grabber or title to dismiss, Close button, dim-area tap, reduced motion fades instead of sliding).
- Sheet: `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` 5.2 declares reanimated 4 support but needs its own provider and portal and cannot be proven here without a device, so the sheet is built on the libraries already in the app (about 100 lines, one fewer dependency). The web keeps the dialog (`Sheet.web.tsx`); the props did not change.
- Row to record: no shared-element transition. Reanimated 4's `sharedTransitionTag` is experimental (a static feature flag and a native rebuild) and cannot be tried without a device. A record opens with the platform's own push (the iOS spring, the Android system transition; a fade under reduced motion), then the back row, title and body rise in with staggered springs.
- Table: `Table.tsx` is the native implementation (Rows, no TanStack); `Table.web.tsx` is the wide implementation with TanStack Table; the phone-width web list is the same Rows (`TableRows.tsx` holds what both share, so neither platform file imports the other). Same props.
- Type: the font setting now reaches the text. `sans` stays Instrument Sans (the brand default); `system` is the platform's own (SF on Apple, Roboto on Android, Inter then the system UI font on the web: Inter is not bundled); `serif` is the platform serif.

#### ui: one UI codebase, @vyre/ui in the Expo app (user ruling, 3 Oct 2026)

- `apps/app/ui` is `@vyre/ui`: the one design system for iOS, Android and web (the Mac and Windows shells load the web build). Tokens come from `lib/theme/tokens.json` only: `tailwind.config.cjs` maps each name to a CSS custom property and `ui/theme.tsx` writes them (defaults, then the space, then the person) with NativeWind `vars()`. Components are cva and NativeWind on `@rn-primitives` (Switch, Tabs, Sheet, Menu), TanStack Table (wide tables) and `@dnd-kit` (web board). New dependencies and why: nativewind, tailwindcss, class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge (the shadcn-style component stack); @rn-primitives/* (accessible primitives); @tanstack/react-table (tables); @dnd-kit/core (board drag); babel-preset-expo (NativeWind's JSX transform).

#### ui: tokens v3, the theme resolver and the UI contracts (work/ui, step 1)

- `lib/theme/tokens.json` gains a `v3` group (what a space and a person may configure: the five accents with dark and paper values, density, font, corner steps, the component and field-kind lists). `scripts/gen-tokens` writes `deck/css/tokens-v3.css` (space, radii, density, font and corners as root attributes; with none set every value equals v2) and `deck/ui/tokens-v3.js`.
- `lib/theme/contrast.js` is the colour maths a custom accent needs (contrast, mix, ink by luminance, the nearest passing colour), pure, shared by Node and the Deck (served at `/lib/theme/contrast.js`).
- `deck/ui/theme.js` resolves defaults, then the space, then the person, and writes the result onto the root: attributes for density, font and corners, custom properties for the accent. A custom accent that fails contrast is replaced by the nearest that passes, and the result says so.
- `deck/ui/contracts.js` holds the types (records, tasks, events, the Store interface) the generated screens read.

- feat(sessions): budgets. core/space-sessions/budget.js meters `session_hours` (reserved at start, settled at end) and turns a door `ai_spend` refusal into `budget_exhausted`, stops the session and raises a task for the person. fix(kernel): the door gives its reservation back when a call fails or is refused (`doorBudget.release`).
- fix(flows): the flows harness uses the sealing Presence, wires the rule evaluator and the gateway's stage hooks; stages made of tasks hang on `onStageEnter` and `stageTasks`; door-bridge moves to lib so voice no longer imports core/sessions.
- feat(kernel): the rule evaluator moves into the kernel (kernel/expr: parseExpr, evalExpr, LanguageError; records/language/expr.js and errors.js re-export it) and is the gateway's default, so no consumer wires one. `createKernel` (kernel/index.js) is the composition root: log, store, chains, grants store (or the caller's grants and members for a rig), limits, tasks, evaluator, sealing client and door, gateway; `bootKernel` is the same with the durable log and store.
- feat(kernel): the durable kernel on the home. `createSqliteStore` (the reference store written through to SQLite, same conformance suite), `createSqliteEventLog` (the hash-chained log with its salts and cursors, written before an event counts as appended) and `bootKernel` (the log, store, grants store rebuilt from the log, limits, tasks and gateway assembled for one Space). `kernel/golden`'s diff records new tools instead of failing on them and the stored set is refreshed to the integrated registry.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's grants-store gate. G-1: the store seals every event it writes with a MAC under the kernel's key and `rebuild` takes authority only from events that verify, so a forged `grant.created` or `member.set` is ignored; `bootstrap` is refused once the log has any history (G-5). G-2: `events.read` and `subscribe` cut a record event's `before`, `after` and `changed` to the fields the chain's grant allows and the `human`-level seals its role may see. G-3: `removeMember` (a presence-proved grant act) removes the membership, revokes the person's grants and offers, tells the runner, and keeps the last owner.
- feat(kernel): the registry installs through the module host. With `deps.moduleHost`, a module that is not first party never runs in the core process: it is installed under the supervisor (refused with `supervisor_absent` while the sandbox is unproved), its manifest tools call into it, and it has no ctx. Without `deps.moduleHost` nothing changes; it turns on with the kernel default-on path.
- feat(kernel): the Space checkpoint key. It is made and held by the sealing process (`spacekey.pub`, `spacekey.sign`, checkpoint bytes of this Space only), endorsed by an owner's device (`kernel/audit/key.js endorse`) and accepted by a device only after `verifyEndorsement` checks it against the Space's identity chain (names/worker/chain.js). `sealerKey` gives the checkpointer a signer backed by the sealing process.
- feat(kernel): K6, the module supervisor and egress proxy (kernel/modules). A module that is not first party runs out of process under a sandbox command (bubblewrap on Linux: a new network namespace, a read-only view of its own folder, a private tmpfs, a cleared environment; a sandbox profile on macOS; Node's permission model on top: no child process, worker or addon). `createSupervisor().selfTest()` runs a probe under that exact command line and requires network, write, read-outside, child-process and worker attempts all to fail; until it has, `available()` is false and `createModuleHost().install` refuses a non-first-party module (`supervisor_absent`). The module's only way out is `egress.request` (https only, hosts its manifest declared, never a private, loopback, link-local or metadata address, checked on the resolved address, redirects re-checked, bounded size, no cookies or ambient credentials, one event per request, no body logged). Windows has no OS sandbox yet, so such modules are refused there.
- feat(kernel): K5, signed checkpoints (kernel/audit). The home signs `{ space, seq, hash, time, key_id }` with the Space key (a `sign` function, never the private key) every 1,000 events or 10 minutes and appends `checkpoint.signed`; `verifyLog` (and `gateway.audit.verify` when given the Space's public key) recomputes the chain and checks every checkpoint; a device keeps the latest checkpoint it has seen (`createDeviceCheckpoints`: refuses an older one, detects a rollback, a rewrite and a split), and `compareCheckpoints` lets two devices expose a split. Rate windows are durable: each counted act on a rate-limited grant writes `rate.used`, replayed by `rebuild`.
- feat(kernel): compute offers in the grants store (DESIGN-wink 7): `gateway.grants.offers.{offer, unoffer, active, onRevoke}`. The Space's side (`space_allows`, an owner or admin, for a member of the Space) and the member's side (`member_accepts`, the member's own act, per computer) are two risk-`grant` acts with events (`offer.created`, `offer.revoked`); `active({ member, device })` is true on both only for that member's own computer, and `onRevoke` tells the runner at once when either is withdrawn or the member's role changes. Also reviewer-2's K4 N1 and N2: a delivery names only a sink and the recipients on the card (the card shows the sink), a sealed slot must belong to the record its ref names, `revise` is refused while a decide is running, and an approval with no doer is refused.
- fix(kernel): the rest of reviewer-2's K4 list. `tasks.card` is gated by `tasks.read` and `observeDenial` takes only the kernel's own service chain (item 10); a malformed or expired sealed-use proof is refused at `decide` (item 12); the approved body carries a hash of the template body and `seal.use` refuses a template that is not that body (template immutability); `createGateway` refuses a door not built with the kernel's `isChain`.
- feat(kernel): stage gates in the gateway, from records' `defineStage` and `defineRule` (a type's `stages` with task templates, `rules` with a `require` expression): a record cannot enter a stage unless the type's rules hold for the record as it would be (evaluated by the injected `expr`, records' own evaluator), and cannot leave a stage until its required tasks are done (`stageTasks`, the kernel's view in kernel/tasks). Fail closed: rules with no evaluator wired refuse the change. Entering a stage calls `onStageEnter` so the tasks side creates the stage's task templates. Field limits now also fail closed under row predicates, through a type-level probe that skips predicates and is never an access decision.
- feat(kernel): `once`, `rate` and `budget` conditions are enforced (kernel/core/limits.js, wired in the gateway through the shared gate). `once` is consumed atomically on the act and replayed from the log; `rate` is a sliding window per grant and actor; a meter is reserved and settled with `meter.reserved` and `meter.settled` events. The model door gets `limits.doorBudget` (`ai_spend`) and sessions `sessionStart` and `sessionEnd` (`session_hours`). A query, aggregate or search counts once, not per row. Acts by tasks, sealing and grants count too.
- feat(kernel): the grants store (kernel/grants). Grants and memberships are kernel records with one event per change (grant.created, grant.revoked, grant.narrowed, member.set, actor.added) and `rebuild()` from the log. `grants.create`, `revoke`, `narrow`, `list`, `setRole` and `addActor` are risk-`grant` acts: a fresh presence proof by the granting person bound to the exact input (verified by the one verifier, `grant.*` ops), never from a chain holding a model (`model_chain`). Widening is a new grant; narrowing is in place and only smaller; a delegated grant is contained in its parent and made by its holder; revoking a parent revokes its children. The five roles instantiate their bundles (kernel/grants/roles.js); temp carries a scope and an expiry; a Space keeps an owner. `authorize` reads grants and members from the store (the retrofit path stays when no store is given). Selectors take an optional `fields` allow-list: the gateway omits other fields on read, refuses writes to them (`field_not_allowed`) and refuses filters, sorts and groups on them; `human`-level seals hide a field from members outside the reveal roles. Stage gates are not built yet.
- feat(kernel): the tool surface (kernel/tools, built by the assistant team, landed here once) and the kernel facade it reads: `Store.types()` (suite revision 3), `gateway.definitions(chain)` through authorize, `actions()`, `members.roleOf` and `isAdmin`, `serviceChain(name)`, `tasks.list`, `ask` and `model.call` when tasks and a door are wired. Not yet: grants.list, create and revoke, chainFor and chainForPerson, stage gates.
- fix(kernel): reviewer-2's K4 gate items 1 to 8 and 11. A task is decided once at a time, the kernel's skip proposal has no doer and its card says skip, the card's recipients and slot classes are resolved by the kernel (`resolve`), the approved body is `{ action, resource, payload, facts }` as a frozen copy and a send must name an outward action, `seal.deliver` is unblocked by an approval for exactly its sink and recipients, `use` and `deliver` belong to the task's doer and expire after a day, a sealed slot must be on the task's record, `revise` goes through the table, and `reveal` is refused when no door is wired.
- fix(wink) gate: closes reviewer W-3, W-3b, W-4, W-5, W-7, W-8 and the node-key claim hijack. The relay peer slot frees on every exit (the hook ending or resetting the stream, or installing no handler), and `allow` is asked about the device. `wink.server.adopt` records its first caller for every caller kind, and any later change needs the owner's presence and that caller. A node key binds only when the host reports it as the key that proved the device secret (claims lapse after a minute). `devices.add` refuses a change of identity, kind or owner. Compute offers have one store at a time (an `offers` port, else `wink_compute`). `relay.devices.drop` is for module:wink only.
- feat(wink, embedded node host and the relay peer stream): `core/wink/node/host.js` runs one embedded node per space (one `wink-forwarder` process each) and gives the Wink module and the runner `connect(space)`: a channel with `call(tool, input)`, `ping()` and `status()` that starts the direct dial first, starts the relay peer stream when direct is not up in 3 s (a tsnet dial with no path takes 25 s to fail), prefers direct as soon as it is up and retries a dead direct path once a minute. New `core/wink/node/peer-wire.js`: calls and answers between two homes with fair queueing (small messages first, bulk in 16 KiB slices that take turns, so a ping does not wait behind a bulk result) and, on the node path, a proof of the device key bound to the node key and the home (an HMAC under the static DH of the device and home keys); the same protocol runs on both paths. `core/relay/bridge.js` serves a `peer` stream (`{peer: "wink", space}`) to a paired device only when the box passes `peers`: authenticated channel, same space, `allow()` true, 30 new streams a minute and 8 open per device, else 403 or 429. `core/wink/node/peer-channel.js` accepts the relay form of the header (`via: "relay"`, device id and space). `wink/forwarder` gains `-dial-sock`: outbound dials on a private Unix socket, tailnet addresses only, cancelled when the client gives up. `core/wink/node/relay-peer.js` is the paired server's relay client. Measured on two real machines: scripts/spike-wink/net-proof.mjs, docs/work/tailnet.md. No new dependency.
- feat(flows) 0.3: stages made of tasks (kernel/flows/stages.js) and the real-kernel harness (kernel/flows/testing/real-kernel.js). Entering a stage makes its tasks once per entry, wires depends_on, and moves the record on by itself when the required tasks are done; a hand-moved record is left alone, a stage with no tasks never advances by itself. The Estate planning Kit runs end to end on the real gateway and tasks (kernel/flows/e2e).
- feat(sessions) 0.3: sessions and voice behind the inference door (core/sessions/door-bridge.js, docs/work/door-retrofit.md). The API-key chat driver calls door.call (purpose session, the thread as session); Codex and Grok have their prompt and reports sanitised at the edge; spoken text is sanitised before it reaches the speech provider. No door means no model call unless VYRE_LEGACY_DIRECT_MODEL=1, which warns once per provider. Refusals read in plain words. kernel/door/sinks.json: retrofit_pending is empty, speech audio is declared audio_only.
- feat(sessions) 0.3: sessions under Wink (core/space-sessions). A session belongs to one Space. It runs on a member's own computer only when the Space has offered and the member has accepted for that device (two kernel grants), never someone else's. Its working copy is AES-256-GCM encrypted under a per-session key the vault releases at use, syncs back to the Space continuously with file versions (a clash keeps the Space's version and our file as a sibling), and never holds a credential. A checkpoint at every turn and a lease with a fencing token let it move between machines, never active on two. Continue in another space starts a new session from a summary that is stripped of sealed and source-only facts and delivered only after a person approves that exact text. No new dependency.
- feat(0.3, work): `kernel/tools` generates the assistant's tool surface from a Space's definitions and the action registry, cut by the chain's grants, with outward acts held as a task (a person's own act asks for presence). `core/work` registers it with the situation, teammates, the three-layer memory (`know.*`) and the Engineer as module tools with reach on each. Action names are the registry's. The fit eval runs on the real gateway and the generated surface, with an OpenRouter adapter and a protected manual workflow (`assistant-fit-eval.yml`, hard stop $5).

- feat(0.3, native assistant): `core/assistant/native`: the kernel-generated situation (space, role, record with sealed fields as placeholders and why, stage, team, open tasks, what waits on you; about 400 tokens, deterministic, external content quoted as data), Kit playbooks (external until reviewed, at most two, only where they apply), the tool-surface port (generated from definitions, cut by grants, outward acts come back `held`), tool results as eight closed Vyre component kinds with a validator and no raw-JSON fallback, and a per-model fit eval (five deterministic tasks, 100-point score, hard budget stop, a guarded real runner that needs a key and --yes). Factories over the kernel port; not wired until the gateway lands.

- feat(0.3, teammates, memory, @Engineer): built against `kernel/contracts` as factories over a `kernel` port and tested on `test/fake-kernel.js` (not wired to the daemon until the kernel's gateway lands). `core/team`: Kit roles to teammates (Kit text `external` until reviewed, 5 per assistant, no outward powers without a person), grants delegated under the adder's ceiling with the adder's presence, approval and surface conditions as obligations and a fail-closed parent recheck, context from the project and its links with sealed fields as placeholders, the "doing now" line (at most once a minute), and the stuck watch (seven triggers, kernel-composed fix, no model-words one-tap grant, 7-day cool-down). `core/memory/engine`: line-by-line session detail, fact proposals by the three outcomes of contract 7.9 (note applies, empty field is a suggestion, a changed or sealed or required field is one task to the owner), meaning search and answers with per-source authorization and citations, sealed values never indexed. `core/engineer`: admin-only; writes definitions as guarded TypeScript, compiles and simulates through ports, shows a diff card built from the canonical form; only the admin's own chain approves and applies. `lib/labels.js` and `lib/sealed.js` are shared helpers.
- feat(kernel): K4, tasks with approval (kernel/tasks): the transition table as data, human-only `decide` from a chain that is exactly one person with a hardware-signer proof bound to the payload hash, decision and chain (single use), the kernel-built approval card, kernel output checks, stuck detection. An approved task is an approval: `createApprovals` hands the sealing wiring the approver chain, the template version, the record and the sealed slots from the canonical body the person approved, so `seal.use` and `seal.deliver` open only for an approved task. The gateway registers the task actions and takes an optional `tasks`.

Constants IDENTITY_KINDS, DEVICE_KINDS, OFFER_KINDS, DEVICE_OFFERS.

Wildcards cover only read and write actions and need an action-set version, unknown trust or class labels are refused, a delegated grant dies with its adder's membership, a predicate on a missing attribute never matches, URN segments refuse dot, encoded and control forms, a model chain cannot filter, sort or group on a sealed field (new `Store.describe`), the retrofit's presence and asked gates fail closed, `fromLegacy` moved to a legacy-Space-only builder, `recover` completes only on an exact match, `gateway.events` goes through authorize, type and id are validated on every call.
