- feat(records): the records team's first build. `records/` is the language: a source-only parser with limits (no imports but the SDK, no execution, a worker with a memory ceiling), the SDK vocabulary (`defineKit`, `defineType`, `defineField.<kind>`, `defineStage`, `defineTask`, `defineTemplate`, `defineRule`, `defineRole`, `defineFlow`, `defineView`, `defineCodeStep`) whose types compile to the kernel's `TypeDefinition`, an Expression language, a canonical printer (stored form to text and back, identical), and the first Kit, "Estate planning matter". `stores/twenty/` is the Twenty store: it implements the kernel's Store interface and passes the kernel conformance suite against a real Twenty v2.44.0 on testbox (14 of 14) and against a fake one in CI, plus its own suite (versions that notice an edit made inside Twenty, the signed-webhook change feed, the version hash, sealed references), per-Space provisioning (compose with no published port and an internal network, headless service user and key, upgrade with backup and rollback) and a Stripe test-mode connector that finds or creates the contact and the matter through the Kit's own flow. No new dependency.
- feat(wink): pairing as DESIGN-wink section 4, devices belong to the identity. Two ways in only: scan a code, or two-sided typed codes (the pick-a-number path is gone from `core/wink/code.js`, `relay/client/code.js` and `relay/client/join.js`, which now has `typeWinkCode` and `finishJoin` around the ack code). New `core/wink/pairing.js`: a device registry keyed by identity with a kind (phone, computer, server, storage), per-device offers and an owner (the identity, or a space the person administers, for servers and storage), in new migrations after the grants one; devices are never members of spaces and no device grant is written (older device grants are adopted once and revoked). Tools `wink.pair.targets`, `wink.pair.server`, `wink.pair.status`, `wink.server.code`, `wink.server.confirm`, `wink.server.adopt`, `wink.phone.open`, `wink.phone.scan` (a phone pairs to the identity only and is refused any space), `wink.offer.set`, and the two-grant compute check `computeAllowed`. `wink.access` answers `{ devices, grants }`. New `scripts/install/i.sh` for `curl -fsSL vyre.run/i | sh` (system check, signed release installer, then a pairing code), served at /i by `scripts/assemble-site.sh` when the release has it.
- feat(wink): storage devices (`core/wink/storage/`, module `core/wink-storage/`). Find network drives and plugged-in disks from a device (mDNS and DNS-SD, smbclient, showmount; on demand, at most once a minute), pair a drive or an S3-compatible bucket or cloud volume as a storage device under a person or a space they administer, with a `storage` offer (capacity, used, class cold and backup by default, schedule, expiry, residency). The bucket login is tried with a small SigV4 client (node:crypto, no SDK) and saved in the vault only; the row holds a reference. Events storage.paired, storage.removed, storage.unreachable; remove can record a drain for the pool engine. No new dependency.
- feat(wink): the typed Wink code `WINK-NNPP-PPPP` (spec 6.5), the PAKE path (wink-code). `relay/client/code.js` parses, formats and folds the code (Crockford base32 without U, case, spaces and hyphens ignored) and runs a CPace exchange (CPACE-RISTRETTO255-SHA512, initiator/responder, the typist as initiator, role-bound identities, the rendezvous in the session id and the showing device's route in its transcript, explicit key confirmation, a 3-digit number and a sealing key from the transcript). It follows the draft with audited primitives and is not an audited CPace library; it matches the draft's published vectors for the generator, the two messages, K and ISK (draft-irtf-cfrg-cpace-20, B.3). New vendored dependency: @noble/curves 2.4.0 (ristretto255) and @noble/hashes 2.4.0 (sha512), MIT, bundled unminified into `relay/client/vendor/noble-ristretto255.js` with their licences and a NOTICE entry, because WebCrypto has no ristretto255 and the PAKE must run in a browser and in React Native. Both relays (`relay/node/server.js`, `relay/worker/index.js` with a new `CodeSlot` Durable Object, migration tag v3) give a registered box one free rendezvous for 5 minutes over its control socket (`code.alloc`, `code.release`, `code.msg`, `code.reply`; feature flag `code`) and forward a typing device's `POST /v1/wink/code` only to the route that holds it. The relay keeps nothing derived from a password. Every session is charged to the asking address (10 a minute), later steps 30 a minute, and a miss on a rendezvous that is not live 30 a minute more; there is no global budget (GHSA-25xh-w9j7-7v28), nothing is created for a rendezvous that is not live, and an unknown, closed, expired, refused or silent code gets one answer. `core/relay/link.js` gains `oncode`, `codeAlloc`, `codeRelease`, `codeReply`, `codes`. `core/wink/code.js` is the showing device's state machine: the typist confirms first, every session that processed message 1 counts as an attempt, the ceiling is checked before each key evaluation and the tenth attempt closes the code, a closed code is replaced with no tap (`wink.code.closed`, `wink.code.replaced`), one try for the number, single use, 5 minutes.
- feat(wink, control plane library, v0.3): `core/wink/control/` holds the three pieces of a space's network that vyred will supervise, with no module and no tool yet (the lead wires those). `headscale.js` supervises one Headscale per space: it writes the config (a random /24 inside 100.64.0.0/10 that avoids the prefixes it is given, no IPv6, MagicDNS, OIDC, logtail, Taildrop or update check, policy in file mode, admin socket 0600 in a 0700 directory, loopback listeners, DERP map emptied), starts, health-checks (60 s floor), restarts with backoff, runs as a given uid when root, and mints single-use pre-auth keys over the admin socket (the key is returned in memory or written to a new 0600 file, never in an argument, log, event or error); it also lists and deletes nodes and reloads the policy. `VYRE_HEADSCALE_BIN` picks the binary (none under node --test unless `VYRE_WINK_REAL=1`). `policy.js` is the network half of the grant compiler: a pure, deterministic function from device rows and grants to a deny-by-default hub-and-spoke policy where an unbound node gets no rule and no role ever comes from a tag. `gate.js` and `gate-main.js` are the front door as its own process: an HTTP-aware proxy with an exact-match allow-list (/key, /ts2021, and /derp and /derp/probe only when DERP is on), one generic 404 for everything else, upgrades as raw bytes, the client address written from the socket (or one header of a trusted forwarder) with every client-supplied copy dropped, header, body, idle and handshake limits, per-address upgrade and concurrency budgets, a reactive block fed from Headscale's log, no banner, and TLS with a public-key pin. Tested with a fake Headscale and, on the test server with `VYRE_WINK_REAL=1`, against a real Headscale v0.29.4 and a real tailscaled node registering through the gate.
- feat(wink): the Wink core's Node side and the peer door, no tools or module wiring yet (the lead wires them). `core/wink/node/core.js` manages a Vyre-owned userspace tailscaled (`start`, `stop`, `status`, `whois`, `leave`, `check`): private 0700 state, a 0600 key file deleted right after `up`, binaries only from `VYRE_WINK_CORE_BIN` and `VYRE_WINK_CLI_BIN` or `<home>/bin` (never the person's Tailscale), a refusal of system mode beside a running Tailscale, the daemon run with `--state=<file>` and no `--statedir` so it has no Taildrop storage ("Taildrop disabled; no storage directory", proved on a real core), and a fixed pref set (routes, DNS, SSH, exit node, tags, Taildrive, updates) re-checked every 60 s: any drift is an error event, re-applied once, and a core that will not hold stops (EC-9). `shim.js` is the pinning proxy for `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`: it dials the real control address over TLS and accepts only the sealed SPKI pin, never a certificate authority, forwards `/key`, the `/ts2021` upgrade and the DERP upgrade only, and refuses redirects and other paths (EC-8). `peer-channel.js` listens on a 0600 Unix socket for the Go forwarder `wink/forwarder` (new, own go.mod, one dependency `tailscale.com` v1.102.4, the same version as the core), which joins as a tsnet node, calls WhoIs on each accepted connection and writes a `WKH1` length-prefixed header with the node key before the first peer byte; a connection with no WhoIs result, or a missing or malformed header, is refused (EC-1). Proved on testbox against a headscale of its own: the peer channel received the second core's node key and stable id.
- feat(kernel): K3, sealing and the inference door (kernel/seal, kernel/model). The sealing process (serve.js: a line protocol on stdin and stdout, run under the Node permission model with no child processes, no workers and no files outside its own and the vault and egress folders) holds sealed values encrypted under the Space's vault key and is the only place plaintext lives; `put` returns metadata only, `use` merges into a template's body at a declared slot and hands the output to the egress boundary (a verified contact point or a document of the same record only; from a model's plan always an Ask), `reveal` needs a kernel ticket bound to the exact call plus, on the kernel side, a chain that is exactly one person and a signer's proof over that reveal, used once. The class registry (SSN, ITIN, EIN, card, bank account, routing, IBAN, passport, tax id, medical, free), one normaliser (full-width, digit words, separators), best-effort detectors, a per-session seal ledger of keyed hashes, and `model.call`, the one door: it refuses a service that is not a declared sink, a provider the Space does not allow and any prompt containing a value the session resolved, and sends only detector-sanitised text. The gateway returns placeholders to declared sinks as well as to a model in the chain. The shared `gate` moved to kernel/core/gate.js. 18 tests.
- feat(kernel): K2b, the retrofit. `Registry.call` can now take `deps.gates` (kernel/retrofit/gates.js): the static permission gates (module reach, outward, visibility, callers, guest, person session), the presence requirement and the asked requirement are then decided by `authorize` over grants compiled from today's rules, and the inline rules run only when no gates are given (the default, so nothing changes in a shipped build yet). The golden set proves the two paths give the same answer for every tool, caller shape and world (120k cells on the box and local roles); seven deliberately broken gates were each caught. Schema checks, projectArg, the rules hook, proof verification, the asked-match and running stay in the registry.
- feat(kernel): K2a: the gateway's record calls (kernel/gateway: authorize first, an intent before the store call and one event after, rows filtered by the gateway itself so a store cannot leak, ids minted by the gateway and kept, version hashes verified on read with `modified_outside`, sealed values as placeholders for a model, recovery of intents a crash left open), the in-memory reference store (kernel/store) and the conformance suite that defines "a store" (kernel/conformance, 14 rules plus 5 broken stores the suite must catch). Retrofit against the golden set is K2b.
- feat(kernel): K1 (kernel/core): `authorize` (contract 6.3: space check, candidates and an effective grant per hop, structural narrowing with the parent rechecked and its obligations carried, policy by risk class, taint, sealed placeholders; deny by default and fail closed), the kernel-built chain (`createChainBuilder`: only SurfaceFacts in, a model's call is never the person, unvouched agent claims have no chain, a stored job chain is sealed with a key), time-prefixed ids, canonical JSON and one hash, and the event envelope with a hash-chained, salted-commitment in-memory log (erasure keeps the chain verifiable, at-least-once consumers with durable cursors). 31 tests. Presence signatures and approvals are K4; durable storage is K2.
- feat(kernel): K3, the sealing door. `kernel/seal`: a separate sealing process (stdio, bare environment, its own 0700 folder, AES-GCM bound to ref, Space, record and field) that holds sealed values: `put`, `use` (sealed slots merged into a sealed derivative, only to the record's own verified contact point or a document for it, else a presence proof), `deliver` (to an egress sink socket, only a status returns), human-only `reveal` (a hardware-signed proof over the exact payload, one use), `detect` (placeholders), `lookup`. `kernel/door`: the inference door and seal ledger, and a CI check that no file outside the sink registry names a model provider. Vault and Drive actions, events and the "used for Gmail 3 times today" summary in `kernel/seal/uses.js`. Tests: canary-corpus and no-plaintext properties.
- feat(flows) 0.3: the Flow runner, built on kernel/contracts (kernel/flows). Triggers: an event pattern (with a condition), entering a stage, a time (cron, every, at), an inbound web call and a manual run. Steps: find, pick, filter, create, update, upsert, remove, decide, repeat, wait, ask, assign, agent, call, stage, classify, http and fn (a Code step, run only in the sandbox port). Every effect step is checked against the Flow's declared caps, then authorized as [automation, approver]; an ask raises a held-act card and waits, a denial for a lost grant pauses the Flow and says why. A run is the same run however often its trigger is delivered (id from flow and trigger key), each step is written to the run's ledger before and after it acts and carries an idempotency key, a replay gives back recorded outputs, and branches, loop lists and wait deadlines are recorded once. Runs started by or reading outside content are tainted and need an Ask for outward and grant steps; a model-drafted Flow asks on every run that uses a destination read from records. Loop control (cause depth 8, 60 runs a minute, 500 steps a run) pauses the Flow and raises a card. Runs are pinned to their version. Simulation replays past events with actions stubbed and reports runs, approvals, writes and outward acts. Definitions, approvals and runs are records (`def_flow`, `flow_approval`, `flow_state`, `flow_run`) through the kernel, or in memory.
- feat(flows) 0.3: Flows as TypeScript. The Expression language (no eval, bounded), the stored form with canonical JSON and hash, a compiler against the Space's catalog (unknown types, fields, stages, roles, teammates and actions, caps that must cover the steps, an effects summary for the approval card), a source-only parser of the declarative subset (rejects imports but the SDK, require, dynamic import, triple-slash, @ts- pragmas, spreads, computed keys, getters, tagged templates, interpolation, __proto__; limits on size, depth, nodes and time; a worker with a memory ceiling; a Code step's source is an opaque span), a canonical printer, and `defineFlow`, `step.*` and `expr` for @vyre/sdk.
- feat(flows) 0.3: Kits install with the grant card (everything the Kit adds, outward steps, sealed uses, Code steps, assistants that start from outside text), update with a diff that names every widening and risk, and remove cleanly (Flows stop, definitions go, a type that still holds records is kept, data is never deleted). Approving a Flow version or a Kit is a person's own act: a chain with an agent in it is refused.
- feat(flows) 0.3: the Flow canvas data: the graph in plain words with lanes and marks, a run painted over it, See as code both ways with changes described in words, and the builder's edits on the stored form.
- feat(records): the records team's first build. `records/` is the language: a source-only parser with limits (no imports but the SDK, no execution, a worker with a memory ceiling), the SDK vocabulary (`defineKit`, `defineType`, `defineField.<kind>`, `defineStage`, `defineTask`, `defineTemplate`, `defineRule`, `defineRole`, `defineFlow`, `defineView`, `defineCodeStep`) whose types compile to the kernel's `TypeDefinition`, an Expression language, a canonical printer (stored form to text and back, identical), and the first Kit, "Estate planning matter". `stores/twenty/` is the Twenty store: it implements the kernel's Store interface and passes the kernel conformance suite against a real Twenty v2.44.0 on testbox (14 of 14) and against a fake one in CI, plus its own suite (versions that notice an edit made inside Twenty, the signed-webhook change feed, the version hash, sealed references), per-Space provisioning (compose with no published port and an internal network, headless service user and key, upgrade with backup and rollback) and a Stripe test-mode connector that finds or creates the contact and the matter through the Kit's own flow. No new dependency.
- refactor(kernel): one presence verifier. The sealing process's (kernel/seal/proof.js) is the only one; `kernel/core/presence.js` is the kernel's interface to it (`check`), a new `presence.check` op serves task acts only, and `tasks.decide` and `unblock` call it. The tasks' own verifier is deleted. A proof is used up when checked.
- fix(kernel): the rest of reviewer-2's K1 and K2 lists. A standing service reads only what it declared, a presence session never stands for an assistant on admin or grant, an unknown condition makes the effect ask and `rate` is an obligation, stored job chains expire, a poison event is retried then set aside, `audit.verify` checks commitments, the gateway owns kernel attributes (a record it did not write matches no predicate), a store that alters a field or returns a stale version is caught (`store.disagreed`), no cursor when only unreadable rows remain, and a generated-caller differential test proves the gates match the registry beyond the golden matrix.
- feat(kernel): K4, tasks with approval (kernel/tasks): the transition table as data, human-only `decide` from a chain that is exactly one person with a hardware-signer proof bound to the payload hash, decision and chain (single use), the kernel-built approval card, kernel output checks, stuck detection. An approved task is an approval: `createApprovals` hands the sealing wiring the approver chain, the template version, the record and the sealed slots from the canonical body the person approved, so `seal.use` and `seal.deliver` open only for an approved task. The gateway registers the task actions and takes an optional `tasks`.
- feat(kernel): kernel/contracts/identity.d.ts: Identity (id plus kind: user, space, device, agent, project, session, task) as the base type, devices owned by a user or space identity and never members of a space, DeviceKind and offers, Node, Offer and Use (a member's computer runs a space's work only with both grants, for that member's own sessions). Constants IDENTITY_KINDS, DEVICE_KINDS, OFFER_KINDS, DEVICE_OFFERS.

- fix(seal): R-8 gate items 3 and 4 (reviewer-2). Once a chain is pinned every presence key needs a bind from a listed device (`needs_bind`), `presence.sync` drops keys nobody bound or whose device left the list and bars those devices, and a key saved before the age field counts as the oldest (a newcomer cannot remove it). `health` lists `needs_recovery` per person and the process-wide flag clears only when nobody is left without a key. The chain verifier moved to `kernel/identity/chain.js` (windows authors the final file and pins its hash); the seal process imports it from there and the `names/worker` exception is gone.
- feat(seal): key leases for a lent computer's encrypted workspace (DESIGN-local-runner.md section 3), `kernel/seal/leases.js`. The sealing process derives the workspace key from the home's master, the Space, the device and a revocation epoch: stable while access holds, one hour per lease, renewed only while the kernel says both Offer grants hold, never issued again after a revoke (survives a restart), and different after a reinstatement (which needs a presence proof). Only a person's chain can ask. `leasedUse` in `kernel/seal/uses.js` is vault use at the point of use for the runner's egress proxy: a live lease, the credential resolved per request, nothing cached, an event without the value.
- feat(storage): `kernel/storage/controller.js`, Vyre's controller for a pool: probe, heal and drain on a timer no faster than 60 s, with plain events. Erasure coding on SeaweedFS verified with four nodes (team/0.3/SPIKE-storage.md); the pool keeps full copies for cold data until the controller step that encodes sealed volumes is built.
- feat(kernel): the storage pool, `kernel/storage` (DESIGN-space-storage.md, DESIGN-wink.md sections 3 and 6). One pool per owner (a person or a space): chunks are named by a keyed hash, compressed, encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave the home, and kept at their class's copy count (working: home plus one replica, cold: two nodes, backup: off the home, rebuildable: one copy, given up first; hot data is refused and stays on the home). Healing after a grace period, draining before a node is released, one usable-space number after copies, plain nudges, meters (quotas), residency (owned nodes or regions only). Nodes are backends: a directory (local disk, USB, mounted network drive, attached cloud volume), or S3 and any S3-compatible bucket signed with AWS Signature V4 using only node built-ins (checked against a real SeaweedFS). A node may keep copies inside itself (`copies`), which is how a SeaweedFS service fits. Engine pick for multi-server spaces: SeaweedFS (team/0.3/SPIKE-storage.md). Phones do not offer storage. No new dependency.
- feat(seal): R-8, the recovery path for presence keys (DESIGN-wink.md section 2). The sealing process verifies the person's identity chain itself (names/worker/chain.js, its one outside import): `presence.sync` pins the chain head and drops keys whose device left the list, `presence.recover` gives a person with no key left a new first key from chain evidence (a listed device vouches for the key, the chain continues the pin, a replayed older list is refused, a revoked device stays barred). A key under 24 hours old removes only newer keys. Works after the key file is lost (pins live in the sealed anchor).
- feat(kernel): K3, the sealing door. `kernel/seal`: a separate sealing process (stdio, bare environment, its own 0700 folder, AES-GCM bound to ref, Space, record and field) that holds sealed values: `put`, `use` (sealed slots merged into a sealed derivative, only to the record's own verified contact point or a document for it, else a presence proof), `deliver` (to an egress sink socket, only a status returns), human-only `reveal` (a hardware-signed proof over the exact payload, one use), `detect` (placeholders), `lookup`. `kernel/door`: the inference door and seal ledger, and a CI check that no file outside the sink registry names a model provider. Vault and Drive actions, events and the "used for Gmail 3 times today" summary in `kernel/seal/uses.js`. Tests: canary-corpus and no-plaintext properties.
- feat(identity): the identity chain (ADR 0051, names/worker/chain.js). A person or space is a permanent id plus a signed, chained list of who can speak for it: devices, a recovery code (scrypt of the code and an optional PIN, public half only) and optional recovery contacts (two approve); a space's list holds its owners. Any entry adds or removes others, each change signed by an entry on the list; a new sign-in works at once but for 24 hours cannot remove older entries or change the code or contacts, and an older device removes it in one op. The directory Worker (names/worker/ids.js) now serves chains (claim, append, exact-name resolve, update, alias, release), verifies every op against the previous list and has no listing; the client (core/names/ids.js) re-verifies the whole chain and refuses a stale or forked answer against the head it pinned. spaces: identity tools (entries, entry add and remove, code replace, sync, recover by code or by contacts, contact key), the space's owners follow its members, invites can be made to an identity and a join is checked against the directory's current list, and the compute grant pair (lib/spaces/compute.js: the space allows, the member accepts, only their own sessions on their own machine).
- feat(kernel): kernel/contracts/roles.d.ts: the five fixed roles (owner, admin, manager, member, temp) as grant bundles (`ROLE_BUNDLES`), `Membership` (temp needs a scope and an expiry), `VyreName`, `SpaceIdentity` (a Space is an identity with a vyre.run name and a root key) and the optional person name on `Actor`. Types and frozen tables only.
- feat(runner): core/runner runs a space's sessions on a member's own computer. Seatbelt (macOS) or bubblewrap (Linux) sandbox, an egress proxy that fetches credentials from the space's vault per request, a one-hour key lease held in memory, an encrypted workspace (hdiutil AES-256 image, gocryptfs), transcript and file sync with a checkpoint every turn, placement (here, server or wait with a reason), and the runner module (runner.status, place, start, stop, lock, revoke, move). The vault, sync and grant ports are seams until those teams land theirs. New runtime needs on Linux: bubblewrap, gocryptfs, fuse3. Windows waits on the spike (team/0.3/SPIKE-runner-windows.md).
- fix(install-box): the installer ends only when the vyre container is running (verify_up), and fails with a plain line otherwise; run as root with --from it starts the box as the owner's account, because a root `vyre up` refuses a box built from a checkout. Tests: not running fails, running passes.
- release: prepare refuses a push of a tag that already has a release or draft (a moved tag is never signed); a patch (hotfix) run shows the approver the whole diff from the previous stable and a loud summary; the Mac status carries the sha256 of each dmg and zip and the release job recomputes them; mac-app.yml passes inputs through env; setup-hashes hashes dotfiles and config.json and requires /w. Version 0.2.3-rc.2 and release/notes/0.2.3.md.
- ci(matrix): the iPhone Safari lane waits for the springboard, starts Safari and retries openurl.
- fix(install-box): the installer ends only when the vyre container is running (verify_up), and fails with a plain line otherwise; run as root with --from it starts the box as the owner's account, because a root `vyre up` refuses a box built from a checkout. Tests: not running fails, running passes.
- fix(vitals) #71: a machine with no nvidia-smi is not asked again for an hour. The failed spawn forked the whole daemon once a minute, which was most of the idle CPU blip (about 80 ms a minute, now about 10 ms). perf-check reads CPU from /proc ticks (10 ms) instead of `ps` time (1 s), with budgets p95 2% and sustained 3%; the one remaining blip is the update check two minutes after start.
- site: the version text on every page comes from the release tag (assemble-site.sh passes VYRE_SITE_VERSION), with a per-version "out now" line in gen-site.mjs; vyre.run says 0.2.2, and the roadmap reads Sessions 0.2.3, Scale 0.2.4, Spaces 0.2.5.
- fix(site): scripts/gen-og.sh launches Chrome with --use-mock-keychain and --password-store=basic, so it never raises a Keychain dialog on a Mac (test/chrome-flags).

- Lumen Deep glass proof: the first Mac run (36954290280) showed the same left-to-right brightness gap with the glass on as with Reduce Transparency forced on, so a window-only capture shows no blur. The check now also captures the screen region under the panel, which includes the window server's blur, and prints whether the Mac itself has Reduce Transparency on. New drive command: windowframe.
- Lumen Deep glass: proved on the built app. CI now compiles a small probe, puts a window that is white on the left half and black on the right behind the panel, captures the panel with macOS's own window capture, and compares the panel's two halves with the glass on and with Reduce Transparency forced on, in dark and light (the Mac check prints the numbers and the stills glass-<look>-<ground>.png). New drive commands `display` and `appearance` set those two for the check.
- Lumen: the # picker's connector rows drew empty dark squares because the server names their icon "plug", which is not a macOS symbol (#31). Connector rows now use the plug symbol (powerplug), account rows a person, and any symbol name the system does not know draws a neutral glyph instead of nothing, in every tile, chip and module command. The real-daemon check now asserts every # row's icon draws, and saves a still of the picker.
- Lumen: a drive command sends real key events through the panel alone, and the Mac check types "@" as the US, German Mac (Option-L) and German PC (AltGr-Q) keyboards send it and asserts it reaches the box (#30; the cause on the user's Mac is not yet found, see the run).
- Release: release.yml has a stable-only `mac` job (the reusable mac-app workflow). A dmg reaches dist only when both architectures report signed=developer-id, notarized=yes and gatekeeper=accepted; then Vyre-Lumen-aarch64.dmg, Vyre-Lumen-x86_64.dmg, their zips and the versioned files go in before SHA256SUMS, so the Ed25519 signature covers them, and `check-release-dist.mjs --mac` gates the release. An unsigned run publishes no dmg (built and checked only; the site keeps "built on your Mac"). The Apple secrets live in the protected GitHub Environment "apple"; mac-app.yml takes them only on a publish (`sign: true`), only its package step receives them, and release.yml names none. mac-app-package.sh prints a skip line for each missing secret, signs the dmg container, notarizes and staples it (reading the Accepted verdict), then runs spctl and stapler validate on the app and the dmg and fails on any miss. mac-app-package.sh, scripts/mac-app, install-mac-server.sh and Lumen.entitlements are in the approver's signing-path diff. The repo variable MAC_SIGNING=required makes a publish fail when the Mac build is not signed and notarized, instead of quietly leaving the dmgs out. No secret is a command-line argument: the .p12 is re-exported with an empty password (openssl reads the password from the environment), the throwaway keychain has an empty password, and the notary key goes into a notarytool keychain profile in that keychain, which the script's EXIT trap deletes. Notarization takes an App Store Connect API key only; the Apple ID password path is gone. mac-app.yml is two jobs: `build` compiles Lumen with no environment and no secret and uploads the unsigned app; `package` starts from a fresh checkout, runs only mac-app-package.sh on that upload and is the only job in the `apple` environment. local/capsule/native/build.sh, Package.swift and Package.resolved are in the approver's signing-path diff.
- Lumen first-run words (app-design): while the app has the bundled setup to run and no vyre is on the Mac, the button, the row and the menu say "Set up Vyre on this Mac" (and "Setting up Vyre on this Mac…" while it runs); once Vyre is set up and just not running they say "Start Vyre". The password dialog says "Vyre needs your Mac password once, to set up its system service."
- Lumen setup hardening (reviewer-2, LOW): the sudo helper also pins the installer's flags after `install`: only --owner-uid, --owner-name, --owner-home, --vyred-wrapper, --gh-bin and --colima-program, with the owner uid, name and home equal to the user running it and the wrapper path under that home.
- Lumen setup hardening (reviewer-2): the bundled sudo helper runs only the installer's one root step, pinned at build time (vyre-sudo-check: the sha256 of the root script and the verify script, the architecture's Node checksum, the release key, the name and the verb), and refuses anything else before the password is asked for. The installer runs with a scrubbed environment (the system PATH, HOME, USER, LANG and the two setup variables, nothing inherited). Lumen refuses to run its bundled setup when a file in it is a link, is writable by others, or the app's own signature no longer verifies.
- Release: a `mac-app` workflow builds Lumen for Apple silicon and for Intel and packages each as Vyre-Lumen_<version>_<aarch64|x86_64>.dmg and .zip, plus the stable Vyre-Lumen-<arch>.dmg and .zip, collected into one `mac-app` artifact for the release job (#28). Each app carries the pinned Node tarball (checked against the checksum in scripts/install-mac-server.sh), the installer script and a dialog sudo helper in Contents/Resources/setup. With the user's Developer ID and notarization secrets present it signs with the hardened runtime, notarizes and staples; without them it is signed ad hoc and says so. build.sh app takes VYRE_CAPSULE_ARCH.
- Lumen: with no vyre on the Mac, Start Vyre runs the app's bundled installer with its own Node and asks for the Mac password in a dialog instead of a terminal (so a Mac with no npm and no Node can set Vyre up from the app). Without a bundled setup it says what it said before.
- link (tailnet, companion core transport, box side, v0.2.3): a companion core proves its own P-256 key on every call, with no dependence on the tailnet node. A token `c1.<companion>.<ts>.<nonce>.<sig>` signs the tool, the input digest and the box id; the box checks the companion row, that its parent app device is live and trusted right now, the time, a fresh nonce and the signature (`verifyCall` in core/link/companion.js). New tools `link.companion.hello` (tailnet callers) and internal `link.companion.verify`; the pair and approve answers carry `box: { pub, id }` for the core to pin; the five `sync.upload.*` tools accept `companion`, and the chunk route reads it from `x-vyre-companion`. A token made before the daemon started is refused (nonces are in memory only, so a restart cannot replay a captured one), and the nonce table is per companion. A companion may call only those tools; nothing is forwarded to it. The wire contract is in docs/work/tailnet.md.
- fix(install): install-box.sh ends on the next step, not a send-off. The closing "Go do your best work. We'll keep the thread.", the Friday "Nice way to end the week." and the "a fine moment for a coffee" wait line are gone, and the wait line no longer names apt. test/installer-copy.test.js keeps sign-offs and filler out of the three installers' output.

Fixes #9.
- feat(release): the release carries setup.json (the hashes of what vyre.run serves for the setup page, /i and /w), listed in the signed SHA256SUMS, and the release gate requires it (check-release-dist --setup). - fix(update): the updater compares versions as semver. A release is above its own prereleases and prereleases compare identifier by identifier, so a box no longer treats 0.2.0 and 0.2.0-rc.N as equal: it is not offered an earlier prerelease of its own version as an automatic update, and the floor holds the same rule. J2b has a case for it. Fixes #15.

When it has the answer, <agent> uses it and no model runs"; it says the agent answers every question and memory gives it the relevant facts, with where they came from, as context. Nothing on the box ever short-circuited an assistant (agents.ask and the assistant path call a model), so there is no setting to turn off; the memory-only answer stays the explicit `memory.ask` ("Ask memory"). What changed so memory actually helps the assistant: a prompt from an assistant with no project (scope "*", the hook) now reads the whole account's relevant facts instead of only the unfiled room, and `memory.prompt` (the per-prompt block for Codex, Grok and the person's own chat) now answers for the person's own assistant or chat and a named agent with no project, scoped by memory's own rules (a narrow agent still gets nothing of another project). Tests: core/harness and core/memory/brief. The Lumen side (typed text goes to the assistant by default, memory only on an explicit "Ask memory" action or prefix) is native-core's.
- fix(chat): one model per turn (#41). The header chip, the picker and each reply label name the same model with the same words (shortModel). The thread follows what the provider says it runs: when the init differs from what the thread asked for (an alias, an account default), the record moves to it and `model.switched {model, live, reported}` is said once, so the header and picker move with it; a live `threads.model` switch now also sets the model the next reply is stamped with, so old replies keep their model and new ones carry the new. `core/events` delivers an event emitted by a listener after the one being delivered (the settings hub answers `model.switched` with `settings.changed`, and the SSE stream's id cursor dropped the 12 after hearing the 13, so a live Deck never saw the switch). The fake Claude takes `FAKE_CLAUDE_REPORT_MODEL`.
- fix(chat): one model per turn (#41). The header chip, the picker and each reply label name the same model with the same words (shortModel). The thread follows what the provider says it runs: when the init differs from what the thread asked for (an alias, an account default), the record moves to it and `model.switched {model, live, reported}` is said once, so the header and picker move with it; a live `threads.model` switch now also sets the model the next reply is stamped with, so old replies keep their model and new ones carry the new. `core/events` delivers an event emitted by a listener after the one being delivered (the settings hub answers `model.switched` with `settings.changed`, and the SSE stream's id cursor dropped the 12 after hearing the 13, so a live Deck never saw the switch). One drain is capped at 10,000 events (listeners that emit each other stop with a log line naming the types, the daemon keeps running), a reported model is bounded to 80 characters, and the Deck draws it as text. The fake Claude takes `FAKE_CLAUDE_REPORT_MODEL`.

#### lumen: "Import my history" (#26)

- A new Lumen command, "Import my history" (`local/capsule/native/Sources/Extensions/history/`). It opens a panel that asks this Mac's Vyre what it holds in Claude Code, Codex and Grok (`import.scan`) and says it in words: "Found 412 sessions on this Mac across 23 projects." Each project has a tick with its session count, size and dates, ticked unless Vyre would not suggest it (its own and temporary folders come unticked and say why). "See what that takes" asks for the exact plan for the ticked folders (`import.plan`); the person then chooses how fast Vyre should understand them (fast or gentle, with the real estimates, neither pre-chosen) and whether to send just these or new ones too, and "Send them" starts it (`import.start`). It follows the sending by counts (`import.status`, `import.progress`) with Stop, and says "Sent N sessions to <box>" only once something was sent. Honest states: not paired says "Pair this Mac first, then import from here" and reads nothing; nothing found says where it looked and is never done; a run that sent nothing is a failure. Claude Code's 30-day keep is stated when the scan reports it. Tests (`HistoryImportTests.swift`, 7) run against a fake vyred.

- test(presence): `core/presence/testing/windows-hello.json`, a real WebAuthn registration and assertion from Windows Hello (Windows 11 build 26100, PIN, Edge against a throwaway localhost relying party; packed attestation, alg -257). Checked once through `verifyAssertion` with the key from the attestation (ok, signCount 2). Data only; vault adds the test.
- test(presence): a real Windows Hello capture, `test/fixtures/windows-hello.json`, from a KeyCredentialManager credential on Windows 11 (build 26100) after a PIN prompt: the RSA-2048 public key as SPKI and PKCS1, the challenge, and one RS256 signature (public data only, alg -257). `core/presence/hello-fixture.test.js` verifies the signature with node crypto, shows both key exports are the same key, and enrolls the real key as a device key. No code changed.
- onboard (tailnet, #50): the box's own onboarding no longer disagrees with the setup page about the name and the address. While the box holds a vyre.run address (the setup page claimed it), step 1 "Your name" is not prefilled with the address, `onboard.you` no longer overwrites the address with the person's name (it stored "robin" over "acme-lab" before, which is what made step 4 say "Not reserved yet" and fail with "this server already holds"), the status `name` the greeting uses is the person's, and step 4's reserve/claim on a held address only reads its progress instead of claiming again. The fuller separation of the person and the address into two fields is #11's one-flow build. Test in `test/onboard.test.js` (run on the test box).
- setup (tailnet, #57): the address field on the setup page now shows the suggestion it is judging (the form was built before the suggestion arrived, so an empty-looking field read "that name is reserved"), and an empty field shows "3 to 32 letters, digits and dashes" instead of a verdict. On the setup-recover branch.
- feat(threads): threads.continue-here {thread, machine?} (#32, box side). When a paired Mac is asleep, the person carries a Mac session on in a new box thread: its conversation comes over the link (recall.thread, read only) while the Mac is awake, or from the last synced copy on the box when it is not; a box session on the same provider starts with that history as context in front of the person's first words (quoted as data), and the new thread's id comes back with {name, project, provider, account, from: {machine, thread}, source: "mac"|"synced", turns, notice}. The new thread opens with "Continuing on your server with your <Provider> account (<who>). Your Mac's files stay on your Mac." (plus a line when the Mac was asleep and this is its last synced copy), records `continued_from` (threads.get) and emits thread.continued. The Mac's own session is untouched and none of its files come over. A person's own surface only (reach person); what a Mac says is data: its name is cleaned of control characters and brackets and capped at 80, its provider counts only if this box has it (else Claude), its project only if it is a box project slug (else a plain folder); every provider including Claude needs credentials on this box; errors not_found, no_history, account_required ("Add one in Settings > Your AI"), bad_input (already on this box), denied.

- link (tailnet, companion pairing, box side): a local core can join the box as a companion of the desktop app already paired on the same machine, with no second passkey prompt (`core/link/companion.js`). The app calls `link.companion.pair {core, name, nonce, ts}` over its own relay channel with a presence proof from its own device key; the presence layer makes that proof cover the whole call and checks it against the key enrolled for that device, so the proof is the countersign, and the core's own public key is registered (the core is authenticated by its own private key; the box issues no secret the app could carry, and a companion has no bearer key). Inside 15 minutes of the app's pairing and with no companion yet it is approved at once; otherwise one request waits (5 minutes, one at a time) for the person's one tap, `link.companion.approve` (no Touch ID), and a second companion also needs the tap. Only a desktop app device (kind app) can ask, never the hosted web app; it needs a person session on that device; 5 attempts per device per 10 minutes; each refusal is a `companion.refused {device, reason}` event, and the audit events are `companion.paired {device, companion, fingerprint, approved, nonce}`, `companion.requested` and `companion.removed`. A companion is valid only while its parent device is live, evaluated on every use (an untrusted parent makes an equally limited companion, a removed one invalidates it at once, and a startup and `device.removed` tidy-up deletes the row); `link.companion.remove` revokes only the companion; `link.companion.list` shows them. New internal tool `relay.device.info`. NOT USABLE YET: it needs a transport that authenticates the core's key (v0.2.3: over the tailnet, as the Mac's link). Tests: `core/link/companion.test.js`.
- the sealed 0.2 eval world can be recorded (0.2.2): `.github/workflows/memory-sealed-record.yml`, dispatch only, in the protected `eval` environment, once per release candidate, records the model's replies for the sealed world and prints its scores and nothing else. `node scripts/eval-bar.js --world sealed --record-sealed` refuses to run outside that workflow (it needs GITHUB_ACTIONS, VYRE_EVAL_SEALED_RECORD and VYRE_EVAL_RECORD, and only for the sealed world); the replies go to the runner's temp folder for that one run, so no sealed question, answer or reply is printed, uploaded or committed, and the only artifact is the score table. It keeps the key-usage guard (refuses to start at $14, stops before a call that could pass $4). A plain `--record` or `runBar({ record: true })` on the sealed world is still refused. Tests: test/eval/bar-sealed.test.js.

- test(eval): the sealed half of the 0.2 eval world. A second fictional world with the open world's shape and counts (185 sessions, 408 turns, 280 gold questions in the same ten classes) and a different story: a firmware consultant, two clients, a shared tooling repo, personal notes, agents wren, oskar and tern, and the same hard cases planted differently. `node scripts/eval-bar.js --world sealed` scores it and prints counts only; it still refuses `--explain` and `--record`, and the freshness probe no longer prints its question text for a sealed world. New: test/fixtures/iq02-sealed.js, test/eval/iq02-sealed.json, an empty test/eval/asks/iq02-sealed.json and test/eval/bar-sealed.test.js (class counts, every expected string in its cited turn, no open-world string in the sealed world, leak probes only about strings another project holds, and the bar run with no question or answer in the report). The people who tune memory must not read its questions; it is recorded per release candidate on a hosted runner and never tuned against (docs/work/iq.md).
- hosted app (tailnet): a relay named inside a pairing record must be the relay that served it. `resolveTicket` now refuses a record whose `relay` has another scheme or host, or carries a path, credentials, query or fragment (`sameRelay` in `relay/client/client.js`), so a box cannot send a phone to another server after the person taps Pair; the hosted app asks only wss://relay.vyre.run, so only that is accepted. The app Worker's CSP connect-src gains `https://relay.vyre.run` (the ticket lookup). The `#pair=` Chrome test now runs against the REAL relay Worker (wrangler dev, `relay/app/testing/real-relay.mjs`) with a real registered ticket, a host rule keeping relay.vyre.run on the runner, and covers one lookup that uses the ticket up, the card, no socket or key store before the tap, Not now, the tap, and a record naming another relay (refused with no card). The app's one pairing path is `pairWithCard(ticket, {resolve, confirm, pair})` in `relay/app/loader/fragment.js`; pwa's in-app scanner calls the loader's flow with it.
- The phone app and the hosted app wait 90 seconds for the person's Confirm when they pair (the box holds a redeem until the screen it came from confirms; the handshake default was 15 s).

#### Pairing: the arriving phone shows its own key fingerprint

While the phone waits for the screen's Confirm it shows "This phone: <fingerprint>", the same format as the box's pairing.requested card, so the person compares two. Both the hosted app's card (relay/app/loader) and the Deck's scan sheet use tailnet's `onFingerprint` on `pairOffer`. Text only, capped.

#### Wink card: a fresh code for whoever is looking, so the second scan always works

- The shared ring card (`js/wink-card.js`, used by onboarding's devices step and Settings > Devices) renews its code by itself after the person's one tap: in the last 30 seconds, or at once when they come back to a code that has run out. The renewal asks for no proof; a server that wants one gets the plain Refresh, as before. Only while the card is in view and focused (nobody looking, nothing minted), at most six renewals in a row, and none after the phone has paired or the device was removed. The line under the ring now points at wink.vyre.run. Tests in `deck/test/wink-card.test.js`.

- relay (security, reviewer-2 LOWs on the pairing window and pair-limit): `relay.pair.window.reject` ("Not you?") refuses the phone waiting to be confirmed and frees the single pending slot at once, with the window still open, so a stranger cannot hold it for 60 seconds (`pairing.rejected` event). `pairOffer`/`pairTicket` take `onFingerprint(fp)`, called before the handshake waits for Confirm, so the arriving phone's own screen shows the same fingerprint as the box's and the person compares two. A ticket its owner withdraws (revoke) leaves a tombstone until its own expiry in both the Node relay and the Worker: no box registers that locator again, and it resolves to nothing.
- relay (tailnet): the pairing window, so a screen can keep a fresh Wink code without a prompt every five minutes. One presence proof on `relay.pair.window.open` opens up to 10 minutes; inside it `relay.pair.window.renew` mints a new code (no proof) only for the same caller, node and person session, only while the screen pings (`relay.pair.window.ping`, every 15 s; 30 s of silence closes it), at most one renewal every 15 s and 40 a window. Each renewal first withdraws the previous ticket at the relay (new relay message `revoke`, answered `revoked`, advertised as the `revoke` feature, only by the route that registered the ticket, never a setup offer), so at most one ticket is live, and a closed window withdraws the live one. A phone that redeems a window code is held: the box emits `pairing.requested {window, device, name, fingerprint}` and enrols nothing until the screen calls `relay.pair.window.confirm {window, device}`, which enrols the phone and closes the window; no confirm (or a close, or 60 s) refuses it. The window is in memory only. Events: `pairing-window.opened|renewed|closed {window, reason}`. All five tools are for the owner's own deck or device, never a terminal, agent or module. The relay (Worker and Node) needs the new revoke message, so it needs a relay redeploy. A phone redeeming a window code should pass a handshake timeout of about 90 s, since the box waits for the confirm. Tests: `test/relay-window.test.js`, `relay/worker/worker.test.js`, `relay/node/server.test.js`.
- relay (tailnet, security, GHSA-25xh-w9j7-7v28): two shared rate limits on the hosted relay let any outsider block everyone, and both are gone. `/v1/pair` always looks the ticket up and serves a hit (200) or a contested ticket (409) with no charge; only a miss is charged, to its own address's limit, and there is no global limit. The setup mailbox's global append limit is replaced by a per-locator limit (`SETUP_LOC_LIMITER`, 60 a minute) beside the per-address ones; storage stays bounded by the 64 KB cap and the expiry. `relay/worker/wrangler.toml` drops `PAIR_LIMITER_GLOBAL` and `SETUP_LIMITER_GLOBAL` and adds `SETUP_LOC_LIMITER`. Tests in `relay/worker/worker.test.js`. The edge cost cap is code: `scripts/deploy/relay-edge-rule.mjs` upserts one Cloudflare rate-limiting rule (50 requests per 10 s per address on those two routes, the Free plan's shape, about 300 a minute) and leaves other rules alone; `relay-deploy.yml` runs it with `relay_edge_rule=true` (a separate environment secret `CLOUDFLARE_WAF_TOKEN`, scoped to Zone WAF Edit on vyre.run, used by that step only; the Workers deploy token stays narrow). Test in `scripts/deploy/relay-edge-rule.test.js`. The self-hosted Node relay (`relay/node`) gets the same: misses-only per address on `/v1/pair`, no global limit (test in `relay/node/server.test.js`).
#### the hosted app pairs inside itself: its own card for a handed ticket, and the scanner on first launch

- `app.vyre.run/#pair=<ticket>` (from the camera page) is read once and scrubbed from the address, then the app looks the ticket up AGAIN and shows its OWN confirm card before it redeems anything; the ticket is redeemed only on the tap, by this origin's own device key (`relay/app/loader/pairing.js`, the same screen as wink.vyre.run's, `relay/wink/page.js` with a `ticket` and a `redeem`). With no server yet (the installed app's first launch) the scanner opens in the app itself, never by navigating to wink.vyre.run (on an iPhone that leaves the installed app for a browser sheet). The sealed loader ships the scanner's 20-odd files under their repo paths (`relay/wink/closure.js` finds them) and no Deck API client or shell. Tests in `relay/app/app.test.js` (every import in the sealed tree resolves; `pairing.js` run from the sealed tree with fakes: looked up again, nothing redeemed before the tap, redeemed with the same ticket after it). Not tried on a phone; the passkey enrolment at the app origin is open with platform.

- hosted app (tailnet): a real-Chrome test of the camera page's hand-off (`relay/app/testing/pair-fragment-chrome.mjs`, in the `app-boot` workflow): the real sealed loader opens `/#pair=<ticket>`, and the test holds the first outbound request to read the page's own address then. It fails unless the fragment was already cleared, the only host contacted was relay.vyre.run (POST /v1/pair), and the ticket was in no URL and never reached the page's own server. It does not run a pairing to the end, so the device key made at the app origin holds by construction (the loader pairs with its own IndexedDB key store and imports nothing of wink's), not by this test.
- hosted app (tailnet): a `#pair=<ticket>` link no longer pairs on arrival, since anyone can send a person one. The loader reads the fragment once and scrubs it from the address and history at once, resolves the ticket (read only), and shows its own confirm card ("This code says it is alex.vyre.run", the key fingerprint, Pair this device or Not now, written as text and never markup). Only the tap on Pair makes this origin's device key and opens the pairing channel; Not now or leaving pairs nothing. A real-Chrome test (`relay/app/testing/pair-fragment-chrome.mjs`, in `app-boot`) opens the real sealed loader on a hostile link with a real sealed record: it must show the card, contact only the relay (POST /v1/pair), open no socket and make no key store before the tap, pair nothing on Not now, and start pairing only after the tap. Note: resolving a ticket consumes it on the relay (single use), so the camera page must not resolve a ticket it hands over, or the app's own resolve will find it gone.
- hosted app (tailnet): the first phone pairing hands off from wink.vyre.run. The loader at app.vyre.run now reads `#pair=<ticket>` (`relay/app/loader/fragment.js`, sealed with the loader), clears it from the address at once, and redeems the ticket with this origin's own device key (`pairTicket` against the hosted relay), then continues as a paired browser; the passkey is enrolled by the app once connected (pwa). Test in `relay/app/app.test.js`.
- Lumen: a quick question about the screen waits for the screen chip again (that wait lived in the memory-first path I removed, so the screen would have gone without the question). Found by running the Swift suite locally before the next Mac run.
- Fixes from the first Mac run of the paired-Mac work (36958350321): the wiring test's fixture now answers agents.list through link.call, since a linked Mac asks its server for agents; the paired-Mac check reads the link afresh when it looks for the server being away, clears the earlier answer, and asserts the question reached the assistant's thread on the box.
- Lumen says "server", never "the box" or "your box", to a person (team/RULES.md): the menu's "Server direct" and "No server", "Send to server", the Glass rows, the session-limit message and the chat-link messages. The guard suite now fails on those words too.
- Lumen tells vyred the Mac's IANA time zone name (context.report {surface, device, tz}, nothing else about where it is) when it finds vyred, when it shows, and when the zone changes, so the Planner reads "6pm" in the person's zone (#58).
- Lumen asks the assistant by default; memory never answers in front of it (#46). What is typed goes to the assistant (on a paired Mac, the server's, through the link). The memory answer above the results as you type and the memory.ask default for a plain quick question are off. Memory answers only when asked for: an Ask memory row after the assistant, or "memory: ...", with its sources and Wrong?/Forget as before. With no assistant, a question goes to the fast model. The old memory-first code is removed outright (iq's ask): the as-you-type memory.answer and its box, the memory.ask default, the "memory answered above" state, Route.ownThings and the helpers that fed them; the tests that exercised them now ask memory with "memory: ...".
- Lumen: no more sitting on "starting" (#36). On a paired Mac the memory question (which asks with a live draft) now goes to the server too; the draft overload had skipped the new routing and asked the Mac's own, slow memory. memory.ask waits at most 12 seconds, then says "Memory did not answer in time. Ask <assistant> instead, or try again." A slow server is not called away: only an unreachable one is. A reply that has said nothing for 45 seconds gets "Nothing has come back yet. Esc stops it, or wait a little longer." The paired-Mac check asks a quick question and fails if it is left pending.
- Lumen tells a paired server when the Mac sleeps and wakes: link.sleep on willSleep (a 3-second call) and link.wake on didWake, so the box marks the Mac offline at once and it serves again on wake. Nothing is called when the vyred has no such tools or under the tests.
- Lumen on a paired Mac asks the paired server (#36). The Mac's own vyred has no assistant, so Lumen said "there is no assistant on this Vyre" while the person's assistant was on their server. When link.status says the Mac is linked, agents.*, memory.* and learn.lessons go through link.call to the server, as do the thread calls for a thread the server owns; the server's thread, ask and memory events are followed on /v1/link/events and reach the same screens as the Mac's own. Apps, files, clipboard, the Mac's sessions, the vault and the Gate stay on the Mac. With the server away Lumen says so in words and never falls back to the Mac's empty answer. New: Vyred/BoxLink.swift, BoxLinkTests, scripts/capsule-paired-check.mjs and a CI step that runs the built Lumen against a real paired box and Mac.
